docs.title: mcp-gee-sweet
docs.text: An MCP server that gives AI clients deep, direct access to Google Workspace — Sheets, Drive, Docs, Calendar, and Gmail.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Read and write Google Sheets — cell values, formulas, sheet structure, batch updates
  • Manage Google Drive — list, search, upload, download, move, copy, and sync files and folders
  • Work with Google Docs — create documents, read content, write formatted content from HTML or Markdown
  • Access Google Calendar — list calendars and events, create and update events, find free slots
  • Use Gmail — search and read messages and threads, send and reply, manage drafts and labels (OAuth only)

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text:
This project started as a fork of xing5/mcp-google-sheets and has since diverged substantially — full Sheets read/write/formulas/structure/formatting/charts plus a raw batch_update passthrough for anything a named tool doesn't cover, an AST-based Docs pipeline (HTML and Markdown input, theming, structural table editing), Drive file/sharing/sync operations, Calendar, and Gmail. See Project Fork for the original fork history.

This project deliberately consolidates related operations into fewer, more parameterized tools, with batch_update as the escape hatch for whatever doesn't fit a named tool — see Design Principles for the reasoning ("Tool count as a cost").

Known gaps (full comments CRUD, conditional formatting, protected ranges, multi-tab Docs, and more) are tracked as candidates in the roadmap, not silently ignored.

docs.title: Key design decisions
docs.text:
Tool count is a cost. Every registered tool is a name the AI must reason about on every call. This server applies a strict inclusion test — see Design Principles — and defers borderline cases to the batch_update passthrough rather than adding named tools speculatively.

Composite tools only when it matters. Multi-step workflows are left to the AI client unless they involve binary data, pagination loops, or encoding decisions that Claude handles inconsistently in practice. See Design Principles for the policy.

Caching by default. Sheet structure, sheet data, Drive folder listings, doc content, and calendar metadata are all cached in a local SQLite database with TTL + dirty invalidation. See Configuration for details.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
# Run locally
uv run mcp-gee-sweet

# Docker
docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 \
  -e MCP_SERVER_TOKEN=<token> \
  -e CREDENTIALS_CONFIG=<base64-service-account> \
  -e DRIVE_FOLDER_ID=<folder-id> \
  mcp-gee-sweet

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: The server tries auth methods in a waterfall by default. Set AUTH_METHOD to pin a specific method with no fallback.

docs.title: Auth waterfall (default)
docs.text:
1. OAuth (CREDENTIALS_PATH / TOKEN_PATH)
  2. Service account (CREDENTIALS_CONFIG or SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH)
  3. Application Default Credentials (ADC)

OAuth is tried first because it authenticates as a user and has full personal Drive access. Service account is the headless fallback. ADC covers GCP-hosted deployments.

docs.title: Pinning a method
docs.text:
AUTH_METHOD=oauth            # OAuth only — fails fast if credentials are missing
AUTH_METHOD=service_account  # Service account only
AUTH_METHOD=adc              # ADC only

docs.title: Method A: Service account (recommended for servers)
docs.text:
Best for headless or automated environments. Credentials don't expire.

  1. Create a service account in GCP Console → IAM & Admin → Service Accounts.
  2. Download the JSON key file.
  3. Share a Google Drive folder with the service account's client_email (Editor access).
  4. Set environment variables:
  5. SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH — path to the JSON key file
  6. DRIVE_FOLDER_ID — ID of the shared Drive folder

Limitation: service accounts cannot create files in a user's personal Drive (no quota). Use OAuth or a Shared Drive when you need to create files. Service accounts also have no personal Drive identity, so transfer_ownership always fails — that one requires OAuth, with no Shared Drive workaround. Gmail tools require OAuth — service-account / domain-wide delegation is not wired yet. See server://auth-status to check your active auth method and affected tools (Gmail's are listed under the no_user_mailbox category).

docs.title: Method B: OAuth 2.0 (personal use / local dev)
docs.text:
Authenticates as you — gives full access to your personal Drive. Requires a one-time browser login.

  1. Configure an OAuth consent screen in GCP Console → APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen.
  2. Create an OAuth Client ID credential (type: Desktop app) and download the JSON.
  3. Set environment variables:
  4. CREDENTIALS_PATH — path to the downloaded OAuth JSON (default: credentials.json)
  5. TOKEN_PATH — where the refresh token is stored after login (default: token.json). Use an absolute path: the default is relative to the working directory, and an MCP client may start the server somewhere other than your shell's directory.
  6. Log in once from a terminal, with the same CREDENTIALS_PATH, TOKEN_PATH and ENABLED_TOOLS the server will use:
mcp-gee-sweet auth              # cloned repo: uv run mcp-gee-sweet auth
uvx mcp-gee-sweet auth          # PyPI install
mcp-gee-sweet auth --no-browser # print the URL instead of opening a browser

This opens the Google consent page, waits for you to finish, and writes the token to TOKEN_PATH, replacing any token already there. It requests the scopes the registered tools need, so --include-tools / ENABLED_TOOLS narrow it the same way they narrow the server.

Without a usable token, a stdio server doesn't open a browser itself. Under stdio, stdout is the protocol channel and the client gives up on a slow start, so the server can't show a consent prompt. It starts without Google access instead, and server://auth-status reports auth_method: "none" with an oauth_not_authorized limitation. In the waterfall, the server first tries a service account and ADC, and only starts without access if neither is available. If a service account or ADC was configured on purpose (SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH or GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS set) but wasn't usable, the error says why. An expired token whose refresh Google rejects at startup (for example, a revoked refresh token) is handled the same way. If Google simply can't be reached at startup (say, the network isn't up yet), the server keeps the token and refreshes it on the first tool call.

Re-authorizing from the client. When a tool call finds no usable token, or Google rejects a token refresh mid-session, the call offers the Google consent page itself, without a restart:

  • A client that supports MCP URL elicitation (Claude Code does) gets a prompt with the consent link. The server never opens a browser on its own: you choose to open the link.
  • Any other client gets an error whose text carries the link.

Open the link, approve access, and retry the call. The server saves the token to TOKEN_PATH (mode 0600) and the retried call uses it, on every connection. The link works for OAUTH_CONSENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 5 minutes). Calls that fail while it's open get the same link, along with how long it still works, and a call after it expires gets a new one. A call whose token is rejected partway through isn't re-run, since it may have already done part of its work: its error includes what the tool itself reported. This works over stdio and SSE alike. It applies to OAuth only: a service account or ADC connection reports a rejected refresh as an ordinary error.

mcp-gee-sweet auth still works as the alternative, for example when the client can't show the link. Run it with the same settings as the server, then retry the call. The server re-reads TOKEN_PATH on the next call, so no restart is needed.

Over SSE, the server still runs the browser consent itself when there's no usable token. The prompt goes to stderr, and the server waits at most OAUTH_CONSENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 5 minutes). The rest of the server keeps working during the wait. Connections that open during it wait for the same consent instead of starting another one, and stopping the server (SIGTERM, Ctrl+C) ends the wait. If consent is denied, fails, or isn't finished by then, the connections waiting on it start without Google access as described above. The server doesn't start that browser consent again for later connections, so an unattended server doesn't make each new connection wait out the timeout. Those connections still offer the consent link from their first tool call, as described above.

mcp-gee-sweet auth checks that the TOKEN_PATH directory exists and is writable before it opens the consent page, and saves the token readable by your user only (mode 0600). The server rewrites it the same way when it refreshes.

Re-authenticating after a scope change: at startup the server checks that the saved token was authorized for every scope the registered tools need. It never opens a browser to fix a shortfall on its own. What happens depends on which scope is missing:

  • Only the Gmail scope is missing (for example, a token from before the Gmail tools existed): the server starts normally and Sheets, Drive, Docs, Calendar and activity tools keep working. Every Gmail tool returns an error naming the missing scope and how to re-authorize, and server://auth-status lists the Gmail tools under a gmail_not_authorized limitation.
  • Any other scope is missing: under stdio, startup stops with an error naming the missing scopes. Most tools can't work without them. (Under a stdio client this error goes to stderr, which the client usually doesn't show; the client just reports that the connection closed. Set DEBUG_LEVEL and LOG_FILE to capture it in a file.) Over SSE, the server keeps running and the connection starts without Google access: every tool returns that error, with the instructions to re-authorize. The same applies to any other authentication failure over SSE.

Either way, run mcp-gee-sweet auth (see step 4 above) and restart the server to re-authorize. A tool call doesn't offer the consent link for a missing scope.

Gmail scope is only requested when a Gmail tool is registered. With no ENABLED_TOOLS filter every tool is registered, so the server asks for gmail.modify (read, compose, send, label, trash). If you don't want to grant mailbox access, leave the Gmail tools out of ENABLED_TOOLS / --include-tools. The server then neither requests nor requires the Gmail scope, and an existing pre-Gmail token keeps working.

docs.title: Method C: Base64 credential injection
docs.text:
Useful in Docker/Kubernetes where file mounts are inconvenient. Encode your service account or OAuth JSON as Base64 and pass it via environment variable.

# macOS / Linux
base64 -i service_account.json | tr -d '\n'

Set the output as CREDENTIALS_CONFIG. The server detects the credential type automatically.

docs.title: Method D: Application Default Credentials
docs.text:
For GCP-hosted environments (GKE, Cloud Run, Compute Engine) or local dev with gcloud.

# Local development
gcloud auth application-default login \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform,\
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets,\
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive,\
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.activity.readonly,\
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/documents,\
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar,\
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify

gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project YOUR_PROJECT_ID

On GCP, attach a service account to your compute resource — ADC picks it up automatically. The GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS env var (Google's standard) also feeds into ADC.

ADC can resolve to either a real user or a service identity, and the two have different limitations: a real user credential (gcloud auth application-default login, or Workforce Identity Federation) has full personal Drive access, while a service identity — a GCE/Cloud Run/GKE attached metadata identity, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS pointed at a service account key, Workload Identity Federation, an impersonated service account, or a GDCH service account — has the same restrictions as Method A above. server://auth-status reports which one is actually active — auth_method stays "adc" either way, but is_service_account_identity distinguishes them.

docs.title: Required Google APIs
docs.text:
Enable these in GCP Console → APIs & Services → Library:

  • Google Sheets API
  • Google Drive API
  • Google Drive Activity API (required for list_file_activity)
  • Google Docs API
  • Google Calendar API
  • Gmail API

docs.title: Environment variable summary
docs.text:
Auth-specific variables only — see Configuration for the full list including cache, tool filtering, and transport settings.

Variable Auth method Description Default AUTH_METHOD all Pin to one method: oauth, service_account, adc waterfall SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH service account Path to service account JSON key — GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS ADC Path to service account key (Google standard) — DRIVE_FOLDER_ID service account Drive folder shared with the service account — CREDENTIALS_PATH OAuth Path to OAuth client ID JSON credentials.json TOKEN_PATH OAuth Path to store the OAuth refresh token token.json CREDENTIALS_CONFIG service account / OAuth Base64-encoded credentials JSON —

docs.title: Claude Desktop
docs.text: Install the MCP Bundle, or add a block under mcpServers in claude_desktop_config.json yourself: stdio (cloned repo) or SSE (Docker).

docs.title: Install as a bundle
docs.text:
A GitHub Release carries an MCP Bundle, mcp-gee-sweet-<version>.mcpb, under its assets. Open it in Claude Desktop on macOS to install the server, without editing any config file. The bundle declares macOS and Linux; Windows isn't tested yet, so it's left out.

The install dialog asks for:

  • OAuth client file (required): the OAuth Client ID JSON for a Desktop app, downloaded from Google Cloud Console. See Authentication for how to create one.
  • Enabled tools (optional): a comma-separated list of tool names. Leave it empty to enable every tool (see Tool filtering).

The bundle ships the source and uv.lock, not the dependencies: the first start runs uv run --frozen, which installs Python and the locked dependencies, so it takes longer than later ones. It uses OAuth only (AUTH_METHOD=oauth) and keeps the token at ~/.mcp-gee-sweet-token.json, outside the extension directory, so the token survives an update. For a service account or Application Default Credentials, use the manual config below instead.

There's no token on the first start. The server starts without Google access, and its first tool call returns a Google consent link. Approve it in a browser, then retry the call. To authorize from a terminal instead, run CREDENTIALS_PATH=/path/to/credentials.json TOKEN_PATH=~/.mcp-gee-sweet-token.json ENABLED_TOOLS=<your Enabled tools value> uvx mcp-gee-sweet auth, then retry. Give ENABLED_TOOLS the same value as the install dialog's Enabled tools, or leave it out if that was empty: the consent asks for mailbox access only when a Gmail tool is enabled, so leaving it out after excluding Gmail grants a scope the server doesn't use.

docs.title: stdio — cloned repo
docs.text:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mcp-gee-sweet": {
      "command": "uv",
      "args": [
        "run",
        "--directory",
        "/path/to/mcp-gee-sweet",
        "mcp-gee-sweet"
      ],
      "env": {
        "CREDENTIALS_PATH": "/path/to/credentials.json",
        "TOKEN_PATH": "/path/to/token.json"
      }
    }
  }
}

Replace /path/to/mcp-gee-sweet with your clone path. This uses OAuth (the default waterfall's first method, full personal Drive access) — swap the env block for a different auth method — see Authentication.

Before the first connection, log in once from a terminal with the same paths: CREDENTIALS_PATH=... TOKEN_PATH=... uv run --directory /path/to/mcp-gee-sweet mcp-gee-sweet auth. A stdio server with no token doesn't open a browser itself. It starts without Google access, and its first tool call offers you the Google consent link, or you can run this command and retry (see Re-authorizing from the client).

docs.title: SSE — Docker
docs.text:
The container serves over the network interface, so it needs a bearer token (see HTTP transport authentication). Put MCP_SERVER_TOKEN=<token> in a .env file next to docker-compose.yml, start the server (make start), then point Claude Desktop at the SSE endpoint with the same token:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mcp-gee-sweet": {
      "transport": "sse",
      "url": "http://localhost:47000/sse",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer <token>"
      }
    }
  }
}

For Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport sse mcp-gee-sweet http://localhost:47000/sse --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

docs.title: Claude Code (this project's own MCP config)
docs.text: The project runs two instances — one OAuth, one service account — defined in .mcp.json at the repo root. Claude Code picks these up automatically when you open the project.

docs.title: Tool filtering in client config
docs.text:
To restrict tools at the client level, pass --include-tools as a CLI arg:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mcp-gee-sweet": {
      "command": "uv",
      "args": [
        "run", "--directory", "/path/to/mcp-gee-sweet",
        "mcp-gee-sweet",
        "--include-tools", "get_sheet_data,update_cells,list_sheets,list_spreadsheets"
      ],
      "env": {
        "CREDENTIALS_PATH": "/path/to/credentials.json",
        "TOKEN_PATH": "/path/to/token.json"
      }
    }
  }
}

See Configuration for suggested subsets.

docs.title: Clients with a tool limit
docs.text:
Several MCP clients cap how many tools they accept, and with every tool registered the server is over each of these caps:

Client Limit What happens over it VS Code + GitHub Copilot (agent mode) 128 tools per request, VS Code's built-in tools included (docs) The request fails with "Cannot have more than 128 tools per request" Windsurf 100 tools in total, across every server (docs) Not documented Cursor Depends on the model (older builds capped it at 40) "Too many MCP tools are enabled for this mode", or only part of the tool list is used Google Antigravity 100 tools per server (user report) The server is rejected

The fix is the same everywhere: set ENABLED_TOOLS to one of the suggested subsets, each of which is under 100 tools, or to your own list. You can join two subsets with a comma, like the Docs + Drive example there, as long as the total stays under your client's limit. On Windsurf, leave room for your other servers' tools too.

The snippets below use the Read-only Sheets subset with the PyPI install (uvx); swap in the list you want. For a cloned repo, use the uv run --directory command from Claude Desktop instead. --include-tools <list> at the end of args works too, in place of the ENABLED_TOOLS entry.

docs.title: VS Code + GitHub Copilot
docs.text:
In .vscode/mcp.json (workspace) or your user-profile mcp.json. VS Code's format uses a top-level servers key (reference):

{
  "servers": {
    "mcp-gee-sweet": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["mcp-gee-sweet"],
      "env": {
        "CREDENTIALS_PATH": "/path/to/credentials.json",
        "TOKEN_PATH": "/path/to/token.json",
        "ENABLED_TOOLS": "get_sheet_data,get_sheet_formulas,get_multiple_sheet_data,get_multiple_spreadsheet_summary,find_in_spreadsheet,list_sheets,list_spreadsheets"
      }
    }
  }
}

The 128 includes VS Code's own tools and every other server's, so a subset near 100 can still go over it with other servers enabled. You can also deselect tools or whole servers in the chat view's tools picker. That choice is saved in your VS Code profile, while ENABLED_TOOLS travels with the server config.

docs.title: Cursor
docs.text:
In .cursor/mcp.json (project) or ~/.cursor/mcp.json (global):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mcp-gee-sweet": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["mcp-gee-sweet"],
      "env": {
        "CREDENTIALS_PATH": "/path/to/credentials.json",
        "TOKEN_PATH": "/path/to/token.json",
        "ENABLED_TOOLS": "get_sheet_data,get_sheet_formulas,get_multiple_sheet_data,get_multiple_spreadsheet_summary,find_in_spreadsheet,list_sheets,list_spreadsheets"
      }
    }
  }
}

Cursor doesn't publish its per-model caps. If you still see "Too many MCP tools", use a smaller subset or switch to a model that allows more tools.

docs.title: Windsurf
docs.text:
In Windsurf's mcp_config.json (its location per platform is in Windsurf's MCP docs):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mcp-gee-sweet": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["mcp-gee-sweet"],
      "env": {
        "CREDENTIALS_PATH": "/path/to/credentials.json",
        "TOKEN_PATH": "/path/to/token.json",
        "ENABLED_TOOLS": "get_sheet_data,get_sheet_formulas,get_multiple_sheet_data,get_multiple_spreadsheet_summary,find_in_spreadsheet,list_sheets,list_spreadsheets"
      }
    }
  }
}

Windsurf's 100 counts the tools from every server you have enabled. Windsurf also has a per-server disabledTools array, but it lists the tools to hide, so with this server you'd be naming most of them. ENABLED_TOOLS names the ones to keep.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Description Default AUTH_METHOD Pin auth to one method: oauth, service_account, adc waterfall SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH Path to service account JSON key — GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS Google's standard service account path (feeds ADC) — DRIVE_FOLDER_ID Default Drive folder for service account operations — CREDENTIALS_PATH Path to OAuth client ID JSON credentials.json TOKEN_PATH Path to store the OAuth refresh token token.json OAUTH_CONSENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS SSE only: how long the server waits for the browser consent when there's no usable OAuth token, before starting without Google access. See Authentication 300 CREDENTIALS_CONFIG Base64-encoded credentials JSON (for containers) — ENABLED_TOOLS Comma-separated list of tool names to register all tools LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS Which local files tools may read and write: full, roots, or off. See Local file access full under stdio, off under SSE and streamable HTTP LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS With LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=roots, the directories tools may use, separated by : (; on Windows), like PATH — CACHE_DB_PATH Path to the SQLite cache database (:memory: for none) mcp-gee-sweet/cache.db in the user's cache directory (see Caching) CACHE_TTL Cache time-to-live in seconds. Also adjustable at runtime via the set_cache_ttl tool, no restart needed 1800 (30 min) CACHE_VALIDATE_MODIFIED_TIME Validate sheet/doc cache hits against Drive's modifiedTime before serving them, catching edits from other sessions without waiting out the TTL. Costs one extra Drive API call per cache lookup true MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_CHARS Safety cap on response size, in characters, for tools that can return large inline payloads (get_sheet_data, get_multiple_sheet_data, get_multiple_spreadsheet_summary, find_in_spreadsheet, get_doc_content, find_in_doc, list_doc_comments, list_file_activity, export_file, sync_folder, list_all_events, list_calendar_acl, get_message, get_thread). Defense-in-depth against MCP clients that don't degrade gracefully on an oversized tool response — see decision-response-size-cap-reevaluation-519.md for why the default was raised and what it does and doesn't protect against 1000000 LIST_ALL_EVENTS_MAX_CONCURRENCY Most calendars list_all_events queries at once, shared across every concurrent list_all_events call on the server, to stay under the Calendar API's per-user rate limit. Raise it for faster fan-out on accounts subscribed to many calendars; lower it for a stricter rate-limit posture. Values below 1 are treated as 1 20 HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS How long one socket operation of a Google API request (connecting, sending, or waiting for data) may block before the request fails. It applies per operation, not to the whole request: a long download or upload that keeps moving data never hits it. A read that times out is retried once on a new connection; a write isn't, and its error says it may still have been applied. Raise it if Google legitimately takes longer than this to start answering a request, such as a very large export or batchUpdate. An invalid or non-positive value logs a warning and uses the default; a value over one day (86400), inf included, logs a warning and uses one day. See decision-http-socket-timeout.md 60 GMAIL_SEND How send_message, reply_to_message and send_draft deliver mail: confirm or direct. An unrecognized value logs a warning and uses confirm. See Gmail sending confirm GMAIL_SEND_WARN_RECIPIENTS Flag a send whose unique To, Cc and Bcc addresses number more than this. An invalid or negative value logs a warning and uses the default. See Gmail sending 10 HOST (or FASTMCP_HOST) Bind address for the SSE and streamable HTTP transports. FASTMCP_HOST is a fallback if HOST isn't set. Any address other than loopback needs MCP_SERVER_TOKEN. See HTTP transport authentication 127.0.0.1 PORT (or FASTMCP_PORT) Port for the SSE and streamable HTTP transports. FASTMCP_PORT is a fallback if PORT isn't set 8000 MCP_SERVER_TOKEN Bearer token every SSE and streamable HTTP request must send. See HTTP transport authentication — ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP 1 or true lets a non-loopback HOST serve with no token, for a deployment behind an authenticating reverse proxy. Ignored when MCP_SERVER_TOKEN is set — DEBUG_LEVEL Logging level: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR — controls package and access logs — LOG_FILE Write server logs to this file path (requires DEBUG_LEVEL) — ACCESS_LOG_FILE Write tool access logs to this file path (requires DEBUG_LEVEL) —

See Authentication for auth-specific variable details.

docs.title: .env file
docs.text:
The server loads src/mcp_gee_sweet/.env at startup (before any environment variables are read), so you can configure it without shell exports or MCP client config changes. A template with all available variables is at src/mcp_gee_sweet/.env.template — copy it to .env and uncomment what you need.

Environment variables set by the OS or the MCP client always take precedence over .env.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
By default the server logs warnings and above to stderr. Set DEBUG_LEVEL to enable richer output — it controls both the package logger and uvicorn HTTP access logs with a single value.

# src/mcp_gee_sweet/.env
DEBUG_LEVEL=DEBUG   # DEBUG | INFO | WARNING | ERROR

Every tool call emits a single access log line at INFO level to the mcp_gee_sweet.access logger:

2026-06-23 22:45:19 INFO mcp_gee_sweet.access "127.0.0.1" "claude-code/1.x" "TOOL list_recent_files" 200 0.475s

IP and user agent are populated from the HTTP request in SSE mode; they fall back to - in stdio mode.

Docker (make logs): DEBUG_LEVEL=DEBUG is the default in docker-compose.yml. Server logs, tool access lines, and uvicorn HTTP access logs all write to stderr; Docker captures everything in make logs.

stdio (OAuth server via Claude Code): stderr is dropped by the host. Set LOG_FILE to capture all output — server debug lines and access log lines are mixed in the same file, differentiated by logger name (mcp_gee_sweet.server vs mcp_gee_sweet.access). Set ACCESS_LOG_FILE to also write access lines to a separate file.

DEBUG_LEVEL=DEBUG
LOG_FILE=/tmp/mcp-gee-sweet.log
ACCESS_LOG_FILE=/tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-access.log   # optional, access-only view

make dev-logs      # tail mixed server + access logs
make access-logs   # tail access lines only (requires ACCESS_LOG_FILE)

Access logs are emitted at INFO level — they appear when DEBUG_LEVEL is DEBUG or INFO and are suppressed at WARNING or above.

Claude Desktop: logs are written automatically to ~/Library/Logs/Claude/mcp-server-<name>.log — no extra configuration needed.

docs.title: Tool filtering
docs.text:
By default all 143 tools are registered. Use ENABLED_TOOLS (or --include-tools on the CLI) to restrict the server to exactly the tools you need. This reduces the AI's context window cost — each registered tool is a name the model must reason about on every call.

# Environment variable
ENABLED_TOOLS=get_sheet_data,update_cells,list_spreadsheets,list_sheets

# CLI flag
uv run mcp-gee-sweet --include-tools get_sheet_data,update_cells,list_spreadsheets

If neither is set, all tools are registered.

docs.title: Suggested subsets
docs.text:
Some MCP clients cap how many tools they accept, and the full tool set is over every cap: VS Code with GitHub Copilot allows 128 tools per request, built-in tools included; Windsurf allows 100 across all servers; Cursor's cap depends on the model. On those clients, pick one of these subsets. Each one is under 100 tools. See Clients with a tool limit for each client's config.

To combine two subsets, join their lists with a comma (a name listed twice is fine) and add up the counts to check you're still under your client's limit. Windsurf's 100 also counts every other server's tools.
