docs.title: HTTP transport authentication
docs.text:
Under --transport sse or --transport streamable-http, the server listens on 127.0.0.1 by default, so only this machine can reach it. stdio is unaffected by everything in this section.

To serve on any other address (HOST=0.0.0.0, a LAN address, a hostname), set MCP_SERVER_TOKEN to a long random value, for example from python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))". Every request must then send it:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

A request with a missing or wrong token gets 401 Unauthorized with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, the same response either way. The server logs the client address and path of each rejected request, and never logs the token or the Authorization header. A token set on a loopback HOST is enforced there too.

Refusing to start. The server stops at startup, before it serves, with a one-line message naming the setting to fix when:

  • HOST isn't a loopback address (127.0.0.0/8, ::1, or localhost) and MCP_SERVER_TOKEN is unset or empty, or
  • ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP is set to anything other than 1 or true.

mcp-gee-sweet auth still runs either way.

With no token, the server still fails closed per request, however it was launched (uvicorn mcp_gee_sweet.server:app directly included). It serves a request only when the connection arrived on a loopback address and its Host header is localhost or a loopback IP such as 127.0.0.1 or [::1] (with or without a port), or, on a non-loopback HOST, when ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP is 1 or true. Everything else gets the same 401. The Host check stops a web page from reaching a local server through DNS rebinding. The first such rejection is logged as a warning naming MCP_SERVER_TOKEN, and later ones only at DEBUG.

Behind an authenticating reverse proxy, set ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP=1 to serve a non-loopback HOST without a token. The server then accepts every request it receives, so make sure only the proxy can reach it. It also has no DNS-rebinding protection on a non-loopback HOST. The setting does nothing on a loopback HOST, and is ignored, with a warning, when MCP_SERVER_TOKEN is set.

A proxy forwarding to a loopback HOST, with or without a token, must pass Host as localhost or 127.0.0.1 (with the port). mcp checks the Host and Origin headers itself when HOST is 127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1, and answers anything else with 421 Invalid Host header; with no token, the server also answers 401 to a Host that isn't localhost or a loopback IP.

Docker. The image sets HOST=0.0.0.0 so a published port reaches the server, so a container needs MCP_SERVER_TOKEN:

docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 \
  -e MCP_SERVER_TOKEN=<token> \
  -e CREDENTIALS_CONFIG=<base64> \
  mcp-gee-sweet

docker-compose.yml reads MCP_SERVER_TOKEN from a .env file next to it, falling back to src/mcp_gee_sweet/.env when that one doesn't set it, and publishes port 47000 on 127.0.0.1 only. See Client Setup for the matching client config.

A token doesn't change local file access: an HTTP transport still defaults to off.

docs.title: Local file access
docs.text:
Some tools read or write files on the machine the server runs on: uploads, downloads, sync_folder, create_doc_from_file, Gmail attachments, local images in Markdown, and the local_path destination that large results can be written to. LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS decides which files they may use:

Mode What tools may use full Any local path the server process can open roots Only paths under a directory listed in LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS. Paths are resolved first, symlinks included, so a link inside a root that points outside it is refused off No local files

Default: full under stdio, where the caller is the person running the server, and off under SSE and streamable HTTP, where it may not be. A network-facing server that should use local files needs LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS set explicitly.

Always refused, in every mode: the server's own credential, config, cache, and log files. That's CREDENTIALS_PATH, TOKEN_PATH, SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, gcloud's default ADC file, src/mcp_gee_sweet/.env, CACHE_DB_PATH (and its -wal/-shm files; with the default location, the whole mcp-gee-sweet cache directory), the pre-0.9.3 cache /tmp/mcp_gee_sweet.db (and its -wal/-shm files), LOG_FILE, and ACCESS_LOG_FILE. A file is matched by identity, so a hardlink or a differently cased path to one of them is refused too.

In off mode these tools aren't registered, since they can only work on local files: upload_local_file, upload_local_folder, download_file, download_folder, sync_folder, import_csv_to_sheet, create_doc_from_file, update_doc_from_file, and insert_local_images. Tools with an optional local path stay registered and return an error if one is used. That covers local_path on large-result tools, Gmail's attachments[].local_path (content_base64 still works), and local image paths in create_doc/write_doc_content content, which fail per image while the doc is still written.

During a folder walk (upload_local_folder, download_folder, sync_folder), each file and subfolder is checked, not just the top directory. A refused entry is listed under failed, and the rest of the walk continues.

server://auth-status reports the active policy under local_file_access: its mode, whether it was set explicitly, the roots in roots mode, and the unregistered_tools that off mode left out.

Docker example, with the host's ./data directory as the only one tools may use:

docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 \
  -v "$PWD/data:/data" \
  -e MCP_SERVER_TOKEN=<token> \
  -e LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=roots \
  -e LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS=/data \
  -e CREDENTIALS_CONFIG=<base64> \
  mcp-gee-sweet

An invalid LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS value, roots mode without LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS, or a root that isn't an existing directory stops the server at startup, before it serves. mcp-gee-sweet auth still runs, so a root that isn't mounted yet doesn't block re-authorization. Design: local-file-access-policy.md.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text:
The server caches responses in a local SQLite database to reduce API calls and latency. Five namespaces are cached: sheet structure, sheet data, Drive folder listings, doc content, and calendar metadata.

  • TTL-based expiry: controlled by CACHE_TTL (default 30 minutes); change it at runtime with the set_cache_ttl tool instead of restarting the server
  • Dirty invalidation: write operations mark the relevant cache entries stale immediately
  • Change-based invalidation: for sheet structure/data and doc content (the namespaces keyed by a single Drive file), a cache hit is checked against that file's live modifiedTime before being served — an edit from another session or tab invalidates the entry immediately instead of waiting out the TTL. Controlled by CACHE_VALIDATE_MODIFIED_TIME (default true); disable it if the extra Drive API call per lookup isn't worth the freshness guarantee for your usage pattern. Not applied to Drive folder listings (a folder's own modifiedTime doesn't change when its children do) or calendar metadata (no comparable field via the Calendar API)
  • Scoped flush: refresh_cache accepts a spreadsheet_id, doc_id, folder_id, or calendar_id to invalidate only that resource; omit all params to flush everything

The DB lives in the user's own cache directory by default: ~/.cache/mcp-gee-sweet/cache.db on Linux (or under an absolute $XDG_CACHE_HOME), ~/Library/Caches/mcp-gee-sweet/cache.db on macOS, and %LOCALAPPDATA%\mcp-gee-sweet\cache.db on Windows. In the Docker image that's /root/.cache/mcp-gee-sweet/cache.db. Set CACHE_DB_PATH to use another file (an empty value counts as unset), for example one on a volume so the cache survives container restarts, or :memory: for no file at all.

The cache directory is created owner-only (0700) and the DB and its -wal/-shm files are 0600; an existing default directory with looser permissions is tightened. An explicit CACHE_DB_PATH's files get the same 0600, but its directory is left as it is. A cache directory or file owned by another user, or a symlink in place of one, isn't used: the server warns and caches in memory instead. The same happens when there's no home directory to put the cache in, e.g. a container run with --user and no home.

Each entry is stored under the Google identity it was fetched as (the account's Drive permission ID, or a service account's email when Drive can't say), so two accounts sharing one DB file never see each other's entries. Invalidation isn't per identity: refresh_cache and a write's invalidation reach every identity's copy. Until the server has read the identity (at connection start, retried on every tool call), nothing is cached. A cached sheet list is served stale only when Google couldn't answer (a 5xx, a 429, or a network failure), never in place of a refusal such as a 403 or 404.

Versions up to 0.9.2 kept the cache in /tmp/mcp_gee_sweet.db, readable by every local user. The server never reads that file again; on start-up with CACHE_DB_PATH unset it makes the file owner-only if it's yours, but doesn't delete it. Delete /tmp/mcp_gee_sweet.db and its -wal/-shm files yourself.

docs.title: Gmail sending
docs.text:
By default (GMAIL_SEND=confirm) no email goes out on the agent's call alone:

  • send_message and reply_to_message first save the message as a Gmail draft. A reply draft goes in the original thread.
  • If the MCP client can show a form, the server asks the user to confirm. The form shows any recipient flags (below) first, then the From address, every recipient grouped by To, Cc and Bcc, the subject, the attachment names, and the first 500 characters of the body, with its full length. When the email has an HTML part that most mail apps show instead, its text is shown too. That text is an approximation of what a mail app renders: it errs toward showing more (for example, the content of Outlook-only conditional comments), not less. Body text is marked off line by line, so it can't pass for the form's own lines. The form is built from the draft as Gmail stores it.
  • Only an explicit yes sends the draft. Declining, cancelling, no answer within 10 minutes, or a failed request leaves the draft unsent. The tool then returns sent: false, a reason, the draft_id, and a note saying the email is waiting in Gmail's Drafts folder, where the user can review and send it.
  • If the client can't show a form, nothing is sent: send_message and reply_to_message return the held draft, and send_draft refuses.
  • A draft changed after the user confirmed it (for example by update_draft) isn't sent, since it's no longer what the user saw.

Confirmation needs a client that connects with the 2025-11-25 initialize handshake and supports form elicitation. On a 2026-07-28 connection the server has no way to ask, so mail always stays a draft there (#1235).

Claude Code currently connects on 2026-07-28 (2.1.310, checked 2026-10-26). So under confirm, every send from Claude Code is held as a draft: send_message and reply_to_message return sent: false, and send_draft refuses. Send the drafts from Gmail's Drafts folder, or set GMAIL_SEND=direct to send at once.

A client hook that auto-accepts elicitations with a yes makes confirm behave like direct. The server can't tell a hook's answer from the user's.

GMAIL_SEND=direct restores immediate delivery for all three tools, with no draft step and no confirmation. Their only guard is then destructiveHint, which clients treat as a hint and skip once a tool is auto-approved.

Recipient flags. Every send under confirm reports these in the confirmation and in the result's recipient_flags:

Flag When outside_organization Google Workspace accounts only: a recipient whose domain isn't the account's own domain or one of its send-as alias domains. A consumer alias domain (gmail.com, googlemail.com) doesn't count, so a personal Gmail alias doesn't hide the flag for Gmail recipients. Matching is exact, so sub.example.com counts as outside example.com. Never shown on consumer accounts outside_organization_unchecked The server couldn't look up the mailbox's own address, so the check above didn't run many_recipients More than GMAIL_SEND_WARN_RECIPIENTS unique addresses across To, Cc and Bcc hidden_recipients Any Bcc, with the count

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text: This document is the living reference for how mcp-gee-sweet is designed and how design decisions get made. It is updated as the project's thinking evolves. For the historical reasoning behind specific decisions, see the Decision Log. For code-level convention — module size, test structure, linting — see the Style Guide.

docs.title: What This Server Is
docs.text: An MCP server for Google Workspace. Its job is to give an AI client reliable, direct access to Google APIs that the client cannot call itself. Every tool added to this server is a named entry in a flat list that the AI must reason about — more tools means more noise, not more capability.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The server covers Google Workspace productivity tools — the suite a person uses to write, organise, communicate, and schedule. The line is drawn at Google Cloud infrastructure and analytics, which are a different product category serving a different purpose.

In scope Out of scope Google Sheets BigQuery / BigTable Google Docs Google Analytics Google Drive Google Cloud Storage (raw GCS) Google Calendar Compute Engine / GKE / GCE Google Slides Maps / Places Google Forms Pub/Sub / Dataflow Gmail Any non-Google service Google Tasks / Keep General local file system ops Google Chat

Not all in-scope services need to be implemented — the table above is the ceiling, not a commitment. Priority follows actual use. Adding a new Workspace service requires a decision record in docs/decisions/ explaining the use case and estimated tool count cost.

docs.title: Adding a Tool — The Inclusion Test
docs.text:
A tool belongs here if it passes all three gates:

  1. Requires Google API access — the operation calls a Google API (Sheets, Drive, Docs, Calendar, Gmail). Tools that only manipulate local data or do pure computation don't belong here.

  2. Not already coverable — the operation is not already expressible via an existing tool, including the batch_update passthrough, which is the intended escape hatch for raw Sheets API operations.

  3. Atomic or justified composite — the operation is a single logical action, OR it is a multi-step chain where Claude fails or requires retries without a server-side wrapper. See When to Build a Composite below.

docs.title: What doesn't belong
docs.text:
• Simple sequential chains — if a workflow is two predictable API calls in order, Claude handles the primitives. A wrapper adds surface area and a duplicate name the AI has to disambiguate.
  • Convenience aliases — re-exposing an existing tool with different defaults is not a new tool.
  • Speculative features — tools added because they might be useful someday. The roadmap tracks candidates; they stay there until there is a real use case.
  • Non-Google operations — format conversion, local file transforms, computation. These belong in the client or a separate server.

docs.title: Tool count as a cost
docs.text: The tool list is flat. The AI sees every registered tool on every call. Each additional tool increases the chance of the AI picking the wrong one, makes descriptions harder to keep distinct, and adds a parameter schema the AI has to reason about. Prefer depth over breadth — a well-parameterised export_file that handles PDF, DOCX, HTML, and XLSX is better than four separate export tools.

docs.title: The batch_update rule
docs.text: If an operation can be expressed as a raw Sheets batchUpdate request, it does not automatically need a named tool. A named tool is warranted when the operation is common enough that spelling out the raw request every time is unreasonable.

docs.title: When to Build a Composite
docs.text:
The default position is that the AI client chains atomic tools. Server-side composite tools are built only when intermediate steps are fiddly enough that Claude will fail or require retries in normal use. The test: would a developer write a helper script to avoid doing this by hand?

Three failure modes justify a server-side wrapper, based on observed usage:

  1. Binary data handling — tools that return base64-encoded content (XLSX exports, PDF exports, image downloads) require a decode step that Claude handles inconsistently. A server-side tool that handles decode and local write once is more reliable than Claude doing it on every call.

  2. Pagination loops — bulk operations over a folder or large file list require correctly following nextPageToken. Claude can do this but will occasionally stop at the first page or loop incorrectly under load.

  3. Data encoding decisions in transformation chains — operations like sheet_to_doc involve choices about how to encode tables, handle formatting, and structure output that benefit from a consistent server-side implementation.

For everything else, the right investment is clear tool docstrings that describe when and how to combine the primitives — not a new tool.

See Decision: Composite Tool Policy for the full case analysis and the specific tools approved or ruled out at the time this policy was established.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Unit tests (tests/test_tools.py) cover helpers, HTML conversion, tool filtering, A1 notation parsing, and cache TTL/invalidation logic. These run in CI on every push and PR.

AI-directed manual verification is the primary QA method for tool correctness. Test cases are natural language prompts paired with explicit check lists (docs/qa/tests/). A Claude session connected to the live server executes the prompts, evaluates results against the checks, and saves a results report. Tests run against the real Google APIs under real conditions — the same environment as production.

Automated integration tests against live Google APIs were evaluated and deferred. The setup cost (managed credentials, fixture maintenance, API quota, test flakiness) does not pay off at current scale. See Decision: Testing Approach for the full rationale and the conditions under which this should be revisited.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text: Constraints imposed by the Google Docs/Drive/Sheets APIs or by current implementation scope. Each entry describes what the limitation is, why it exists, and the available workaround (if any).

docs.title: Blank paragraph before every table
docs.text:
What: A blank paragraph always appears in the document structure immediately before each table, even when none was written in the source HTML/Markdown.

Why: insertTable is a structural Docs API operation that requires at least one paragraph before the table. When phase-1 insertText is used to write document content, it displaces the document's initial empty paragraph to the position just before the table. Attempting to remove this paragraph via deleteContentRange is rejected by the API ("Invalid deletion range") because the paragraph is a required structural element — even though the Google Docs UI allows the equivalent manual deletion.

Workaround: The emitter collapses the blank paragraph to zero visual height using updateParagraphStyle (spaceAbove/spaceBelow = 0, lineSpacing = 1) and updateTextStyle (fontSize = 1pt). The paragraph remains in the document structure but is invisible in the rendered output. The one exception is a paragraph between two tables: it keeps its height, as the blank line that keeps the tables from touching and reading as one (#1098). Every such paragraph is also reset to plain NORMAL_TEXT, with no bullet, indent, or border (#1097). Related: #190.

docs.title: get_doc_structure — top-level body elements only
docs.text:
What: get_doc_structure reports elements in the document body at the top level only. Content inside nested table cells (tables within table cells) is not exposed.

Why: The tool walks the body content array one level deep. Deeply nested structures require recursive traversal that is not currently implemented.

Workaround: For inspecting nested cell content, fetch the raw document via the Docs API documents.get endpoint (accessible via batch_update passthrough or by reading the raw API response). Related: #133.

docs.title: Nested tables not supported via Markdown input
docs.text:
What: Markdown content passed to create_doc/write_doc_content (content_format='markdown') or create_doc_from_file (.md files) cannot produce a nested table — a table inside a table cell.

Why: GFM's pipe-table syntax has no way to write a table inside another table's cell.

Workaround: Supply raw HTML instead — the HTML→AST pipeline fully supports nested tables (see #109). Related: docs/qa/tests/docs_content.md TC-DOC51.

docs.title: Markdown input doesn't read footnotes, definition lists, or other Python-Markdown extra syntax
docs.text:
What: Markdown passed to create_doc/write_doc_content (content_format='markdown'), create_doc_from_file/update_doc_from_file, or upload_file(source_format='markdown') is read as CommonMark plus GitHub-flavored Markdown (tables, strikethrough, task lists, autolinks). These constructs from Python-Markdown's extra extension aren't part of that:

  • Footnotes: Text[^1] and [^1]: …. A note written as prose ([^1]: This is the note.) stays literal text, both the [^1] marker and the note line. A note of a single word or URL ([^1]: note) is a valid CommonMark link reference definition instead, so the note line disappears and the marker shows as ^1. It's linked when the note is a URL; otherwise the link is dropped (no scheme, #1120) and reported in dropped_links.

These come out as literal text:

  • Definition lists: Term followed by : definition.
  • Abbreviations: *[HTML]: Hyper Text Markup Language.
  • Attribute lists: {#id} or {.class} after a heading or paragraph.
  • Markdown inside an HTML block marked markdown="1"; the block's contents stay as written.

Why: upload_file converted with Python-Markdown extra until #1102 moved it onto this server's CommonMark/GFM converter, which the Docs tools already used. They never read these constructs.

Workaround: Write a footnote as an inline parenthetical or a "Notes" list at the end (creating real Docs footnotes is #149), a definition list as **Term**: definition lines, and put HTML that needs Markdown inside it as HTML instead.

docs.title: get_doc_as_markdown exports a table or quote that ends a list's last item outside the list
docs.text:
What: A table inside a list's last item (1. a | x | |---| ) is written to the Doc indented under the item, but get_doc_as_markdown exports it at the margin, after the list. A quote that ends a list's last item (- a > q ) exports as a deeper quote at the margin (> > q). So does a paragraph, code block, heading, or rule inside the last item of a quoted list (> - a > > b exports b as > > b). Any of these exports inside its item when the list goes on after it: a later item of the list, a sublist nested under the item (of either type), or a paragraph indented in the item. A paragraph, code block, or heading inside an item of an unquoted list always exports inside it.

Why: The export finds a block inside an item from its indent (#1302). A table's indent isn't reported anywhere in the Docs API: the JSON of a table inside an item matches one at the margin (checked live). A quote's is, but a quote inside an item sits exactly where a deeper quote at the margin would (a quote in a top-level item is at 72pt, like a margin > >), so the indent can't tell them apart. A block inside a quoted list's item is written the same way, at the item's text indent plus the quote's and with the quote's border, which is exactly where a deeper quote at the margin goes. Such a block counts as inside an item only when the list goes on after it, which it never does after a list's last item. Reading an ambiguous quote as the margin quote keeps every quote level; reading it into the item would drop one.

Workaround: None in the export. Indent the table or quote under its item by hand in the exported Markdown. Related: docs/qa/tests/docs_content.md TC-DOC244.

docs.title: A list inside a blockquote draws its own quote bar, offset from the quote's
docs.text:
What: In Markdown or HTML content written to a Doc, a list inside a blockquote shows its gray left bar at the list item's indent, not at the quote's. A quote that mixes paragraphs and list items therefore shows two bars, the items' sitting to the right of the paragraphs'. For example, create_doc(content="> quote text > > - item ", content_format="markdown") gives "quote text" a bar at the quote indent and "item" a second bar further right. The same mechanism puts a nested item's bar at its own, deeper indent. Reading the Doc back with get_doc_as_markdown is unaffected: every item comes back at its correct quote depth.

Why: Docs has no blockquote style, so a quoted paragraph gets a left border and an indent. Docs draws a paragraph's borderLeft at its indentStart, and there's no separate setting for where the border goes. A list item needs its own indentStart too, past the quote's: it's where the item's wrapped lines start, under the text rather than under the bullet. Setting a quoted item's indentStart to the quote indent does join the two bars, but then every wrapped line lands left of the item's bullet and nested items lose their indent after the first line. One paragraph can't have both the quote's bar position and a list's hanging indent, so the offset bar is the lesser problem.

Workaround: None that keeps a real list. To get one continuous bar, keep the list outside the quote, or write each item as its own quoted paragraph starting with a bullet character, which isn't a Markdown list marker: > • one > > • two . Keep the blank > line between items, or the lines join into one paragraph. Decided in #1242.

docs.title: A horizontal rule is a bordered paragraph, not a Docs horizontal line
docs.text:
What: A Markdown thematic break (---, ***, ___) or an HTML <hr> written by create_doc, write_doc_content, create_doc_from_file, update_doc_from_file, or upload_file (Markdown source) appears as a thin gray line, but in Docs it's an empty paragraph with a bottom border (6pt, or 4pt inside a quote), not the element Insert > Horizontal line adds, so editing it in Docs behaves like editing a paragraph. Inside a quote the line sits closer to the text below it than to the text above: space below it would break the quote bar. get_doc_as_markdown reads both kinds of line back as --- (*** when it's the document's first line, where --- would open front matter). A native line that shares a list item's paragraph but comes before its text exports at the margin, ending the list there. An <hr> inside a table cell is dropped: a cell holds no paragraph styling the converter writes (#1327).

Why: The Docs API has no request that inserts a horizontal line (#1096).

Workaround: For a native line, use Insert > Horizontal line in the Docs UI, or convert the file with upload_local_file(convert=True), whose Drive import draws native lines (with the other differences listed under Google Drive below).

docs.title: create_bookmark doesn't create a bookmark Docs lists
docs.text:
What: create_bookmark creates a one-character named range. It doesn't appear under Insert > Link > "Headings, bookmarks, and tabs", and no link can point to it.

Why: The Docs API has no request that creates a bookmark; only the Docs UI can.

Workaround: Link to a heading instead: every heading has a headingId (get_doc_structure) that a link can target. Tracked in #1076.

docs.title: get_doc_as_markdown — nested tables, temporary image URLs, and inline-vs-block code ambiguity
docs.text:
What: get_doc_as_markdown (#300) has three read-side gaps, each rooted in a genuine Markdown-format or Docs-API constraint rather than missing implementation:

  1. A table nested inside another table's cell has no Markdown table syntax to express — the mirror image of the write-side limitation above. That cell renders a placeholder note (*(nested table omitted...)*) instead.
  2. An inline image resolves to Drive's temporary contentUri, which expires (roughly 30 minutes). The exported Markdown's ![alt](url) links go stale if consumed well after generation.
  3. Both inline code (`x`) and a fenced code block (```...```) are written to the Docs API identically — a run (or every run in a paragraph) with font_family="Courier New" — see docs/design/markdown-support.md's mapping table. There is no other marker to tell them apart on read. get_doc_as_markdown treats a paragraph as a fenced block only when every run in it is code-styled; a paragraph containing nothing but a single inline code span (no surrounding text) is indistinguishable from a one-line code block and renders as a fenced block either way. An all-code paragraph with a linked run renders as inline code spans instead, since a fenced block can't carry a link.

Why: (1) and (3) are Docs-representation-level ambiguities, not gaps in this tool's traversal; (2) is inherent to how Drive serves inline image bytes.

Workaround: For full fidelity on any of these three cases, use get_doc_structure (or the raw Docs API via batch_update passthrough) instead. Related: docs/design/doc-to-markdown.md.

docs.title: export_revision on a Google Doc — links, images, and vanishing revision IDs
docs.text:
What: export_revision (#959) returns a Doc revision as Markdown through the same converter as get_doc_as_markdown, with these differences and gaps:

  1. A link to a heading renders as a GitHub-style #slug anchor, not as a docs.google.com URL. A link to a bookmark, or to a heading that doesn't render as one (a bulleted heading, or one in a table cell), is dropped and leaves its text. An image renders as image:sha256-<hash>, with no viewable URL: the temporary Doc's image URLs stop working once it's deleted, so an old revision's images can't be viewed this way.
  2. The export doesn't include comments, which aren't part of a revision.
  3. A revision ID from list_revisions can stop existing: Docs folds a recent revision into the next one while editing continues (measured: edits 90 seconds and 5 minutes later both merged it). The export then fails with an error saying to list revisions again.
  4. Each call creates and removes a temporary Google Doc holding the revision's full content, which takes several seconds. A user identity (OAuth, or ADC with user credentials) creates it in My Drive root, not shared with anyone. That needs room in My Drive and permission to create files there, even when DRIVE_FOLDER_ID is a Shared Drive with room: a full My Drive, or a Workspace policy that blocks creating files in My Drive, makes the export fail. A service account has no My Drive storage, so it uses the default folder, which must be a Shared Drive. The source Doc's own sharing doesn't limit who can see that copy:
  5. Every member of the Shared Drive can open it while the export runs, including the image downloads.
  6. A Content manager can only trash it, not delete it, so it stays in the Shared Drive's trash for 30 days, where the drive's managers can see it.
  7. If removal fails, the copy stays live, and the result's warning names the Doc to delete by hand.

Why: The Docs API reads only a document's current state, so the revision is exported as DOCX and imported into a temporary Doc to be read. That Doc's ID, heading IDs, and image URLs are new on every import, so (1) replaces them with values that stay the same between exports and keep diffs clean. A bookmark has no text to make a stable anchor from, and an invented one could be matched to the wrong heading if the Markdown is written back. (3) is how Drive keeps Docs revision history. (4) follows from that import: a service account can create files only in a Shared Drive, and member access there is inherited, so the copy's permissions can't be narrowed.

Workaround: For (1), diff one revision's export against another's, not against get_doc_as_markdown output. For (3), export a revision only after editing has settled. For (4), when a revision's content shouldn't reach the Shared Drive's members, export it with a user identity (OAuth), or point DRIVE_FOLDER_ID at a Shared Drive whose membership matches the source Doc's audience. Related: docs/design/doc-revision-export.md.

docs.title: Service account cannot create files in personal Drive
docs.text:
What: When authenticated as a service account (AUTH_METHOD=service_account), tools that create new files (create_doc, create_doc_from_file, create_spreadsheet) will fail with a permission error if the target folder is in a personal Google Drive.

Why: Service accounts have their own Drive storage quota separate from any user's personal Drive. They can only create files in shared drives or in folders explicitly shared with the service account.

Workaround: Manually create the file in Drive and share it with the service account, then use write_doc_content or update_cells to populate it. Alternatively, use OAuth authentication (AUTH_METHOD=oauth) which authenticates as the user and has full personal Drive access. Related: project memory service_account_limit.

docs.title: Converting .md on upload uses Drive's Markdown import, which renders differently
docs.text:
What: upload_local_file(convert=True), upload_local_folder(convert=True), and sync_folder(convert_markdown=True) hand a .md file to Drive's own Markdown importer. The Docs tools (create_doc, write_doc_content, create_doc_from_file, update_doc_from_file) use this server's converter instead. The same Markdown comes out differently:

  • Bullets use a - glyph at every level, not ● / ○ / ■.
  • Numbered lists use 1. numbering at every level, not a. / i. for nested levels. A 1) list keeps the ). A top-level item after a nested numbered sub-list can repeat the previous number (1, 2, 2).
  • Code blocks (fenced or indented) aren't monospace: each line becomes its own Arial paragraph, with paragraph spacing between lines.
  • Inline code is green monospace rather than Courier New, so get_doc_as_markdown reads it back as plain text, without backticks.
  • Blockquotes are indented but have no left border.
  • Task lists become native Docs checklists rather than ☐ / ☑ text. A numbered task list loses its numbers.
  • Sub-lists indented by 2 spaces under a numbered item don't nest; 3 or more spaces do.
  • Extra empty paragraphs appear around paragraphs, rules, lists, and tables. A table gets a visible empty line above it when it starts the document, and between it and a paragraph directly before it.
  • <del> and <mark> inline HTML isn't rendered as strikethrough or highlight.
  • Images with a local path or drive: source aren't embedded. Only this server's converter uploads and shares those.
  • www. links, bare (www.example.com) or written ([x](www.example.com)), point to http://. This server's converter gives both https:// (#1180, #1281).

Why: The rendering is Drive's, not this server's. These tools upload the file and set a Google Doc as the target type, and Drive's importer converts it. QA recorded the differences above in the #1044 Markdown baselines (docs/qa/results/2026-10-18-markdown.md, 2026-10-18-markdown-phase2.md, 2026-10-22-markdown-boundaries-state.md); the www. scheme in PR #1298's QA round 1. Routing these tools through this server's converter is a design question (#1113).

Workaround: For a single file, use create_doc_from_file, and update_doc_from_file to refresh it. They render .md the same way as the other Docs tools. There's no equivalent for a whole folder or for sync_folder's change tracking yet. Related: get_doc_as_markdown exports a Drive-imported list as blockquoted numbered items (#1104).

docs.title: sync_folder — renaming a long-named convert_markdown Doc in Drive unlinks it
docs.text:
What: sync_folder(convert_markdown=True) normally keeps matching a converted Doc to its local .md file even after the Doc is renamed in Drive. That doesn't hold for a .md filename longer than 103 UTF-8 bytes, .md included: 101+ ASCII characters, or 34+ CJK characters, before the .md. (Drive's 124-byte cap, minus the 21-byte geeSweetConvertSource key.) Names of 103 bytes or less still survive a rename. If a Doc converted from a longer name is renamed in Drive, the next sync no longer recognizes it. The local file then reads as "local only" and is uploaded again as a new Doc, and the renamed one is left as an ordinary, unrelated Doc.

Why: sync_folder records the source filename in a Drive custom property, and Drive caps each property's key + value at 124 bytes. A name too long to fit is stored as a sha256: digest, which can't be read back. The source name is then taken from the Doc's own display name, which keeps its .md suffix, and checked against the digest. After a rename, the two no longer agree (#805).

Workaround: Don't rename these Docs in Drive. To change the name, rename the local file and delete the old Doc in Drive; the next sync converts the file again under its new name. Renaming both sides to the same new name doesn't restore the link, because the digest still records the old name.

docs.title: sync_folder — a convert_markdown Doc edited in Drive needs a manual resolve
docs.text:
What: Once a converted Doc is edited in Drive, every sync_folder run reports it under conflicts, including after the local .md is edited too. Editing or touching the local file doesn't clear the conflict. Clearing it takes a call that names the Doc in resolve.

Why: There's no reverse conversion (Doc → Markdown), so the Drive edit can't be downloaded, and uploading the local file would overwrite it. sync_folder used to do that silently and now refuses (#814), so which side wins is the caller's choice.

Workaround: Name the Doc in resolve. The right choice depends on whether the local file has edits of its own:

  • Only the Doc was edited: copy the Drive edits into the local .md by hand, so the two match, then sync with resolve={"<name>": "keep_drive"}. Nothing in Drive changes.
  • Both were edited: merge the Drive edits into the local .md, then sync with resolve={"<name>": "keep_local"}, which uploads the merged file in place. Don't use keep_drive here. It records the local file as matching the Doc, so its own edits would never reach Drive.
  • To discard the Drive edit: sync with "keep_local" without merging. The edit stays in the Doc's version history.

Either way the Doc keeps its file ID, sharing, comments, and links. Preview the call with dry_run=True first.

docs.title: sync_folder — a convert_markdown Doc from before #814 can stay stuck in conflicts
docs.text:
What: A converted Doc created before #814 has none of the properties #814's change detection uses, so it stays on the old modifiedTime comparison until it's next re-uploaded. If Drive's late modifiedTime update overwrote its restamp (the bug #814 fixed), it reads as "Drive newer" and is reported under conflicts on every sync. A conflict never uploads, so it never picks up the properties that would fix it.

Why: Migrating such a Doc means choosing a baseline revision for it. While it reads as Drive newer, sync_folder can't tell a lagging timestamp from a real Drive edit, so it doesn't guess.

Workaround: Sync once with resolve={"<name>": "keep_drive"}. That stamps the properties without changing the Doc's content, and from then on the Doc uses the new detection. Use it only when the local file matches the Doc: if the Doc was edited in Drive, copy those edits into the local file first. If the local file has edits of its own, merge and use "keep_local" instead, which re-uploads in place and stamps the same properties.

docs.title: Downloads and sync_folder skip names that aren't a single filename
docs.text:
What: Drive allows / in a file or folder name, and a name of . or ... download_file (with a directory as local_path), download_folder, and sync_folder refuse such a name instead of writing it, and report it under failed (download_file raises an error). A name containing \ is refused too, on every OS. That includes a local file or folder whose name contains \, which macOS and Linux allow: sync_folder won't upload it.

Why: A Drive name is used as the local filename. One that isn't a single ordinary filename would land somewhere other than the requested folder. \ is a separator on Windows, so it's refused everywhere, which means the same names are refused as path separators on every OS. (Other Windows filename rules, such as : or reserved names like CON, aren't checked here.)

Workaround: Rename the file or folder in Drive (or locally). For a single file, download_file with a full file path as local_path downloads it under that name.

docs.title: Downloads replace the local file rather than rewriting it
docs.text:
What: download_file, download_folder, and sync_folder write a download to a temporary .gee-sweet-partial-* file next to the destination, then rename it over the old file. The replacement is a new file, so:

  • It keeps the old file's permission bits, and its owner and group only when the server may set them (running as root, as the Docker image does). Running as a regular user, a file owned by someone else becomes owned by the server's user; its group is kept if the server's user belongs to that group. ACLs, extended attributes (macOS Finder tags, the quarantine flag), and the creation time aren't carried over.
  • Another hard link to the old file keeps the old content.
  • The server needs write permission on the destination's folder, not just on the file. A writable file inside a read-only folder can't be downloaded over.
  • A FIFO or socket at the destination is refused instead of written to. A device such as /dev/null is still written directly.

A download the server is killed partway through leaves its .gee-sweet-partial-* file behind. sync_folder and upload_local_folder never upload one and list it under skipped; they don't delete it, since it may belong to a download that's still running.

Why: Writing into the existing file left a truncated file behind when a download failed partway, with a fresh mtime that made sync_folder upload it over the intact Drive copy (#844). A rename means the destination only ever holds the old content or the complete new content.

Workaround: Re-apply ACLs, tags, or ownership after downloading, if they matter. Delete a leftover .gee-sweet-partial-* file once no download into that folder is running.

docs.title: LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=roots checks a path before it's used, not as it's used
docs.text:
What: A path is resolved, symlinks included, and checked against LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS just before the tool opens it. If a symlink inside a root is swapped to point outside it between that check and the open, the tool follows the new link.

Why: Closing the gap fully means descriptor-relative I/O (openat) through every local read and write, which is out of proportion here. No tool can create a symlink (downloads write regular files and sync_folder never creates links), so a remote caller can't stage the swap. It takes a local user with write access inside a root.

Workaround: Don't give untrusted local users write access to a directory listed in LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS.

docs.title: roots mode can refuse a path spelled in a different case on macOS
docs.text:
What: On a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS's default), a path whose directories are spelled with a different case than the configured root, such as /Data/x.csv under the root /data, can be refused even though it names a file inside the root.

Why: Containment is a test on the resolved path's text, and resolving keeps the caller's spelling of existing directories. A case mismatch can therefore refuse a path inside a root, but never allows one outside it. The always-refused credential files are matched by file identity instead, so a case variant of one of them is still refused.

Workaround: Spell paths with the same case as the LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS entry.

docs.title: Only the server's own files are protected
docs.text:
What: In every mode, tools can't read or write the server's own credential, config, cache, and log files. Any other secret is readable in full mode, or in roots mode when it's inside a root.

Why: The server can't know which other files are sensitive. roots mode is how an operator limits tools to directories meant for them.

Workaround: Use LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=roots with roots that hold only files meant for the server.

docs.title: Some clients refuse the full tool set
docs.text:
What: With every tool registered (the default), the server is over the tool cap of several MCP clients. VS Code with GitHub Copilot fails every agent request with "Cannot have more than 128 tools per request". Windsurf allows 100 tools across all servers. Cursor's cap depends on the model and reports "Too many MCP tools are enabled for this mode", or uses only part of the list. Google Antigravity is reported to reject a server with more than 100 tools.

Why: The caps are the clients' own, and the server registers every tool unless told otherwise, so it works out of the box on clients without a cap. A smaller default tool set is a separate design question.

Workaround: Set ENABLED_TOOLS (or --include-tools) to one of the suggested subsets, each under 100 tools. Per-client config is in Clients with a tool limit.

docs.title: A write that times out may still have been applied
docs.text:
What: A Google API request fails with Google API request timed out: once Google sends nothing for HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 60). A read is retried once on a new connection; a write (create, update, delete, a batchUpdate) is not. A timed-out write may still have been applied, since Google can finish it after the connection stops answering.

Why: The client can't tell a dead connection from a request Google is still working on. Without the timeout, a silently dead connection hung a call for up to 30 minutes (#1129). Retrying a write automatically could apply it twice, such as a duplicate file or a repeated append.

Workaround: After a timed-out write, check its result (e.g. list_files, get_sheet_data) before repeating it. If a request legitimately takes Google longer than the timeout to start answering, such as a very large export or batchUpdate, raise HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. See docs/decisions/decision-http-socket-timeout.md.

docs.title: A send confirmation can't ask on a 2026-07-28 connection
docs.text:
What: Under the default GMAIL_SEND=confirm, a client connected on MCP 2026-07-28 never sees a confirmation: send_message and reply_to_message save the email as a draft and return sent: false, and send_draft refuses. This happens even when the client declares form elicitation. Claude Code currently connects on 2026-07-28 (2.1.310, checked 2026-10-26), so every send from Claude Code is held as a draft.

Why: Revision 2026-07-28 removed server-initiated requests. Asking there takes an InputRequiredResult round trip, which isn't implemented yet (#1235).

Workaround: Send the draft from Gmail's Drafts folder, connect with a client on the 2025-11-25 initialize handshake, or set GMAIL_SEND=direct.

docs.title: The changed-draft check has a short window before the send
docs.text:
What: After the user confirms, the server reads the draft again and sends it only if its message ID is unchanged. An edit that lands between that read and Gmail's drafts.send would still be sent.

Why: drafts.send takes no precondition, so the check has to be a separate request. The window is the time between two back-to-back API calls.

Workaround: Don't edit a draft while its send confirmation is open.

docs.title: get_multiple_spreadsheet_summary — range notation (read.py:207)
docs.text:
range_to_get = f"{sheet_info.title}!A1:{max_row}"

With rows_to_fetch=5 and a sheet named "Budget", this produces:

Budget!A1:5

docs.title: What A1:5 actually means
docs.text:
The Sheets API accepts A1:5 and interprets it as "all columns, rows 1–5" — so in practice it likely returns data from every column, not just column A. But the notation is ambiguous: A1:5 looks like it could mean A1:A5 (column A only, rows 1–5).

The unambiguous equivalents would be:

  • Budget!1:5 — rows 1–5, all columns (explicit row-only range)
  • Budget!A1:Z5 — rows 1–5, columns A–Z (explicit column cap)

docs.title: Product decision needed
docs.text:
The current behavior probably works, but two questions worth resolving before PyPI:

  1. Does A1:5 actually return all columns in production? Needs a live check against a sheet with data in columns B, C, D, etc.
  2. Should the summary cap columns? A sheet with 50 columns returns a lot of data in a "summary" call. If yes, pick a reasonable cap (e.g., A:Z) and switch to f"{sheet_info.title}!A1:Z{max_row}".

This is a product decision, not a bug — the QA checklist item is a placeholder until that call is made.

docs.title: Feature Roadmap
docs.text:
This doc is a high-level orientation — feature ideas, architectural direction, and historical context. Active work is tracked in GitHub Issues. When a roadmap item is scheduled, an issue is opened; the checkbox here stays as a reference.

Features are ordered by practical priority within each tier, cross-domain. Items marked with a source were identified by auditing competing projects — see decision-fork.md for full credits.

docs.title: What's implemented
docs.text: Sheets, Drive, Docs, and Calendar are all covered — see Tools for the full, auto-generated, per-domain list of every tool and its parameters. That list is regenerated from the source tool registry on every commit, so it's never out of sync the way a hand-maintained enumeration here would be.

docs.title: Release cadence
docs.text:
Version Scope Signal v0.7.0 ✅ First stable PyPI release — 63 tools across Sheets, Drive, Docs, Calendar Published 2026-06-21 v0.8.0 ✅ Tier 1 complete — all "frequently needed" items across all domains (84 tools) Published 2026-06-29 v0.8.1 Defect & documentation cleanup — no new tools, ships the QA/refactor work already on develop plus fixes for #235, #242, #213, #239, #236 Stabilizes before Tier 2 feature work begins v0.9.0 ✅ Tier 2 complete — power-user and structured-work layer, plus defects that surfaced after v0.8.1 shipped (#248) Published 2026-09-08 v0.9.1 ✅ Security hotfix cut from v0.9.0 — download_file, download_folder, and sync_folder keep every write inside local_path. Nothing else from develop Published 2026-10-04 v0.9.2 Post-release defect fixes & infrastructure addons, plus the Gmail domain (pulled forward from v1.1+ 2026-09-23, community PR #786) Stabilizes before Tier 3 begins v0.9.3 ✅ Security release — fixes GHSA-mpw3-mr4r-6cqh and GHSA-8jqx-w7j8-6xwm, plus what merged since v0.9.2 (#1052, #1124) Published 2026-10-21 v0.9.4 ✅ Security hotfix cut from v0.9.3: Pillow 13.0.0 for 12.3.0's open CVEs, which drops Python 3.10 (#1158). Nothing else from develop Published 2026-10-22 ornithomimus Queued, next after v0.9.4. Feature set: Markdown → Docs fidelity (#1044 and its defects), comments as a first-class capability (breaking rename), Gmail sending safety, launch readiness. Plus a ranked fill (was v0.9.4 until 2026-10-22) Gets a number when it goes in flight ankylosaurus Queued: hardening. Feature set not yet set; fill candidates moved from the v0.9.4 feature set (then numbered v0.9.3) and the decision backlog 2026-10-18 Gets a number when it goes in flight v1.0.0 API stability declaration — Tier 3 items that make the cut + any breaking cleanups from v0.8–0.9 Backwards-compatibility commitment v1.1.0+ Future domains — Tasks (separate minor release, needs a new API client; Gmail pulled forward to v0.9.2) Expanded scope

Tier 4 items remain backlog with no assigned version.

Queued versions are named, not numbered (#1085). A version is a named feature set plus a locked fill. Until it's in flight, its section below is headed by its name and its tickets carry a planned: <name> label, so queued versions can be reordered and a hotfix doesn't renumber them. Only the in-flight version gets a number (the next tag in sequence); at that point its planned: label becomes vX.Y.Z and its section heading becomes vX.Y.Z — <Name>. The full rules are in .claude/team-roles/kai.md §"Release scoping".

docs.title: v0.8.1 — Defect & documentation cleanup (target: v0.8.1, before Tier 2 begins)
docs.text:
No new tools. Stabilize on what Tier 1 shipped before starting Tier 2 feature work.

Already on develop, awaiting release - [x] Playwright per-test tagging policy, conductor prompt improvements (PR #228) - [x] QA test case fixes — share_file fixtures, TC-D148 setup, Playwright tags (PR #229) - [x] SQLite cache defensive recovery from read-only/corrupted DB files at connect time (PR #230) - [x] tools/docs/__init__.py split into content.py/tables.py/style.py/layout.py (PR #232)

Remaining defects to fix before cutting the release - [x] get_sheet_data(include_grid_data=True) without a range fetches the full padded grid instead of the used range (#235) - [x] Generalize the #235 response-size safety net (post-fetch size check + configurable cap + local_path bypass) to other tools that can return large responses — export_file, get_doc_content, get_multiple_sheet_data, find_in_spreadsheet, list_file_activity. Oversized responses silently kill the MCP session today (client-side output cap, e.g. Claude Code's MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS), requiring a server restart to recover — confirmed live, not hypothetical. Renamed MAX_GRID_DATA_RESPONSE_CHARS to MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_CHARS (single global cap); live-verified thresholds per tool (#242) - [x] create_doc_from_file markdown $ escape renders as literal backslash+dollar in the doc — Python-Markdown's default ESCAPED_CHARS omitted $ (unlike CommonMark); fixed via a small extension adding it, respecting code-span/fenced-code protection (#213) - [x] Unknown tool parameters are silently dropped instead of raising a validation error — FastMCP's generated pydantic arg models default to ignoring extra fields, so a typo'd kwarg (e.g. parent_id instead of parent_folder_id) silently falls back to default behavior instead of erroring. Fixed centrally in the tool() decorator (applies to all ~84 tools uniformly) (#239) - [x] Auto-generate docs/tools.md from tool source as a pre-commit hook — makes the manual tools.md backfill in #236 unnecessary (PR #240) (#94) - [x] Correct docs/roadmap.md's own tool catalog counts, known-limitations.md's list_all_events entry, and rework README's/docs/client-setup.md's Configuration examples to lead with OAuth (not service account) for local/dev quick-start — currently mismatches the project's own auth priority order and PyPI's page inherits it verbatim (#236) - [x] Rewrite CONTRIBUTING.md — fix broken links to removed README anchors, fix stale "Available Tool Names" and bug-label references, add better local-dev setup examples including observability (DEBUG_LEVEL/LOG_FILE/ACCESS_LOG_FILE) (#95) - [x] Define and document community PR expectations — template, testing bar for non-tool PRs, scope/size convention, CLA/DCO/code-of-conduct decision, review turnaround (#237)

docs.title: Tier 2 — Useful for structured work, plus defects surfaced since v0.8.1 (target: v0.9.0)
docs.text:
Defects (found after v0.8.1 shipped; too late for that release, don't warrant a standalone patch) - [x] Dev prereleases become unreachable once the base version's stable release ships — format-jinja never bumps past the last tag, so X.Y.Z.devN is a PEP 440 pre-release of the already-published X.Y.Z and always loses precedence to it; fix is bump = true in [tool.uv-dynamic-versioning] (PR #318) (#317) - [x] sync_folder doesn't recurse into subfolders — one-level-only Drive query silently reports a clean "in sync" result while ignoring every nested file (confirmed live: 225 files across 22 subfolders ignored, only the root-level file seen) (PR #328) (#315) - [x] download_folder's file loop is genuinely sequential (for f in ...: await asyncio.to_thread(...)) — the one multi-file transfer path missed when the asyncio.gather pattern was established (#183); sync_folder's own transfer step already uses it correctly (PR #351) (#316) - [x] sync_folder re-uploads every file after its first download — download never sets the local file's mtime to match Drive's modifiedTime, so any real time gap past the 5s tolerance makes the local copy look "locally newer" on the next sync; confirmed live during #315/#328 QA, reproduces on both new and long-standing files, unrelated to recursion (PR #357) (#346) - [x] Bare URLs in markdown content aren't autolinked — Python-Markdown's built-in autolink only fires on <https://...> or [text](url), not a bare URL (PR #265) (#248) - [x] zip(doc_tables, ast_tables) in emitter.py silently cross-pairs tables when one is skipped (zero-row/zero-col table), misapplying fill/merge/style requests to the wrong table — surfaced during #276's review (PR #282) (#277) - [x] Nested <li> silently deletes the parent list item's own text (HTML and Markdown paths) — handle_starttag clobbers the outer block's in-progress run buffer with no save/restore; found by Aziz auditing the markdown/HTML-to-Doc pipeline (PR #369) (#335) - [x] Nested bullet/numbered list depth is computed correctly but never emitted as Docs indentation — every list renders flat regardless of source nesting; ast_to_requests never reads BulletItem.depth; found alongside #335 — was held back until #360 merged (both rewrite the same ast_to_requests bullet-handling logic in emitter.py); #360 shipped 2026-07-24, so ready-for-development/lane-b again, queued behind #402 (#336) (PR #432) - [x] emitter.py computes Docs API insertion offsets via Python len() instead of UTF-16 code units — wrong for any astral-plane character (most emoji, some CJK/math symbols); fixed via external contributor PR #360, live-verified in PR #407 — unblocks #372's content.py split (PR #360) (#358) - [x] spreadsheet://{id}/info MCP resource throws 'FastMCP' object has no attribute 'get_lifespan_context' — discovered live during #361's QA, possibly a regression from the mcp SDK bump (#349/#350) (PR #368) (#363) - [x] Plain-text content (no wrapping tag) silently produces an empty doc body (PR #385) (#343) - [x] _get_sheet_id catches all exceptions from the sheet-lookup fetch and returns None, the same value it returns when the sheet genuinely doesn't exist — every caller (24 call sites) then misreports a transient API error as "sheet not found"; flagged during #380/#89's QA (PR #390) (#384) - [x] _AstParser.handle_endtag pops _list_ordered only on a matching close tag — a mismatched <ol>/<ul> pair leaves it permanently desynced, corrupting nesting depth for every subsequent list in the document; pre-existing, confirmed live during #369/#335's review — ready-for-development/lane-b re-added now that #401/#402 (both shipped) are no longer blocking it, queued behind #408/#409 (PR #449) (#382) - [x] When the markdown-to-Doc converter can't represent a construct (unsupported image path, thematic break ---, or anything else unhandled), it deletes that construct's entire paragraph rather than leaving an empty block — breaks fidelity with how every CommonMark viewer degrades (paragraph boundaries hold even when an inline element fails to resolve); confirmed live across 21 real policy documents converted via create_doc_from_file, every one needed manual insert_doc_text patches to restore lost paragraph breaks. General fix, not image-specific; doesn't require #333's image rendering to land first (PR #406) (#401) - [x] Paragraphs containing only whitespace/  are silently dropped — distinct root cause from #401 (this is an ordinary, fully-understood HTML character reference, not an unsupported construct; likely an empty-after-strip check skipping emission), but same silent-collapse symptom and same real-document discovery session (PR #441) (#402) - [x] style_doc_range rejects link_url=null with "Links must include at least one type" instead of clearing an existing hyperlink — found while trying to strip a dead #slug anchor link left over from markdown conversion (see #409) (PR #446) (#408) - [x] Markdown-to-Doc conversion keeps GitHub/GitLab-style #slug heading-anchor links as dead hyperlinks instead of resolving them to Docs-native internal links (createNamedRange/bookmark targets) — links render correctly on the source Markdown host but go nowhere once converted. Depends on #408 (need working link-clearing/rewriting first). (PR #453) (#409) - [x] _get_sheet_index has the identical catch-and-swallow bug _get_sheet_id was just fixed for (#384/PR #390) — misreports transient API failures as "sheet not found" to its only caller, duplicate_sheet's insert_index default. Same fix shape as #384, same file family (sheets, not docs) as #384's own fix (PR #440) (#391) - [x] Thematic breaks (---) are silently dropped during markdown conversion with zero trace, worse than docs/design/markdown-support.md anticipated (that doc only discusses front-matter incidentally rendering as an <hr> paragraph, not vanishing entirely); confirmed resolved as a side effect of #401's general fix (PR #406) — closed as duplicate, no separate PR (#399) - [x] html_parser.py: mismatched <ol>/<ul> close can leave a stale block-interruption frame that a later, unrelated list closes by coincidence — pre-existing, confirmed live during #382's own review round, distinct from #382's own fix (PR #478) (#450) - [x] html_parser.py: whitespace-only <pre> resumed-block flush doesn't get the fresh-vs-resumed gate #402's fix gave other block tags — found during #402's own review round, pre-existing, confirmed live. Docs domain, sequence behind lane-b's current queue (PR #515) (#443) - [x] Neither the AST schema nor html_parser.py has any concept of a blockquote — <blockquote>/> quoted text silently converts to a plain, visually indistinguishable Paragraph, no indent or styling of any kind. Docs domain, same conversion-pipeline surface as #334 (lane-b's current ticket) — sequence behind it rather than run in parallel (#476) (PR #546) - [x] Inline-image pre-validation (#400) only checks Google's 25-megapixel ceiling, not its 50MB file-size ceiling — a large, low-compressibility image under the megapixel limit passes check_image_bytes silently and only fails later at the real Docs API call; auto_downscale=True also has no effect for this case, since the downscale path only triggers off a check_image_bytes error. Confirmed live during #400/PR #554's QA round 2. (#562, PR #580) - [x] list_calendar_acl doesn't handle pagination (nextPageToken) — silently returns only the first page for a calendar with enough sharing entries to paginate. Calendar domain, found during #158's review round (#460) (PR #612) - [x] add_calendar_acl silently ignores scope_value when scope_type='default' instead of rejecting it — docstring implies it's optional/ignored but the real behavior is undocumented silent acceptance of a value that has no effect; live-verified. Calendar domain, found during #158's review round (#458) (PR #616) - [x] Three convert_markdown matching/status-reporting edge cases found during PR #414's round-3 review — drive_map has no collision guard between a plain file and a converted Doc sharing the same name; _upload_local_file never stamps modifiedTime on a converted Doc, so it falls outside the sync tolerance and reports conflict instead of skipped on almost every first re-sync after upload_local_file(convert=True); a drive-only converted Doc always reports conflict even when direction='upload'. Two of the three confirmed live. ready-for-development/lane-a — scoped entirely to transfer.py, distinct from lane-b's docs-emitter defect chain, so it runs in parallel rather than queuing behind it (#422) (PR #433)

Sheets - [x] update_borders — border style, width, color on a range (PR #325) (#122) (freema/mcp-gsheets) - [x] hide_rows / hide_columns / unhide — toggle row or column visibility (#123) (freema/mcp-gsheets) (PR #311) - [x] resize_rows / resize_columns — set pixel height/width, or auto-fit to content (PR #321) (#124) (freema/mcp-gsheets) - [x] add_data_validation / get_data_validation — dropdowns, checkboxes, value constraints (#125) (freema/mcp-gsheets) (PR #361) - [x] update_sheet_properties — tab color, hide/show gridlines (PR #301) (#126) (freema/mcp-gsheets) - [x] duplicate_sheet — copy a sheet within the same spreadsheet (PR #286) (#127) - [x] Partial (rich-text) hyperlinks in update_cells (PR #380) (#89) - [x] import_csv_to_sheet — populate a spreadsheet from a local CSV file (PR #272) (#187)

Calendar - [x] create_calendar / update_calendar / delete_calendar — calendar lifecycle (PR #266) (#156) - [x] add_calendar_to_list / remove_calendar_from_list — subscribe/unsubscribe (PR #269) (#157) - [x] Calendar ACL — share a calendar with users or groups (PR #455) (#158) - [x] list_all_events — query all subscribed calendars in parallel, reusing the asyncio.gather/execute_in_thread pattern #183 established and the inline-per-item-error convention already used by get_multiple_sheet_data/share_spreadsheet/share_file (both open questions resolved; no longer decision-blocked) ready-for-development/lane-a (#194) (PR #464) - [x] Non-blocking follow-ups from #194/PR #464's review: scripts/gen_tool_docs.py's "Calendar only" SUBSETS entry omits list_all_events, shaping code duplicated with list_events, no concurrency cap on the parallel fan-out. No lane assignment yet (#466) (PR #625)

Docs - [x] insert_page_break — explicit page break at an index (#148) (PR #314) - [x] merge_table_cells — merge cells in an existing table (distinct from write-time colspan) (#150) (PR #310) - [x] Comments API — list, add, resolve doc comments (PR #324) (#151) - [x] create_named_range / create_bookmark — anchor points for internal links (PR #337) (#152) - [x] Rowspan emitter — closed as duplicate, already implemented via #100 (rowspan support) and PR #287 (nested-table colspan/rowspan) (#195) - [x] Warn/error on mixed text + nested table in same cell — shipped as the fuller Cell.children: list[Run | Table] ordered model, also fixing trailing-text-after-nested-table ordering (#275) in the same PR (PR #276) (#108) - [x] colspan/rowspan inside nested tables (PR #287) (#109) - [x] find_in_doc — search doc text and return match locations, parallel to find_in_spreadsheet; removes the manual index math currently needed to retrofit links (or any style) onto text already in a doc, raised while fixing #248 (PR #353) (#262) - [x] Markdown-to-Doc image support — ![alt](path) silently dropped today; local file path, drive:<id>, or HTTPS URL should all resolve to an inline image at the right position — deprioritized behind formatting fixes (#401/#402/#399, #403/#404) per user request; no lane assignment yet (PR #502) (#333) - [x] insert_inline_image fails with the raw Google Docs API error ("The provided image is too large") for images over ~25 megapixels — no upfront size check, no mention of the actual limit or the image's own megapixel count; diagnosing required external tooling (sips) and prior knowledge of Google's ceiling. Same image codepath as #333, which has since shipped (PR #502) — no longer blocked. (#400) (PR #554) - [x] Expose paragraph list/nesting info in get_doc_structure, plus a tool to set/change bullet membership and nesting level on an existing range (createParagraphBullets/deleteParagraphBullets equivalent) — markdown converter currently flattens indented sub-lists into the parent list with no way to detect or fix it after the fact (#334) (PR #524) - [x] Soft-break paragraph helper (single paragraph, multiple lines joined by soft breaks, explicit named style) + document delete_doc_range's paragraph-merge-inherits-neighbor-style behavior (#332) (PR #362) - [x] update_doc_from_file — update an existing Doc in place from a local .md/.html file, reading server-side like create_doc_from_file instead of round-tripping full content through the caller's context; real friction confirmed live — reporter had to fake this via delete-then-recreate. Wants #401/#402 landed first so the same paragraph-collapse defects don't just resurface via the update path (#341) (PR #564) - [x] style_doc_table_cells applies border_color/border_width/border_dash_style uniformly to all four cell edges — no per-edge control (top/bottom/left/right independently), even though the Docs API's own TableCellBorder supports it; blocks the classic "signature line" (bottom-border-only) cell pattern. Queued for lane-b behind #409/#382's remaining defect chain (defect-before-enhancement precedent) (#403) (PR #462) - [x] No way to set custom paragraph tab stops — Docs API supports tabStops on paragraphStyle directly, wrapper doesn't expose it; needed for form-style label/value column alignment without building a full table. Closed as infeasible — ParagraphStyle.tabStops is read-only in the Docs API, confirmed via live discovery-schema check (PR #471); follow-up #473 documented the borderless-table workaround (#404) - [x] Markdown export for Google Docs — get_doc_content (and/or export_file) has no markdown output, only plain-text; the write side already has a full HTML→AST→emitter markdown pipeline, but nothing mirrors it on read. Real competitive gap (taylorwilsdon's server has this). No lane assignment yet (#300) (PR #591) - [x] Extract named_ranges.py from content.py — create_named_range/create_bookmark share one private helper and have no dependency on anything else in the file; zero-risk mechanical move, do first, unblocks #339/#340 to be built directly against the new module (#371) (PR #570) - [x] Split remaining content.py responsibilities into editing.py (range-mutation tools) and images.py (image insertion), relocate the shared _collect_doc_paragraphs/_utf16_units offset helpers into ast.py, drop dead _html_to_text — sequenced after #360 merges, since that PR touches the exact helpers being relocated (#372, PR #576)

Drive - [x] restore_file / empty_trash — undelete or permanently purge trashed files (PR #386) (#138) - [x] star_file / unstar_file — mark files with a star for easy retrieval (PR #387) (#139) - [x] transfer_ownership — transfer a file to another user (PR #445) (#140) - [x] create_shortcut — create a Drive shortcut to a file (PR #405) (#141) - [x] sync_folder — option to convert markdown files to Google Docs on upload (PR #414) (#211) - [x] upload_local_file with Drive format conversion (CSV→Sheets, MD→Docs) (PR #410) (#188) - [x] Expose md5Checksum in list_files/get_file_metadata for real content-diffing, and let sync_folder diff by checksum instead of/in addition to modifiedTime — mtime is unreliable across in-place overwrites, upload_local_file's "now" stamp, and content-preserving regenerations; related to #239 (PR #472) (#274) - [x] Drive Activity API — file change history (#72) - [x] upload_local_folder doesn't route through _upload_local_file, so the convert capability (#188) is unreachable from bulk folder uploads — no way to bulk-import a folder of CSV/DOCX/PPTX into native Workspace formats. Same domain as #274, candidate for lane-a once #274 ships (PR #505) (#411) - [x] Reconcile the two independent Drive-conversion mechanisms — _upload_local_file's _CONVERT_MIME map and upload_file's convert_to_doc param do the same thing (source mimetype upload + destination-metadata mimeType override) with no cross-reference; risk of drift as more conversion paths get added. Related to #411 (#412, PR #543) - [x] sync_folder's convert_markdown upload path: two Drive files sharing the same geeSweetConvertMarkdownSource property (e.g. a Drive-UI copy of a converted Doc) collide as the same drive_map key — the later one in iteration order silently wins with no error. Narrow trigger, flagged non-blocking during PR #414's round 2 QA review (#419) - [x] sync_folder's convert_markdown upload path: create() and its metadata-only update() re-stamp share one try/except — a transient failure in the second call after a successful create() reports upload_fail even though the Doc now exists in Drive, leaving an untracked orphan with no ID recorded. Same code path as #419 — candidate for one PR fixing both (PR #645) (#420)

Infrastructure - [x] Harden concurrent-session access — fail-open on cache read/write errors, busy_timeout (PR #280) (#234) - [x] Cache reliability & configurability — runtime-configurable TTL, smarter invalidation for shared files (PR #284) (#99) - [x] Async tool execution — asyncio.gather() for parallel Google API calls; establishes the project's parallel-call pattern, which #194 should reuse rather than introducing its own ThreadPoolExecutor (PR #293) (#183) - [x] Log the running mcp-gee-sweet package version at startup — server.py::main() logs tool-filtering state but never the version, which is dynamic (uv-dynamic-versioning) so needs an importlib.metadata.version() lookup rather than a static string (PR #479) (#356) - [x] server.py::main()'s new version-logging call (#356) has no fallback for importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError — a broken/repackaged install or invoking main() directly without the package installed crashes the whole server before any tool-filtering log or transport startup, instead of degrading gracefully. Found during #356's own QA (PR #483) (#481) - [x] transfer_ownership missing from server://auth-status's _SA_LIMITED_TOOLS despite its own docstring documenting the OAuth-only restriction — found during #140's review. Needed a design call on generalizing _auth_status_json's failure-reason schema (storage-quota vs. no-Drive-identity are different failure classes), so routed to Joy instead of Amy. (PR #507) (#447) - [x] server://auth-status's auth_method: "adc" can't distinguish a real user credential from a service-account-backed one (GCE/Cloud Run/GKE metadata identity, or GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS pointed at a key file) — both get tagged plain "adc" with can_create_in_personal_drive: true and zero limitations, which is wrong whenever ADC resolves to a service account. Found during #447's design work; not blocking it. ready-for-development (on deck, no lane yet) (#506) (PR #613) - [x] Dependabot's pip-ecosystem config doesn't always regenerate uv.lock for a version bump (confirmed on 2 of 7 PRs in the same batch) — silently defeats every --frozen CI/release install, which doesn't validate lock-vs-manifest consistency. Immediate drift fixed by hand 2026-08-06; switched to native uv ecosystem config and added a lockfile-sync CI guard (#528, PR #533) - [x] Migrate mcp.server.fastmcp → mcp.server.mcpserver (mcp SDK v2) — was held as a watch-item while v2 was alpha; mcp hit 2.0.0 stable 2026-08-20, live-confirmed fastmcp is fully removed (not deprecated) and mcpserver.MCPServer exists as expected (PR #642) (#175) - [x] Docs version switcher never renders and each release's mike deploy overwrites the previous version instead of versioning alongside it — the latest/develop split from #267 isn't actually working — config/workflow fix in PR #668; post-merge gh-pages ops (purged the stale pre-mike tree, mike set-default develop) done + live-verified: root redirects to /develop/, switcher renders, stale paths 404 (#667)

Documentation - [x] Tool-count figures have drifted out of sync across README/docs/roadmap.md/docs/tools.md (the only auto-generated one, authoritative at 122) — generate the hand-maintained ones instead of manually recounting each time this is caught. Routed to Amy (PR #550) (#467) - [x] Document transfer_ownership's server://auth-status limitation once #447's schema work lands — the tool's own docstring already promises discoverability via that resource. Delivered as part of #447's own PR (docs/auth.md's limitation bullet, decision-auth-status-limitation-categories.md, and QA's TC-I27) rather than as separate follow-up work; audited and confirmed complete, no additional doc changes needed. (PR #507) (#503) - [x] Rewrite positioning/differentiation in README and docs/index.md — official Google MCP servers are now in developer preview, which undercuts the current "no official alternative exists" framing; lead with concrete differentiators (tool breadth, stability/QA gate, design philosophy) instead, checked against what the official servers actually cover (PR #306) (#263) - [x] Markdown-support documentation gaps — README/docs/tools.md/docs/known-limitations.md/docs/design/markdown-support.md never caught up to the Docs markdown-input pipeline shipped via #102/#103/#104/#248; consolidates #297/#298/#299/#302 (PR #482) (#303) - [x] CLAUDE.md's convert_markdown note overstates its download-branch guard as reachable — round-2 review moved that case earlier in the plan-building loop, where it's now classified conflict, not failed; the guard described is dead defensive code, not live behavior. Found during PR #414's round-3 review, routed to Amy (#423) (PR #492)

v0.9.0 Full Regression QA pass (2026-09-04) — 623 PASS / 12 FAIL / 38 SKIP / 1 N/A across 674 TCs (effective 630 PASS / 5 FAIL after the two fixes below); see docs/qa/runs/v0.9.0.md for the full sign-off. Unconditional sign-off finalized in PR #703 — cleared to tag. Two real bugs found, both routed to lane B and now shipped: - [x] share_spreadsheet fails with "File not found" on any Shared Drive file — missing supportsAllDrives=True on its permissions().create() call, the only one in sharing.py without it (ready-for-development, lane-b) (#687) (PR #695) - [x] Folder-listing cache key omits max_results — silent truncation on a cache hit, and a small-limit fetch poisons the cache for later larger-limit calls (ready-for-development, lane-b) (#688) (PR #697)

docs.title: v0.9.2 — Post-release defect fixes & infrastructure addons (target: v0.9.2, before Tier 3 begins)
docs.text:
Renumbered from v0.9.1 on 2026-10-04: v0.9.1 shipped as a security hotfix cut from v0.9.0, so this release (and the old v0.9.2, now v0.9.3) moved up one. The GitHub labels were renamed to match.

Same shape as v0.8.1 — stabilize on defects that surfaced since v0.9.0 shipped, plus a handful of infrastructure/tooling additions that don't belong to any specific tool tier. Started because v0.9.0's own scope kept growing past its original Tier 2 definition; splitting this out keeps that pattern from repeating indefinitely. The one exception to its original "no new tools" scope is the Gmail domain, pulled forward from v1.1+ on 2026-09-23 because a community contributor had already implemented it (see Gmail domain below).

Defects - [x] Isolated depth>0 bullet run renders the wrong glyph (disc instead of circle) despite correct indentation (PR #711) (#439) - [x] create_paragraph_bullets (style.py) has the same isolated-run collapse-to-nestingLevel 0 bug #439 fixed in emitter.py only — port PR #711's anchor-paragraph approach to the sibling path (PR #723) (#713) - [x] Lock in the isolated-run rendering rule — an isolated bullet run renders at its true depth (depth N → nestingLevel N) at every depth, never clamped (decided 2026-09-09: consistency over avoiding orphaned indent; the markup generator owns the depth it emits). Extend TC-DOC190 with a min_depth >= 2 case; state the rule in emitter.py's bullet-pass comment and the docs/emitter.py paragraph of CLAUDE.md (PR #731) (#714) - [x] create_doc markdown: a fenced code block whose body is raw HTML tags renders as loose plain paragraphs (fence ignored, indentation flattened) instead of a monospaced code block — python-markdown's raw-HTML-block handling appears to pre-empt fenced_code.
