Surfaced during #714 triage (PR #730) (#719) - [x] Bundle: Docs write side (emitter, html_parser, images, content), one PR closing #509, #567, #581, #638, #715 — lane A (PR #961) (#894) - [x] Bundle: Calendar hardening, one PR closing #459, #615, #626, #627, #726 — lane B (PR #912) (#890) - [x] delete_file(permanent=True) surfaces a misleading 404 when the caller can trash but not permanently delete (Shared Drive Content manager) — an agent can read it as "already gone" and skip cleanup; check capabilities.canDelete first — lane B (#876) (PR #888) - [x] SSE: SIGTERM with an SSE stream open logs an "Exception in ASGI application" traceback; the server still exits cleanly, pre-existing before #833 — lane A (PR #911) (#868) - [x] sync_folder's convert_markdown restamp-failure handling: quota-message gap, duplicated create()+update() try/except, test fixture isolation — companion to #420 (PR #669) (#650) - [x] sync_folder convert_markdown's modifiedTime restamp fires for all convert types (over-broad), and its create()+update() pattern is duplicated across two call sites (#435) (PR #817) - [x] _sync_level._run_one's outer catch-all leaks a raw storageQuotaExceeded message instead of the friendly _SA_QUOTA_ERROR used everywhere else — #669 follow-up, same friendly-error-consistency shape as #614/#459 (PR #710) (#670) - [x] sync_folder reports "in sync" when mtimes match but content differs (an in-place rename that preserves mtime) — use_checksum doesn't catch it either; equal-mtime + size-divergence now reports conflict for every direction (PR #712) (#659) - [x] sync_folder: an explicit use_checksum=True should verify a same-size within-tolerance pair too, overriding the abs(diff) > _SYNC_MTIME_TOLERANCE gate that #659 left in place — #712 follow-up (#716) (PR #841) - [x] list_folders with no parent hardcodes 'root' in parents, ignoring DRIVE_FOLDER_ID — wrong scope on any Shared-Drive deployment / no results for a pure service account. Found in the v0.9.0 QA pass (TC-D27), has an explicit-parent workaround (PR #717) (#689) - [x] download_file with a non-existent trailing-slash directory creates a clobbering file instead of the directory. Found in the v0.9.0 QA pass (PR #722) (#690) - [x] find_free_slots's per-calendar error shape is less detailed than list_all_events's for the same failure mode. Found in the v0.9.0 QA pass (PR #725) (#691) - [x] A bare - marker alone on its line isn't recognized as a list item by python-markdown regardless of indentation — distinct from the tracked sane_lists threshold bug. Found in the v0.9.0 QA pass; documented as a known limitation rather than fixed (PR #733) (#692) - [x] PyPI project page drops the logo — README <img src> is a relative path, which PyPI's readme_renderer strips. Found on the published v0.9.0 page (PR #707) (#706) - [x] PyPI project page 404s four README links (CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/qa/runs, docs/qa/README.md, LICENSE): repo-relative, same class as #706, which /release step 4 checks for images only. loud/narrow, in-flight by user decision since a published README can't be changed (PR #1063) (#1062) - [x] sync_folder/upload_local_file convert: Drive's modifiedTime for a Google Doc lags real edits by minutes, and the async import can overwrite the post-create restamp. Change detection for convert_markdown Docs needs a new signal. Joy scopes; decision doc in PR #819 (#814) (PR #854) - [x] sync_folder convert_markdown: a Drive-edited converted Doc stays a conflict on every run, and the only way out today is replacing the Doc (new file ID, loses sharing/comments/links). Decide: accept the Drive version as the baseline, force-upload, or both. #814 follow-up; Joy scopes (#860) (PR #1016) - [x] auth: with no token.json, a stdio server blocks on OAuth consent with no timeout, and the consent prompt goes to the protocol channel (#811) (PR #828) - [x] auth: under --transport sse, the OAuth consent wait runs synchronously on the event loop, stalling every other session and ignoring SIGTERM until consent or timeout. #811 follow-up, found in PR #828 (#833) (PR #867) - [x] Tool errors are opaque on PyPI installs: mcp 2.3 (what uvx resolves; the lock pins 2.0.0) hides any non-ToolError exception text, so #811's "run mcp-gee-sweet auth" message and uncaught Google API errors reach the client as a bare Error executing tool <name>. Observed live. Urgent: lane-a, next after #844 (#872) (PR #905) - [x] auth: offer OAuth re-authorization from the failing tool call, via URL-mode elicitation with the consent URL in a ToolError as fallback, then rebuild services in place. Covers a refresh token revoked mid-session too. No unprompted browser. Lane-a, after #872 (#873) (PR #925) - [x] sheets: an A1 range with a dangling colon (A1:, A:, 5:, :5, :B, :B5) passes _parse_a1_notation and widens through _grid_range to the whole sheet or a bigger rectangle. Hits every _grid_range_or_error tool; for sort_range/merge_cells it changes data. Found reviewing community PR #922, which rejects only a bare ":" (merged). Also covers 1:B and non-ASCII .upper() cases (see issue comment). Community PR #931 claims it (pulled from lane B 2026-10-08; back to lane B if #931 stalls) (#926) (PR 931) - [x] get_doc_as_markdown mangles inline code containing backticks. Community PR #923 (community-PR track, closes it on merge) (#936) (PR #923) - [x] get_doc_as_markdown: remaining code-span/code-block delimiter gaps (fixed `` fence, lost edge spaces, merged adjacent code runs, newlines and|inside inline code, strict-CommonMark test coverage). Same before and after #923, not a regression; found reviewing it. Same files as the #893 read-side bundle. Item 1 shipped in community PR #940; items 2–6 lane B; defect, so ahead of #893 (PR #968) ([#938](https://github.com/khuisman/mcp-gee-sweet/issues/938)) - [x] SIGTERM with an open streamable-httpGET /mcpstream truncates it ("ASGI callable returned without completing response"); sibling of #868 — lane A, after #894 (PR #975) ([#917](https://github.com/khuisman/mcp-gee-sweet/issues/917)) - [x]get_doc_as_markdown: a paragraph exported as a fenced code block drops links on its code runs and images (_render_code_blockkeeps only run text). Found reviewing #940 — lane B, after #938 (same file), ahead of #958 (PR #976) ([#951](https://github.com/khuisman/mcp-gee-sweet/issues/951)) - [x]get_doc_as_markdown: plain text ending in!right before a linked run exports as, which renders as an image. Affects every link, not just code; fix belongs in_escape's cross-run handling. Found in PR #968 — lane B, after #951 (same file), ahead of #958 (PR #981) ([#969](https://github.com/khuisman/mcp-gee-sweet/issues/969)) - [x]get_doc_as_markdown(local_path=…)writes the JSON result envelope, not the markdown:markdown_export.pyroutes through the generic JSON-to-disk helper — lane B, after #938 (same read-side area) (PR #982) ([#958](https://github.com/khuisman/mcp-gee-sweet/issues/958)) - [x]add_chart: a cell-to-row (B2:5) or row-only (1:5) range silently charts one column —_per_column_rangesdefaultsendColumnIndexto start+1. Found reviewing #931 — lane A, after #917 (PR #983) ([#954](https://github.com/khuisman/mcp-gee-sweet/issues/954)) - [x]_parse_a1_notationhardening: one compiled grammar, index bounds, validate before the sheet-ID fetch. #931 review follow-ups, no behavior change for valid input — lane A, after #954 (same A1 area); its QA also runs #953's live checks for #931 (folded in) (PR #986) ([#955](https://github.com/khuisman/mcp-gee-sweet/issues/955)) - [x] Write side drops image links:(or) imports throughcreate_doc/create_doc_from_file/write_doc_contentwithout its URL, so it doesn't round-trip with #951's export. Found in PR #976 — lane A, after #955 (PR #992) ([#977](https://github.com/khuisman/mcp-gee-sweet/issues/977)) - [x] Comment quoted text comes back HTML-escaped (Café) fromadd_doc_comment,list_doc_comments, andget_doc_as_markdown(include_comments=True):comments.pypasses Drive's escapedquotedFileContent.valuethrough unchanged. Found reviewing #958 — lane B, after #959 (defect, next pick) (PR #991) ([#984](https://github.com/khuisman/mcp-gee-sweet/issues/984)) - [x]write_capped_result_to_diskwritesdir/as a file when the directory doesn't exist: a trailing separator should mean "directory" (create it, appenddefault_filename). Shared by everylocal_path` writer. Found in PR #988 — lane B, after #984 (defect) (PR #1000) (#990)

Sheets hardening (triaged out of backlog 2026-09-11 — see the "Backlog triage" note below) - [x] update_sheet_properties/dimension-tool hardening + dedup follow-ups from PR #321's review (#323) (PR #734) - [x] update_borders hardening + dedup follow-ups from PR #325's review (#330) (PR #738) - [x] No tool clears a data validation rule, and no tool exposes a range's numeric sheetId (#365) (PR #745) - [x] add_data_validation: validate the values count/shape against condition_type before the API call (#366) (PR #750) - [x] Dedupe _get_sheet_id/_get_sheet_index lookup logic; add happy-path test coverage (#442) (PR #754) - [x] _parse_a1_notation/_grid_range raise an uncaught ValueError on invalid A1 notation instead of returning {"error": ...}, across ~10 call sites in data.py/structure.py (PR #745 follow-up) (#747) (PR #756) - [x] add_data_validation's docstring and _CONDITION_VALUE_COUNTS are two independently-maintained sources of the same per-condition_type fact, no derivation link — needs a design pass (PR #750 follow-up) (#751) (PR #759) - [x] update_cells's plain-cells branch (+ get_sheet_data/get_sheet_formulas/get_multiple_sheet_data/clear_values) hand a raw range string to the Sheets values API with no local validation, leaking a raw HttpError on malformed input (PR #756 follow-up) (#757) (PR #764)

Docs hardening & dedup (triaged out of backlog 2026-09-11) - [x] html_parser.py: readability + reset-consistency nits in _emit_block_node/_block_had_unsupported_content (#417) (PR #766) - [x] emitter.py: non-blocking cleanup findings from PR #432's nested-bullet review (#434) (PR #768) - [x] html_parser: a resumed block's genuine trailing   is still silently dropped after #402's fix (#444) (PR #772) - [x] docs/style.py/docs/content.py: no shared helper for the "omit key but keep field mask" link-clear pattern (#448) (PR #778) - [x] html_parser: merge identical ol/ul close-tag branches in handle_endtag (#451) (PR #779) - [x] Heading-anchor resolution (#409): minor duplication/efficiency cleanups in anchors.py/content.py (#454) (PR #783) - [x] insert_local_images/create_doc: image alt text is parsed but never used. Closed as infeasible — no Docs API request can write EmbeddedObject.title/description, confirmed via live discovery-schema check (#508) - [x] content.py: image-fetch-failure retry mechanism is fragile, resends the whole document per bad image (#510) (PR #787) - [x] content.py: duplicated image upload/share/revoke logic across create_doc and insert_local_images, plus an avoidable extra Drive round trip (#511) (PR #842) - [x] docs/images.py oversized-image handling: duplicated logic + unneeded full pixel decode (#400 follow-up) (#560) (PR #801) - [x] write_doc_content/update_doc_from_file leave the doc empty when the replacement fails after the clear — fixed by a pre-clear backup copy that is named in the error (backupId) and deleted on success; this replaced the 2026-10-04 revision-ID plan (docs/design/doc-replace-backup.md) — lane A, ahead of #957 (defect; same write path) (#878) (PR #1017) - [x] download_file (missing export_format) and sync_folder(dry_run=True) create local directories on calls that write nothing. Observed in Aziz's v0.9.1 hotfix regression pass; predates v0.9.1 — lane A, after #878 (defect, ahead of #957) (#1012) (PR #1023) - [x] write_doc_content/update_doc_from_file refuse the write when the pre-clear backup copy can't be created in the doc's folder (no permission to add files there, or the Shared Drive is at its item limit). Decision 2026-10-13: fall back to replacing without a backup, chosen by Drive's error reason and not the HTTP status, with a warning on success. New in v0.9.2 via #878 (from-review condition (a)) — lane A, after #1012, ahead of #957 (same write path) (#1018) (PR #1034) - [x] write_doc_content/update_doc_from_file: decide whether the cannotCopyFile (owner restricted copying for writers) and activeItemCreationLimitExceeded backup-copy refusals also replace without a backup, as #1018 does for the folder case. loud/narrow, regression since v0.9.1 (#878 introduced the copy); 2nd follow-up in #878's chain. Found in PR #1034's review — lane A, after #796. Decision 2026-10-15: keep refusing by default, with an opt-in allow_no_backup override; #1018's three reasons unchanged (#1035) (PR #1042) - [x] CLAUDE.md: fix the stale _SA_QUOTA_ERROR invariant (PR #1006 made it false) and add the GHSA-hx2f _safe_local_dest rule for Drive-name joins. CLAUDE.md-only, via Bob's gate. Kept by maintainer decision 2026-10-13 (not a review-bar ticket) — Bob, v0.9.2 (#1014) (PR #1043) - [x] export_revision: support Google Docs revisions (returned as markdown), and fix list_revisions' docstring claim that native-file revisions are pruned after 30 days. Also what #878's recovery path points callers at — lane B, after #958 (PR #988) (#959) - [x] export_revision's temporary Doc exposes an old revision's content to the default folder's audience (a whole Shared Drive) — decided 2026-10-11: under OAuth create it in My Drive root; a service account keeps the default folder, and that remaining exposure goes in docs/known-limitations.md. Found in PR #988 — lane B, after #990 (PR #1006) (#989) - [x] Quota-exceeded error tells a user identity to switch to OAuth: _quota_error_detail renders _SA_QUOTA_ERROR for every identity. Found in PR #1006's QA — v0.9.2 under condition (a): #1006 (this release) makes it reachable for an OAuth user with a full My Drive (PR #1006) (#1009) - [x] insert_local_images: temporary anyone:reader image shares aren't revoked when the call is cancelled — apply PR #877's shielded-cleanup pattern — lane B (#883) (PR #903) - [x] Bundle: Docs image-share cancellation follow-ups (from PR #903), one PR closing #904, #907, #908, #666 — lane B, moved from lane A 2026-10-13 so it runs alongside lane A's #1012 and #1018 (shares content.py with #1018, different functions) (#909) (PR #1029) - [x] _apply_doc_content: temporary anyone:reader image shares aren't revoked when the doc edit raises — revoke pass should run in a finally. Same share/revoke surface as #666 and #511 (#789) (PR #877) - [x] Extract a shared helper for the isolated-bullet-run zero-tab anchor mechanic (emitter.py ↔ style.py); harden its regression test (lane-a) (#727) (PR #735)

Drive hardening & dedup (triaged out of backlog 2026-09-11) - [x] download_folder/sync_folder progress notifications: report bytes transferred, not just file count (#352) (PR #739) - [x] download_folder's candidates tuple: fragile positional access across consumer sites, could be a dataclass (PR #739 follow-up) (#740) (PR #748) - [x] download_folder: opt-in flag to report byte-based progress/total in report_progress's structured fields (default stays file-count for consistency) (PR #739 follow-up, decision resolved) (#741) (PR #753) - [x] Unify the two progress-counter idioms in transfer.py (nonlocal vs. list-box) (#354) (PR #746) - [x] Extend notifications/progress to the remaining asyncio.gather-based multi-call tools (#355) (PR #758) - [x] sync_folder's plan/step dicts have the same untyped-access fragility #740's dataclass fix addressed for download_folder (PR #748 follow-up) (#749) (PR #755) - [x] Expose starred state via get_file_metadata/list_files — star_file/unstar_file (#139) set it but nothing reads it back (#388) (PR #760) - [x] drive: consolidate convert_markdown's duplicated matching/messaging logic in transfer.py (PR #414 follow-up) (#424) (PR #763) - [x] sync_folder: is_workspace recomputed inline in the use_checksum block instead of reusing drive_map's stashed value (#474) (PR #765) - [x] upload_local_folder: convert skip logic has a duplicate-name edge case + logic duplication vs. _upload_local_file (#514) (PR #767) - [x] sync_folder: actions list built unconditionally even when dry_run=False (#521) (PR #770) - [x] Extend the _GOOGLE_DOC_MIME sweep to remaining hardcoded-literal and comparison sites (#412 follow-up) (#544) (PR #777) - [x] refactor(drive): dedupe mime_type quote-escaping and list-files response mapping in files.py (#578) (PR #780) - [x] list_folders/list_spreadsheets no-parent + no-DRIVE_FOLDER_ID path is unbounded across all drives, no max_results (lane-a) (#718) (PR #736) - [x] download_file trailing-slash guard: fail-fast ordering, dead os.altsep clause, raw NotADirectoryError surface (PR #722 follow-up) (#724) (PR #827) - [x] upload_local_folder(convert=True): an unrelated Drive file sharing a candidate's extension-stripped name can cause a false-positive skip — decided 2026-09-23: Drive properties marker on converted uploads, legacy name-only matches still skip but are flagged as unverified (#769) (PR #800) - [x] sync_folder(convert_markdown=True): a .md name over ~95 bytes overflows Drive's 124-byte property cap — upload fails with propertyLengthLimitExceeded but Drive still creates an unmarked orphan Doc, repeated on every sync. Needs a design call on converted-Doc recognition (PR #800 follow-up) (#805) (PR #812) - [x] Deduplicate the max_results clamp expression, hand-copied 8x across drive/files.py with inconsistent caps (PR #736 follow-up) (#737) (PR #781) - [x] download_file: one pre-flight local_path check before any Drive call, for both trailing-slash and plain branches, naming the blocking path (#724/#827 follow-up; on-deck, good first issue) (PR #855) (#836) - [x] sync_folder: a failed mid-stream download leaves a truncated local file with a fresh mtime, which the next sync uploads over the intact Drive copy — download to a temp file and os.replace on success; check download_file/download_folder too. Found by code review, not yet observed live (lane-a, after #814 since both touch _run_one) (#844) (PR #884) - [x] Bundle: Drive transfer follow-ups (download_file preflight + _write_atomically), one PR closing #874, #887 — lane A (PR #1001) (#895) - [x] upload_local_file/sync_folder: compressed files upload with the inner MIME type (x.csv.gz → text/csv). Lane A, after #895 (both touch transfer.py uploads); community PR #934 closed unmerged 2026-10-10 (PR #1002) (#930) - [x] sync_folder: size_bytes never counts uploaded bytes, so an upload-only sync reports 0 (found in PR #1002's QA, observed live). Lane A, after #930 (PR #1007) (#1003) - [x] Share one HttpError reason-check helper across the storageQuotaExceeded sites. Lane A, after #1003; community PR #921 closed unmerged 2026-10-10 (PR #1011) (#916)

Testing (triaged out of backlog 2026-09-11) - [x] Bundle: test-suite tightening, one PR closing #392, #526, #551, #561, #574 — lane B (PR #924) (#891) - [x] Live verification for PR #922 (reject unbounded A1 ranges); coverage in PR #929 (PR #929) (#927) - [x] Live verification for community PR #940 (literal fences in code-block exports) (#952) (PR #1027)

Infrastructure - [x] pre-commit's ruff hook pins v0.11.9 while CI runs the project's locked 0.16.x, so a commit can pass a lint CI rejects. Seen live on PR #1000 (RUF043, three red CI runs). Moved out of the #897 bundle 2026-10-12 — lane B, after #989 (#974) (PR #1022) - [x] /release + prep-for-pr backstop checks for README render breakage on PyPI — the human-facing companion to #708's CI guard, routed to Bob (#709) (PR #967) - [x] supportsAllDrives=True is hand-inlined at ~58 Drive call sites — retrofitted twice now (#687 plus its own original miss); wants a shared wrapper or lint guard so a new call site can't omit it (#696) (PR #784) - [x] Extract a shared _BaseCache helper for the rows_fetched sufficiency check + epoch-guarded store — #688's fix copy-pasted the pattern into DriveFolderCache instead, and the epoch guard is still missing there (#698) (PR #788) - [x] Team setup: give each worktree only its own MCP server — other roles' tool names are an estimated ~15–20k of the ~80k lane bootstrap; measure first. Prioritized 2026-09-29, lane-b ahead of #789 (#850) (PR #856) - [x] Context-size backstop hook for lane sessions, plus a warning before a cold --resume — code half of #843; lane-b after #850 (#847) (PR #866) - [x] Cut CLAUDE.md and the role files down to lasting rules + pointers, moving per-PR history to docs/design//docs/decisions/ — Amy writes it (user-assigned), Bob reviews each PR under the prompt-QA gate; can land as one PR per file (PR #852, #948, #950) (#849) - [x] merge-pr.md step 6: guard the team-slot reset against in-flight work on another ticket, mirroring #837's receiving-side guard in dev.md — Bob's track (#838) (PR #853) - [x] Kai applies community at intake to outside-contributor PRs/issues, plus needs-ticket (PR with no linked issue) and verify-content (unreproduced contributor issue), and its prompt says how to resolve a community PR colliding with a lane ticket — Bob's track (PR #943) (#942) - [x] Kai intake follow-up: find a PR's issue references in comments and commit messages too, and report (don't act on) an unreferenced PR that likely duplicates a lane issue — Bob's track (PR #946) (#945) - [x] Team launch: pin each role's model and effort explicitly in the Makefile instead of inheriting the client default — Bob's track (PR #949) (#947) - [x] qa.md steps 7–8: every QA round comment starts with the fixed line ## QA round <N> (<Name>) @ <short-sha>: <sent back|approved>, so round counts and verdicts are machine-readable — Bob's track (#960) (PR #962)

Gmail domain (pulled forward from v1.1+ 2026-09-23; implementation is community PR #786, merged 2026-09-25) - [x] Gmail domain primitives (#785), via community PR #786 - [x] Gmail scopes opt-in + verify granted scopes at startup. Existing OAuth tokens weren't granted the new scopes, so refresh likely fails into a surprise browser consent or a headless hang. Must ship in the same release as #786 (#790) (PR #807) - [x] reply_to_message should honor Reply-To and handle replies to your own sent mail (#791) (PR #815) - [x] Decode message bodies using the part's charset; tolerate missing base64 padding (#792) (PR #816) - [x] get_message/get_thread return no body when Gmail delivers a large (~MB) text/plain/text/html part by attachmentId. Found in #803's live QA (#825) (PR #829) - [x] get_thread/get_message: add a body-less option — a long thread trips the response-size cap and there's no other way to get its message IDs, so it can't be read at all (#793) (PR #885) - [x] Bundle: Gmail cleanup, one PR closing #795, #802, #823 — lane B (#896) (PR #928) - [x] Local-file read policy across local-path tools — in a remote/SSE deployment these read the server's own filesystem (token, SA key), and Gmail attachments can now mail them out. Decided 2026-10-04: LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=full|roots|off (default off under SSE/HTTP), one shared check for every local read and write; also covers _read_doc_source_file's synchronous read. Lane A after #1018, solo-only: lane B holds after #909 until it ships (#796) (PR #1039) - [x] Release-pass Gmail QA (docs/qa/tests/gmail.md, added by #786). Many cases are destructive (send/draft/trash), so they need a dedicated mailbox fixture plan — Aziz (#803) - [x] Rewrite TC-GM01–22 prescriptively, add TC-GM26–44 and the Smoke rows, per docs/qa/gmail-test-plan.md §4. Part of #803, Aziz (#822) - [x] README and docs/index.md: add Gmail coverage (recounted per-domain tool counts) and remove the comparisons with other MCP servers. Docs-only, no file overlap with PR #1039, so it runs alongside #796 despite the solo-only hold (user decision 2026-10-16) — lane B (#1033) (PR #1041)

Tool surface (from the original v1.1+ plan):

Requires gmail/v1 client and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify scope (or narrower gmail.readonly / gmail.send scopes where appropriate). Add gmail_service to SpreadsheetContext and wire up in auth.py lifespan.

Reading - [ ] list_messages — list messages with optional query string (same syntax as Gmail search), label filter, and pagination - [ ] get_message — fetch a single message by ID; return headers, body (plain text + HTML), and attachment metadata - [ ] list_threads — list conversation threads with optional query and label filter - [ ] get_thread — fetch all messages in a thread - [ ] list_labels — list all labels (system and user-defined)

Sending and drafts - [ ] send_message — send an email (to, cc, bcc, subject, body, optional attachments) - [ ] create_draft — create a draft without sending - [ ] send_draft — send an existing draft by ID - [ ] reply_to_message — send a reply in an existing thread

Organization - [ ] modify_labels — add or remove labels from a message or thread (covers archive, mark read/unread, star, etc.) - [ ] trash_message — move a message to trash - [ ] ~~delete_message — permanently delete a message~~ — dropped from #786 in review: needs the full https://mail.google.com/ scope

QA & docs (moved out of v0.9.0 2026-09-02 so they don't gate the release; see #629, closed) - [x] CONTRIBUTING.md: say how a ticketless PR is handled — a bug fix gets a maintainer-filed issue, a feature needs an issue explaining its reasoning first — Amy (#941) (PR #944) - [x] list_files/get_file_metadata docstrings cite a stale upload_local_file modifiedTime caveat (fixed at the root by PR #472) and carry a broken self-referential contrast — from Bob's docs/tools.md docstring sweep; Dev/QA track, batches with #682/#683 (#681) (PR 898) - [x] create_doc family docstrings name only the ~25MP inline-image limit; the ~50MB byte-size limit (#562) is equally enforced, and 3 deferring docstrings inherit the gap — from Bob's docs/tools.md docstring sweep. Routed to Amy (documentation); closed community PR #932 has a diff (#682) (PR 970) - [x] QA test-doc cross-reference cleanup after the drive.md/docs.md split (PR #582) — triaged out of backlog 2026-09-11 (#590) (PR #851) - [x] Stale "upload_local_file doesn't stamp modifiedTime" premise remains after #898; TC-D238 no longer reliably reproduces its drift. Routed to Amy (documentation); community PR #933 closed unmerged 2026-10-10, and its diff has a working TC-D238 setup. Touches transfer.py docstrings alongside lane A's #930/#916; the reworked TC-D238 needs a live run by QA (#956 closed as a duplicate) (#913) (PR 973)

Backlog triage, 2026-09-11 (Kai orchestrator session): open issues were growing ~2:1 against closures (37 opened vs. 20 closed over the prior 14 days); the 60 issues sitting in unscheduled backlog with no version were the other half of that — filed as legitimate findings, never given a real release slot. Retriaged all 60 into actual tiers rather than pruning them: everything fixing/hardening/testing already-shipped functionality went into this v0.9.1 release (now v0.9.2) (the sections above marked "triaged out of backlog"), one comments-API cleanup went to v0.9.2 (now v0.9.3) (below, since it overlaps that release's own comments-generalization work), and net-new capabilities that were never started went to Tier 3 (v1.0) or a new lighter-weight tier below Tier 3 (v1.1+) based on scope — see those sections. backlog (no version) is now empty; going forward, an issue either has a version or gets triaged promptly, it doesn't accumulate unversioned.

docs.title: v0.9.3 (target: v0.9.3)
docs.text:
Ships ahead of the Markdown-fidelity feature set (now ornithomimus, below): what merged since v0.9.2, plus #1052 and #1124. Maintainer decision 2026-10-19.

  • [x] Blockquote indent invisible on single-line quotes (no indentFirstLine) — wrong/narrow, observed; #1044-relevant — lane B (#1056) (PR #1089)
  • [x] Stale per-thread HTTP connection fails the first call after idle (Errno 54/Errno 60), with no retry. Placed in v0.9.3 by the user 2026-10-17; re-read 2026-10-18 as severe (a call can hang for minutes), observed: urgent in-flight, exempt from the fill lock; lane A after #1057 (#1052) (PR #1126)
  • [x] get_doc_as_markdown emits a raw \u000b for a soft line break in non-code text — wrong/narrow, observed; #1044-relevant — lane A (#1057) (PR #1088)
  • [x] Publish dev and stable releases from one workflow file, so PyPI stops flagging every stable release with a "Change of provenance" warning. Added to the locked fill by the maintainer 2026-10-19; lane A after #1052; maintainer adds the new trusted publisher on PyPI before merge (#1124) (PR #1131)
  • [x] Release-scoping rules in kai.md: a version is a named feature set plus a locked 10–15-item fill, ships when the feature set is done; planned: <name> labels until in flight; feature-placement order; needs-version-call circuit breaker. Process ticket, v0.9.3 by the release-gate test: v0.9.3's fill is to be set under these rules. Kai writes it, Bob reviews (prompt-QA). The backlog re-triage is separate and maintainer-led (#1085) (PR #1106)
  • [x] Fix the stale Tier 4 "zero comment tooling on Docs today" line; close or re-scope #142 (asks for what #151 already shipped under different naming). (#662) (PR #978)
  • [x] html_parser: the </a> of an href-less anchor nested in a linked one pops the outer link, so text or an image after it is written unlinked. Found in PR #992's QA, which sent back the same bug in its new _bare_link_url stack; may close with PR #992 — lane A; moved from v0.9.2 2026-10-11 (pre-existing, invalid nested HTML only) (PR #992) (#994)
  • [x] list_spreadsheets, search_files, search_spreadsheets return trashed files — wrong/common — lane A (#1054) (PR #1083)
  • [x] Table column widths fail on any table after the first in a written doc (stale startIndex in fill_tables) — loud/narrow, observed — lane B (#1053) (PR #1082)
  • [x] style_doc_range has no font_family parameter — can't apply monospace to an existing range — community PR #1026 (#720) (PR #1026)

docs.title: v0.9.4 — hotfix (target: v0.9.4)
docs.text:
Security hotfix cut from the v0.9.3 tag, with nothing else from develop (maintainer decision 2026-10-22). Pillow 12.3.0 has open CVEs, and the only fixed release, 13.0.0, needs Python 3.11+, so this release drops Python 3.10. The release notes say so, and that 3.10 users stay on v0.9.3 until they move to 3.11+. The change reaches develop through community PR #1161; the hotfix is a lane-A backport of the same change onto v0.9.3, with uv.lock regenerated on the tag.

  • [x] Pillow 12.3.0 has 9 open security alerts (1 critical); the fix (13.0.0) needs Python 3.11+ (#1158) (PR #1161; shipped in v0.9.4 via PR #1172)
  • [x] Backport the Pillow 13 / drop-3.10 change onto v0.9.3 — lane A (#1169) (PR #1172)

docs.title: v0.9.5 — hotfix (target: v0.9.5)
docs.text:
Security hotfix cut from the v0.9.4 tag, with nothing else from develop (maintainer decision 2026-10-24). The eMudhra/emSign CA incident makes any certifi older than 2026.10.19 trust forgeable TLS chains. v0.9.4's lock pins 2026.5.20, and pyproject.toml sets no minimum. The fix lands on develop first, then is cherry-picked onto the tag (release.md §"Hotfix from the last tag").

  • [x] Require certifi>=2026.10.19 and ship it as the v0.9.5 hotfix. severe/narrow — lane A, after #1069 (#1217) (PR #1218; shipped in v0.9.5 via PR #1219)

docs.title: ornithomimus — launch release: Markdown fidelity, Gmail sending safety, launch readiness (queued, label planned: ornithomimus; gets a number when it goes in flight)
docs.text:
Feature set and fill set by the maintainer 2026-10-18, under the release-scoping rules in #1085. The release ships when the feature set is done and passes release QA. Locked 2026-10-18, after Aziz's #1044 Phase 1 baseline: the baseline's defects joined the Markdown feature set, and #646, #957, #1078, #1100, #1103 and #1104 moved to ankylosaurus. From here only urgent fixes join (the rubric's in-flight cases and security fixes); Phase 2 findings come in only that way.

Re-split 2026-10-24 (maintainer): ornithomimus is the launch release: Markdown → Docs fidelity, Gmail sending safety, launch readiness, and #1060 for the release pass. The comments feature set (with its breaking rename), the docstring and font_family fill items, #1076, #897 and #1202 moved to ankylosaurus (#1069 went too, then came back the same day as a Markdown fidelity item), which now carries every breaking rename together. #1205 joined the Gmail feature set.

Renamed 2026-10-22 (maintainer): this feature set was v0.9.4 until the Pillow hotfix took that number. It's queued again as ornithomimus, ahead of ankylosaurus, and its open tickets moved from v0.9.4 to planned: ornithomimus. The fill lock above still holds.

Renumbering, 2026-10-19/20 (maintainer): this feature set was v0.9.3. 0.9.3 now ships ahead of it (section above), so it is v0.9.4; every open ticket here moved to the v0.9.4 label on 2026-10-20, and its shipped items moved to the v0.9.3 section.

Feature set: Markdown → Docs fidelity

  • [ ] QA: Playwright-verified test plan for Markdown → Google Docs rendering (full syntax, every entry point) — absorbs #477 (full-construct fixture), closed into it 2026-10-18 (#1044)
  • [x] Markdown sub-lists indented 2 or 3 spaces don't nest (#1071) (PR #1228)
  • [x] A numbered list restarts its numbering after a nested bullet list. #1241, the reverse case in the same run grouping, was folded in (maintainer, 2026-10-28) but PR #1286 didn't fix it, so #1241 stays open below — lane A (#1072) (PR #1286)
  • [x] Two adjacent Markdown lists render as one Docs list. wrong/narrow, observed in TC-MD105/108. Folded into #1072 (maintainer, 2026-10-28), but PR #1286 didn't fix it: it needs a list boundary in the AST — lane A (#1241) (PR #1295)
  • [x] Images inside table cells are dropped silently (#1073) (PR #1215)
  • [x] HTML input: whitespace between list tags becomes stray bullet paragraphs — lane A (#1074) (PR #1315)
  • [x] A bare '-' (empty list item) isn't recognized in Markdown — lane A (#1075) (PR #1322)
  • [ ] Bundle: Markdown/HTML inline styles — one PR closing #1077 (strikethrough, <del>) and #1119 (<sub>, <sup>, <mark>); after PR #1228, check how much of #1077 the GFM strikethrough rule already fixed. Bundled 2026-10-25 (maintainer) — lane B (#1231)
  • [x] get_doc_as_markdown indents a numbered sub-list under a numbered item by only 2 spaces, so it re-imports flat. Found in the 0.9.3 release-QA pass (#1128) (PR #1234)
  • [x] get_doc_as_markdown renumbers a numbered list from 1 after a table (or any block) interrupts it, so it re-imports as two lists. wrong/narrow, observed in PR #1201 QA (#1208) (PR #1234)
  • [x] create_paragraph_bullets adds the requested nesting level to an item's current level instead of setting it. It's the repair path get_doc_structure points to for a Markdown conversion that flattened a nested list, so it belongs with Markdown fidelity; moved back from ankylosaurus 2026-10-24 (maintainer) — lane A (#1069) (PR #1216)
  • [x] Bundle: Markdown/HTML image sources — one PR closing #1121 (relative path against the .md file), #1139 (update_doc_from_file has no folder_id) and #1099 (unfetchable image dropped without a trace); after PR #1228. Bundled 2026-10-25 (maintainer) (#1232) (PR #1310)
  • [x] YAML front matter is rendered as text instead of omitted (plan rule D3). Triaged 2026-10-24 (#1173) (PR #1303)
  • [x] Markdown/HTML conversion: tell the caller when a link is dropped. Added 2026-10-24 (maintainer) (#1180) (PR #1272)
  • [x] search_files/search_spreadsheets/list_spreadsheets miss Shared Drive files under a service account when no folder is given. wrong/narrow, observed in the 0.9.3 release-QA pass; v0.9.3's fill is locked (#1127) (PR #1200)
  • [x] Loose list items (

  • …

    • ) lose their bullet — community PR #1164 (pulled from lane A), html_parser cluster (#1111) (PR #1164)
  • [ ] Bundle: Markdown/HTML line breaks — one PR closing #1093 (soft break), #1117 (hard break) and #1091 (<br> in prose), html_parser cluster; after PR #1228. Bundled 2026-10-25 (maintainer) (#1230)
  • [x] A fenced code block or second paragraph inside a list item breaks the list — html_parser cluster; fence half may fold into #1116 (#1094) (PR #1301)
  • [x] Adjacent blocks run together: separate quotes merge, consecutive code blocks merge, quotes have no spacing — lane B, after #1056 (#1098) (PR #1199)
  • [x] A thematic break (---) renders as an empty paragraph — lane A (#1096) (PR #1326)
  • [ ] GFM table column alignment is ignored (#1095)
  • [x] A table takes on the style of the paragraph that follows it (#1097) (PR #1201)
  • [x] Drive's native Markdown import (EP-5 to EP-7) renders differently from our converter — ornithomimus scope: document EP-5 to EP-7 as Drive's engine; routing is #1113 (#1101) (PR #1270)
  • [x] upload_file(source_format="markdown", convert_to_doc=True) (EP-8) loses list nesting, code styling and task glyphs, and is nondeterministic — route EP-8 through the create_doc Markdown path, plus a CHANGELOG line (#1102) (PR #1283)
  • [x] Switch the Markdown parser to CommonMark/GFM (decided 2026-10-18), keeping the HTML → AST → Docs pipeline. Absorbs Joy's spike #1112, closed into it 2026-10-24. Doesn't fix #1071 on its own (needs a pre-pass), nor #1093/#1115/#1117 (HTML → AST step) (#1116) (PR #1228)
  • [x] A loose list (blank lines between items) loses its bullets and numbers — #1044 Phase 2 finding; HTML → AST step, not fixed by #1116 alone (#1115) (PR #1164)
  • [ ] An ordered list's start number is ignored; the Docs API has no request that sets it, so a fix needs a workaround — #1044 Phase 2 finding (#1118)
  • [ ] Tables, rules and nested quotes inside a blockquote render outside it — #1044 Phase 2 finding (#1122)
  • [x] A relative link becomes http://./guide.md — community PR (#1120) (PR #1149)
  • [x] Blank paragraph before a table keeps the preceding heading's style — community PR (#1092) (PR #1138)

Feature set: Gmail sending safety

  • [x] Safe-by-default sending: send_message/reply_to_message/send_draft don't deliver without explicit confirmation (drafts-first or elicitation), flag external-domain and over-threshold recipients, documented opt-out. Behavior change, needs a CHANGELOG.md note. Spec updated 2026-10-25 from Joy's design pass (detection needs elicitation.form and can_send_request; catch NoBackChannelError; refuse a draft changed after confirmation); hold lifted (maintainer). The 2026-07-28 round trip, #1235, is not planned (#1081) (PR #1249)
  • [x] Gmail: list, get, update and delete drafts, so a drafts-first flow can be managed end to end. Added 2026-10-24 (#1205) (PR #1227)

Feature set: launch readiness

  • [x] Ship an MCP Bundle (.mcpb) for one-click install; the Smithery listing was dropped, since Smithery ends its CLI and connection services 2026-10-31 (#1036) (PR #1255)
  • [ ] Demo screenshot or GIF for the README — routed to Amy; how the asset gets produced is still open (#589)
  • [ ] Fact-check and word competitive/benchmark claims once real benchmark numbers exist — routed to Amy, triaged out of backlog 2026-09-11 — only if the competitor comparisons come back; otherwise it moves out. Labeled planned: ornithomimus 2026-10-24 (#585)
  • [x] CI tests Python 3.11–3.13 only; add 3.14 and 3.15, and fold in #1171's Python 3.10 leftovers. Added 2026-10-24 (#1212) (PR #1222)
  • [x] Make Lint and test 3.14/3.15 required status checks on develop and main — #1212 review follow-up, a branch-protection settings change with no PR (#1224)
  • [x] A next-release label so contributors can find what ships next. Added 2026-10-24 (maintainer) (#1185) (PR #1253)
  • [ ] Docs for client tool limits: VS Code's 128-tools-per-request cap breaks a default install on the first call. README note, configuration.md subsets framed around client limits, per-client snippets, a known-limitations entry; VS Code and Cursor checks may be Aziz's. Added 2026-10-24 (maintainer) (#1214) (docs landed in PR #1254; VS Code + Copilot and Cursor live checks still open)

Fill (rank order, locked 2026-10-18)

  • [x] transfer.py interpolates folder IDs unescaped into Drive queries (#1084) (PR #1140)
  • [x] get_doc_structure hides inline images, so an image's index can't be found (#1070) (PR #1110)
  • [x] thread_http's per-thread httplib2.Http has no socket timeout, so a silently dropped connection hangs a call until ETIMEDOUT. severe, observed: a 30-minute create_doc_from_file hang in the #1044 run left an empty Doc. Joined after the lock and ranked first by the maintainer, 2026-10-22 (#1129) (PR #1198)
  • [x] transfer_ownership(send_notification=False) can never succeed — loud/narrow (#1055) (PR #1142)
  • [x] Refresh stale TC expectations found in the v0.9.2 pass (#1060) (PR #1271)
  • [x] Test modules fail to collect on Windows (os.geteuid() in skipif decorators) — community PR (#1156) (PR #1162)
  • [x] setup_team.sh never re-syncs a slot's credentials after they change, so release QA ran on stale identities — release-gate, Aziz (#1223) (PR #1225)
  • [x] write_doc_content/update_doc_from_file clear the Doc before converting the Markdown, so a failed conversion with no backup leaves it empty. severe/rare; joined the locked fill 2026-10-28 (maintainer) — lane B after #1102 (#1240) (PR #1296)
  • [x] A bare www. autolink gets http:// while an explicit www. target gets https:// (#1180). wrong/common now that the maintainer chose https for both, 2026-10-28; joined the locked fill (#1281) (PR #1298)
  • [x] Drive transfer tools raise HttpError on a 404 instead of returning an error result. loud/narrow; community PR #1278 merged 2026-10-31; moved from ankylosaurus, the maintainer's call to ship it here (#1275) (PR #1278)
  • [x] style_doc_range with only font_family clears bold on the range. wrong/narrow, observed, not a regression; community PR #1279 merged 2026-10-31; moved from ankylosaurus, the maintainer's call to ship it here (#1273) (PR #1279)
  • [x] A table inside a list item renders at the left margin instead of under the item's text (C14). wrong/narrow, observed in #1268's live check; fixed by #1094's change, confirmed live 2026-10-31 (TC-MD201 CT-08/18/28/38/48/58) (#1277) (PR #1301)
  • [x] get_doc_as_markdown exports a block inside a list item at the margin, and a quote inside an item as > >. wrong/narrow, observed; the quote half is a regression since v0.9.5 (PR #1301 put it at 72pt). Joined the locked fill 2026-10-31 (maintainer); from PR #1301's review — lane A (#1302) (PR #1311)

Live QA for merged community PRs (their code ships in this release; run on the gee-sweet-biz side)

  • [x] qa: live verification for PR #1110 (inline images in get_doc_structure runs) (#1157) (live PASS 2026-10-27)
  • [x] qa: live verification for PR #1138 (blank paragraph before a table) (#1160) (live PASS 2026-10-27)
  • [x] qa: live verification for PR #1140 (escaped folder IDs in transfer.py queries) (#1167) (live PASS 2026-10-27)
  • [x] qa: live verification for PR #1149 (scheme-less link targets) (#1190) (live PASS 2026-10-27)
  • [x] qa: live verification for PR #1026 (font_family in style_doc_range). Moved from ankylosaurus 2026-10-31 (maintainer) so the #1273 fix shipping here is checked live (#1153) (live PASS 2026-10-31; heading-bold add-on failed → #1300)
  • [x] qa: live verification for PR #1279 (font_family keeps direct bold, table cells, explicit bold in the same call) (#1299) (live PASS 2026-10-31)
  • [ ] qa: live verification for PR #1164 (loose list items keep their bullets); run after #1228 so it covers the new parser (#1268)
  • [x] qa: point docs_markdown.md's EP-5 to EP-7 expected rendering at the Drive-importer known-limitations entry; closes out #1101 (#1263) (PR #1270)

Moved out 2026-10-18: #379 (unversioned, Joy decides whether to do it); #378 closed (ASYNC240 stays off). Everything else formerly here is under ankylosaurus below.

docs.title: ankylosaurus — hardening and tool-surface cleanup (queued, label planned: ankylosaurus; gets a number when it goes in flight)
docs.text:
Fill candidates moved from v0.9.3 and the decision-needed backlog on 2026-10-18. The maintainer sets this version's feature set and locks its fill when it opens.

Re-split 2026-10-24 (maintainer): ankylosaurus is now hardening plus tool-surface cleanup. It carries all the breaking renames together: the comments generalization (moved from ornithomimus, below) and #665's share_spreadsheet removal. It also gets the docstring cleanup, and whatever the tool-reduction spike recommends.

Feature set: comments (moved from ornithomimus 2026-10-24) — follows docs/decisions/decision-comments-first-class.md (#661) and ships a breaking rename that the release notes must call out.

  • [ ] Deprecation policy for renamed and removed tools: an old name stays as an alias for one release, with a CHANGELOG note. Prerequisite of #663/#664 and #665, decided 2026-10-24 (#1209)
  • [ ] Generalize the three comment tools to tools/drive/comments.py and rename list_doc_comments/add_doc_comment/resolve_doc_comment → list_file_comments/add_file_comment/resolve_comment (param doc_id → file_id); retire tools/docs/comments.py. Breaking change. (#663)
  • [ ] Full comments/replies CRUD parity — get/update/delete for comments; plain reply/reopen/update/delete/list for replies. Depends on #663. (#664)
  • [ ] Follow-up cleanup for the docs comments API (add_doc_comment/resolve_doc_comment/list_doc_comments) — same surface #663/#664 generalize, do it there rather than twice; triaged out of backlog 2026-09-11 (#329)

Moved from ornithomimus at the re-split, 2026-10-24

  • [ ] create_bookmark doesn't create a bookmark Docs lists — docstring fix (option 2) now (#1076)
  • [ ] Docstrings, one item: Tool docstrings: strip internal issue refs again, and add a guard test (#1045), Docstrings: 'Requires OAuth or ADC auth' is wrong for a service account on a Shared Drive (#1046), list_spreadsheets docstring sends callers to list_files for a result cap it now has (#1047), Docstring fixes: named-style resets, and set_cache_ttl's transport claim (#1058), Docstrings: create_paragraph_bullets carries internal API-quirk mechanics plus residual bare issue refs in style.py tool docstrings (#683), Docstring ref guard: cover every tool regardless of env, tighten the pattern, finish the prose cleanup (#1197)
  • [ ] font_family, one item: Document font_family on insert_softbreak_paragraph and widen the style_doc_range font test (#1037), Harden font_family in Docs text-style requests: preserve weight, reject empty values, share one builder (#1038)
  • [ ] Bundle: CI tidy (on deck, no lane), one PR closing #536, #619, #308, #708 (#897)
  • [ ] Unscoped Drive listings don't surface incompleteSearch under corpora=allDrives, so a partial result reads as complete. Review follow-up from PR #1200; changes five tools' output schema, decision-needed (#1202)

Decided behavior changes

  • [ ] batch_update_cells empty input — validation error vs silent no-op — decided 2026-10-18: return {"error": ...} (#32)
  • [ ] search_spreadsheets empty query — return all or require non-empty input — decided 2026-10-18: return {"error": ...} pointing to list_spreadsheets (#39)
  • [ ] Deprecate share_spreadsheet in favor of share_file, and remove it before 1.0 (decided 2026-10-18) (#665)

Candidates

  • [ ] Optional expiration on sharing tools (#1059)
  • [ ] server://auth-status doesn't list export_revision under a service account's no_drive_storage_quota limits. Found in PR #1006's QA; predates v0.9.2 and not observed failing, so v0.9.3 per the review-ticket rule (#1010)
  • [ ] _parse_a1_notation rejects A:B5, which the Sheets values API accepts as A5:B — decided 2026-10-11: keep rejecting (a destructive GridRange tool acting on "row 5 onward" is worse than an error); document in the docstring that this is deliberately stricter than Sheets. Found in PR #986 — lane A; moved from v0.9.2 2026-10-11 (docstring only, current behavior is the safe one) (#987)
  • [ ] Bundle: Calendar follow-ups from PR #912, one PR closing #915, #918 — lane B, after #892 (#985)
  • [ ] Bundle: Docs read side (doc_to_ast/ast_to_markdown), one PR closing #596, #600, #732 — lane B (#893)
  • [ ] Bundle: server/infra hygiene (start after #872), one PR closing #517, #607, #614, #579, #637 — lane B (#892)
  • [ ] Dedicated QA calendar, teardown for creation-only tests, and a cleanup_stray_artifacts sweep — split from #304, no second account needed — Aziz (#886)
  • [ ] sync_folder(export_format=...): converted Sheets/Slides probably have #814's modifiedTime lag and restamp race too. Suspected, not yet observed (#818)
  • [ ] Add a tool to set (and read back) Google Docs table column widths — tableColumnProperties isn't reachable through any tool today (#809)
  • [ ] Bundle: Docs link storability — one PR closing #1189 (refuse javascript:/vbscript:/data:; decided 2026-10-25: converter falls back to plain text, style_doc_range errors), #1179 (scheme-less link_url in style_doc_range), #1191 (drive-letter and host:port targets, padded cell anchors) and #1237 (get_doc_as_markdown re-emits script links), through one shared helper. Bundled 2026-10-25 (maintainer) (#1238)
  • [ ] create_spreadsheet/import_csv_to_sheet response has no web link, unlike sibling create/copy tools — enhancement or fix TC-D01's expectation instead, still open. Found in the v0.9.0 QA pass (#693)
  • [ ] Several drive_files.md cases assume My-Drive semantics now that fixtures live in a Shared Drive (TC-D58/D61/D03/D59/D27/D04/D175); TC-D27 overlaps #689's list_folders gap — Aziz reviews during Full Regression prep (#680)
  • [ ] QA .env has no single source of truth — setup_team.sh only copies .env into a worktree when absent, so fixture-ID changes never propagate (had to hand-sync 9 copies for #305); also run.md vs setup.md disagree on docs/qa/.env vs repo-root .env. Surfaced by PR #677, relates to #648 (#679)
  • [ ] TC-DOC80 can no longer trip the response-size cap post-#519 — large-doc fixture is under the raised default; needs a per-case low-cap override — Aziz (#678)
  • [ ] Automate the mechanical release.md steps as GitHub Actions (#660)
  • [ ] Harden tests/integration's local-fs live QA harness — error surfacing on API failures, subprocess/handshake timeouts, cleanup-masking a real test failure, per-test subprocess overhead (#648)
  • [ ] Define the correctness rubric and own execution for the composite-vs-primitive efficiency benchmark — Aziz (#584)
  • [ ] qa: search_files has no unit test coverage for the error-dict path (#573)
  • [ ] Investigate other MCP clients' response-overflow handling for platform-specific MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_CHARS guidance (#555)
  • [ ] Automated tooling for dependency-bump security review — today's manual skim can miss a well-disguised supply-chain compromise (#520)
  • [ ] Split tools/sheets/structure.py by domain (1865 lines, 25 tools) (#376)
  • [ ] Domain and public sharing tests (TC-D135–D139) — decision landed 2026-09-02: provision a real non-Google test email for external-share coverage; the type=anyone public-link tests stay unresolved (exposure risk not yet accepted) (#49)

Moved from v0.9.3 at the lock, 2026-10-18

  • [ ] update_doc_from_file: opt-in incremental (mode="patch") update that diffs block by block and rewrites only changed blocks, so comment anchors and revision history survive — lane A, after #878 (same write-path files) (#957)
  • [ ] Interaction-log middleware for tool calls — structured, append-only JSONL log per call (inputs, duration, cache hit, error), opt-in ID redaction, swappable backend (#646)
  • [ ] get_doc_as_markdown: nested-table placeholder runs into the cell text (#1078)
  • [ ] A document ending in a table can get a blank last page (#1100)
  • [ ] get_doc_as_markdown exports the collapsed pre-table paragraph as an empty heading (#1103)
  • [ ] get_doc_as_markdown exports Drive-imported lists as blockquoted numbered items (#1104)
  • [ ] Design: route Drive's Markdown import paths (EP-5 to EP-7) through our converter — Joy design; EP-5 to EP-7 stay on Drive's engine in v0.9.3 (#1113)

Triaged in 2026-10-18

  • [ ] create_paragraph_bullets drops a blockquoted paragraph's quote indent — wrong/narrow, observed; from PR #1089's review, after v0.9.3's lock (#1090)
  • [x] Document as a known limitation: a list inside a blockquote draws its border at the list indent, not the quote's. Maintainer's call 2026-10-29, after community PR #1258 (closed) showed Docs draws the border at indentStart, the same setting as the item's hanging indent. Out of ankylosaurus since then: a docs ticket with no version label, Amy (#1242) (PR #1294)
  • [x] DocContentCache.store has no epoch guard; a pre-edit fetch can overwrite an edit's mark_dirty — wrong/rare (#1032) (PR #1264)
  • [x] Doc-edit tools outside content/images leave the doc cache stale when cancelled mid-edit — wrong/rare (#1030) (PR #1264)
  • [ ] Sheets and Calendar write tools leave their caches stale when cancelled or failed mid-write. wrong/rare; found in PR #1264, the same gap #1030 closed for Docs and Drive (#1265)
  • [ ] pre-commit's ruff-format hook skips Markdown, but CI's ruff format --check . formats it (#1087)
  • [ ] Make scripts/qa_compile_results.py the standard compile step of a release QA pass (#1067)
  • [ ] Track release-QA spend across releases so passes can be sized ahead of time (#1068)

Triaged in 2026-10-24

  • [x] transfer.py folder listings stop at 1,000 children: download_folder truncates, sync_folder and upload_local_folder upload duplicates. wrong/narrow (#1165) (PR #1261)
  • [ ] Drive query escaping: the MIME filter skips backslash; consolidate the escape sites. loud/rare (#1166)
  • [ ] transfer_ownership follow-ups: send_notification has one valid value (schema change); consumer and shared-drive transfers fail opaquely. loud/narrow (#1181)
  • [ ] Cache TTL docs and log line say process-wide; under SSE it's per connection. Docs, with the docstring cleanup (#1187)
  • [ ] Service-account storage limit: remaining docstrings and docs disagree with #1046's corrected note. Docs, with the docstring cleanup (#1188)
  • [ ] Windows: permission and symlink tests fail now that their modules collect (#1162 follow-up). loud/narrow, test-only (#1194)
  • [ ] insert_inline_image(drive_file_id=) should grant and revoke the temporary anyone:reader share itself through ImageShareLifecycle, like the Markdown image path, instead of pushing a share_file call onto the caller. Tool-surface cleanup; version call 2026-10-25 (maintainer) (#1183)
  • [ ] HTML table cells: source newlines become paragraph breaks instead of collapsing like a browser. Enhancement; whether a cell newline should collapse was left open in PR #1215 (#1221)
  • [ ] HTML input: source line breaks at a block's start or end become empty paragraphs (pretty-printed HTML). wrong/narrow, not observed; found in PR #1228, grouped with #1221 (#1229)
  • [ ] html_parser: edge cases in a list item's transparent <p> (trailing line breaks, etc.). wrong/narrow, not observed; found in PR #1164's review (#1266)
  • [ ] Reauth offer (#873) on MCP 2026-07-28 connections: capability-only check and a retired -32042. loud/rare; found in #1081's design pass (#1236)

Triaged in 2026-10-28

  • [ ] Drive tools: one HttpError policy after #1278 (lost logging and access-log status, the isError contract across sibling tools, stale text, quota/5xx tests). loud/narrow; from the #1278 review, after it merges (#1287)
  • [ ] style_doc_range font-only bold restore (after #1279): no revision guard between the read and the write, unmasked read, read error indistinguishable from a write error, no table-cell test. wrong/rare; from the #1279 review (#1289)
  • [ ] Markdown D1: also move a fence or paragraph indented beside a moved sub-list marker. Enhancement, needs the maintainer's parse-rule call (#1243)
  • [ ] Markdown task lists as native Docs checkboxes (BULLET_CHECKBOX) instead of a disc bullet plus a glyph. First check live whether the API can set the checked state (#1280)

docs.title: Bugs found in Phase 1 QA run (2026-06-02)
add_chart — multi-column range fails (BUG-1)
docs.text: Severity: High — affects all practical chart use cases. The tool passes the full data range (e.g. A1:D5) as a single ChartSourceRange. The Sheets API requires separate source range objects per column — one for the domain (X axis / categories) and one per series. Fix: parse the A1 range, split into domain (first column) and series (remaining columns), pass as separate entries in sources. ✅ Fixed.

docs.title: add_chart HISTOGRAM — wrong API spec (BUG-2)
docs.text: Severity: Medium — HISTOGRAM specifically broken even after BUG-1 fixed. HISTOGRAM is not a valid BasicChartType enum value. The Sheets API uses a histogramChart spec field rather than basicChart.chartType. Fix: detect chart_type == "HISTOGRAM" and build a histogramChart spec instead. ✅ Fixed.

docs.title: add_chart BAR — wrong series target axis (BUG-3)
docs.text: Severity: Medium — BAR charts fail with "series may only target the BOTTOM_AXIS". BAR charts (horizontal) have a horizontal value axis. Series must target BOTTOM_AXIS, not LEFT_AXIS. Fix: detect chart_type == "BAR" and set targetAxis accordingly. ✅ Fixed.

docs.title: add_chart COMBO — no per-series type specified (BUG-4)
docs.text: Severity: Medium — COMBO charts fail with "No basic chart type specified". The Sheets API requires each series in a COMBO chart to declare its own type. Fix: when chart_type == "COMBO", add type: COLUMN to all series except the last, which gets type: LINE. ✅ Fixed.

docs.title: TC-W03 — test case assumption wrong
docs.text: The test expected the API to silently truncate a 2D array that's wider than the target range. The API actually rejects it with a 400 error. The test case needs to be updated to reflect correct API behaviour. ✅ Fixed.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
Requires tasks/v1 client and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/tasks scope. Add tasks_service to SpreadsheetContext and wire up in auth.py lifespan alongside the existing clients.

Task lists - [ ] list_task_lists — list all task lists for the authenticated user - [ ] get_task_list — fetch metadata for a single task list - [ ] create_task_list — create a new task list - [ ] delete_task_list — delete a task list and all its tasks

Tasks - [ ] list_tasks — list tasks in a task list with optional due date filter and completed/hidden flags - [ ] get_task — fetch a single task by task list ID + task ID - [ ] create_task — create a task (title, notes, due date, parent for subtasks) - [ ] update_task — update fields on an existing task (tasks().patch()) - [ ] delete_task — delete a task - [ ] complete_task — mark a task as completed (shortcut for update_task with status='completed') - [ ] clear_completed — delete all completed tasks from a list (tasks().clear())

docs.title: Potential / under consideration
docs.text:
• Google Keep — philosophically in scope (Workspace productivity tool) but the Keep API v1 is read-only for most operations and was historically restricted to Workspace Business/Enterprise accounts. Creating and editing notes via an officially supported third-party API is not currently possible. Revisit if Google opens the API further.

  • SQLite cache encryption at rest — the cache DB (/tmp/mcp_gee_sweet.db) stores Google Sheets data in plaintext. For deployments that handle sensitive data, consider SQLCipher (open-source, AES-256, mostly API-compatible with standard SQLite) or rely on filesystem-level encryption (FileVault, LUKS, BitLocker). The official SQLite Encryption Extension (SEE) is an alternative but is commercial/proprietary. Not needed for typical local-dev use.

docs.title: Style Guide
docs.text:
Code-level convention: how source and tests are organized, and what tooling enforces automatically. For product/architecture policy (what belongs in this server, when to build a composite tool), see Design Principles. For the reasoning behind a specific past decision, see the Decision Log.

This is a v0, written after months of fast iteration with no retroactive documentation of the conventions that emerged. It codifies what the codebase already does in practice, plus a couple of low-churn additions — it isn't a wishlist of everything a style guide could cover. Sections not yet here (docstring conventions beyond the tool-docstring check below, error-handling patterns, naming, type-hint policy) are gaps to assess later, not omissions decided against.

docs.title: Module size and domain splitting
docs.text:
There's no enforced line-count limit. The signal that a file needs splitting is domain cohesion, not size — a file mixing unrelated responsibilities should split along those lines even if it's short; a large file that's genuinely one cohesive domain doesn't need to shrink for its own sake.

In practice, files that grow past ~1000 lines have tended to be the ones that did drift into bundling unrelated responsibilities — treat crossing that size as a prompt to check, not a rule to enforce mechanically.

Precedent: tools/docs/__init__.py was split into content.py/tables.py/style.py/layout.py (PR #232) once it outgrew being one file. content.py has since grown large enough to warrant the same treatment — planned extraction into named_ranges.py, editing.py, images.py (#371, #372, both open), each a self-contained domain with its own dependency footprint verified against real ticket history before committing to the split (see architecture/content-py-split-plan.md-style verification, not a split done on line-count alone).

Known outlier: tools/sheets/structure.py has grown larger than content.py was before its own split — tracked in #376.

When a split is warranted, split by domain (mirroring the existing sheets/, drive/, docs/ package boundaries), not by arbitrary line ranges.

docs.title: Test structure — mirror tools/ 1:1
docs.text:
Every module under src/mcp_gee_sweet/tools/<domain>/<module>.py should have a corresponding tests/<domain>/test_<module>.py. This is already true for sheets/ and drive/:

tools/sheets/structure.py   ↔  tests/sheets/test_structure.py
tools/drive/transfer.py     ↔  tests/drive/test_transfer.py

A single-file domain (no subpackage in src/) gets a single flat test file — no subpackage needed until the source itself becomes one: tools/calendar.py ↔ tests/test_calendar.py, cache.py ↔ tests/test_cache.py, response_limits.py ↔ tests/test_response_limits.py, and the top-level auth.py/server.py/http_transport.py similarly.

tools/docs/ hasn't been promoted to a test subpackage yet — tests/test_docs_content.py currently covers everything that's about to become four separate modules (content.py, named_ranges.py, editing.py, images.py). #371 and #372 include splitting the corresponding tests as part of their scope.

Going forward: a PR that splits a tools/ module splits its test file in the same PR — not as a follow-up, and not left for whoever notices the mismatch later.

docs.title: Linting — Ruff
docs.text:
Current config lives in pyproject.toml's [tool.ruff] and [tool.ruff.lint] tables; uv run ruff check --show-settings prints the resolved rule set. It isn't copied here, since a copy drifts out of date.

The Ruff version is the project's own locked dev dependency (uv.lock). CI and the pre-commit hooks both run it through uv run --frozen ruff, so pre-commit applies the same Ruff version and config as CI (#974). Pre-commit checks staged Python files; CI checks the whole tree. A commit that changes pyproject.toml or uv.lock also runs a whole-tree ruff check . and ruff format --check ., since a config or version change can fail files the commit doesn't touch.

Expanding the rule set further is tracked, not decided here: - #378 — ASYNC (needs a manual per-call-site look, not a blanket enable) - #379 — ANN (needs a phased adoption plan, not a flag flip)

docs.title: Formatting
docs.text: ruff format runs via pre-commit (.pre-commit-config.yaml) alongside ruff check --fix, both as uv run --frozen hooks on the locked Ruff version. Nothing further to configure here — formatting is already automatic and enforced at commit time.

docs.title: Playwright
docs.text: The operational protocol (lock path, acquire/release, staleness recovery for coordinating a single browser tab across parallel QA shards) already lives in docs/qa/run.md — that's QA-execution detail, not code style, so it's linked here rather than duplicated.

docs.title: Assessment process
docs.text: When this guide gains a new section or an existing recommendation changes, re-run the relevant check (Ruff dry-run, file-size scan, test-mirror scan) against the current codebase and file findings as GitHub issues — one per violation or violation category, same as any other ticket — rather than accumulating a separate audit document that drifts out of sync with the roadmap.

docs.text:

docs.text:
Tool Description Key parameters share_spreadsheet Share a Google Spreadsheet with multiple users via email, assigning specific roles. spreadsheet_id, recipients, send_notification? list_permissions List all permissions on a file or folder in Google Drive. file_id update_permission Change the role on an existing permission for a file or folder. file_id, permission_id, role remove_permission Revoke a permission on a file or folder. file_id, permission_id transfer_ownership Transfer ownership of a file or folder to another user. file_id, new_owner_email, send_notification? share_file Share any file or folder with one or more principals. file_id, permissions, send_notification?

docs.title: Decision: Async Tool Execution (issue #183)
docs.text: Date: 2026-07-12 Snapshot commit: branch feat/ash/issue-183

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Every tool in this server made Google API calls synchronously and sequentially, even when a single tool logically does several independent calls — syncing N files, fetching N sheets, sharing with N recipients. FastMCP supports async tool handlers natively, so the fix is to convert the tool layer to async def, push each blocking .execute() call onto a worker thread via asyncio.to_thread(), and use asyncio.gather() to run genuinely independent calls within one tool concurrently instead of one at a time.

This touches all 13 tool files (~144 .execute() call sites) plus two non-@tool helper chains that tool functions call into: sheets/helpers.py (_get_sheet_id, _get_sheet_index) and docs/emitter.py (fill_tables and its recursive fill chain).

docs.title: 1. Shared-transport thread-safety fix (new scope, found during design review)
docs.text:
Direct inspection of mcp's func_metadata.call_fn_with_arg_validation confirmed sync tool handlers previously ran straight on the event loop thread — the server was effectively single-threaded for tool execution, so there was no existing thread-safety exposure. Converting to to_thread/gather changes that: multiple .execute() calls can now genuinely run in parallel OS threads against the same sheets_service/drive_service/etc. objects that auth.py builds once at startup and reuses forever. google-api-python-client's default httplib2-backed transport is not safe for concurrent use of one instance — a new risk introduced by this change, not a pre-existing one, and in scope to fix here.

The mechanism: googleapiclient.http.HttpRequest.execute() accepts an http= override — no need to rebuild whole service objects per thread, just swap the transport at the call site. auth.py gained a thread_http(service) helper: a threading.local()-cached AuthorizedHttp per (thread, service), built from the credentials already attached to that service's Resource object (service._http.credentials, set by googleapiclient.discovery.build()). Standard call sites became await asyncio.to_thread(chain.execute, http=thread_http(service)).

MediaIoBaseDownload.next_chunk() doesn't accept an http= override (it reads self._request.http internally), so the three/four chunked-download sites (export_file, download_file, download_folder, sync_folder) instead set request.http = thread_http(drive_service) before starting the chunked loop, then wrap the whole loop in one to_thread call.

docs.title: 2. cache.py (SQLite) stays fully synchronous
docs.text: Deliberate, not an oversight: only the actual Google API .execute() call inside a cache-touching helper gets to_thread-wrapped; the sync cache.get()/cache.store() calls stay on the single event-loop thread, interleaved between awaits. Since only one coroutine runs on the event loop at a time (to_thread only offloads the specific blocking call it wraps), concurrent SQLite access never actually occurs even under gather() — no lock needed. A comment at the top of cache.py's _open() spells this out so a future edit doesn't "fix" it by adding to_thread/locks that would actually introduce the race they're meant to prevent.

docs.title: 3. gather() restructuring — six tools, uniform pattern
docs.text:
Named in the issue: sync_folder, get_multiple_sheet_data, get_multiple_spreadsheet_summary. Extended per the issue's own "any tool that currently loops over API calls serially" scope to three more found during design review: import_csv_to_sheet (chunked row writes to disjoint ranges), share_spreadsheet, share_file (per-recipient/per-permission loops).

batch_update_cells scope correction: the issue named it as a parallelization target, but it has no loop over API calls — it's a single already-batched .execute() call (the loop present is a pure Python list comprehension building the request body, no I/O). Gave it the standard async/to_thread conversion only; there was nothing to gather().

Shared pattern across all six: extract per-item work into an inner async def, gather with return_exceptions=True, reduce in one pass afterward. return_exceptions=True matters even though each per-item helper already catches its own errors and returns a tagged result — it also lets every in-flight item finish before an unexpected exception (a genuine bug, not the expected per-item failure path) surfaces, instead of orphaning still-running tasks. gather() preserves the order of the awaitables list, so get_multiple_sheet_data/get_multiple_spreadsheet_summary need no reordering. share_spreadsheet/share_file/sync_folder bucket results by outcome (successes/failures, uploaded/downloaded/failed) — relative order within a bucket now reflects completion order, not input order, since each item still carries its own identity (email, filename) in its result. sync_folder's reduce pass also sums total_bytes and populates five separate lists from one tagged-result stream, avoiding concurrent mutation of shared accumulators entirely (only the single-threaded reduce pass after gather() touches them).

asyncio.to_thread's default executor caps at min(32, os.cpu_count() + 4) workers, shared process-wide — a batch larger than that queues rather than fully parallelizing. Timing stays accurate, just with diminishing returns past the cap; noted at each gather() site so it isn't mistaken for a bug later.

docs.title: 4. Test infrastructure: pytest-asyncio, asyncio_mode = "auto"
docs.text: Confirmed via user decision over two alternatives (anyio pytest plugin, manual asyncio.run() wrapper per test). asyncio_mode = "auto" means converting a test is purely mechanical — def test_x(): → async def test_x(): plus await at each call site — no @pytest.mark.asyncio decorators needed anywhere. MagicMock/Mock-based service chains needed no changes; asyncio.to_thread(mock_chain.execute, http=...) runs the sync mock callable in a worker thread and awaits the result normally — the mocks don't know or care about the extra http= kwarg.

docs.title: 5. A bug the mocked test suite structurally couldn't catch
docs.text: _timed's wrapper (server.py) became unconditionally async def ...: return await func(...). Any tool registered through tool() that was not itself converted to async def would break at call time — await on a plain sync return value raises TypeError. tools/cache.py's three tools (get_cache_ttl, set_cache_ttl, refresh_cache) have zero .execute() calls, so they were correctly left out of the .execute()-driven conversion sweep — but that left them as plain def under an async def-only wrapper. Every existing unit test captures the raw inner function via a fake tool registry, bypassing _timed entirely, so pytest -q stayed green throughout even with this broken. Only caught by importing server.py directly and checking inspect.iscoroutinefunction() on every registered tool's unwrapped inner function — a check worth keeping in mind for any future addition of a tool with no I/O of its own. Fixed by converting all three to async def (trivial — no await needed inside, they just satisfy the wrapper's calling convention).

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Full unit suite (665 tests) green; ruff check clean; zero unwrapped .execute() calls remaining (grep -rn "\.execute()" src/mcp_gee_sweet/tools/).
  • Manual smoke test: 5 concurrent sync_folder uploads (each artificially delayed 0.2s in the mock) completed in ~0.22s total, not the ~1.0s a serial implementation would take — confirms real concurrency, not just non-blocking syntax.
  • Live QA: see docs/qa/tests/infra.md TC-I24 and the six new per-tool cases: TC-D176/177 (docs/qa/tests/drive_sharing.md), TC-D178 (drive_transfer.md), TC-D179 (drive_files.md), and TC-R36–37 (sheets_read.md). The four TC-D cases were written into a single drive.md that PR #582 later split by submodule, which is why they now live in three files. Each case forces enough distinct, identifiable concurrent items to catch cross-item attribution corruption under the real Drive/Sheets transport, which no mock can exercise.

docs.title: Round 2 — QA findings from PR #293 review (2026-07-13)
docs.text: QA (/code-review --effort high + live testing) sent the PR back with one live-reproduced blocking bug (TC-R36) and 8 further code-review findings. All 10 are fixed here.

docs.title: 6. The actual thread_http() bug: eager kwarg evaluation, not per-thread isolation
docs.text:
The mechanism described in §1 was correct in intent but broken in every call site: await asyncio.to_thread(chain.execute, http=thread_http(service)) evaluates thread_http(service) as a keyword argument before to_thread schedules the worker thread — Python evaluates all arguments to a call before making the call. So thread_http() always ran on the event-loop thread, and every concurrently-gathered call for a given service resolved the same cached transport, which then got used by N worker threads simultaneously — the exact hazard §1 was meant to prevent. Live-reproduced as intermittent SSL/connection errors under real concurrent load (docs/qa/tests/sheets_read.md TC-R36).

Fix: http_transport.py (new module, extracted from auth.py to avoid a circular import with cache.py — see #9 below) gained execute_in_thread(execute_fn, service):

async def execute_in_thread(execute_fn: Any, service: Any) -> Any:
    return await asyncio.to_thread(lambda: execute_fn(http=thread_http(service)))

execute_fn is the bound but not yet called .execute method (evaluating it is just attribute access — harmless on the event-loop thread); thread_http(service) is now called inside the lambda to_thread runs on the worker thread. All 141 standard call sites converted from asyncio.to_thread(chain.execute, http=thread_http(service)) to execute_in_thread(chain.execute, service) via a verified 1:1 mechanical transform (every site's preceding line ended in .execute, and following line was a bare ), confirmed by scripted audit before transforming — no ambiguous block boundaries, unlike the regex-corruption incidents from round 1). One non-standard site (export_revision's raw .request() call) fixed by hand with the same lambda-deferral pattern.

docs.title: 7. get_spreadsheet_info MCP resource handler was still fully synchronous
docs.text: server.py's @mcp.resource("spreadsheet://{spreadsheet_id}/info") handler predates the tool-layer conversion and was out of scope per the original plan ("tool files," not @mcp.resource handlers) — but that left one synchronous .execute() call blocking the event loop during a live API request, undermining the point of the whole conversion for that one code path. Converted to async def, wrapped via execute_in_thread.

docs.title: 8. get_modified_time()/fetch_sheets() in cache.py issued unwrapped blocking Google API calls
docs.text: Both are cache-touching helpers, not @tool()-registered functions, so they were missed by the tool-file-scoped conversion sweep despite being called from async tool code (sheets/data.py, sheets/helpers.py, sheets/structure.py) — every call blocked the event loop for the duration of the underlying Drive/Sheets API request. Converted both to async def, wrapped their .execute() calls via execute_in_thread, and awaited all call sites. This is not the same decision as "cache.py's SQLite I/O stays synchronous" (§2) — that's about the sync cache.get()/store() calls, which correctly stay unwrapped; this is about the actual network call these two helpers make before touching the cache at all.

docs.title: 9. Extracted thread_http/execute_in_thread into http_transport.py
docs.text: Fixing #8 requires cache.py to call execute_in_thread, but execute_in_thread lived in auth.py, which already imports from cache.py (SheetStructureCache et al.) — a circular import. Moved both functions into a new http_transport.py with no dependency on either module; auth.py re-exports them (from .http_transport import execute_in_thread, thread_http) so none of the 13 tool files' from ...auth import execute_in_thread, thread_http imports needed to change.

docs.title: 10. share_spreadsheet/share_file lost the identity of a malformed input entry
docs.text: Both tools' per-item _share_one closures extracted fields via .get() before entering their own try/except — a non-dict entry (e.g. a bare string in the recipients/permissions list) raised AttributeError from that very first .get() call, escaping to the outer gather(..., return_exceptions=True) catch-all, which only records {"email_address": None, "error": ...} / {"entry": None, "error": ...} — indistinguishable from any other anonymous failure if multiple bad entries were in the same batch. Fixed by wrapping each closure's entire body (field extraction included) in its own try/except, echoing the raw input back as entry even when extraction itself is what failed.

docs.title: 11. import_csv_to_sheet's concurrent chunk writer could leave holes mid-sheet on partial failure
docs.text: Before #183, a chunk-write failure stopped the (then-sequential) loop immediately, leaving a clean truncated prefix — rows 1..N present, nothing after. Under asyncio.gather(), chunks write concurrently, so a later chunk can succeed while an earlier one is still failing, leaving an ambiguous hole rather than a clean boundary, with the old code surfacing only the first raw exception and no indication of which rows were affected. Fixed: _write_chunk now returns a tagged {start_row, end_row, ok, error?} result instead of raising; on any failure the tool returns (rather than raises) an error payload with failed_ranges and written_ranges (each with exact row boundaries) so the missing rows can be retried precisely, alongside the already-created spreadsheetId.

docs.title: 12. Redundant per-sheet get_modified_time() call in get_multiple_spreadsheet_summary
docs.text: The per-sheet loop refetched get_modified_time(drive_service, spreadsheet_id) for every sheet, even though modifiedTime is a Drive file-level property — identical for every sheet tab in the same spreadsheet at a given instant. The original comment justified this as catching an edit that happened mid-request, but that race-window benefit is marginal compared to N redundant Drive API calls per spreadsheet (now each one a full execute_in_thread round trip).
