docs.title: Design: Blockquote Representation in the Docs AST
docs.text: Date: 2026-08-06 Issue: #476 Status: shipped, fixed in PR #546's own QA round 1 (see below)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Neither the AST schema (ast.py) nor the HTML parser (html_parser.py) had any concept of a blockquote. A <blockquote> (HTML) or > quoted text (Markdown, core syntax — no extension needed) converted to a plain, visually indistinguishable Paragraph/BulletItem/ etc. Text content survived; the semantic distinction did not.

docs.title: Decision: a flat blockquote_depth field, not a wrapper node
docs.text:
The issue's own text flagged two options: a new Blockquote node wrapping child content, or a flag on the existing leaf node types. This follows the flag approach, for the same reason BulletItem.depth encodes list nesting as an integer on each leaf node rather than a wrapping List node, and BulletItem.checked encodes task-list state as a field rather than a new node type (see docs-ast-pipeline.md's Nested Table Rewrite section for the one case where this project did choose a wrapper — nested tables — and why: table cells need genuine structural nesting to express colspan/rowspan/multi-child ordering, which a flat depth counter can't). A blockquote can wrap arbitrary block content (paragraphs, headings, lists, even a further nested blockquote), but nothing about rendering one requires a wrapper — each contained leaf just needs to know how deep inside a blockquote it is, exactly the same shape of problem list nesting already solved.

blockquote_depth: int = 0 was added to Heading, Paragraph, BulletItem, and NamedBlock — the four DocNode variants that already share paragraph_style. 0 means "not in a blockquote"; N ≥ 1 is the nesting depth, supporting > > nested / <blockquote><blockquote>.

Rejected: reusing paragraph_style.indent_start directly instead of a new field. ParagraphStyle.indent_start already exists in the schema, and the issue floated reusing it. Rejected because it conflates two independent concerns: "this paragraph happens to be indented" (a Phase 3 styling input, settable by a caller for unrelated reasons) and "this paragraph is semantically a blockquote" (a parser-derived fact used to decide what to render, including the left border, which is not just an indent value). A dedicated field keeps the semantic marker independent of Phase 3's styling knobs, matching how BulletItem.checked is a dedicated field rather than reusing an existing Run flag.

docs.title: Parser: reusing the interrupt/resume machinery
docs.text:
html_parser.py already has a generic mechanism for a block-ish construct (<ol>, <ul>, <table>, <pre>) interrupting whatever leaf block is currently open, flushing it, and resuming it afterward (_interrupt_open_block / _resume_interrupted_block). <blockquote> plugs into this unchanged: on open, _interrupt_open_block("blockquote") runs (flushing any outer text at the pre-increment depth, since that text is not inside the quote) and self._blockquote_depth increments; on close, _resume_interrupted_block("blockquote") runs before decrementing (so a malformed trailing flush during resume — content left open right up to the close tag — still reads the correct "still inside" depth).

_emit_block_node reads self._blockquote_depth directly at the moment it builds each node, the same way _make_bullet_item reads len(self._list_ordered) fresh rather than threading depth through as a parameter. No new state machine, no _BlockFrame changes — blockquote's interruption is always a single matching open/close pair (unlike <ol>/<ul>, which the existing frame design tolerates being mismatched); the plain frame.interrupted_by != closing_tag equality check in _resume_interrupted_block already handles it correctly.

docs.title: Emitter: left border + scaled indent
docs.text:
Google Docs has no native blockquote namedStyleType — ParagraphStyle in the Docs API schema has no direct blockquote-style field either. Two options were live-tested against a scratch document before committing to either (per this project's rule to verify an API premise live before implementing — see CLAUDE.md's tabStops/#404 cautionary tale):

  • paragraphStyle.indentStart — already used elsewhere in this codebase's schema, known writable.
  • paragraphStyle.borderLeft — never previously used in this codebase. Its discovery-schema description carries no "read-only" note, but that alone wasn't trusted (#404's tabStops looked identical and turned out unsettable). Confirmed live via a scratch doc: updateParagraphStyle with borderLeft set succeeds, and a re-fetch shows it persisted.

Both are applied together via one updateParagraphStyle request per blockquote-tagged node (_blockquote_style_request in emitter.py):

  • indentStart: 36pt × blockquote_depth — scales with nesting.
  • indentFirstLine: the same value as indentStart (#1056). The Docs API's indentFirstLine is absolute, measured from the margin like indentStart, not an offset from it. Left unset, it stays 0, so a single-line quote's only line sat at the margin and only wrapped continuation lines were indented: the quote showed nothing but its border, and a nested quote looked no deeper than its parent.
  • borderLeft: a constant gray (0.6, 0.6, 0.6), 3pt solid line, 8pt padding — a visual "quote bar," independent of depth.

Applied uniformly regardless of node type (Heading/Paragraph/NamedBlock/BulletItem can all be blockquote content) rather than special-cased per type, since the condition is just node.blockquote_depth > 0.

Rejected: forcing italic=True on contained runs. The issue's own text floated this ("e.g. indent + optional italic") as a common blockquote convention. Rejected because it would override or conflict with a run's own explicit formatting decisions (e.g. bold text quoted verbatim should stay bold, not be silently forced italic too) — the border + indent already give a strong, unambiguous "this is a quote" visual without touching text styling at all.

Quoted list items (#1056). createParagraphBullets writes the list preset's own indentStart/indentFirstLine onto every paragraph it bullets, overwriting whatever was there. The bullet pass runs after the per-node styling pass, so a quoted list item's quote indent was silently replaced and a quoted list sat at exactly an unquoted list's indent, with only the border to tell them apart. (This section used to say the two indents "both apply"; live reads show they didn't. The deeper indent it described came from list nesting alone.)

So a BulletItem's blockquote request is emitted after the whole bullet pass, not in the per-node pass, and before the combined table/image insert pass. By then every synthetic depth-tab in the doc has been consumed, so its range maps through _after_bullet_pass exactly like the table and image positions do: the start moves back by the tabs ahead of the item, the end also by the item's own. Paragraph styling doesn't shift anything, so the inserts that follow are unaffected. (PR #1089 round 1 first put each request inside its own run's bullet requests, with a third hand-built copy of the tab-shift arithmetic; QA asked for one mapping, and the whole-pass placement allows it.)

Its indents are the list level's own plus the quote's: indentStart = 36 + 36n + 36d and indentFirstLine = 18 + 36n + 36d for nesting level n and quote depth d, keeping the glyph's hanging indent (emitter.list_level_indents). The level geometry (18/36 at level 0, +36 per level) is the same for both presets the emitter uses, BULLET_DISC_CIRCLE_SQUARE and NUMBERED_DECIMAL_ALPHA_ROMAN, confirmed live. Docs caps nestingLevel at 8: an item with more leading tabs lands at level 8, so n is capped at 8 too. Uncapped, items nested 9 and 10 deep got indents for levels that don't exist and read back as quoted two and three times (PR #1089 QA round 1, live).

doc_to_ast.py's _infer_blockquote_depth subtracts the list level's own indentStart (read from the doc's lists map, falling back to the preset value) before dividing by 36, so a level-1 item quoted once reads back as quote depth 1, not 2. A bordered list item written before #1056, with only the level's own indent, still reads as depth 1.

docs.title: Adjacent quotes and spacing (#1098)
docs.text:
Docs joins the left borders of adjacent paragraphs with the same border and indents into one continuous bar. Two separate quotes in a row therefore rendered as one, and nothing put space between a quote and the paragraphs around it. Checked live on a scratch doc (PDF export), each pair styled as a depth-1 quote:

Between the two paragraphs Result nothing one bar spaceBelow/spaceAbove 12pt one bar, with the gap inside it zero-width borderTop/borderBottom one bar border color 0.6 vs 0.61 (stored as 0.6117647), width 3 vs 3.01 one bar border padding 8 vs 9 two bars, visibly offset by 1pt an empty unbordered paragraph two bars an empty unbordered paragraph collapsed to 1pt (as before a table), quotes spaced 8pt two bars, a clean gap

The last row is what the emitter does. A flat blockquote_depth can't tell "the second paragraph of one quote" from "the first paragraph of the next quote", so the parser also records blockquote_path on every leaf node: the ids of the <blockquote> elements it sits in, outermost first, a fresh id per element. Two quoted nodes are in one quote when one path is a prefix of the other. The ids are arbitrary, so the field is excluded from node equality; doc_to_ast.py leaves it empty, and empty paths are never separated.

emitter._with_quote_separators inserts an empty Paragraph between two adjacent quoted nodes that aren't in one quote, and _collapse_paragraph_requests shrinks it (the same styling the blank paragraph before a table gets). The separator is unquoted even between two quotes nested in one outer quote: carrying the outer quote's border, its 1pt height left a stray dash of that bar. The outer bar already breaks around the deeper-indented nested quotes, so nothing is lost. A separator between two quoted lists also splits them into two Docs lists, as the source has.

_block_spacing gives a quoted node 8pt above where its quote meets content outside it (an unquoted node, a table, or the start) and 8pt below likewise, and nothing between the paragraphs of one quote. A code block gets 8pt above and below, which is what tells two consecutive code blocks apart.

Two exceptions, both from PR #1199's QA round 1:

  • A separator is spaced on one side only, below the quote before it. Spaced on both sides, two separate quotes sat about 41px apart, baseline to baseline, against 31px between a quote and a plain paragraph.
  • A Heading, or a NamedBlock with a TITLE/SUBTITLE style, gets no quote-edge space. An explicit spaceAbove replaces the named style's own, so a quoted H1 lost HEADING_1's 20pt above.

The paragraphs insertTable leaves before a table take the style of the block after the table (#1097). At full height, the one between two tables showed a following list's bullet as an empty numbered item, and collapsed or not, they pushed that list's numbering on and carried a following quote's indent and border. _build_blank_para_before_table_collapses now deletes their bullets and clears indentStart, indentFirstLine, and borderLeft, in that order, since deleteParagraphBullets adds indent to keep a paragraph's visual level. The table itself and its cells took the following block's style too, including its indent. Since #1097 each table is inserted at a plain placeholder paragraph of its own instead (see docs-ast-pipeline.md), so none of it reaches the table, and the reset above stays as a backstop. A table inside a quote used to get the quote's indent only by that accident, from the quote paragraph after it. Now the parser records its quote depth on the Table (blockquote_depth, no path), and its placeholder gets the quote's indent (36pt per level) and no border. A table can't take a left border, so a quoted table sits indented between the quote's bordered paragraphs, with a gap in the bar beside it.

Markdown input was affected by the parser until #1116. Python-Markdown parsed > a, a blank line, > b as one <blockquote> with two paragraphs, where CommonMark has two quotes, so it rendered as one quote. The CommonMark parser (#1116, docs/design/markdown-parser.md) emits two <blockquote> elements, and they render as two with no change here.

docs.title: QA round 1 (PR #546): two gaps in the interrupt/resume integration
docs.text:
Reproduced directly against parser output (html_to_ast), no live Google API calls needed — both were pure AST-construction bugs.

1. Three Paragraph-construction sites bypassed _emit_block_node entirely. The initial implementation's single point of truth — "_emit_block_node reads self._blockquote_depth directly at the moment it builds each node" — was true for _emit_block_node itself, but html_parser.py has three other call sites that construct a Paragraph node directly without going through it: a bare <hr> with no open block, a bare <img> with no open block, and <pre>'s own close-tag handler (which builds its Paragraph directly rather than dispatching through _emit_block_node, for reasons unrelated to blockquotes — see the <pre>/#443 history in CLAUDE.md). All three silently defaulted to blockquote_depth=0 when they were the sole content of a <blockquote>. Fixed by passing blockquote_depth=self._blockquote_depth explicitly at each of the three sites — the "single point of truth" claim was correct in spirit but incomplete in coverage; the fix doesn't introduce a fourth code path, it just closes the three gaps in the existing rule.

2. Malformed HTML with <blockquote> opening at top level lost the split entirely — <blockquote><p>text</blockquote>after merged into one Paragraph(text="textafter", blockquote_depth=0) instead of two nodes. Root cause traced deeper than the blockquote code itself: _interrupt_open_block correctly pushes no frame when nothing is open to interrupt (there's nothing to resume), but _resume_interrupted_block's own flush-whatever's-open step (the PR #478 fix, see that function's docstring) was only reachable from inside the "a frame exists and will be resumed" branch — so a wrapper construct that opened frameless (nothing outer to interrupt) with its own inner content left open at close time skipped the flush entirely, regardless of whether that content was blockquote's or anyone else's. Confirmed this is not blockquote-specific: plain <ul>text</ul>after (no blockquote involved, verified against develop before this PR's own changes) reproduces the identical merge. Fixed by moving the flush to run unconditionally at the top of _resume_interrupted_block, before the if not self._block_stack: return check — closing the gap for every wrapper construct (<ol>/<ul>/<table>/<pre>/<blockquote>) at once, per this project's "take the generalized fix, not just the reported case" rule (see .claude/team-roles/dev.md's Retro section), rather than a blockquote-specific patch that would have left the identical defect reachable through <ul>/<ol> at top level.

docs.title: What this does NOT do
docs.text:
• At the time of #476 there was no Doc → Markdown read path. One exists now (get_doc_as_markdown, docs/design/doc-to-markdown.md): doc_to_ast.py's _infer_blockquote_depth reads a paragraph as quoted only when it carries both a borderLeft and an indentStart beyond its list level's own (see "Quoted list items" above), so a hand-indented paragraph without a border isn't mistaken for a quote.
  • No comprehensive multi-construct fixture — tracked separately as #477, which explicitly depended on this issue landing first.

docs.title: Design: Borderless-Table Pattern for Form-Style Column Alignment (issue #473)
Problem
docs.text:
Issue #404 asked for a way to set custom paragraph tab stops, to align independent lines of text (a label on one line, a value on another) to a shared horizontal position without a visible table — form-style layouts like signature lines or label/value pairs. That issue is closed as infeasible: the Docs API's ParagraphStyle.tabStops field is documented read-only, and no request type in the API can set it (see decisions/ for prior tab-stop findings).

The underlying need — columnar alignment without a table's visual footprint — is still real.

docs.title: The recipe
docs.text:
A table gives exact column positions for free; the only missing piece is hiding its visible structure so it reads as plain aligned text rather than a table:

  1. insert_doc_table to create a single-row table with the needed number of columns.
  2. insert_doc_text (using the cell indices insert_doc_table returns) to fill each cell.
  3. style_doc_table_cells with padding_top/padding_right/padding_bottom/padding_left: 0 on every cell, to remove the table's default cell padding so column content sits flush.

Content written into each cell lands at a precise, guaranteed column position — the same alignment guarantee tabStops would have provided.

docs.title: Open question: suppressing the default visible border
docs.text:
A freshly inserted table renders visible default borders in the Docs UI even though a fresh cell's tableCellStyle has no borderTop/borderRight/borderBottom/borderLeft keys at all (confirmed via TC-DOC146's live documents().get() read, docs/qa/tests/docs.md). That means the visible default grid isn't controlled by the absence/presence of those cell-level fields the way you'd expect — "just don't call style_doc_table_cells with any border_* keys" does not hide it, since the default is visible whether or not those keys are set.

Unverified: whether an explicit border_width: 0 override (with no border_color, since the API only requires a color when width is non-zero — see style_doc_table_cells's per-edge-override docstring note) on every cell actually suppresses the default rendering, as opposed to being a no-op against whatever mechanism draws that default border. This needs a live check via documents().get() plus a Playwright/visual snapshot before being treated as confirmed — same class of check as TC-DOC146 itself. Until confirmed, treat step 4 below as a hypothesis, not a working step:

  1. (unconfirmed) style_doc_table_cells with border_width: 0 on every cell, to suppress the default visible grid.

If width:0 turns out not to suppress the default border, the fallback worth testing next is an explicit white/background-matching border_color at a small nonzero width, so the border still "exists" for API purposes but is visually indistinguishable from the page background.

docs.title: Convenience wrapper (lower priority)
docs.text: Once the recipe above is confirmed end-to-end, it's worth evaluating whether a small align_columns-style helper — create a borderless table and fill it in one call — is worth adding on top of the documented recipe, rather than requiring three separate tool calls every time. Not pursued here; the documented recipe is the near-term deliverable issue #473 asked for.

docs.title: Invalidating Caches for Cancelled and Failed Writes
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-27 Issues: #1030 (with #1032 folded in)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
PR #1029 (#909) fixed one race for the image-embedding doc edits: a write whose call is cancelled while its worker thread runs still lands after the cancellation unwinds, because asyncio.to_thread can't stop a started thread. Every other write tool still marked its cache dirty only after a successful response:

  • Docs edit tools in editing.py, tables.py, style.py, layout.py, and named_ranges.py (doc_cache).
  • Drive tools that change a folder's contents in tools/drive/files.py and tools/drive/transfer.py (drive_folder_cache): the creates, uploads, copy, move, rename, star/unstar, trash/delete, restore, and sync_folder's per-level writes.

A cancelled call left the cache serving the pre-write state until the TTL or a refresh_cache. A failed call did too, although a request that times out may still have been applied. Some sites had narrower versions of the same gap: insert_doc_table marked the doc dirty only once its re-fetch found the table, import_csv_to_sheet marked the folder only after every chunk write, and delete_file marked the folder before the delete, so a read between the mark and an abandoned delete landing re-cached the file.

docs.title: 1032 is the same stale read from the other side. DocContentCache.store had no epoch guard, so a get_doc_content fetch that started before an edit could store its pre-edit result after the edit's mark_dirty, and store writes dirty=0.
http_transport.invalidating(callback, *, on_success=True)
docs.text:
A context manager around a tool's write requests. It enters after_abandoned_calls(callback) (#907), so an abandoned request reruns the callback once its thread finishes, and runs the callback once more on every exit from the block. Every exit includes a failure, since the request may have landed, except a 4xx (is_rejection): that's the API's answer that it ran nothing, so the callback is skipped (PR #1264 QA round 1). Each tool's old post-success mark_dirty is removed, since the block's own exit replaces it. Docs edits go through tools/docs/invalidation.doc_invalidating, so the rules live in invalidating alone.

on_success=False skips the normal exit and leaves it to the caller. Three sites need that because they decide on a normal exit whether anything changed: upload_local_file and upload_local_folder (a skip must not invalidate, PR #645 QA round 1) and sync_folder's levels (level_changed). Each of those now also counts a failed upload, a failed resolve, and an unexpected exception from a step as a change. _upload_local_file catches its own errors and returns {"error": ...}, which doesn't say whether it was a 4xx, so a rejected upload still marks its one known folder. That costs one listing refetch, never the whole cache.

docs.title: tools/drive._FolderInvalidation
docs.text: The callback for a Drive write. It's built with the folders known before the write (a create's target, a move's old and new parents, a delete's parents from its pre-read), and found(parents) takes the response's parents when nothing was known up front. A rename, star/unstar, restore, or a copy with no destination only learns its folder from the response. If that write fails without a 4xx, or is abandoned, there is no response, so the callback marks every folder listing dirty (mark_all_dirty()). That fallback needs both: no folder known and no response (found() never called). A response that names no parents, such as a non-owner's rename of a file shared with them, marks nothing, since there's no listing of the caller's to mark (PR #1264 QA round 1). So a normal rename still invalidates just its own folder. Fetching the parents up front instead would add a files.get to every call to cover a rare case.

docs.title: sync_folder
docs.text: _sync_level runs about 1,100 lines of planning and gathered writes, so each call site (the top level in sync_folder._run, each child in _descend) is wrapped by _sync_level_invalidation(lc, drive_folder_id, dry_run) instead of reindenting the body. A level's own wrapper replaces its parent's hook for that level's requests, because the hook is a ContextVar. A subfolder's create() runs in the parent level, so it marks the parent. A dry run writes nothing and gets a nullcontext().

docs.title: #1032: the epoch guard
docs.text: DocContentCache.store takes epoch= like the sheet and folder caches. get_doc_content snapshots it after its cache lookup misses and before the export, the order list_files and fetch_sheets already use. mark_dirty already bumped the key's epoch, so only the snapshot and the conditional store were missing. Round 1 snapshotted before the lookup, and that broke caching: with modifiedTime validation on, a lookup that finds a stale row marks it dirty itself (_check_modified_time), which bumps the epoch past the snapshot, so every refetch of an edited doc skipped its store and re-exported on the next call (PR #1264 QA round 1).

docs.title: In the same files
docs.text: Three more gaps sat in files this PR already changes, so they're fixed here. create_doc/create_doc_from_file (_create_doc_file) hooked only an abandoned create, and only when a folder was named, so a create that failed after Drive applied it left the listing stale; it now goes through invalidating and _FolderInvalidation like the other creates. _replace_doc_content's backup copy (content.py) never marked its folder dirty, either after the copy or after removing it, so a listing read in between kept showing a deleted backup. import_csv_to_sheet (files.py) now wraps its sheet rename/resize in invalidating for cache, and its chunk writes for sheet_data_cache.

docs.title: Not covered
docs.text:
• The Sheets tools under tools/sheets/ and the Calendar write tools in calendar.py still invalidate only after a successful response, and calendar.py's calendar-list fetch stores without an epoch guard. The Calendar tests assert that a failed write doesn't invalidate, so changing that is a policy change of its own.
  • A create into My Drive's root with no folder named: an abandoned one can't be placed, and the root's listing is keyed by whatever ID the caller passed to list_files. _FolderInvalidation falls back to mark_all_dirty() there.

docs.title: Design: Backup Copy Before Replacing a Doc's Content
docs.text: Status: Implemented. Issue #878. Live-verified against real Drive/Docs API calls via scratch scripts per CLAUDE.md's "Verify a ticket's API premise live" convention (2026-10-12).

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: write_doc_content and update_doc_from_file share _replace_doc_content (tools/docs/content.py). It clears the doc in its own batchUpdate and then writes the new content in later calls. The clear has to be separate because of the same-batch insertText style-inheritance quirk. If anything after the clear fails (the content batchUpdate, a non-image retry failure, fill_tables, anchor resolution), the original content is already gone, and the error didn't say so.

docs.title: The decision that didn't survive measurement
docs.text:
The issue was triaged on 2026-10-04 to record the doc's current Drive revision ID before the clear, and to name it in the error for recovery with export_revision. Restoring the old content by re-inserting a snapshot was ruled out, because formatting, images, and tables don't round-trip.

Measured live before implementing:

Case Revisions before the clear Right after the clear revisions.get on the recorded ID Doc written 5 s before the clear 1, 3 (3 exported the original text) 1, 4 404 at +0 s, +30 s, +2, +5, +8 min Doc idle for 7 min before the clear 1, 3 (same) 1, 4 404 at +0 s, +30 s, +2, +5, +8 min

Docs merges the revision that was current before the clear into the clear's own new revision straight away, however old it is. The pre-clear content is no longer reachable through the revisions API, so an error naming that revision would point at a 404. This matches the merge behavior doc-revision-export.md recorded, except that here it happened immediately rather than after a later edit.

docs.title: Decision (maintainer, 2026-10-12)
docs.text:
Copy the doc with Drive (files.copy) before the clear. A copy is the real document, so formatting, images, and tables survive, which a re-inserted snapshot wouldn't.

  • Only a doc with content is copied. An empty doc (endIndex <= 2) has nothing to lose and isn't cleared.
  • Name and location. "<title> (backup before replace)". With no parents in the request, the copy inherits the source's parents, so it sits next to the doc.
  • Success: the copy is removed with markdown_export._discard_temp_doc, the same helper export_revision's temporary Doc uses. It deletes the copy, or trashes it when canDelete is false (a Content manager on a Shared Drive, #876), and retries on a 5xx or 429. A failed removal doesn't fail the call. The result gets a warning naming the copy.
  • Failure after the clear: the copy is kept. The result is {"error", "docId", "backupId"} (plus images when there are any), and the error names the copy.
  • The clear answered with a 4xx (429 included): the API ran nothing, so the doc is unchanged. The copy is removed and the error says so. Anything else from the clear (a 5xx, a timeout, a transport error) doesn't say whether it landed, so the copy is kept and the error says the content may have been cleared. QA reproduced a 503 returned after a clear that had run (PR #1017 round 1), which an earlier version treated as rejected, deleting the only copy.
  • The doc is re-read after the copy. The copy takes seconds, and a concurrent edit meanwhile would otherwise survive the clear (the doc grew) or make it fail (it shrank). A failed re-read stops before the clear: the doc is unchanged and the copy is removed. A doc emptied meanwhile isn't cleared, and a later failure still names the copy.
  • The copy fails: nothing is changed, and an error is returned. A 429 is retried (up to 3 times, with backoff), since Drive ran nothing. A 5xx isn't, since the copy may already exist and a retry would make a second one. For a failure other than a 4xx, the error names the copy that may have been created, so the caller can find and remove it. Some failures replace without a backup instead (_no_backup_reason). That function decides from Drive's error reason, not the status, because rateLimitExceeded and userRateLimitExceeded are 403s too and must still refuse. The reasons that fall back, all 403s:
  • storageQuotaExceeded. A service account can't own a copy of a user-owned doc, and write_doc_content is the documented way for a service account to write into such a doc (known-limitations.md's quota section).
  • insufficientFilePermissions. The copy has no parents, so it goes into the doc's folder, and a caller who can edit the doc but only read or comment on that folder can't add it. Measured live on 2026-10-14 with the service account as the caller. The doc was shared to it as writer, and it was a reader or commenter on a My Drive folder, or a commenter member of a Shared Drive. All three layouts returned this reason. With writer access to the My Drive folder, the same copy returned storageQuotaExceeded, so the folder permission is checked first.
  • teamDriveFileLimitExceeded and numChildrenInNonRootLimitExceeded. The doc's Shared Drive, or its My Drive folder, is at its item limit, so the copy can't be added there. Neither limit can be reached in QA, so both rest on Drive's documented reason strings.

Each of these callers could write the doc before #878, which is why the maintainer chose to replace without a backup rather than refuse (2026-10-13, #1018). Copying somewhere else was rejected because it changes who can see the copy (the #989 trade-off). The fallback logs a warning. A successful replace returns a warning naming the reason. If only the webViewLink lookup after it fails, the raised error starts with that same warning, so the caller still learns the old content is gone (PR #1034 QA round 1). If the replace fails after the clear, the error says the content couldn't be backed up and why. In that case the original content can't be recovered, since the pre-clear revision is merged away at once (table above).

Two more 403 reasons replace without a backup only when the caller passes allow_no_backup=True (_opt_in_no_backup_reason; maintainer decision, 2026-10-15, #1035): - cannotCopyFile. downloadRestrictions.itemDownloadRestriction.restrictedForWriters is set, and the caller is a writer. The reason text names the doc's sharing settings, not an owner: a Shared Drive doc has no owners, and there a manager sets the restriction (PR #1042 QA round 1). Measured live on 2026-10-14, with or without parents. On 2026-10-16 the same writer also got 403 cannotExportFile from files.export, and its revisions.list entries had no exportLinks. Whoever set it chose to stop writers from copying the file, so the backup is never made another way (an export or a download). - activeItemCreationLimitExceeded, the account's item-creation cap (a documented reason; it can't be produced in QA).

A reader gets cannotCopyFile too, when copyRequiresWriterPermission is set, and the flag can't help it: the clear would fail. So for either reason the doc's capabilities.canEdit is read after the copy fails (_can_edit). If it's false, the call refuses with an error saying the account can't edit the doc, whatever the flag says (PR #1042 QA round 1). If it can't be read, the call goes on by the flag; a non-editor's clear then gets a 4xx, which still leaves the doc unchanged. The read only runs on these two reasons, so it costs nothing on the normal path.

Without the flag the call refuses, leaving the doc unchanged. The error names the reason and the flag, and says export_revision can't recover the previous content afterward. That was measured in the same 2026-10-16 run: after the writer's clear, the revisions were 1, 4, and the owner's export of both was empty. The flag has no effect on #1018's reasons above, which replace without a backup either way, or on any other copy failure, which still refuses. With the flag, the success warning and the after-clear failure text are the same as for #1018's reasons. - Cancellation: the copy is created inside a shielded scope, so its ID is always recorded (the PR #877 rule). The scope is bounded by _BACKUP_COPY_TIMEOUT (60 s, all attempts together), per CLAUDE.md's rule that a cancel waits for shielded work; a timeout is reported like a 5xx. Once the copy exists, a cancellation keeps it and logs a warning with its ID, since the doc may already be cleared and the call has no result left to report it in. - On success, the copy's removal and the webViewLink lookup run together.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: Measured on a 20 KB doc: files.copy 2.5–4.0 s, delete 0.8–1.3 s, so about 3.5–5 s added to every replace of a non-empty doc. The maintainer accepted this over options with no recovery path.

docs.title: Options rejected
docs.text:
• Name the pre-clear revision in the error. The revision is gone at once (table above).
  • Snapshot and re-insert on failure. Formatting, images, and tables don't round-trip (2026-10-04 triage).
  • Error message only, no recovery. A silently emptied doc is real data loss (2026-10-04 triage).
  • Backup behind an opt-out parameter. Considered on 2026-10-12. Not chosen: the default would have been on anyway, and the latency cost is accepted.

docs.title: Design: Google Doc Revisions as Markdown (export_revision)
docs.text: Status: Implemented. Issue #959. Live-verified against real Drive/Docs API calls via scratch scripts per CLAUDE.md's "Verify a ticket's API premise live" convention (2026-10-11).

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: export_revision handled only Sheets (XLSX export → cell values). list_revisions already listed Doc revisions, but nothing could read one, so "what changed in this Doc since revision N" couldn't be answered through the server. The issue asked for a Doc revision as Markdown "through the same converter get_doc_as_markdown uses", so that diffing two revisions' exports shows only the edit.

docs.title: The constraint
docs.text: get_doc_as_markdown walks documents().get() into the AST (doc-to-markdown.md). The Docs API reads only a document's current state; it has no revision parameter. Drive is the only source of an old revision, and only as a file from the revision's exportLinks. Measured on a Doc revision: text/markdown, text/x-markdown, text/html, text/plain, DOCX, ODT, RTF, PDF, EPUB, and a zipped HTML.

docs.title: Options measured
docs.text:
Each option was run against the same Doc, written through write_doc_content with headings, bold and italic, inline code, a fenced code block, a blockquote, nested ordered/bulleted lists, task items, a table, an image, and heading links.

  1. Drive's own text/markdown export. Lossy: inline code became plain text, the fenced code block became soft-broken plain lines, the blockquote became a plain paragraph, a nested bullet inside a numbered list became a separate numbered item with a literal \-, and the image was inlined as a base64 data: URI (10KB for one small logo). It's a different dialect from get_doc_as_markdown, and a much less faithful one.
  2. text/html export → this project's html_parser → AST. Google's export carries styling in CSS classes (.c3{font-weight:700}), which html_parser doesn't read, so bold, italic and code fonts would be lost without a CSS resolver. Importing that HTML back into a Doc (to reuse the Docs-side converter) was also measured: it split the code block into one fence per line and turned every list item after the blockquote into a quote.
  3. DOCX export → import as a temporary Google Doc → document_to_ast → ast_to_markdown. The output was identical to get_doc_as_markdown on the live Doc, except for the two import-specific values below. The zipped-HTML export can't be imported (400).

Chosen: (3). It is the same converter, not an equivalent one, so everything get_doc_as_markdown supports and documents carries over unchanged.

docs.title: What differs on every import, and how it's made stable
docs.text:
Measured across two imports of the same DOCX:

  • Inline image contentUri. A new URL each import; the image bytes are identical (same SHA-256). _stabilize_images fetches each image (concurrency 8) while the temporary Doc still exists and replaces its contentUri with image:sha256-<first 16 hex digits>, so an unchanged image doesn't show in a diff and a changed one does. A failed fetch renders image:unavailable. No viewable URL is returned: PR #988's QA round found the temporary Doc's image URLs 404 (anonymously and authenticated) once it's deleted, so a returned URL would be dead on arrival. (One earlier probe got a 200 right after deletion; it doesn't hold.)
  • Heading IDs and the document ID. Every heading gets a new headingId, and doc_to_ast._link_url rebuilds an ID-only heading link (the kind the Docs UI creates) as a URL containing the temporary Doc's ID. That changes on every export and points at a deleted Doc. _stabilize_internal_links rewrites a heading link to #<slug>, using anchors.py's GitHub-style slug with -1/-2 duplicate suffixes, so the link survives a round trip through the write side's anchor resolver. The slug list holds only paragraphs that render as Markdown headings, classified by doc_to_ast._paragraph_to_node itself (Heading, or a TITLE/SUBTITLE NamedBlock): a bulleted heading renders as a list item and a heading in a table cell as cell text, and counting them shifted every later duplicate's suffix onto the wrong heading (PR #988 QA round 1). A link to a heading that doesn't render as one is dropped, following the project's rule that a wrong link is worse than none.
  • Bookmark links are dropped. A bookmark has no text to name it, and any #fragment made up for one can be fuzzy-matched by anchors.py to a heading when the Markdown is written back (#bookmark-1 → the second heading titled "Bookmark"; PR #988 QA round 1).
  • URL links written by this project's own write side are already absolute URLs and pass through unchanged.

docs.title: The temporary Doc
docs.text:
• Where it's created depends on the identity (#989), because the copy holds the revision's full content and the default folder's audience can differ from the source Doc's:
  • A user identity (OAuth, or ADC with user credentials) creates it in My Drive root, not the default folder, so the copy isn't shared with anyone.
  • A service account identity (lc.is_service_account_identity) creates it in the default folder (lc.folder_id). A service account has no My Drive storage, so only a configured Shared Drive works. The remaining exposure is documented in docs/known-limitations.md: the Shared Drive's members can open the copy while the export runs, a Content manager's copy sits in the trash for 30 days, and a failed cleanup leaves it live.

Rejected alternatives: the source Doc's parent folder matches the source's audience more closely, but the identity may not be able to write there. Restricting the copy's permissions after creation can't work on a Shared Drive, where member access is inherited. - A storageQuotaExceeded error on create renders with the shared _quota_error_text: "storage is full" for a user identity (a full My Drive), _SA_QUOTA_ERROR for a service account (#1009). - Uploaded resumable: Drive takes a multipart upload only up to 5 MB, and a revision with embedded images can exceed it. - Named export_revision temp (<file_id> r<revision_id>), so an orphan is identifiable. - Created inside anyio.CancelScope(shield=True), per CLAUDE.md's cancellation rule: a cancellation can't land after Drive created the Doc but before its ID is recorded. - Removed in a shielded finally: deleted when capabilities.canDelete allows it, else trashed (a Content manager on a Shared Drive can only trash, #876). The removal retries a 5xx or 429 (num_retries=3), since a failed removal leaves a copy of the revision in Drive. A failed removal never hides the export: the result gets a warning naming the Doc's ID. - Because it writes to Drive, export_revision is no longer annotated readOnlyHint; it's destructiveHint=False, since it changes nothing of the caller's. - About 5–6 seconds per call, measured, on top of the image fetches.

docs.title: Errors found while measuring
docs.text:
• The export endpoint answers rapid calls with HTTP 429 and an HTML page, without raising. The Sheets path handed that page straight to openpyxl. _fetch_revision_export checks the status for both paths.
  • Docs folds the latest revision into the next one while editing continues: revision 18 was listed, an edit 90 seconds later produced 19, and 18 then returned 404. A second run with a 5-minute gap merged 19 into 20 the same way. export_revision turns a "Revision not found" 404 into an error telling the caller to call list_revisions again. Any other 404, such as a bad file ID ("File not found"), is re-raised unchanged. A Doc created by Drive import keeps its import revision separate (as #814 measured).
  • revisions.list returns at most 200 revisions per page by default (discovery document), and list_revisions read only the first page. It now pages through every revision via the same _list_revisions helper sync_folder uses.
  • A Doc local_path is checked with response_limits.validate_local_destination before the export, so a bad destination fails before the temporary Doc round trip.

docs.title: Live verification
docs.text: Against a Doc imported through upload_file(convert_to_doc=True), then edited by inserting one word: exporting revision 1 (the import) and revision 2 and diffing the two markdown values gave exactly one changed line, the edited paragraph. On a write_doc_content Doc with every construct above plus two Setup headings linked by ID, the export matched get_doc_as_markdown except the image line and the two links (#setup, #setup-1). With the first Setup bulleted, it rendered as - Setup, the link to it was dropped, and the link to the second rendered as #setup.

docs.title: What this does NOT do
docs.text:
• Comments. They aren't part of a revision, so there's no include_comments.
  • Match get_doc_as_markdown byte for byte. Heading links and images differ by design (above). Diff a revision against another revision's export, not against the live Doc's get_doc_as_markdown.
  • Show an old revision's images. Only their hashes; see above.
  • Multi-tab documents: not measured. How Drive's DOCX export handles a Doc's extra tabs wasn't checked; document_to_ast reads only the imported Doc's body.

docs.title: Design: Docs → Markdown Export (get_doc_as_markdown)
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Issue #300, PR #591. Live-verified against real Docs/Drive API calls (headings, styled runs, nested/ordered/checked bullets, blockquotes, inline code, fenced code blocks, a colspan table, and open/resolved comment filtering) via scratch scripts per CLAUDE.md's "Verify a ticket's API premise live" convention. PR #591's QA round 1 (/code-review high + live QA against TC-DOC173–182) found three blocking correctness bugs the initial version's own live round trip hadn't exercised — merged-cell table corruption, an unescaped link URL, and unescaped leading block-marker text — detailed in "Merged (colspan/rowspan) table cells" and the escaping bullets below, fixed in the same PR, with TC-DOC183–185 added as permanent regression coverage. See docs/qa/tests/docs_content.md for the full QA checklist and results.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The Docs write side has full Markdown support (content_format='markdown' on create_doc/write_doc_content, create_doc_from_file) via a Markdown → HTML → AST → Docs API pipeline (see Markdown Support). Nothing mirrors this on the read side: get_doc_content returns plain text only, and export_file has no Markdown output format. A competitor server (taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp) has a get_doc_as_markdown tool; without an equivalent this project's Markdown story is write-only — a concrete, checkable gap flagged during v0.9 competitive positioning work (see issue #300's comment thread).

docs.title: Approach: Docs API → AST → Markdown (not HTML export + a conversion library)
docs.text:
Two approaches were considered:

  1. Docs API → this project's own AST (docs/ast.py) → Markdown. Walk documents().get() into the same node types the write pipeline already produces, then serialize that AST to Markdown — the read-side mirror of html_to_ast → ast_to_requests.
  2. export_file(export_format='html') → an HTML-to-Markdown library (e.g. markdownify, html2text). Reuse Docs' own HTML export.

Chosen: (1). Google's raw Docs HTML export is heavily styled — redundant inline <span style="..."> wrappers rather than semantic tags — and converting that cleanly to Markdown needs fragile cleanup heuristics. Building on the project's own AST instead means:

  • Reusing exactly the node types and mapping markdown-support.md already documents for the write direction, just inverted — no new intermediate representation to design or trust.
  • No new dependency (an HTML→Markdown library would have been one).
  • Symmetric code structure: doc_to_ast.py (Docs API → AST) sits next to html_parser.py (HTML → AST); ast_to_markdown.py (AST → Markdown) sits next to emitter.py (AST → Docs API requests).

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Full fidelity was chosen over an MVP subset, given issue #300's own elevated-priority framing (a competitive gap worth closing properly, not partially): headings, styled runs (bold, italic, strikethrough, links, inline code), nested/ordered/checked bullet lists, blockquotes (including nesting), inline code and fenced code blocks, images, tables (including nested tables, best-effort — see below), and an opt-in comments section.

Three gaps were kept as documented limitations, not implementation shortcuts — see docs/known-limitations.md's get_doc_as_markdown entry for the full writeup:

  • A table nested inside another table's cell — GFM pipe-table syntax has no way to express this at all, the read-side mirror of markdown-support.md's identical write-side gap.
  • Inline images resolve to Drive's temporary contentUri (expires ~30 min) — inherent to how Drive serves embedded image bytes, not something this tool controls.
  • Inline code vs. a fenced code block are represented identically in the Docs API (a run, or every run in a paragraph, styled font_family="Courier New" — see markdown-support.md's own write-side table). There's no other signal to tell them apart on read; see the heuristic below.

docs.title: doc_to_ast.py — walking documents().get() into the AST
docs.text:
• Bullet ordered/unordered and nesting depth: paragraph.bullet carries listId and nestingLevel but no preset field of its own — the same gap style.py's create_paragraph_bullets already solved by reading document["lists"][listId] ["listProperties"]["nestingLevels"][level] (glyphType present → ordered, glyphSymbol present → unordered). Reused verbatim here rather than re-deriving it.
  • Ordered-item numbers (#1208): Docs numbers a list by listId, so a table, quote, code block or paragraph between two items doesn't restart it. document_to_ast counts body items per listId and nesting level in document order (_ListCounter), clears the deeper levels' counts at each item (Docs restarts a sublist under every new parent item), offsets by the level's startNumber, and sets BulletItem.number. A startNumber of 0 counts as 1 only for lettered and Roman-numeral levels, as the API reference says; a decimal level numbers from 0. Table-cell items aren't counted: with cell paragraphs and body items on one listId, Docs' txt and HTML exports both number the body items after the table from the list's start (measured live, PR #1234 QA round 1). ast_to_markdown writes that number, so an item resuming a list after a table starts its Markdown list there (3. c). One exception: CommonMark lets an ordered list interrupt a paragraph only when it starts at 1, and a sublist's first line follows its parent item's text with just a newline, so a sublist whose first number isn't 1 writes 1. there rather than merging into the parent (- a 5. a1 would read as one item). A blank line would keep the number but make the parent list loose. An AST built by the write side has no number and still renders 1.. Writing a resumed list back still restarts it at 1 when a paragraph interrupts it, because the write side ignores a list's start number (#1118).
  • Checkbox state: the write side has no BULLET_CHECKBOX preset — it prepends a literal "☑ "/"☐ " glyph to the item's own text (see emitter.py's comment on this). Read-back detects that exact prefix on the item's first run and strips it back off, setting BulletItem.checked — a direct inverse, not a new convention.
  • Blockquote depth: emitter.py's _blockquote_style_request writes a specific indentStart (36pt × depth) + borderLeft. Read-back requires both to be present (borderLeft alone signals "this was our blockquote styling"; indentStart alone is ambiguous — plenty of ordinary paragraphs use indentation for unrelated reasons) and infers depth from round(indentStart / 36).
  • Blocks inside a list item (#1302, the inverse of #1094): the write side puts a block inside an item (a second paragraph, code, a quote, a heading, a rule's empty paragraph) after the item, unbulleted, with indentStart and indentFirstLine both at the item's text indent (its list level's indentStart) plus 36pt per quote level, and Docs keeps the list's numbering going past it. _ListItemContext reads that back: a non-bullet paragraph after an item, whose two indents are equal and land on the text indent of that item's level or a shallower one, gets that level as list_depth, and its quote depth counts from the text indent, not the margin (from the margin, a quote in an item at 72pt read as > >). The deepest matching level wins, and the block closes the levels deeper than it. The context keeps the listId open at each depth, since #1072 gives a sublist of the other type its own listId. Anything else, a paragraph at the margin or an item of a list that isn't open, ends the list. Some blocks wait instead of being placed at once: a table, which has no indent the API reports (checked live: an in-item table's JSON matches a margin table's); the empty unindented paragraph Docs puts before a table inserted in an item; and a quote whose indent also reads as a deeper quote at the margin (a quote in a top-level item is at 72pt, like a margin > >; PR #1311 QA round 1). A waiting block is inside an item when the list goes on: an item of a list open at its depth, a sublist nested under the last item, or a plainly in-item block. A table then takes the depth of the item that ends the wait, capped at the last item's (so a table after a sublist, before the parent's next item, is the parent's). Otherwise it stays outside, as read: a table at the margin, a quote at its margin depth. A block that ends a list's last item therefore reads as outside it (known-limitations.md). A margin table between two items comes back as outside too, because the write side splits the list there into two Docs lists (measured live).
  • Bulleted headings (#1302): a bulleted HEADING_N paragraph (what - # Title writes, #1094) reads back as a BulletItem with heading_level. Since it renders as a heading inside its item, markdown_export._rendered_heading_slugs counts it, like the write side's anchor resolver does. A checkbox item doesn't get one: GFM reads - [ ] ## Title as task text, so it would neither render nor take a slug as a heading (PR #1311 QA round 1).
  • Trailing paragraph newline: every paragraph's content ends with a " " in the Docs API's own representation. Stripped from the last Run once, dropping the Run entirely if that empties it — mirrors html_parser.py's own <pre>-close trailing-newline handling.
  • Soft breaks (#1057): a "\v" in any run is a line break inside the paragraph, whoever wrote it: emitter.py's code-block line breaks (#719) or insert_softbreak_paragraph in prose. _text_run_to_run reads it back as " ", the same character an explicit <br> produces on write. Only the raw-text views (get_doc_structure, find_in_doc) keep a prose soft break as "\v", via indices.decode_code_run_text.
  • Table cells are flat, not per-paragraph: Cell.children (ast.py) has no paragraph structure of its own — the write side never produces one (html_parser.py's table-cell handling treats a <td> as flat inline content). Multiple paragraphs within one live Docs table cell are read back joined by a literal " ", the same character an explicit <br> would have produced on write.
  • Merged (colspan/rowspan) table cells — phantom physical cells (PR #591 QA round 1): the first version built one Cell per raw tableCells[] JSON entry unconditionally. Live-confirmed this is wrong: a merged cell does NOT remove the physical entries it covers — the Docs API leaves an empty, ordinary-looking (columnSpan: 1, rowSpan: 1) phantom cell at every absorbed position, both within a colspan's own row and in every later row a rowspan reaches into (a colspan=2 header row actually has two physical tableCells[] entries, not one). There is no field marking a cell as "this is a phantom" — emitter.py's write-side _build_phantom_set/ _physical_to_ast_indices already established this same fact for the opposite direction (mapping a known AST onto live physical cells), but that logic can't be reused directly here since there's no target AST yet — building one is the job. The fix (_table_elem_to_ast) walks each row's physical cells in startIndex order, tracking which (row, col) positions an earlier real cell's own colspan/rowspan already claims; a physical cell landing on a claimed position is consumed (advances past it) but not added to the AST, exactly mirroring the write side's phantom-set concept computed forward instead of backward. Before this fix, a colspan=2 header exported as a 3-column table (TC-DOC177, confirmed live); a rowspan=2 cell's covered row silently lost its own real trailing cell entirely (no test coverage existed for this case at all — added as TC-DOC183).

docs.title: ast_to_markdown.py — serializing the AST
docs.text:
• CommonMark emphasis-delimiter whitespace rule: a naive f"**{text}**" wrapper breaks when text has trailing whitespace ("**Bold **" doesn't close per CommonMark's flanking-delimiter rule — it renders as literal asterisks). Caught live during round-trip verification, not by the initial hand-written test fixtures. Fixed by moving leading/trailing whitespace outside the style markers before wrapping.
  • Fenced code block vs. inline code: since the Docs representation can't distinguish them (see Scope above), the heuristic is: a Paragraph node renders as a fenced block only when every run in it is code-styled; a paragraph mixing code-styled and plain runs renders each code-styled run as an inline `span` instead. Confirmed live that this correctly distinguishes a genuine ```code block``` paragraph from `inline code` sitting next to ordinary text in the same paragraph — the one case it can't resolve (a paragraph containing only a single inline code span, nothing else) is the genuinely ambiguous case documented above, not a bug in the heuristic. One exception (#951): a fenced block's content is literal and can't carry a link, so an all-code paragraph with any linked run renders as inline code spans (each line its own span, joined by <br>) instead of a fence, keeping the link. Only a link that actually renders counts: a linked run that is only line breaks renders as bare <br>, so it keeps the fence (PR #976 QA round 1). A linked image doesn't trigger this either, since images render outside the fence anyway.
  • Line breaks in plain text (#1057): a " " inside a non-code run renders as <br>, the same as in a code run or a table cell. A raw newline would be a Markdown soft break, joining the lines, and could start a new block mid-paragraph ("# x" on the next line). A trailing backslash hard break would end an ATX heading or a list item's line instead. A run's edges, up to its outermost line break and including any whitespace beside it, render outside its link, emphasis, and code span (_split_edge_breaks, shared by plain and code runs; a space beside the break kept it inside the link until PR #1088 QA round 1).
  • Linked images (#951): Docs puts an image's link on its inlineObjectElement's own textStyle.link, the same as a text run (confirmed live). doc_to_ast reads it into Image.link_url, and every image renders through _render_image as [![alt](src)](url), in ordinary text, a code paragraph, and a table cell alike. The write side sets it too (#977; see image-conversion.md), so a linked image round-trips.
  • Same-document links (PR #976 QA round 1): Docs reports a link to a heading or bookmark by ID with no url (confirmed live for a heading: {"headingId": "h.x"}, on a text run and an image alike). doc_to_ast._link_url, shared by both, rebuilds it as https://docs.google.com/document/d/<id>/edit?tab=<tab>#heading=<id> (or #bookmark=), the form get_doc_structure's docstring documents. The tab comes from the newer heading/bookmark object's tabId, else t.0. The bookmark form follows the Docs UI's own URLs; the API can't create a bookmark, so it isn't verified live.
  • Code delimiters (#923, #940, #938): a code span's content is literal, so the serializer can only pick a delimiter and padding. A fenced block's fence and an inline span's delimiter are one backtick longer than the longest backtick run in the content (fences at least 3). An inline span is padded with one space a side when its content starts or ends with a backtick, or starts and ends with a space (CommonMark strips one space from each end in that case). Adjacent code runs sharing a link merge into one span, since two spans side by side would read as one. An inline code run's line breaks become <br> between separate spans: a span can't hold a line break, and a raw newline could start a new block. In a table cell, a code line containing | renders as raw HTML <code>, because the GFM \| escape shows its backslash in renderers that don't implement it. Text inside raw HTML is still parsed as Markdown, so every ASCII punctuation character in that line becomes a numeric entity (|, *, \, ...). Line breaks at either end of a linked code run go outside the link. Because the exporter writes its own <br>/<code> HTML, plain text escapes ~, a < that could open a tag, and an & that starts an entity, so typed markup can't pass for exporter markup. The export tests check these against a strict CommonMark parser (markdown-it-py), since Python-Markdown strips whitespace in code spans and closes a fence only on an exact-length match.
  • Tight vs. loose lists: consecutive BulletItem nodes are joined with a single " " rather than the " " used between other block types — CommonMark still parses a blank-line-separated run of list items as one list either way (just "loose", wrapped in <p> tags), so this is a readability polish on the output, not a correctness fix. Caught during live round-trip verification (the initial version produced a blank line between every single list item, nested or not).
  • Blocks inside a list item (#1302): a node with a list_depth is indented to its item's content column, the width of the item's own indent and marker (_item_prefix), so CommonMark keeps it in the item and the list going past it. _OpenItems records the column of the last item at each depth. A quoted item's quote markers come before its indent (> - a). A block inside it is inside that quote too, whatever depth it reads with (a table reads none, and neither does the empty paragraph Docs puts before one), so the item's quote levels go outside the indent and only the block's extra levels inside, and the blank lines around it carry the item's levels (>) so the quote doesn't end (PR #1311 QA round 1). A bulleted heading renders as - ## Title. Every other item's text now goes through _escape_leading_block_marker, since text after the marker starts the item's first block: - # a is a heading inside the item, and - 1. a a sublist.
  • Tables: the first row is always rendered as the header row — GFM pipe-table syntax structurally requires exactly one header + separator row, and the Docs API has no per-row "is this the header" signal to read back (unlike the AST's own is_header_row, which only ever gets set on the write side from an HTML <thead>/<th>). A merged cell (colspan/ rowspan > 1) renders its text in the first spanned column and blank cells for the rest, reusing emitter.py's own _build_phantom_set to find which (row, col) positions a rowspan covers — the closest a pipe table (no native merge concept) can represent one.
  • Comments: include_comments=True fetches every comment via the same Drive comments resource list_doc_comments uses (paginated, unlike list_doc_comments' single-page default), filters to non-resolved ones (a resolved comment's discussion is already settled — not scoped as diff-worthy content in an export), and appends a ## Comments section with each comment's author, quoted anchor text, content, and replies.
  • Link/image URL escaping (PR #591 QA round 1): run.link_url/image.src were interpolated directly into [text](url)/![alt](url) with no escaping. Live-confirmed a real-world URL containing an unmatched ) (e.g. .../wiki/Foo_(bar)) breaks CommonMark's bare-link-destination parsing, which requires balanced parentheses. Fixed via _md_link_dest: a destination containing whitespace or any parenthesis is wrapped in CommonMark's <...> angle-bracket destination form instead, which has no such restriction (only a literal <, >, or backslash inside still needs escaping). A plain URL with none of those characters is left bare, unchanged.
  • Leading block-marker escaping (PR #591 QA round 1): _MD_ESCAPE only escaped \ ` * _ [ ] — not a line-leading #, >, -/*/+, or an ordered-list N./N). Live-confirmed a plain paragraph reading literally "1. Not actually a list item" or "# Not a heading either" round-tripped unescaped and any CommonMark parser reinterprets it as a real ordered-list item or ATX heading. Fixed via _escape_leading_block_marker, applied to plain Paragraph rendering (not Heading/NamedBlock, whose text follows their own # prefix and is never re-parsed as a new block; a list item's text is escaped too since #1302, see above) and applied before any blockquote "> " wrapping (a "> #" line is parsed as a heading nested inside the blockquote by CommonMark, so the escape has to happen first, not after). One CommonMark subtlety this surfaced: digits are not in CommonMark's escapable ASCII-punctuation set, so \1 is not a valid escape and renders as a literal backslash — the fix escapes the trailing ./) punctuation after the digit run instead (1\.), which is the actual mechanism that neutralizes ordered-list-marker detection.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
1. uv run python -m pytest tests/ — full suite passes, plus tests/test_docs_markdown_export.py (unit coverage for doc_to_ast.py, ast_to_markdown.py, and the tool itself).
  2. Live round-trip via a scratch script (mcp_gee_sweet.auth._oauth_creds() + googleapiclient.discovery.build, per CLAUDE.md's documented same-session verification method — the jay MCP server only serves the main checkout's installed code, not an in-progress worktree change): built a real Doc through the existing write pipeline from a Markdown source covering every construct in scope, then read it back through get_doc_as_markdown and diffed the output against the original source. Caught and fixed two real bugs (the emphasis-whitespace CommonMark violation and the tight-list join) this way — neither was caught by the hand-written unit tests, which had no way to independently verify what the live Docs API actually returns for bullet.nestingLevel, lists[...].glyphType, or tableCellStyle.columnSpan/rowSpan shapes.
  3. Live-verified comment export separately: created open and resolved comments (with a reply) on a real Doc, confirmed only the open one appears in the rendered ## Comments section.
  4. See docs/qa/tests/docs_content.md for the QA checklist test cases covering this tool (TC-DOC173–185).
  5. PR #591 QA round 1 (/code-review high + live QA against TC-DOC173–182) caught three blocking bugs the round above's own live round trip hadn't exercised — a single Markdown source covering every construct doesn't guarantee coverage of every edge case within a construct (a merged table cell specifically, a URL with parens, plain text that happens to look like a block marker). Fixed and re-verified live via the same scratch-script method against the exact reported repros (a colspan header, a rowspan second row, a parenthesized Wikipedia-style URL, and both flagged plain-paragraph texts) — all four now round-trip correctly. TC-DOC183–185 added so this bug class has permanent regression coverage rather than living only in a PR comment thread.

docs.title: Design: Docs AST Pipeline (Phase 2)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-06-17 (updated 2026-06-18) Issue: #87 Status: complete (Phase 2 implemented; AST schema is final)

Point-in-time implementation design — captures the data model, file layout, algorithm choices, and scope decisions as they were made. See decision-docs-formatting.md for the architectural "why".

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
docs.py has a monolithic _DocParser (HTMLParser subclass) that simultaneously parses HTML and emits Docs API requests. It has several known bugs:

  • #41 — <h2>–<h6> all collapse to HEADING_3
  • #65 — <th> cells not bolded
  • #66 — width on <col>/<td> ignored; no updateTableColumnProperties emitted
  • #67 — colspan/rowspan ignored; no mergeTableCells emitted
  • #69 — inline formatting (<b>, <i>, <u>, <s>, <a>) inside table cells is lost

Adding fixes piecemeal would make the parser more complex. This design replaces it with a three-stage pipeline: HTML → AST → Docs API requests.

docs.title: File Layout
docs.text:
src/mcp_gee_sweet/tools/docs.py        ← deleted
src/mcp_gee_sweet/tools/docs/
    __init__.py     — register(), _html_to_doc_requests wrapper, _html_to_text (preserves test imports)
    ast.py          — comprehensive AST dataclasses
    html_parser.py  — html_to_ast(html: str) -> list[DocNode]
    emitter.py      — ast_to_requests(nodes, start_index) -> (requests, list[Table])
                      fill_tables(docs_service, doc_id, tables: list[Table]) -> None

tools/__init__.py does from . import docs; docs.register(tool) — unchanged; the package satisfies it. Test file imports from mcp_gee_sweet.tools.docs import _html_to_doc_requests, _html_to_text — satisfied by __init__.py.

docs.title: AST Node Design
docs.text:
The AST is designed as the final product — the complete schema covers all Docs API content-formatting operations. Phase 3 styling fields are present as None defaults; the emitter ignores them until Phase 3 adds a theme_applier.py. This mirrors the ChartSpec decision (PR #84): design fully now, implement incrementally.

@dataclass
class RGBColor:
    red: float
    green: float
    blue: float


@dataclass
class ParagraphStyle:
    alignment: str | None = None  # LEFT, CENTER, RIGHT, JUSTIFIED
    indent_start: float | None = None  # pt
    indent_end: float | None = None  # pt
    indent_first_line: float | None = None  # pt
    space_above: float | None = None  # pt
    space_below: float | None = None  # pt
    line_spacing: float | None = None  # 100=single, 150=1.5×, 200=double
    page_break_before: bool | None = None
    keep_lines_together: bool | None = None
    keep_with_next: bool | None = None


@dataclass
class Run:
    text: str
    bold: bool | None = None
    italic: bool | None = None
    underline: bool | None = None
    strikethrough: bool | None = None
    link_url: str | None = None
    font_size: float | None = None  # Phase 3 only
    foreground_color: RGBColor | None = None  # Phase 3 only
    font_family: str | None = None  # Phase 3 only
    background_color: RGBColor | None = None  # Phase 3 only; text highlight
    baseline_offset: str | None = None  # Phase 3 only; SUPERSCRIPT, SUBSCRIPT
    small_caps: bool | None = None  # Phase 3 only


@dataclass
class Cell:
    runs: list[Run]
    colspan: int = 1
    rowspan: int = 1  # AST only; emitter deferred (see below)
    is_header: bool = False  # <th> → runs get bold=True
    content_alignment: str | None = None  # TOP, MIDDLE, BOTTOM
    background_color: RGBColor | None = None  # Phase 3 only
    padding_top: float | None = None  # Phase 3 only
    padding_right: float | None = None  # Phase 3 only
    padding_bottom: float | None = None  # Phase 3 only
    padding_left: float | None = None  # Phase 3 only
    border_color: RGBColor | None = None  # Phase 3 only
    border_width: float | None = None  # Phase 3 only
    border_dash_style: str | None = None  # Phase 3 only


@dataclass
class Row:
    cells: list[Cell]
    minimum_height: float | None = None  # pt
    is_header_row: bool = False


@dataclass
class Table:
    rows: list[Row]
    col_widths: list[float | None] = field(default_factory=list)  # Phase 2
    table_alignment: str | None = None  # ALIGNED_START, CENTER, ALIGNED_END


@dataclass
class Heading:
    level: int  # 1–6, maps directly to HEADING_1…HEADING_6
    runs: list[Run]
    paragraph_style: ParagraphStyle | None = None


@dataclass
class Paragraph:
    runs: list[Run]
    paragraph_style: ParagraphStyle | None = None


@dataclass
class BulletItem:
    runs: list[Run]
    depth: int = 0
    ordered: bool = False
    paragraph_style: ParagraphStyle | None = None


@dataclass
class NamedBlock:
    style_type: str  # TITLE, SUBTITLE, NORMAL_TEXT
    runs: list[Run]
    paragraph_style: ParagraphStyle | None = None


DocNode = Union[Heading, Paragraph, BulletItem, Table, NamedBlock]

Out of scope for the AST: images, page headers/footers, footnotes, charts (separate ChartSpec path), named ranges, table of contents.

NamedBlock: covers TITLE and SUBTITLE named styles not expressible as Heading(level=1–6). html_parser.py does not emit NamedBlock yet; it will be added when the HTML subset is extended (e.g. a data-style="title" attribute convention, or a dedicated <title> wrapper element).

ParagraphStyle: shared across Heading, Paragraph, BulletItem, and NamedBlock. The html_parser ignores it for now (HTML has no structural equivalent for most of these properties). Phase 3 theme application will set these fields via the theme_applier.py.

docs.title: html_parser.py
docs.text:
html_to_ast(html: str) -> list[DocNode]

Standard-library HTMLParser subclass. Tracks tag context and emits AST nodes on end-tags.

docs.title: Block elements → AST nodes
docs.text: HTML AST node Notes <h1>–<h6> Heading(level=1–6, runs=...) Fixes #41 <p> Paragraph(runs=...) <li> BulletItem(runs=..., ordered=...) ordered from enclosing <ol>/<ul> <table> Table(rows=..., col_widths=...) <th> Cell(is_header=True, runs=[Run(text, bold=True)]) Fixes #65 <td colspan="N"> Cell(colspan=N, runs=...) Fixes #67 (colspan; rowspan deferred)

docs.title: Inline elements → Run fields
docs.text:
Tracked as a stack of active formatters. Each active formatter contributes a field to the next Run emitted.

HTML Run field <b>, <strong> bold=True <i>, <em> italic=True <u> underline=True <s> strikethrough=True <a href="url"> link_url=url

Inline elements work inside <td>, <th>, <p>, <li>, and headings — fixing #69 for table cells.

docs.title: Column widths
docs.text:
<col width="N"> or <td width="N"> → Table.col_widths[i]

  • Numeric value assumed to be pixels; converted: pt = px * 72 / 96
  • Percentage widths skipped (can't resolve without page width)

Fixes #66.

docs.title: Deferred
docs.text:
• Rowspan — rowspan attr captured into Cell.rowspan but emitter does not yet emit mergeTableCells for row merges; the phantom-cell mapping after merge is complex. Follow-on ticket.
  • Nested tables — <table> inside <td> is out of scope (#68). Recursive AST node exists; multi-pass insert deferred.

docs.title: ast_to_requests(nodes, start_index=1) → (requests, tables)
docs.text:
Returns (phase1_requests, list[Table]) where tables are the Table AST nodes (no longer list[list[list[str]]]).

Phase 1 requests built:

  1. One insertText for all non-table text (concatenated with \n separators)
  2. For each heading: updateParagraphStyle(HEADING_{level}) + deleteParagraphBullets
  3. For each paragraph: deleteParagraphBullets
  4. For each bullet: createParagraphBullets (preset varies by ordered)
  5. For each link_url run in non-table content: updateTextStyle(link=...)
  6. insertTable requests in reverse order (last-to-first preserves earlier positions)

Table placeholders (#1097). insertTable gives the table its left indent, and every empty cell its text style, from the paragraph at the insertion point. The Docs API has no field to reset the table's indent afterward (it shows only as margin-left in the HTML export). Inserted at the start of the next block, a table after a list or quote was indented to it, and one before a bold, Courier New, or heading-styled first character put that style in every cell. So step 1's text holds an empty placeholder paragraph at each table's position. After the bullet pass, _table_placeholder_requests resets it to plain: deleteParagraphBullets, then updateParagraphStyle with fields: "*" (NORMAL_TEXT, every other field at its default), then updateTextStyle with fields: "*". It runs after the bullet pass because a table between two same-preset list items sits inside their one createParagraphBullets range: the run skips Table nodes, so both items stay one list, and the placeholder loses its bullet afterward (PR #1201 QA round 1). A table inside a quote (Table.blockquote_depth, set by the parser) gets the quote's indent on its placeholder, 36pt per level, and no border. It still doesn't count as quoted for separators or quote-edge spacing. The table is inserted at the placeholder, which insertTable pushes to just after the table, and a deleteContentRange right after the insertTable removes it, at position + _inserted_table_length(rows, columns). Deleting the paragraph after a table is allowed; only the one before it is structurally required (see known-limitations.md). _positional_insert_tail_start counts the delete as part of the positional pass by its place right after an insertTable.

docs.title: fill_tables(docs_service, doc_id, tables) → None
docs.text:
Replaces the old _fill_tables / _fill_table_cell_requests_from_doc.

1. Re-fetch doc → get live table structure
2. If any cell has colspan > 1:
   a. Emit mergeTableCells batch for all such cells (across all tables)
   b. Re-fetch doc → get post-merge cell positions
3. For all cells across all tables, sorted HIGH→LOW by paragraphStartIndex:
   a. insertText with joined run text
   b. For each run with a styling field (bold/italic/etc.):
      updateTextStyle at [para_start + offset, para_start + offset + len(run.text)]
4. If any table has col_widths:
   Emit updateTableColumnProperties per column with a non-None width

Index arithmetic for styled runs:

offset = 0
for run in cell.runs:
    run_start = paragraphStartIndex + offset
    run_end   = run_start + len(run.text)
    if run has any style field:
        emit updateTextStyle([run_start, run_end], ...)
    offset += len(run.text)

All fill requests sorted high→low by insertText location index to prevent shifting.

New tests to add:

docs.title: Scope Boundaries
docs.text: Feature In Phase 2? Notes Correct heading levels h1–h6 Yes #41 <th> bold Yes #65 Inline formatting in cells Yes #69 Column widths Yes #66 Colspan Yes #67 partial Rowspan Yes Cell.rowspan in AST; #91 added mergeTableCells in emitter Nested tables Yes Cell.nested_table: Table \| None; #92 added stages 3+5 in fill_tables. Superseded 2026-07-06 by Cell.children: list[Run \| Table] — see "Nested Table Rewrite" below Phase 3 styling fields (colors, fonts) No In AST as None; emitter ignores them <ol> ordered bullets Yes BulletItem.ordered → different bullet preset

docs.title: Nested Table Design (#92, superseded 2026-07-06 by #108/#275 — see below)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-06-19

A <table> inside a <td> is now supported (one level of nesting).

docs.title: Parser changes (html_parser.py)
docs.text:
_AstParser previously guarded <table> pushes with if self._table_depth == 1. Removing that guard means a new _TableBuilder is pushed for every <table>, regardless of depth. On </table>, the completed Table is routed based on depth: - depth == 1 → append to _nodes (document-level, existing behaviour) - depth > 1 → assign to self._table_stack[-1]._current_nested_table (new: parent cell accumulates it)

_TableBuilder.end_cell was extended to pass nested_table=self._current_nested_table to Cell and reset it to None. All <tr> / <td> / <th> handlers already reference self._table_stack[-1], so they automatically operate on the innermost builder — no other changes needed.

docs.title: Emitter changes (emitter.py)
docs.text:
fill_tables gained two new phases:

Phase 3 — insert nested table shells: _build_nested_table_inserts(doc_tables, ast_tables) iterates outer cells that have nested_table set and emits insertTable requests at each cell's paragraphStartIndex. Requests are sorted HIGH→LOW so earlier insertions don't shift later indices. Re-fetches live doc after.

Phase 5 — fill nested cells: after outer cell text is filled (phase 4), indices shift. A second re-fetch is performed, then _collect_nested_table_pairs(doc_tables, ast_tables) traverses cell content to find the nested table element and pairs it with the AST Table. _build_fill_requests reuses the same logic as outer cells.

docs.title: Known limitations (first pass, now historical — see rewrite below)
docs.text:
• Cells with nested_table should not also contain text runs (runs are dropped silently) — fixed and superseded, see below
  • One level of nesting only (table-in-table-in-table not supported) — fixed and superseded, see below
  • No colspan/rowspan inside nested tables — still true
  • No col_widths on nested tables — still true

docs.title: Nested Table Rewrite: Cell.children + recursive fill (#108, #275)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-07-06

The single-nested_table-field design above had two real defects, both found while investigating #108:

  1. Text sharing a cell with a nested table was silently corrupted. Root cause was in the parser, not the emitter: _AstParser._run_buf/_pending_runs are shared, unscoped state across nesting levels — opening a nested <table> never flushed them, so text typed before the nested table bled into the nested table's own first cell instead of staying with the outer cell.
  2.
