docs.text: Item Where Up-front scoped write approval; one write first per shard aziz.md preconditions (this PR) Session-budget plan; resume with SendMessage; Resource usage section aziz.md preconditions (this PR) Credential/secret rule; shared shard-rules file aziz.md step 5 (this PR) PR-search date from the last release tag, skipping hotfix tags aziz.md step 1 (this PR) Lane reuse via a src/ diff; git worktree list instead of git -C aziz.md precondition + step 3 (this PR) Warm the server before the barrier loop; printf shell form run.md concurrency section (this PR) Worktree .env and token pre-flight aziz.md step 1 (this PR) Make the compile script a standard release step #1067 Track release-QA spend over time #1068 Product findings #1052–#1060

docs.title: Running QA
docs.text: This file contains the conductor prompt. Paste it into a Claude session that has the mcp-gee-sweet MCP server connected. Claude will read your fixtures, execute every test case against the live server, record outcomes, and save a results report.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. mcp-gee-sweet server running and connected to this Claude session
  2. docs/qa/.env exists and is filled in (see setup.md if not)
  3. For calendar tests: the calendar in .env is accessible to the authenticated account
  4. If using Playwright for visual verification: Playwright MCP connected and a valid token.json present (see docs/qa/playwright_oauth.md)

docs.title: How to start
docs.text:
Copy everything in the Conductor prompt section below and paste it into the Claude chat.

To run a single category instead of the full suite, add after the prompt: "Only run the tests/drive_files.md file" (or whichever category you want).

To resume an interrupted run: paste the prompt and add "Resume from docs/qa/results/<date>-partial.md".

docs.title: Playwright verification
docs.text: Playwright is optional at the run level. Whether a test requires visual verification is a per-test-case decision, marked in the test file itself with **Playwright: required**. The conductor follows those tags — it does not decide at runtime which tests get visual verification.

docs.title: Tiers (authoring reference)
docs.text:
Three tiers replace the earlier "visual whenever visual is possible" guidance (which produced near-zero-signal screenshots on read-only/error-path/count tests — see the v0.8.0 retro's finding #1). Only Required corresponds to an actual tag on the test case; Spot-check and Skip are authoring/runtime guidance, not tags.

Tier When to use Tag the test case? Examples Required The check verifies a mutation with a visual signature the API-level response can't fully confirm — formatting, hyperlinks, images, charts, layout, table-cell run formatting, create/delete/move confirmed in UI, cache invalidation checks Yes — **Playwright: required** on the Prompt line format_cells, freeze, merge, add_chart, delete_file, write_doc_content tables, create_event, style_doc_range (font size, hyperlinks) Spot-check An API response looks unexpected, or a cache discrepancy is suspected — a runtime judgment call during the run, not a fixed property of the test case No Any time the API says success but behavior seems wrong Skip Read-only, error paths, count/pagination, cache-hit-only, unit-tested paths, or a mutation whose visual signature the API response already fully confirms (e.g. plain-paragraph bold/italic runs, checkbox glyphs as literal text, namedStyleType, Drive file metadata) No get_sheet_data, list_events, error returns, create_folder/rename_file (confirmed via list_files/get_file_metadata instead — see Drive fixture note below), row/column counts

A test case's Checks list is the source of truth: if every listed check is answerable from the tool's own response (or a follow-up read-only call), it's Skip even if the mutation sounds visual. If at least one check can only be answered by looking at the rendered result, it's Required. When in doubt, prefer Required — the cost of an unnecessary screenshot is lower than a silently-unverified regression.

Drive mutations are Skip by default policy, not by oversight. Drive's UI mostly just reflects API-returned metadata directly (file name, mimeType, trashed state, parent), so list_files/get_file_metadata is the confirmation source rather than a screenshot — this is documented per-case in docs/qa/tests/drive_*.md Result entries (e.g. TC-D at drive_files.md's create_shortcut test, which uses the shortcut mimeType instead of a screenshot). Permission/sharing changes follow the same policy — see "Known limitations" below.

docs.title: How it works (authoring reference)
docs.text:
When a test case is tagged **Playwright: required**, after the tool call the conductor:

  • Sheets — navigates to https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{SPREADSHEET_ID}/edit and snapshots the affected cells
  • Docs — navigates to https://docs.google.com/document/d/{DOC_ID}/edit and snapshots the affected section
  • Drive — navigates to https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/{FOLDER_ID} (or the file's web_link) and confirms the change
  • Calendar — navigates to https://calendar.google.com and confirms the event appears or is gone

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Footer / header content — Google Docs renders headers and footers outside the main document canvas. For short documents window.scrollTo does not bring the footer into the viewport. When a test involves create_footer or create_header, use the API response as confirmation; a Playwright snapshot of the body is still useful but will not show the footer content.
  • Permission changes — sharing confirmations are not visible in the Drive UI without navigating to the file's "Share" dialog. Use list_permissions API response as the confirmation source for share tests.
  • Charts left on the Sales sheet — every add_chart case in docs/qa/tests/sheets_charts.md now has a Cleanup step that deletes its chart with deleteEmbeddedObject, so a full run leaves no chart behind (the v0.9.2 pass deleted all 13 it created). Before that cleanup existed, charts piled up over rows 1–22 of Sales and hid cells from screenshots. If a run is interrupted before its cleanup, delete the leftover chart the same way before relying on a screenshot of that region. For exact geometry or borders, get_sheet_data(..., range=<affected range>, include_grid_data=True) is more precise than a screenshot in any case: rowMetadata/columnMetadata give each row's and column's pixelSize, and each cell's userEnteredFormat.borders/effectiveFormat.borders gives the style and color of each edge.

docs.title: Verifying Playwright is signed into the right account
docs.text:
"Connected," "signed in," and "signed in as the account that owns the fixtures" are three different states, and only the third makes **Playwright: required** cases meaningful. Playwright MCP keeps a separate persistent browser profile per working directory — the main checkout, each .claude/worktrees/* slot, and every other project on the machine each get their own login. Any one of them can be signed into a Google account that isn't the one owning the mcp-gee-sweet-shared Shared Drive fixtures (see setup.md), or into none at all.

The check, run once before the first **Playwright: required** case in any QA pass (lane QA or release pass):

  1. Get the fixture doc's real title via this role's own get_file_metadata(TEST_DOC_ID).
  2. browser_navigate to https://docs.google.com/document/d/<TEST_DOC_ID>/edit (under the Playwright mutex below, if other shards may be running).
  3. Pass only if the page title contains that exact document name.
  4. Fail on either:
  5. a redirect to accounts.google.com — the profile isn't signed in;
  6. the URL staying on docs.google.com but the page showing "You need access" / "Request access," or a generic "Google Docs" title — the profile is signed into the wrong account. This one is easy to misread as a pass, since there's no sign-in redirect; it's what the old "not a sign-in page" check let through (confirmed 2026-09-23: a lane QA session's browser opened on the personal account instead of the Workspace-org one that owns the fixtures).

On a fail, stop and tell the user which session's browser needs signing in, and to which account (the one that owns the Shared Drive fixtures). Then wait. The sign-in persists in that slot's profile, so this is a one-time fix per slot. Don't fall back to API-only verification for Playwright-required cases unless the user explicitly says to — that's the silent degradation retro-v0.9.0.md describes. Once the user says it's fixed, re-run the check before continuing.

docs.title: Coordinating Playwright across parallel shards
docs.text:
A single Playwright MCP instance is one browser tab. If a QA run is split across multiple agents (e.g. one per domain), any two shards that both hit **Playwright: required** cases at the same time will fight over that tab — one shard's navigation clobbers the snapshot the other was about to take. Spinning up a second authenticated Playwright instance to get true parallelism is possible but costly: the browser profile needs its own logged-in Google session (see playwright_oauth.md), so a second instance means cloning that profile rather than just adding a server entry.

Cheaper fix: a filesystem mutex around Playwright usage, since only one shard needs the tab at a time and each hold is brief (one navigate + snapshot, not the whole run).

  • Lock path: /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-playwright.lock (a directory, not a file — mkdir is atomic on POSIX, so no separate locking library is needed).
  • Acquire: before a Playwright tool call, attempt mkdir /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-playwright.lock. Success means the lock is held — proceed. Failure (already exists) means another shard holds it — back off (a few seconds) and retry.
  • Release: immediately after the snapshot for that one test case, rmdir /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-playwright.lock. Don't hold the lock across an entire test file — only around the actual Playwright step.
  • Stale-lock recovery: if the lock directory's mtime is older than ~120s, treat it as abandoned (the shard that created it likely crashed or was killed) — remove it and re-acquire rather than waiting forever.
  • When it's not needed: a single-shard full run (no parallel agents) never contends with itself — skip the lock entirely in that case.

Give each parallel shard's conductor prompt this protocol explicitly (path, acquire/release commands, backoff, staleness threshold) rather than assuming priority ordering or hoping timing works out.

docs.title: Running true-concurrency test cases
docs.text:
A single MCP client session awaits each tool result before issuing the next, so it can never hold two requests to one server process in flight at once. A handful of test cases need genuinely simultaneous requests and are otherwise perpetually skipped:

TC File What it needs TC-I24 tests/infra.md Two distinct get_sheet_data calls (different spreadsheets) firing at the same instant — checks the shared startup httplib2 transport isn't corrupted across worker threads (issue #183) TC-I02 tests/infra.md A write (update_cells) and a read (get_sheet_data) on the same spreadsheet firing at the same instant — checks SQLite WAL lets the read proceed during the write with no locking error (issue #234)

TC-R36/TC-R37 (tests/sheets_read.md) look similar but are within-call concurrency (get_multiple_sheet_data/get_multiple_spreadsheet_summary gather() several .execute() calls inside one tool call) — a single session already exercises them. They don't need this procedure; just re-run them normally during the pass and record a fresh Result. Only the cross-session cases (TC-I24, TC-I02) need what follows.

docs.title: Mechanism: two subagents, one server, a mkdir barrier
docs.text:
Aziz (never a lane session — this runs during the release pass, see .claude/team-roles/aziz.md) spawns two Agent-tool subagents — real subagents, which inherit this session's already-connected MCP servers; not Agent-View spawns, which don't. Both subagents point at the same server prefix. Prefer mcp__mcp-gee-sweet-kai-sa__ — it runs the main-checkout (release-candidate) code, not a worktree copy. A lane prefix (mcp__mcp-gee-sweet-sky__ / -kit__) also works if the main-checkout server isn't available, but only after that worktree is reset to the release commit; note the substitution in the run file.

Per iteration, the two subagents rendezvous at a filesystem barrier so both .execute() calls hit the wire within a few milliseconds of each other:

  • Barrier dir: /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-qa-barrier (created once by Aziz before spawning; distinct from the Playwright lock). Markers are files inside it.
  • A background release watcher (Aziz starts one run_in_background shell loop before spawning the subagents) does, for each iteration i from 1 to N:
  • wait until both ready-a-<i> and ready-b-<i> exist,
  • touch go-<i>,
  • wait until both done-a-<i> and done-b-<i> exist, then continue to i+1.
  • Each subagent (<id> = a or b), per iteration i:
  • touch /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-qa-barrier/ready-<id>-<i>
  • spin (while [ ! -e .../go-<i> ]; do :; done — a tight poll, no sleep) until go-<i> appears
  • immediately issue its one assigned tool call — no reasoning, no other tool call between the spin ending and the call
  • append the raw result (full response, or the error text) to /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-qa-barrier/result-<id>-<i>.json
  • touch /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-qa-barrier/done-<id>-<i>
  • Loop count: N = 20–50. Transport/SSL corruption and WAL contention are intermittent; one clean pair proves nothing. Stop early and report if any iteration trips a check.
  • Teardown: Aziz rm -rf /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-qa-barrier after collecting results.
  • Shell form. The worktree-isolation guard can refuse a Bash call that uses a shell variable ($i included) or a heredoc. In every command of the prompt template below, replace $i with the iteration number and use the literal absolute path, and write a result with a plain printf '%s\n' '<result>' >> /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-qa-barrier/result-<id>-<i>.json (both v0.9.2 workers lost their first iteration's write to this). A result containing ' breaks that quoting: write the error text, or the result with each ' replaced, rather than dropping the line.

The subagent's job is to run the calls and write result files — it must not edit any tracked repo file. Only Aziz reads the result-* files back, diffs them, and writes the **Result** entries (see .claude/team-roles/aziz.md, the Compile step).

docs.title: Per-TC checks
docs.text:
TC-I24 — subagent a calls get_sheet_data on {SPREADSHEET_ID} / Sales!A1:C3; subagent b calls get_sheet_data on a second, distinct spreadsheet / range with different known values. Across all N iterations: - every result-a-* holds only {SPREADSHEET_ID}'s data, every result-b-* only the second spreadsheet's — no row from one appears in the other's file - no result is empty, truncated, or an SSL/connection error (record layer failure, Connection reset by peer, Remote end closed connection — the signature of the shared-transport bug this guards against)

TC-I02 — subagent a calls update_cells writing a per-iteration sentinel (e.g. QA-I02-<i>-<timestamp>) to {SPREADSHEET_ID} / Empty!A1; subagent b calls get_sheet_data on {SPREADSHEET_ID} / Sales!A1:C3 (a different sheet in the same spreadsheet, so both touch the same cache row). Across all N iterations: - no result-b-* is a database is locked / SQLITE_BUSY error, and none is empty or an SSL/connection error - every result-a-* reports the write succeeded - if the server's LOG_FILE is reachable (from docs/qa/.env or the team MCP config), grep it for database is locked / OperationalError over the run window — there should be none; if it isn't reachable, the response-level checks above still catch the failure mode (WAL contention surfaces as an error in the response, not just the log)

docs.title: Subagent prompt template
docs.text:
Give each of the two subagents a prompt of this shape (fill the bracketed parts; <id> is a for one, b for the other):

You are one of two subagents running a true-concurrency QA iteration loop. Your worker id is <id>. Barrier dir: /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-qa-barrier. Iterations: <N>.

For i in 1..<N>, in order: 1. touch /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-qa-barrier/ready-<id>-$i 2. Spin with a tight shell poll until /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-qa-barrier/go-$i exists. 3. The instant it exists, call exactly this tool, once: [full tool name + params, e.g. mcp__mcp-gee-sweet-kai-sa__get_sheet_data(spreadsheet_id="…", range="Sales!A1:C3")]. Do nothing else first — no other tool call, no reasoning step, between the spin ending and this call. 4. Append the tool's full raw result (or, on error, the complete error text) as one JSON line to /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-qa-barrier/result-<id>-$i.json. Use a plain printf with the literal absolute path, with $i replaced by the iteration number (see "Shell form" above). 5. touch /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-qa-barrier/done-<id>-$i

Call only mcp__mcp-gee-sweet-kai-sa__* tools. Do not edit, create, or delete any file inside the git repo — your only writes are to /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet-qa-barrier/. When the loop finishes, report back: for each i, whether the tool call returned data or an error, and the first ~200 chars of each result. Do not interpret pass/fail — just report what you observed.

docs.title: Drive fixture-folder pollution
docs.text:
TEST_FOLDER_ID accumulates stray items across many creation/copy test categories that don't tear down after themselves (tracked in #304 — dedicated QA account/cleanup sweep). As of 2026-07-17 it held ~15 duplicate leftovers (Copy of mcp-gee-sweet-qa-fixtures ×2, QA-Cache-Check ×2, QA-Copy-Explicit, QA-Create-Explicit, QA-Doc-Copy, QA-DocCache, QA-HTML-Doc ×2, QA-Markdown-Doc ×2, QA-Table-Doc ×2, loose qa-notes.md/qa-upload.txt, two leftover folders).

This matters for any test that syncs, lists, or downloads the whole folder (sync_folder, download_folder, list_files against TEST_FOLDER_ID directly) — the pollution items show up in results alongside whatever the test actually cares about, and a recursive/whole-folder operation will process all of it. Until #304 lands: for a test that needs a clean or isolated Drive tree (rather than "does this tool correctly handle files that happen to be in TEST_FOLDER_ID"), create a throwaway child folder under TEST_FOLDER_ID for that test's own fixtures instead of working at the shared top level, and delete it in teardown. Same tool behavior either way — this only reduces noise and avoids accidentally sweeping up items you don't own.

docs.title: Clearing sheet-level state with no direct tool (e.g. data validation)
docs.text:
Some sheet-level state has a tool to set it but none to clear it, and no tool exposes a sheet's numeric sheetId by name to fall back to the raw batch_update escape hatch (list_sheets returns names only; the spreadsheet://{id}/info resource that's supposed to cover this was broken until #363 fixed it — reading it now works, but it's still no substitute for a tool that returns sheetId by name, tracked as a product gap in #365). Hit live testing add_data_validation/get_data_validation (PR #361, 2026-07-18): no way to clear a validation rule from the fixture's Empty sheet between test cases.

Workaround for a scratch fixture sheet (never do this to a sheet with real data — it destroys everything on the tab, not just the state you're trying to clear): delete_sheet(sheet="Empty") then create_sheet(title="Empty"). Fully resets the tab to blank, including any validation/formatting/merges, and is safe here because every QA tool call references the sheet by name, never by the ID that changes on recreate.

Use disjoint ranges for independent TCs sharing one scratch sheet within a single run. Confirmed on the v0.9.0 pass: re-verifying merge_cells/unmerge_cells TCs and add_data_validation/get_data_validation TCs against overlapping ranges on the Empty sheet in the same subagent run triggered Google Sheets' own merge → validation-carryover behavior (a merge overwrote the overlapping range's dropdown rule with a checkbox rule) — native Sheets semantics, not a tool defect, but it reads exactly like cross-test contamination until investigated. Give each independent TC its own non-overlapping block (e.g. A1:C3 for one, E1:G3 for another).

docs.title: Forcing a real storageQuotaExceeded (service account only)
docs.text:
Several quota-error test cases say a quota error can't be forced live, so they verify only by unit test. That's true for a user identity, since the QA account's My Drive isn't full. A service account's error can be forced: it has no My Drive storage, so creating a file with no parents returns a real 403 storageQuotaExceeded. Run it from a fresh interpreter in the checkout under test (no MCP server involved), and pass the caught exception to the code under test:

uv run python -I -c "
import mcp_gee_sweet
from mcp_gee_sweet import auth
from googleapiclient.discovery import build
d = build('drive', 'v3', credentials=auth._service_account_creds(), cache_discovery=False)
try:
    r = d.files().create(body={'name': 'qa-sa-quota-probe', 'mimeType': 'application/vnd.google-apps.document'}, fields='id').execute()
    print('UNEXPECTED: created'); d.files().delete(fileId=r['id']).execute()
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, e.resp.status)  # then feed e to the helper under test
"

This needs service-account credentials in src/mcp_gee_sweet/.env (CREDENTIALS_CONFIG or SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH). Nothing is created, so there's no teardown. Used for TC-D291 in PR #1006.

docs.title: Missing docs/qa/.env in a role worktree
docs.text:
docs/qa/.env is gitignored, so it doesn't exist by default in a freshly-provisioned .claude/worktrees/<name> slot — confirmed empty/absent across every role worktree and the main checkout, 2026-07-19, while doing a scoped QA pass from Kit's own role process (.claude/team-roles/qa.md step 4), not the full conductor-prompt flow this file otherwise documents. That flow's own fixture-check step (below) would just stop and ask the user to run setup.md, but a scoped single-PR QA pass doesn't need the whole .env — only the one fixture ID relevant to the PR under review.

Workaround: the fixture files have fixed, documented names (setup.md's seed prompt: "Rename the doc to mcp-gee-sweet-qa-fixtures-doc" / "Rename the spreadsheet to mcp-gee-sweet-qa-fixtures"). Find the ID directly instead of blocking: search_files(query="mcp-gee-sweet-qa-fixtures-doc", mime_type="application/vnd.google-apps.document") (swap the doc mime type/name for the spreadsheet as needed). Only reach for this fallback in a scoped pass that needs one or two fixture IDs — a full multi-category run still needs the real .env for TEST_FOLDER_ID/TEST_CALENDAR_ID/etc., which don't have as fixed a name to search by.

docs.title: Running server-startup and CLI cases in a scoped lane pass (e.g. ⚠️ local-filesystem infra cases)
docs.text:
Some cases test how the server starts, not what a tool does: auth waterfall and degraded start, stdio vs SSE behavior, CLI subcommands like mcp-gee-sweet auth. Your own mcp-gee-sweet-<name> server can't exercise these, since its env and transport are fixed. They still run fine in a lane pass. Start a fresh server process from the worktree with the env the case needs, and drive it yourself. Confirmed on PR #807 (Kit) and PR #828 (Sky, TC-I35..I40, 2026-09-26).

  • stdio: use the mcp SDK's stdio_client(StdioServerParameters(command="uv", args=["run", "--directory", <worktree>, "mcp-gee-sweet"], env=...)) + ClientSession. Then initialize, call_tool, and read_resource("server://auth-status"). Strip AUTH_METHOD/TOKEN_PATH/SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH/CREDENTIALS_CONFIG/GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS from the inherited env before applying the case's overrides. Set DEBUG_LEVEL=DEBUG + LOG_FILE=<tmp> for the log-line checks. mcp v2's CallToolResult field is is_error, not isError.
  • SSE: start uv run mcp-gee-sweet --transport sse in its own process group (subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True) from Python, or set -m then cmd & in a bash script; macOS has no setsid). Drive it with mcp.client.sse.sse_client + ClientSession. Stop it with SIGTERM to the server pid: it exits within a few seconds, even mid consent wait (#833), so a server still running after that is a finding. Only then SIGKILL the whole group (os.killpg / kill -9 -- -$PID). Never pkill -f "transport sse" or similar: other lanes' and Kai's servers match. The lifespan (and any consent wait) runs when the SSE stream opens, before initialize, so time the connect, not initialize. Uvicorn's access log goes to stdout, so check stdout for the absence of specific text (e.g. the consent prompt), not for an empty file.
  • Race and hang repros: a concurrency finding needs a repro that forces the overlap. Gate the operations with events (e.g. A's consent waits on an event set from inside B's token load) so the stale operation is still in flight when the other side's event fires. Starting B after A finishes only shows a sequential case, which may be correct behavior. Run the same script against the previous commit as a control: a race or hang that shows up there and not on the fix is the evidence. For an SSE-timing hang, use a raw client that POSTs the instant the endpoint event arrives, not the SDK client: PR #867's intermittent SIGTERM hang reproduced 3 of 39 runs through sse_client and 25 of 25 with the raw client (TC-I44 step 2 encodes it).
  • CLI + OAuth consent: run the command in the background, read the Please visit this URL line from its output, and complete (or Cancel) the consent via Playwright, after the signed-in check and under the mutex above. The account chooser lists more than one account, so pick the Workspace one that owns the fixtures.
  • Worktree-isolation guard: a session pinned to a role worktree rejects Bash commands it can't statically verify: uv/git with $VAR-expanded paths, heredocs, multi-step cd … && … chains. Write each probe as a script under $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp with the Write tool (literal absolute paths inside), then run it as a single bash /abs/path/script.sh or uv run python /abs/path/probe.py KEY=VAL ... call. It also refused these read-only or scratch-only forms on PR #866 (2026-10-01): python3 -c ... with a $var path operand, cd <scratch> && git init && claude -p ..., an inline python3 -c filter containing the word system, and gh pr create --body "<free text>". These ran: a plain cd <scratch> && claude -p ... and VAR=... claude -p .... Give claude -p a scratch project made of .claude/settings.json alone, since it needs no git init. Pull fields from stream-json with grep -oE, not an inline Python filter. Pass a PR body with --body-file.
  • Fixture: point TOKEN_PATH at a nonexistent file in a directory that exists. A missing parent directory now trips the pre-consent writability check (#811), which tests a different path.

docs.title: Conductor prompt
docs.text:
You are the QA conductor for mcp-gee-sweet. Your job is to execute the full test suite against the live MCP server, record outcomes, and save a results report.

You have the mcp-gee-sweet MCP connected. Before starting, check whether Playwright MCP is also connected AND actually authenticated to Google — these are different things: a connected Playwright MCP still runs an unauthenticated browser by default, and navigating it to a Google URL just redirects to `accounts.google.com` sign-in. Do the real check described in "Verifying Playwright is signed into the right account" (above): the fixture doc's page title must match its actual name — a sign-in redirect *or* a "You need access" page (wrong account) both fail. If Playwright isn't connected, or the check fails, tell me: "Playwright is not connected / not authenticated — tests marked **Playwright: required** will run without visual verification. Confirm to proceed, or connect/authenticate Playwright first (see `docs/qa/playwright_oauth.md`) and restart." Wait for my confirmation before continuing. If I tell you mid-run that Playwright is now authenticated, re-verify immediately and switch to using it for all subsequent **Playwright: required** cases — don't keep treating it as unusable for the rest of the run based on the earlier check.

## Step 0 — Fixture setup

Before running any tests:

1. Record the start time (current timestamp).
2. Read `.env` from the repo root. If the file does not exist or the TEST_* keys are missing, stop and say: ".env not found or TEST_* keys missing — follow docs/qa/setup.md to create your fixtures first."
3. Extract TEST_SPREADSHEET_ID, TEST_DOC_ID, TEST_FOLDER_ID, TEST_CALENDAR_ID, TEST_EVENT_ID, TEST_LARGE_DOC_ID, TEST_PERMISSION_EMAIL, SHARED_DRIVE_ID.
4. Verify the fixture spreadsheet with get_sheet_data: confirm sheet tabs Sales, Empty, Notes & Misc exist and Sales data has 6 rows (header + Widget/Gadget/Donut/Gizmo/Totals), columns A–D. If data is missing or in wrong order, use update_cells to restore known seed state (see docs/qa/setup.md §Known fixture state).
5. Verify the fixture doc with get_doc_structure: confirm title "mcp-gee-sweet-qa-fixtures-doc" and body contains heading "Test Document", a paragraph, and a bullet list (Item one / Item two). If content is wrong, use write_doc_content to restore it.
6. Tell me the fixture IDs, start time, and whether the fixture state looks correct, then wait for me to confirm before proceeding.

## Step 1 — Run tests

Work through the test files in this order:
1. `docs/qa/tests/infra.md`
2. `docs/qa/tests/sheets_read.md`
3. `docs/qa/tests/sheets_write.md`
4. `docs/qa/tests/sheets_mgmt.md`
5. `docs/qa/tests/sheets_charts.md`
6. `docs/qa/tests/drive_files.md`
7. `docs/qa/tests/drive_sharing.md`
8. `docs/qa/tests/drive_transfer.md`
9. `docs/qa/tests/drive_activity.md`
10. `docs/qa/tests/docs_content.md`
11. `docs/qa/tests/docs_tables.md`
12. `docs/qa/tests/docs_style.md`
13. `docs/qa/tests/docs_layout.md`
14. `docs/qa/tests/calendar.md`
15. `docs/qa/tests/gmail.md`

`docs/qa/tests/docs_markdown.md` isn't in this sequence: it renders every case through eight entry points twice, so it runs on its own (`run_group` with `group: docs_markdown`), following that file's own "Running this suite" section.

For each test case:

1. Announce the TC number and title.
2. Substitute fixture IDs into the prompt (replace {SPREADSHEET_ID}, {DOC_ID}, etc. with the values from `.env`).
3. Execute the prompt using the mcp-gee-sweet tools available in this session.
4. If the test case is marked **Playwright: required** and Playwright MCP is connected: navigate to the affected resource and take a snapshot before recording the outcome. Also save a screenshot via `browser_take_screenshot`, with `filename` set to `docs/qa/screenshots/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<tc-id>.png` (today's date, lowercase TC number — e.g. `tc-doc12.png`). The date prefix keeps each run's screenshots separate without overwriting a prior run's evidence, and avoids depending on a subfolder that `browser_take_screenshot` won't auto-create.
5. Evaluate each item in the **Checks** list against the actual result.
6. Record one of:
   - **PASS** — every check met, and the result describes no defect
   - **FAIL** — one or more checks failed; note exactly what was wrong
   - **PARTIAL** — the checks that ran were met, but at least one listed check didn't run (including the Playwright check on a `**Playwright: required**` case); name each one that didn't
   - **SKIP** — with reason (e.g. "requires server restart", "skipped by user", "prerequisite TC failed")

   A result that describes a defect is never a PASS. That includes wording like "matches the documented failure mode", "known gap", "pre-existing", "not a new regression", "out of scope", or "still fails": if the case's own output shows a defect, record FAIL, even when its Checks were written to accept it. A known limitation is a FAIL that links an **open** issue: if the one it names is closed, or it names none, file one (or add the evidence to an open one) and link it in the Result. A defect outside the case's own checks (a probe, a side observation) can sit beside a PASS only if the same Result names where it's tracked: sent back on the PR, or an open issue. "Not filed" next to a defect is never acceptable (#1044 audit, `docs/qa/results/2026-10-17-pass-audit.md`).
7. For tests marked ⚠️ destructive: ask me before running. If I say skip, record SKIP(destructive-skipped).
8. For tests marked 🔍 product decision: record PASS and note the observed behavior, unless that behavior is a defect or a limitation; then record FAIL per step 6.
9. Track intermediate IDs as you go — some tests produce IDs (permissionId, eventId, fileId) needed by later tests. Record them in your working notes and substitute them when referenced.

## Step 2 — Save progress

After completing each test file, write current results to `docs/qa/results/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` (use today's date). If a file already exists for today, overwrite it with the fully updated version.

If I say "pause" or "stop" at any point, save immediately to `docs/qa/results/<YYYY-MM-DD>-partial.md` before stopping.

## Step 3 — Final report

After all test files are complete, record the end time and write the final report to `docs/qa/results/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` using this format:

---
# QA Run — <YYYY-MM-DD>

**Auth:** OAuth  
**Fixtures:** SPREADSHEET_ID=`<id>` · DOC_ID=`<id>` · FOLDER_ID=`<id>`  
**Start:** <timestamp> · **End:** <timestamp> · **Duration:** <HH:MM>

## Summary

| Category | PASS | FAIL | SKIP | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure | | | | |
| Sheets Read | | | | |
| Sheets Write | | | | |
| Sheets Mgmt | | | | |
| Sheets Charts | | | | |
| Drive + Docs | | | | |
| Docs Tools | | | | |
| Calendar | | | | |
| **Total** | | | | |

## Failures

For each FAIL, one entry:
**TC-XXX — <title>**
Expected: <what the check said>
Observed: <what actually happened>
Playwright: <what the browser showed, if applicable>

*(none)* if all tests passed.

## Tool coverage

For every tool registered by the server, list which TCs exercise it and whether those TCs passed. Derive this by scanning the test files you ran.

| Tool | TC(s) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| get_sheet_data | TC-R01, TC-R02, … | ✅ all pass |
| create_spreadsheet | TC-D01 | ✅ pass |
| create_calendar | (none) | ⚠️ no coverage |
| … | | |

Use ✅ if all covering TCs passed, ❌ if any failed, ⚠️ no coverage if no TC exercises the tool, and SKIP if all covering TCs were skipped.

## Full results

| TC | Title | Outcome | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-I01 | ... | PASS | |
| ... | | | |
---

If any test case this run was marked **Playwright: required**, tell me: "Screenshots saved to `docs/qa/screenshots/` (prefixed `<YYYY-MM-DD>-`) — delete when no longer needed."

## Resuming an interrupted run

If resuming: read the partial results file I specify, identify the last completed TC, and continue from the next one. Re-confirm fixture IDs from `.env` and re-verify fixture state before continuing.

docs.title: Results location
docs.text: Reports are saved to docs/qa/results/. Files named YYYY-MM-DD.md are completed runs; files named YYYY-MM-DD-partial.md are interrupted runs.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
QA fixtures are a spreadsheet, a doc, a large-content doc, a folder, and a calendar + event that test cases reference. Their IDs live in .env (gitignored) alongside your other server config.

Fixtures are provisioned in the mcp-gee-sweet-shared Shared Drive — common ground that both the OAuth QA identity and the service account can read and write. (The Shared Drive's own ID doubles as a fixture, SHARED_DRIVE_ID, for the list_drives / empty_trash --drive_id test cases.)

Setup has four steps: make sure the required Google APIs are enabled, create the files in the Shared Drive, add the resulting IDs to .env, then run the seed prompt to populate them.

docs.title: Step 0 — Enable the required Google APIs
docs.text:
The OAuth client's GCP project must have every API these tools call enabled, or the tool fails at call time with HttpError 403 ... "<API> has not been used in project <n> before or it is disabled" (reason: SERVICE_DISABLED). File creation still partly succeeds in that state (the file shell is made via the Drive API) while every content read/write fails — a confusing half-broken state, so enable all of these up front:

API Service name Used by Google Drive drive.googleapis.com every Drive tool, and file creation for Sheets/Docs Google Sheets sheets.googleapis.com all sheet read/write tools Google Docs docs.googleapis.com all doc content tools Google Calendar calendar-json.googleapis.com all calendar tools Google Drive Activity driveactivity.googleapis.com list_file_activity 
gcloud services enable drive.googleapis.com sheets.googleapis.com docs.googleapis.com \
  calendar-json.googleapis.com driveactivity.googleapis.com --project=<your-project>

or enable each from the API Library in the Cloud Console. Changes take ~1–3 minutes to propagate.

docs.title: Step 1 — Create the files in the Shared Drive
docs.text: How you create the fixture files depends on your auth method. Either way the target is a folder inside the mcp-gee-sweet-shared Shared Drive (not personal My Drive) so the service account can reach them too.

docs.title: OAuth / Application Default Credentials
docs.text: The AI can create the fixture set for you. In a Claude session with the MCP server connected, run the setup_fixtures operation (see operations.yaml) and it will create the folder, spreadsheet, doc, and large-content doc in the Shared Drive, write their IDs to .env, and populate the fixture data. Skip to Step 3 when done.

docs.title: Service account (SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH / CREDENTIALS_CONFIG)
docs.text: A service account has no personal-Drive storage quota, but it can create files in a Shared Drive it's a member of. Add the service account (service_account.json → client_email) to the mcp-gee-sweet-shared Shared Drive as Content manager, then either run setup_fixtures or create an empty spreadsheet, Google Doc, and large-content Doc in a folder inside that Shared Drive by hand. Continue to Step 2.

docs.title: Step 2 — Add IDs to .env
docs.text:
Add the following to your .env file (create it at the repo root if it doesn't exist):

# Server default create-location — set to the Shared Drive's ID
DRIVE_FOLDER_ID=<mcp-gee-sweet-shared Shared Drive ID>

# QA test fixtures
TEST_SPREADSHEET_ID=<spreadsheet ID>
TEST_DOC_ID=<doc ID>
TEST_FOLDER_ID=<the folder inside the Shared Drive that contains the fixture files>
TEST_LARGE_DOC_ID=<large-content doc ID for TC-D48; create via setup_fixtures or manually>
TEST_CALENDAR_ID=<see Calendar fixture setup below>
TEST_EVENT_ID=<see Calendar fixture setup below>
TEST_PERMISSION_EMAIL=<a second Google account email for permission add/remove tests (TC-D130)>
SHARED_DRIVE_ID=<mcp-gee-sweet-shared Shared Drive ID — same value as DRIVE_FOLDER_ID>

SHARED_DRIVE_ID and DRIVE_FOLDER_ID are the same value: a Shared Drive's ID is also its root folder ID. Get it from list_drives, or from the URL when the drive is open (drive.google.com/drive/folders/<ID>).

File and folder IDs are in the URL when you open them in Drive: - Spreadsheet: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<ID>/edit - Doc: docs.google.com/document/d/<ID>/edit - Folder / Shared Drive: drive.google.com/drive/folders/<ID>

docs.title: Step 3 — Run the seed prompt
docs.text:
Paste the seed prompt below into a Claude session that has both the mcp-gee-sweet MCP server and the Playwright MCP connected. Claude will populate the spreadsheet and doc with the known fixture data, then open each file in Playwright to visually confirm the result.

Set up my QA fixtures for mcp-gee-sweet using these IDs from my .env:
- Spreadsheet: <TEST_SPREADSHEET_ID>
- Doc: <TEST_DOC_ID>

Please do all of the following in order:

1. Rename the spreadsheet to "mcp-gee-sweet-qa-fixtures".
2. Rename the first sheet to "Sales" and populate it with:
   - Row 1 (headers): Product, Q1, Q2, Q3
   - Row 2: Widget, 100, 120, 140
   - Row 3: Gadget, 200, 180, 220
   - Row 4: Donut, 50, 60, 55
   - Row 5: Gizmo, 300, 310, 290
   - Row 6: Totals, =SUM(B2:B5), =SUM(C2:C5), =SUM(D2:D5)
3. Add a second sheet called "Empty" — leave it completely blank.
4. Add a third sheet called "Notes & Misc" with:
   - Row 1 (headers): Date, Note
   - Row 2: =TODAY(), Setup complete
5. Rename the doc to "mcp-gee-sweet-qa-fixtures-doc" and write this content:
   <h1>Test Document</h1><p>This document is used for QA testing of mcp-gee-sweet.</p><ul><li>Item one</li><li>Item two</li></ul>

Confirm when done.

Then open https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<TEST_SPREADSHEET_ID>/edit in Playwright and take a snapshot to visually confirm the sheet names and data are correct. Do the same for the doc at https://docs.google.com/document/d/<TEST_DOC_ID>/edit.

The large-content doc (TEST_LARGE_DOC_ID, "mcp-gee-sweet-qa-large-doc") is padded past ~50,000 characters of filler text so get_doc_content returns a large response without timeout or truncation (TC-D48). setup_fixtures creates it; to build it by hand, create_doc_from_file a .md file of repeated lorem-ipsum paragraphs into the fixture folder.

docs.title: Known fixture state (after seed)
docs.text:
Sheet Row A B C D Sales 1 Product Q1 Q2 Q3 Sales 2 Widget 100 120 140 Sales 3 Gadget 200 180 220 Sales 4 Donut 50 60 55 Sales 5 Gizmo 300 310 290 Sales 6 Totals =SUM(B2:B5) =SUM(C2:C5) =SUM(D2:D5) Empty — (blank) Notes & Misc 1 Date Note Notes & Misc 2 =TODAY() Setup complete

Doc content: <h1>Test Document</h1><p>This document is used for QA testing of mcp-gee-sweet.</p><ul><li>Item one</li><li>Item two</li></ul>

docs.title: Calendar fixture setup
docs.text: Calendar tests need a dedicated calendar plus one pre-existing event.

docs.title: OAuth / ADC
docs.text:
create_calendar makes a secondary calendar owned by the authenticated account — no personal-calendar sharing needed. Seed prompt (paste with MCP server connected):

Set up my calendar QA fixtures for mcp-gee-sweet:

1. Call list_calendars — if a calendar called "mcp-gee-sweet-qa" already appears, use it and skip to step 3.
2. Call create_calendar with summary "mcp-gee-sweet-qa".
3. Create an event in that calendar: title "QA Test Event", tomorrow at 10:00–11:00 in the calendar's timezone.
4. Return the calendar ID and the event ID.

docs.title: Service account
docs.text:
The service account cannot see a calendar shared only with a personal account — you must subscribe it via calendarList().insert(). See the Calendar API setup memory entry for the workaround, or skip calendar tests if you don't need them.

Add the returned IDs to .env as TEST_CALENDAR_ID and TEST_EVENT_ID.

docs.title: Gmail fixture setup
docs.text:
Gmail cases (tests/gmail.md) read from a seeded fixture set instead of the real inbox. The design is in gmail-test-plan.md §3. Two mailboxes are involved:

  • QA mailbox: the Workspace fixture-owning account, the one the OAuth servers (mcp-gee-sweet-oauth / -kai-oauth) authenticate as. This is the mailbox under test.
  • Sender mailbox: a second Google account that only exists to send real mail to the QA mailbox. Mail never goes anywhere else.

Both tokens need the gmail.modify scope, and each token's Cloud project needs the Gmail API enabled (Step 0). scripts/qa_gmail_fixtures.py does everything. It refreshes both tokens in memory and never writes them back:

S="uv run python scripts/qa_gmail_fixtures.py"
$S seed                                   # label + 12 inserted fixtures, IDs -> .env
$S send --sender-token <sender token.json> --dry-run
$S send --sender-token <sender token.json>  # 10 sends + 1 QA reply, waits for delivery
$S seed                                   # labels the sent fixtures, un-spams them, IDs -> .env
$S status                                 # exit 0 only when all 19 fixtures are present

--qa-token defaults to TOKEN_PATH (else ./token.json), and --env-file defaults to the repo-root .env. Every run is idempotent: fixtures are found by exact [mcp-qa:<key>] subject and reused. send refuses any recipient except the two mailboxes, with no Cc or Bcc.

  • Inserted fixtures (inline, reply-to, latin1, page-1–7, spam, trash) are planted with messages.insert. Nothing is sent.
  • Sent fixtures (plain, alt-unicode, attachments, thread, forwarded, large-body, over-cap-thread) are really delivered, so their MIME layout is Gmail's own. They go straight through the Gmail API with the sender token, not through send_message: a 3 MB body can't travel as a tool argument, and a real message/rfc822 forward can't be built with send_message.
  • Gmail's spam filter junks some sender mail; seen live 2026-09-26 for plain, attachments, and large-body. The second seed moves every sent fixture back to INBOX. Rerun seed if a later status or case finds one in Spam again.
  • The trash fixture expires after Gmail's 30-day trash retention. seed re-inserts it.

inspect prints the raw Gmail part tree of every fixture: MIME type, size, and whether the body arrives as inline data or by attachmentId. This is the ground truth for TC-GM28–30.

.env keys written: TEST_GMAIL_ADDRESS, TEST_GMAIL_SENDER_ADDRESS, TEST_GMAIL_LABEL_ID, TEST_MESSAGE_ID, TEST_THREAD_ID, TEST_GMAIL_UNICODE_ID, TEST_GMAIL_ATTACH_ID, TEST_GMAIL_INLINE_ID, TEST_GMAIL_REPLYTO_ID, TEST_GMAIL_FWD_ID, TEST_GMAIL_LARGE_ID, TEST_GMAIL_BIG_THREAD_ID, TEST_GMAIL_LATIN1_ID.

Reset: reset trashes every labeled fixture and any [mcp-qa message a test run left behind, and deletes [mcp-qa drafts. It touches the QA mailbox only. Then run send and seed again.

docs.title: PRD: Saved Searches
docs.text: Status: Draft Author: Product team Last updated: 2026-10-12

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text: Users repeat the same searches every day. Today they retype the query and re-apply filters each time, which takes about 40 seconds per search based on session recordings.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Let a user save a search (query + filters + sort) with a name
  • Show saved searches in the sidebar
  • Notify the user when new results match a saved search

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Sharing saved searches with other users (v2)
  • Saved searches on mobile (v2)

docs.title: 3. User stories
docs.text:
1. As an analyst, I want to save a search so that I can rerun it in one click.
  2. As an analyst, I want to rename or delete a saved search.
  3. As a manager, I want a daily email digest of new matches.

docs.title: 4.1 Functional
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority F1 Save the current search with a name (max 80 chars) P0 F2 List saved searches, most recent first P0 F3 Rename and delete a saved search P1 F4 Daily digest email for new matches P2

docs.title: 4.2 Non-functional
docs.text:
• Saving a search must complete in under 200 ms (p95)
  • A user can have at most 50 saved searches

docs.title: 5. API
docs.text:
The client calls a new endpoint:

POST /api/v1/saved-searches
Content-Type: application/json

{"name": "Open P1 bugs", "query": "priority:P1 status:open", "sort": "updated"}

The response includes the new search's id and created_at.

docs.title: 6. Open questions
docs.text:
• Should the digest respect the user's timezone or the account's?
  • Do we cap digest frequency for searches with hundreds of new matches?

docs.title: 7. Appendix
docs.text: See the search architecture doc and the analytics dashboard.

docs.title: fastqueue
docs.text: A small, dependency-free job queue for Python services.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• In-process or Redis-backed storage
  • Retries with exponential backoff
  • Scheduled jobs (run_at=)
  • Type-annotated API

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install fastqueue

For Redis support:

pip install "fastqueue[redis]"

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
from fastqueue import Queue

q = Queue()

@q.job(retries=3)
def send_email(to: str, subject: str) -> None:
    ...

send_email.delay("user@example.com", "Welcome!")
q.run_worker()

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Option Default Description backend "memory" "memory" or "redis" redis_url None Required when backend="redis" max_retries 5 Upper bound for any job poll_interval 0.5 Seconds between polls

docs.title: Usage notes
docs.text:
1. Jobs must be importable by the worker process.
  2. Arguments must be JSON-serializable.
  3. Use q.job(timeout=...) for long-running work: 
    @q.job(timeout=300)
def rebuild_index(): ...
  4. Call q.shutdown() on exit to flush pending acks.

Note: the in-memory backend loses jobs when the process exits. Use Redis in production.

docs.title: How to Set Up a Local Development Environment
docs.text: This guide walks you through setting up the service on macOS or Linux. It takes about 15 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or newer
  • Docker Desktop (or Docker Engine on Linux)
  • Access to the team's GitHub organization

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository.
git clone https://github.com/example/service.git
cd service
  1. Create a virtual environment and install dependencies.
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
  1. Start the backing services. This starts Postgres and Redis in containers:
docker compose up -d db redis

Wait until both containers report healthy:

docker compose ps
  1. Configure your environment.
  2. Copy .env.example to .env
  3. Set DATABASE_URL to postgresql://dev:dev@localhost:5432/service

  4. Leave FEATURE_FLAGS empty unless you need a specific flag

  5. Run the migrations and start the server.

make migrate
make run

The server listens on http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Port 5432 is already in use. Another Postgres is running. Stop it, or change the port mapping in docker-compose.yml.

pip install fails on psycopg. Install the Postgres client headers:

  • macOS: brew install libpq
  • Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install libpq-dev

Tip: run make doctor to check every prerequisite at once.

docs.title: Comparison: Hosted Postgres Providers
docs.text: We evaluated three providers for the analytics database. Prices are list prices for a 4 vCPU / 16 GB instance with 500 GB storage, as of October 2026.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: Provider A Provider B Provider C Monthly cost $410 $365 $520 Point-in-time recovery ✅ 30 days ✅ 7 days ✅ 35 days Read replicas Up to 5 Up to 3 Up to 10 Private networking ✅ ❌ ✅ Postgres 17 ✅ Preview ✅ SOC 2 Type II ✅ ✅ ✅

docs.title: Provider A
docs.text:
Pros

  • Mature tooling and a good CLI
  • Private networking included at no extra cost

Cons

  • Read replicas cost the same as the primary
  • Support response times are slow on the standard plan

docs.title: Provider B
docs.text:
Pros

  • Cheapest option
  • Very fast provisioning (under 2 minutes)

Cons

  • No private networking, which our security policy requires
  • Postgres 17 is still in preview

docs.title: Provider C
docs.text:
Pros

  • Best replica story (up to 10, cross-region)
  • Longest PITR window

Cons

  • Most expensive, by about 27% over Provider A

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text: Criterion Weight A B C Cost 30% 7 9 5 Reliability 30% 8 6 9 Security fit 25% 9 2 9 Operability 15% 8 7 8 Weighted total 7.95 6.05 7.65

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: Go with Provider A. Provider B fails our private-networking requirement, and Provider C's extra replica capacity doesn't justify the cost at our current scale. Revisit if we need more than 5 replicas.

docs.title: Postmortem: Checkout Outage on October 9
docs.text: Severity: SEV-1 Duration: 47 minutes (14:12–14:59 UTC) Impact: ~18% of checkout attempts failed; estimated $42k in delayed orders

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A configuration change raised the payment service's connection pool from 50 to 500. The database hit its connection limit within minutes, and checkout requests started timing out.

docs.title: Timeline (UTC)
docs.text: Time Event 14:05 Config change merged and deployed 14:12 Error rate alert fires for payments-api 14:18 On-call acknowledges, starts investigating 14:31 Database connection saturation identified 14:44 Config change reverted 14:59 Error rate back to baseline

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The pool size is set per pod, not per service. With 10 pods, the change meant 5,000 potential connections against a database limit of 1,000.

# payments-api/config.yaml (the bad change)
db:
  pool_size: 500   # was 50

docs.title: What went well
docs.text:
• Alerting fired within 7 minutes
  • The revert path was fast and well understood

docs.title: What went poorly
docs.text:
• The change had no review from the database team
  • The config file has no comment explaining that pool_size is per pod
  • It took 13 minutes to connect the errors to the database

docs.title: Action items
docs.text: # Action Owner Due 1 Add a CI check that caps pool_size × replicas Platform Oct 23 2 Comment pool_size semantics in the config Payments Oct 16 3 Add a DB-connections panel to the payments dashboard SRE Oct 20 4 Require DB-team review for pool changes Eng leads Oct 30

docs.title: Lessons
docs.text:
1. Per-instance settings need the multiplier spelled out next to them.
  2. A dashboard panel for the shared resource would have cut diagnosis time:
  3. connections in use
  4. connections waiting
  5. rejected connections

docs.title: Body

  • sku (string)
  • quantity (integer, ≥ 1)
  • shipping_address (object, required)

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Code Meaning 400 Validation failed; see errors[] 402 Payment required 409 Duplicate Idempotency-Key 429 Rate limited; retry after the Retry-After header

Idempotency: send an Idempotency-Key header on every POST. Retrying with the same key returns the original response instead of creating a second order.

docs.title: 1. The problem
docs.text: A group of nodes must agree on a single value, even if some nodes crash or messages are delayed. Consensus is the core of replicated logs, leader election, and distributed locks.

docs.title: 2. Key properties
docs.text:
• Safety: nodes never decide different values
  • Liveness: nodes eventually decide
  • Fault tolerance: works with up to f failures out of 2f + 1 nodes

docs.title: 3. Raft in brief
docs.text:
1. Leader election
  2. Every node starts as a follower
  3. A follower that hears nothing for an election timeout becomes a candidate and asks for votes
  4. A candidate with a majority becomes the leader
  5. Log replication
  6. The leader appends client commands to its log
  7. It sends AppendEntries to followers
  8. An entry is committed once a majority stores it
  9. Safety rule
  10. A candidate can only win if its log is at least as up to date as a majority's

docs.title: 4. Paxos vs. Raft
docs.text: Paxos Raft Designed for Correctness proofs Understandability Leader Optional (Multi-Paxos uses one) Always Typical use Spanner, Chubby etcd, Consul

docs.title: 5. Quick math
docs.text: With n = 5 nodes, a majority is ⌊5/2⌋ + 1 = 3, so the cluster survives 2 failures. With n = 4, a majority is still 3, so it survives only 1 failure, which is why odd cluster sizes are preferred.

docs.title: 6. Questions to review
docs.text:
1. Why can't a node with a stale log become leader?
  2. What happens to uncommitted entries when a leader crashes?
  3. How does Raft handle a network partition that isolates the leader?

docs.title: 7. Sources
docs.text:
• Ongaro & Ousterhout, In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (2014)
  • Lamport, Paxos Made Simple (2001)
  • https://raft.github.io/

docs.title: PRD: Saved Searches
docs.text: Status: Draft Author: Product team Last updated: 2026-10-12

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text: Users repeat the same searches every day. Today they retype the query and re-apply filters each time, which takes about 40 seconds per search based on session recordings.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Let a user save a search (query + filters + sort) with a name
  • Show saved searches in the sidebar
  • Notify the user when new results match a saved search

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Sharing saved searches with other users (v2)
  • Saved searches on mobile (v2)

docs.title: 3. User stories
docs.text:
1. As an analyst, I want to save a search so that I can rerun it in one click.
  2. As an analyst, I want to rename or delete a saved search.
  3. As a manager, I want a daily email digest of new matches.

docs.title: 4.1 Functional
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority F1 Save the current search with a name (max 80 chars) P0 F2 List saved searches, most recent first P0 F3 Rename and delete a saved search P1 F4 Daily digest email for new matches P2

docs.title: 4.2 Non-functional
docs.text:
• Saving a search must complete in under 200 ms (p95)
  • A user can have at most 50 saved searches

docs.title: 5. API
docs.text:
The client calls a new endpoint:

POST /api/v1/saved-searches
Content-Type: application/json

{"name": "Open P1 bugs", "query": "priority:P1 status:open", "sort": "updated"}

The response includes the new search's id and created_at.

docs.title: 6. Open questions
docs.text:
• Should the digest respect the user's timezone or the account's?
  • Do we cap digest frequency for searches with hundreds of new matches?

docs.title: 7. Appendix
docs.text: See the search architecture doc and the analytics dashboard.

docs.title: fastqueue
docs.text: A small, dependency-free job queue for Python services.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• In-process or Redis-backed storage
  • Retries with exponential backoff
  • Scheduled jobs (run_at=)
  • Type-annotated API

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install fastqueue

For Redis support:

pip install "fastqueue[redis]"

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
from fastqueue import Queue

q = Queue()

@q.job(retries=3)
def send_email(to: str, subject: str) -> None:
    ...

send_email.delay("user@example.com", "Welcome!")
q.run_worker()

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Option Default Description backend "memory" "memory" or "redis" redis_url None Required when backend="redis" max_retries 5 Upper bound for any job poll_interval 0.5 Seconds between polls

docs.title: Usage notes
docs.text:
1. Jobs must be importable by the worker process.
  2. Arguments must be JSON-serializable.
  3. Use q.job(timeout=...) for long-running work: 
    @q.job(timeout=300)
def rebuild_index(): ...
  4. Call q.shutdown() on exit to flush pending acks.

Note: the in-memory backend loses jobs when the process exits. Use Redis in production.

docs.title: How to Set Up a Local Development Environment
docs.text: This guide walks you through setting up the service on macOS or Linux. It takes about 15 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or newer
  • Docker Desktop (or Docker Engine on Linux)
  • Access to the team's GitHub organization

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository.
git clone https://github.com/example/service.git
cd service
  1. Create a virtual environment and install dependencies.
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
  1. Start the backing services. This starts Postgres and Redis in containers:
docker compose up -d db redis

Wait until both containers report healthy:

docker compose ps
  1. Configure your environment.
  2. Copy .env.example to .env
  3. Set DATABASE_URL to postgresql://dev:dev@localhost:5432/service

  4. Leave FEATURE_FLAGS empty unless you need a specific flag

  5. Run the migrations and start the server.

make migrate
make run

The server listens on http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Port 5432 is already in use. Another Postgres is running. Stop it, or change the port mapping in docker-compose.yml.

pip install fails on psycopg. Install the Postgres client headers:

  • macOS: brew install libpq
  • Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install libpq-dev

Tip: run make doctor to check every prerequisite at once.

docs.title: Comparison: Hosted Postgres Providers
docs.text: We evaluated three providers for the analytics database. Prices are list prices for a 4 vCPU / 16 GB instance with 500 GB storage, as of October 2026.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: Provider A Provider B Provider C Monthly cost $410 $365 $520 Point-in-time recovery ✅ 30 days ✅ 7 days ✅ 35 days Read replicas Up to 5 Up to 3 Up to 10 Private networking ✅ ❌ ✅ Postgres 17 ✅ Preview ✅ SOC 2 Type II ✅ ✅ ✅

docs.title: Provider A
docs.text:
Pros

  • Private networking included at no extra cost

Cons

  • Support response times are slow on the standard plan

docs.title: Provider B
docs.text:
Pros

  • Very fast provisioning (under 2 minutes)

Cons

  • Postgres 17 is still in preview

docs.title: Provider C
docs.text:
Pros

  • Longest PITR window

Cons

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text: Criterion Weight A B C Cost 30% 7 9 5 Reliability 30% 8 6 9 Security fit 25% 9 2 9 Operability 15% 8 7 8 Weighted total 7.95 6.05 7.65

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: Go with Provider A. Provider B fails our private-networking requirement, and Provider C's extra replica capacity doesn't justify the cost at our current scale. Revisit if we need more than 5 replicas.

docs.title: Postmortem: Checkout Outage on October 9
docs.text: Severity: SEV-1 Duration: 47 minutes (14:12–14:59 UTC) Impact: ~18% of checkout attempts failed; estimated $42k in delayed orders

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A configuration change raised the payment service's connection pool from 50 to 500. The database hit its connection limit within minutes, and checkout requests started timing out.

docs.title: Timeline (UTC)
docs.text: Time Event 14:05 Config change merged and deployed 14:12 Error rate alert fires for payments-api 14:18 On-call acknowledges, starts investigating 14:31 Database connection saturation identified 14:44 Config change reverted 14:59 Error rate back to baseline

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The pool size is set per pod, not per service. With 10 pods, the change meant 5,000 potential connections against a database limit of 1,000.

# payments-api/config.yaml (the bad change)
db:
  pool_size: 500   # was 50

docs.title: What went well
docs.text:
• Alerting fired within 7 minutes
  • The revert path was fast and well understood

docs.title: What went poorly
docs.text:
• The change had no review from the database team
  • The config file has no comment explaining that pool_size is per pod
  • It took 13 minutes to connect the errors to the database

docs.title: Action items
docs.text: # Action Owner Due 1 Add a CI check that caps pool_size × replicas Platform Oct 23 2 Comment pool_size semantics in the config Payments Oct 16 3 Add a DB-connections panel to the payments dashboard SRE Oct 20 4 Require DB-team review for pool changes Eng leads Oct 30

docs.title: Lessons
docs.text:
1. Per-instance settings need the multiplier spelled out next to them.
  2. A dashboard panel for the shared resource would have cut diagnosis time:
  3. connections in use
  4. connections waiting
  5. rejected connections

docs.title: 1. The problem
docs.text: A group of nodes must agree on a single value, even if some nodes crash or messages are delayed. Consensus is the core of replicated logs, leader election, and distributed locks.

docs.title: 2. Key properties
docs.text:
• Safety: nodes never decide different values
  • Liveness: nodes eventually decide
  • Fault tolerance: works with up to f failures out of 2f + 1 nodes

docs.title: 3. Raft in brief
docs.text:
1. Leader election
  2. Every node starts as a follower
  3. A follower that hears nothing for an election timeout becomes a candidate and asks for votes
  4. A candidate with a majority becomes the leader
  5. Log replication
  6. The leader appends client commands to its log
  7. It sends AppendEntries to followers
  8. An entry is committed once a majority stores it
  9. Safety rule
  10. A candidate can only win if its log is at least as up to date as a majority's

docs.title: 4. Paxos vs. Raft
docs.text: Paxos Raft Designed for Correctness proofs Understandability Leader Optional (Multi-Paxos uses one) Always Typical use Spanner, Chubby etcd, Consul

docs.title: 5. Quick math
docs.text: With n = 5 nodes, a majority is ⌊5/2⌋ + 1 = 3, so the cluster survives 2 failures. With n = 4, a majority is still 3, so it survives only 1 failure, which is why odd cluster sizes are preferred.

docs.title: 6. Questions to review
docs.text:
1. Why can't a node with a stale log become leader?
  2. What happens to uncommitted entries when a leader crashes?
  3. How does Raft handle a network partition that isolates the leader?

docs.title: 7. Sources
docs.text:
• Ongaro & Ousterhout, In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (2014)
  • Lamport, Paxos Made Simple (2001)
  • https://raft.github.io/

docs.title: PRD: Saved Searches
docs.text: Status: Draft Author: Product team Last updated: 2026-10-12

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text: Users repeat the same searches every day. Today they retype the query and re-apply filters each time, which takes about 40 seconds per search based on session recordings.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Let a user save a search (query + filters + sort) with a name
  • Show saved searches in the sidebar
  • Notify the user when new results match a saved search

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Sharing saved searches with other users (v2)
  • Saved searches on mobile (v2)

docs.title: 3. User stories
docs.text:
1. As an analyst, I want to save a search so that I can rerun it in one click.
  2. As an analyst, I want to rename or delete a saved search.
  3. As a manager, I want a daily email digest of new matches.

docs.title: 4.1 Functional
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority F1 Save the current search with a name (max 80 chars) P0 F2 List saved searches, most recent first P0 F3 Rename and delete a saved search P1 F4 Daily digest email for new matches P2

docs.title: 4.2 Non-functional
docs.text:
• Saving a search must complete in under 200 ms (p95)
  • A user can have at most 50 saved searches

docs.title: 5. API
docs.text:
The client calls a new endpoint:

POST /api/v1/saved-searches
Content-Type: application/json

{"name": "Open P1 bugs", "query": "priority:P1 status:open", "sort": "updated"}

The response includes the new search's id and created_at.

docs.title: 6. Open questions
docs.text:
• Should the digest respect the user's timezone or the account's?
  • Do we cap digest frequency for searches with hundreds of new matches?

docs.title: 7. Appendix
docs.text: See the search architecture doc and the analytics dashboard.

docs.title: fastqueue
docs.text: A small, dependency-free job queue for Python services.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• In-process or Redis-backed storage
  • Retries with exponential backoff
  • Scheduled jobs (run_at=)
  • Type-annotated API

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install fastqueue

For Redis support:

pip install "fastqueue[redis]"

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
from fastqueue import Queue

q = Queue()

@q.job(retries=3)
def send_email(to: str, subject: str) -> None:
    ...

send_email.delay("user@example.com", "Welcome!")
q.run_worker()

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Option Default Description backend "memory" "memory" or "redis" redis_url None Required when backend="redis" max_retries 5 Upper bound for any job poll_interval 0.5 Seconds between polls

docs.title: Usage notes
docs.text:
1. Jobs must be importable by the worker process.
  2. Arguments must be JSON-serializable.
  3. Use q.job(timeout=...) for long-running work: 
    @q.job(timeout=300)
def rebuild_index(): ...
  4. Call q.shutdown() on exit to flush pending acks.

Note: the in-memory backend loses jobs when the process exits. Use Redis in production.

docs.title: How to Set Up a Local Development Environment
docs.text: This guide walks you through setting up the service on macOS or Linux. It takes about 15 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or newer
  • Docker Desktop (or Docker Engine on Linux)
  • Access to the team's GitHub organization

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository.
git clone https://github.com/example/service.git
cd service
  1. Create a virtual environment and install dependencies.
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
  1. Start the backing services. This starts Postgres and Redis in containers:
docker compose up -d db redis

Wait until both containers report healthy:

docker compose ps
  1. Configure your environment.
  2. Copy .env.example to .env
  3. Set DATABASE_URL to postgresql://dev:dev@localhost:5432/service

  4. Leave FEATURE_FLAGS empty unless you need a specific flag

  5. Run the migrations and start the server.

make migrate
make run

The server listens on http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Port 5432 is already in use. Another Postgres is running. Stop it, or change the port mapping in docker-compose.yml.

pip install fails on psycopg. Install the Postgres client headers:

  • macOS: brew install libpq
  • Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install libpq-dev

Tip: run make doctor to check every prerequisite at once.

docs.title: Comparison: Hosted Postgres Providers
docs.text: We evaluated three providers for the analytics database. Prices are list prices for a 4 vCPU / 16 GB instance with 500 GB storage, as of October 2026.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text: Provider A Provider B Provider C Monthly cost $410 $365 $520 Point-in-time recovery ✅ 30 days ✅ 7 days ✅ 35 days Read replicas Up to 5 Up to 3 Up to 10 Private networking ✅ ❌ ✅ Postgres 17 ✅ Preview ✅ SOC 2 Type II ✅ ✅ ✅

docs.title: Provider A
docs.text:
Pros

  • Mature tooling and a good CLI
  • Private networking included at no extra cost

Cons

  • Read replicas cost the same as the primary
  • Support response times are slow on the standard plan

docs.title: Provider B
docs.text:
Pros

  • Cheapest option
  • Very fast provisioning (under 2 minutes)

Cons

  • No private networking, which our security policy requires
  • Postgres 17 is still in preview

docs.title: Provider C
docs.text:
Pros

  • Best replica story (up to 10, cross-region)
  • Longest PITR window

Cons

  • Most expensive, by about 27% over Provider A

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text: Criterion Weight A B C Cost 30% 7 9 5 Reliability 30% 8 6 9 Security fit 25% 9 2 9 Operability 15% 8 7 8 Weighted total 7.95 6.05 7.65

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: Go with Provider A. Provider B fails our private-networking requirement, and Provider C's extra replica capacity doesn't justify the cost at our current scale. Revisit if we need more than 5 replicas.

docs.title: Postmortem: Checkout Outage on October 9
docs.text: Severity: SEV-1 Duration: 47 minutes (14:12–14:59 UTC) Impact: ~18% of checkout attempts failed; estimated $42k in delayed orders

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: A configuration change raised the payment service's connection pool from 50 to 500. The database hit its connection limit within minutes, and checkout requests started timing out.

docs.title: Timeline (UTC)
docs.text: Time Event 14:05 Config change merged and deployed 14:12 Error rate alert fires for payments-api 14:18 On-call acknowledges, starts investigating 14:31 Database connection saturation identified 14:44 Config change reverted 14:59 Error rate back to baseline

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The pool size is set per pod, not per service. With 10 pods, the change meant 5,000 potential connections against a database limit of 1,000.

# payments-api/config.yaml (the bad change)
db:
  pool_size: 500   # was 50

docs.title: What went well
docs.text:
• Alerting fired within 7 minutes
  • The revert path was fast and well understood

docs.title: What went poorly
docs.text:
• The change had no review from the database team
  • The config file has no comment explaining that pool_size is per pod
  • It took 13 minutes to connect the errors to the database

docs.title: Action items
docs.text: # Action Owner Due 1 Add a CI check that caps pool_size × replicas Platform Oct 23 2 Comment pool_size semantics in the config Payments Oct 16 3 Add a DB-connections panel to the payments dashboard SRE Oct 20 4 Require DB-team review for pool changes Eng leads Oct 30

docs.title: Lessons
docs.text:
1. Per-instance settings need the multiplier spelled out next to them.
  2. A dashboard panel for the shared resource would have cut diagnosis time:
  3. connections in use
  4. connections waiting
  5. rejected connections

docs.title: 1. The problem
docs.text: A group of nodes must agree on a single value, even if some nodes crash or messages are delayed. Consensus is the core of replicated logs, leader election, and distributed locks.

docs.title: 2. Key properties
docs.text:
• Safety: nodes never decide different values
  • Liveness: nodes eventually decide
  • Fault tolerance: works with up to f failures out of 2f + 1 nodes

docs.title: 3. Raft in brief
docs.text:
1. Leader election
  2. Every node starts as a follower
  3. A follower that hears nothing for an election timeout becomes a candidate and asks for votes
  4. A candidate with a majority becomes the leader
  5. Log replication
  6. The leader appends client commands to its log
  7. It sends AppendEntries to followers
  8. An entry is committed once a majority stores it
  9. Safety rule
  10. A candidate can only win if its log is at least as up to date as a majority's

docs.title: 4. Paxos vs. Raft
docs.text: Paxos Raft Designed for Correctness proofs Understandability Leader Optional (Multi-Paxos uses one) Always Typical use Spanner, Chubby etcd, Consul

docs.title: 5. Quick math
docs.text: With n = 5 nodes, a majority is ⌊5/2⌋ + 1 = 3, so the cluster survives 2 failures. With n = 4, a majority is still 3, so it survives only 1 failure, which is why odd cluster sizes are preferred.

docs.title: 6. Questions to review
docs.text:
1. Why can't a node with a stale log become leader?
  2. What happens to uncommitted entries when a leader crashes?
  3. How does Raft handle a network partition that isolates the leader?

docs.title: 7. Sources
docs.text:
• Ongaro & Ousterhout, In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (2014)
  • Lamport, Paxos Made Simple (2001)
  • https://raft.github.io/

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
TC-W03 — Range smaller than data provided Expected: oversized 2D array silently truncated to fit the range. Observed: API returns 400 error "tried writing to row [10]" — no silent truncation. Test assumption was wrong; this is an API constraint, not a bug.

TC-C01 — COLUMN chart Expected: chart created from A1:D5. Observed: API error "ChartSourceRange ranges require all rows or all columns to have length of 1". Root cause: tool passes entire range as a single ChartSourceRange; API requires per-column source ranges for domains and series.

TC-C02 — BAR chart Same root cause as TC-C01.

TC-C03 — LINE chart Same root cause as TC-C01.

TC-C04 — AREA chart Same root cause as TC-C01.

TC-C05 — PIE chart Same root cause as TC-C01 (A1:B5 is still multi-column × multi-row).

TC-C06 — SCATTER chart Same root cause as TC-C01.

TC-C07 — COMBO chart Same root cause as TC-C01.

TC-C08 — HISTOGRAM chart Two separate issues: (1) same multi-column range bug as TC-C01; (2) HISTOGRAM is not a valid BasicChartType — the Sheets API uses a separate histogramChart spec, not basicChart.

TC-C10 — Lowercase chart type input Same multi-column range bug as TC-C01. Lowercase normalization works (confirmed .upper() fires), but chart creation fails at the API.

TC-C12 — Custom position and size Same multi-column range bug as TC-C01.

docs.title: BUG-1: add_chart fails for any multi-column, multi-row data range
docs.text: Severity: High — affects all practical chart use cases. Error: "ChartSourceRange ranges require all rows or all columns to have length of 1" Root cause: charts.py passes the full range as a single source range object. The Sheets addChart API requires separate source range objects for each column — one for the domain (X axis / categories, typically column A) and one per series (subsequent columns). Fix direction: Parse the A1 range into per-column ranges. Split into domain range (first column) and series ranges (remaining columns), pass as separate entries in sources. Confirmed workaround: Single-column ranges work (TC-C03 with B1:B5 passed).

docs.title: BUG-2: add_chart HISTOGRAM type uses wrong API spec
docs.text: Severity: Medium — HISTOGRAM specifically broken even after BUG-1 is fixed. Error: "Invalid value at requests[0].add_chart.chart.spec.basic_chart.chart_type, HISTOGRAM" Root cause: HISTOGRAM is not a valid BasicChartType enum value. The Sheets API uses histogramChart (a separate spec field) rather than basicChart.chartType = HISTOGRAM. Fix direction: In charts.py, detect chart_type == "HISTOGRAM" and build a histogramChart spec instead of a basicChart spec.

docs.title: Quota blocker: service account Drive storage quota exhausted
docs.text: Affected TCs: TC-D01–D12 (create), TC-D43, TC-D67–D69 (copy_file), TC-D88–D92 (upload_file), all download/sync tests. Cause: The write test suite added 1000+ rows and 5+ columns to the fixture spreadsheet (TC-W16, W17–W20), consuming the service account's Drive storage quota. This is not a bug in the tools — all affected tools return clear storageQuotaExceeded errors. The service account documentation should note this limit. Recommendation: Add a note to setup.md that service accounts have limited Drive storage quota. Destructive write tests should reset fixtures promptly to avoid accumulating quota usage.

docs.text:
TC-R12 — Multiple valid queries Expected: two sheet results with data, no error field. Observed: both queries return {"error": "Missing required keys (spreadsheet_id, sheet, range)"}. range is enforced as required by the implementation even though get_sheet_data accepts no range. The test cases (and tool intent) assume range is optional.

TC-R13 — One query with missing required keys Expected: Sales sheet succeeds; second (invalid) query returns error. Observed: both queries fail with "Missing required keys" — the valid Sales query also fails because range is absent.

TC-R14 — All queries fail Expected: both results have error fields referencing sheet-not-found. Observed: both results fail with "Missing required keys" instead — the sheet-not-found path is never reached.

Root cause (R12–R14): get_multiple_sheet_data validates that each query dict contains spreadsheet_id, sheet, and range. range should be optional (defaulting to full sheet, like get_sheet_data does).

docs.title: Observations
docs.text:
link_url auto-underline (TC-D181): Google Docs automatically sets underline: true on runs with a link_url. This is API behaviour, not a tool bug. Test case notes this.

precedingParagraphIndex (TC-D167): The Docs API requires an empty paragraph before every table and will not allow deleting it while the table exists. insert_doc_table now returns precedingParagraphIndex (= tableStartIndex − 1) so callers can delete [precedingParagraphIndex, tableEndIndex] in one range for a clean full-table removal.

Cleanup pattern confirmed: delete_doc_range({start: precedingParagraphIndex, end: tableEndIndex}) removes both the preceding paragraph and the table body in one call, leaving no leftover paragraphs.
