docs.title: Rowspan emitter bugs found and fixed (TC-D187, D188)
docs.text:
Fix #1 — Sort doc_cells by startIndex (_build_fill_requests): After mergeTableCells for rowspan, the Docs API returns covered (phantom) cells last in the tableCells array rather than in column order. Without sorting, the mapping zip was misaligned — the real cell was skipped and the phantom was filled. Fixed by sorting doc_cells by startIndex before zipping.

Fix #2 — Colspan-absorbed cells emit None (_physical_to_ast_indices): For combined colspan+rowspan, the colspan-absorbed col remains as a physical cell post-merge (same as a rowspan phantom). Previously, absorbed cols were skipped with continue, producing no mapping entry, which caused the next zip pair to align against the wrong doc_cell. Fixed by appending None instead of skipping, keeping the mapping length aligned with physical cell count.

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
TC-D73 — Trash folder does not invalidate drive_folder_cache Expected: list_folders no longer shows QA-Folder-Renamed-2 after delete_file trashes it. Observed: action:"trashed" returned, but list_folders still shows the folder. Stale cache not cleared. Playwright: tc-d73-trash-folder.png — folder truly absent from Drive UI, confirming the API call worked; the bug is solely in cache invalidation. → Bug: delete_file does not call invalidate on drive_folder_cache for the parent folder.

TC-D79 — get_file_metadata returns size for Google Sheets files Expected: size field absent for Google Workspace files (no storage quota consumed). Observed: size:"2274" returned — Drive API returns quotaBytesUsed as size for Sheets files. Playwright: n/a (API-only check). → Bug: Tool exposes size field that means quotaBytesUsed, not actual file size; misleading for Workspace files.

TC-D135 — share_file type=domain (environmental) Expected: sharing with example.com domain succeeds. Observed: failures:[{error:"The specified domain is invalid or not applicable..."}]. example.com is not a Google Workspace domain. → Environmental: test requires a real GWS domain. Tool error handling is correct.

TC-D137 — share_file folder with non-Google account (environmental) Expected: sharing QA-Folder-Renamed-2 with test-recipient@example.com succeeds. Observed: failures:[{error:"Forbidden...do not have a Google Account"}]. → Environmental: test-recipient@example.com is not a real Google account. Error propagated correctly.

TC-D139 — share_file send_notification=False with non-Google account (environmental) Expected: send_notification=False suppresses notification email. Observed: failures:[{error:"Bad Request...must check 'Notify people' box...no Google account"}]. Drive requires notification for non-Google account shares. → Environmental: same non-Google account limitation. Tool correctly propagates the Drive API error.

TC-D144 — write_doc_content multiple tables produces single merged table Expected: two separate <table> elements produce two separate tables in the doc. Observed: both tables merged into one 2×2 table; "Second table:" paragraph absent. Playwright: tc-d144-multiple-tables.png — confirmed single merged table. → Known gap (see project memory TC-D228): multi-table index corruption. tables[1].startIndex becomes stale after tables[0] is inserted; the emitter must re-fetch or compute offset adjustments between inserts.

TC-D148 — export_revision read range (environmental) Expected: earlier revision shows A1="QA-BEFORE", later shows A1="QA-AFTER". Observed: Drive grouped both rapid writes into single revision 271; A1="QA-AFTER" on both. → Environmental: Drive revision API coalesces rapid writes. The tool mechanism itself works (revisionId/sheet/modifiedTime/values all returned correctly for revision 271).

TC-CAL09 — list_events time_min docstring bug Expected: when time_min is omitted, API defaults to "now" per docstring. Observed: all past events returned (no timeMin set in API call). Implementation at calendar.py:115 only sets timeMin when the parameter is explicitly provided. → Bug: docstring says time_min "Defaults to now if omitted" — implementation does not match. timeMin must be set explicitly or it is omitted from the API call, returning all historical events.

docs.title: Additional notes (not failures)
docs.text: TC-CAL36/37 — create_event timezone required for recurring events Docstring says timezone is required only for all-day events. It is also required when recurrence is set and the event uses datetime start/end (not all-day). First call failed with "Missing time zone definition for start time"; retry with timezone='America/Los_Angeles' succeeded. → Documentation gap: update create_event docstring to note timezone is also required for recurring datetime events.

docs.title: Findings worth flagging (not scored as TC failures — no existing check covers them)
docs.text:
1. write_doc_content's clear+reinsert path leaks a stale font_size:1 override into freshly-written plain paragraphs — recommend filing a GitHub issue. At session-1 Step 0, get_doc_structure on the fixture doc showed every text run at font_size: 1 even though get_doc_named_styles reported normal named-style defaults (NORMAL_TEXT 11pt). Root cause: write_doc_content's "clear + reinsert" strategy (deleteContentRange(1, end_index-1) then insert at index 1) never touches the final paragraph mark, so a stale explicit textStyle on that trailing character survives every full-document rewrite. Newly inserted content at index 1 appears to inherit ambient style from that untouched trailing context in some cases (plain paragraphs) but not others (headings render correctly; table-cell content renders correctly).

This was reproduced four separate times across the full run — fixed manually via style_doc_range after TC-DOC42, after TC-DOC47, and again independently confirmed in session 2 (post-outage): after a plain write_doc_content restore, get_doc_theme reported NORMAL_TEXT: {font_family: "Courier New", font_size: 1} on a doc whose most recent explicit HTML content contained no code spans — the doc's ambient style was contaminated by leftover state from the previous content, not the new content being written. Session 2 also surfaced a compounding detail: there is no exposed tool parameter to clear an inherited font_family override — style_doc_range supports font_size but not font_family, so the only way to fully normalize a contaminated doc is apply_theme(overwrite=True), which is a much heavier operation than the bug that necessitates it.

Net: calling write_doc_content to replace content whose previous state had an explicit font/size override (e.g. from a table, or a fenced code block) can cause the new content to silently inherit that override, rendering it in the wrong font or at unreadable 1pt size until manually restyled. No existing TC in docs.md checks post-write font styling on plain paragraphs, so this never fails a TC outcome, but it affects real usage (anyone iterating on a doc with write_doc_content after having had a table or code block in it) and is worth a ticket — likely fix is extending the clear+reinsert range in write_doc_content (or the blank-paragraph-before-table collapse logic) to also reset the trailing paragraph mark's textStyle, and/or adding font_family to style_doc_range's supported fields as a mitigation.

2. TC-DOC47 — possible over-broad font_family application (unconfirmed, still needs a follow-up check). After writing Use the `print()` function via markdown, the rendered line appeared uniformly monospace in the Google Docs editor (visual screenshot), and clicking to the very start of the line showed "Courier New" selected in the font toolbar — suggesting the Courier styling may have applied to the whole paragraph rather than just the print() code span. html_parser.py's code-span handling (font_family="Courier New" if (self._in_pre or self._code_depth > 0) else None, lines ~74) looks correct at the AST level — only text nodes inside <code> should get the font override — so this may be a Google Docs toolbar/cursor-position display quirk rather than a real over-application, and may simply be an artifact of Finding 1's contamination rather than a distinct bug. Could not conclusively verify because get_doc_structure doesn't expose font_family per run (an acknowledged existing gap). Recommend a targeted follow-up: call the raw Docs API (or extend get_doc_structure to expose font_family) and check whether only the print() run carries weightedFontFamily: Courier New, or whether the whole paragraph does.

3. TC-DOC57's prescribed test image URI (SVG) is rejected by the live Google Docs API — the test file's prompt needs updating. The test case's exact prompt URI (https://www.gstatic.com/images/branding/googlelogo/svg/googlelogo_clr_74x24px.svg) fails on every attempt with HttpError 400: There was a problem retrieving the image. The provided image should be publicly accessible, within size limit, and in supported formats. — this is Google's own API rejecting the SVG format, not a bug in insert_inline_image. Substituting a PNG at the same host (https://www.gstatic.com/images/branding/googlelogo/1x/googlelogo_color_92x30dp.png) succeeded immediately and rendered correctly. TC-DOC57 is recorded PASS on the basis of the PNG substitution (matching what appears to have happened in the historical result too, which mentions "PNG" despite the test file specifying an SVG URL). Recommend updating the test file's prompt to use a PNG/JPEG URL so future runs don't need to silently substitute.

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
TC-R10 — Mixed cells — formulas and literals Expected: "B2 returns =TODAY() (formula string)". Observed: The test case's cell reference does not match the actual fixture layout. Per setup.md's seed data, Notes & Misc is Date (column A), Note (column B) — so A2 contains =TODAY() and B2 contains the literal "Setup complete". Live call to get_sheet_formulas(sheet="Notes & Misc") returned [["Date","Note"],["=TODAY()","Setup complete"]] — i.e., the tool correctly differentiates formula vs. literal cells (no computed value where a formula exists, header row is literal), but strictly by the check as written, B2 does not return =TODAY(). This reads as a test-file documentation defect (swapped A2/B2 reference) rather than a product bug — recording FAIL rather than silently "fixing" the interpretation, per the checks-as-written. Recommend the test file be corrected to reference A2.

TC-R19 — rows_to_fetch=0 — clamped to 1 (🔍 product decision) Expected: "Server clamps to 1 (max(1, 0))" and "Behaves identically to TC-R18." Observed: Cache-state-dependent bug, not just a product-decision question. Traced to source (src/mcp_gee_sweet/tools/sheets/data.py:304, src/mcp_gee_sweet/cache.py:189): - Cold cache (immediately after refresh_cache, rows_to_fetch=0 as the very first call): correctly clamps via max(1, rows_to_fetch) on the fetch path (data.py:304) → range A1:1 → first_rows: []. Matches TC-R18. - Warm cache (cache already primed by an earlier call with a larger rows_to_fetch, e.g. the default 5 from TC-R16): the cache-hit truncation path (cache.py:189, data["first_rows"][: rows_to_fetch - 1]) does not apply the same clamp. rows_to_fetch - 1 = 0 - 1 = -1, and Python's negative-slice semantics ([:-1]) silently drop only the last cached row instead of returning an empty list. Live-verified: on a warm cache, rows_to_fetch=0 returned 3 data rows (Widget/Gadget/Donut — all but the 4th cached row, Gizmo), not the empty list TC-R18-equivalent behavior would produce.

This is more than the anticipated 🔍 "should 0 mean only-headers or clamp-to-1" product question — it's an actual inconsistency: the same input (rows_to_fetch=0) produces different, disagreeing outputs depending on prior cache state, regardless of which product answer is intended. Recording FAIL (not the usual auto-PASS for 🔍-tagged cases) because a real defect was found underneath the product question. Suggested fix: apply the same max(1, rows_to_fetch) clamp in cache.py's truncation slice as data.py applies on the fetch path.

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
TC-R10 — Mixed cells — formulas and literals (sheets_read shard) Test-file defect, not a product bug: the check references B2 for =TODAY() but the actual fixture layout has it in A2 (Date=col A, Note=col B in "Notes & Misc"). The tool correctly differentiates formula vs. literal cells. Action: correct the cell reference in docs/qa/tests/sheets_read.md's TC-R10 — no code change needed.

TC-R19 — rows_to_fetch=0 clamping (sheets_read shard) Real bug: rows_to_fetch=0 clamps correctly to 1 on a cold cache (src/mcp_gee_sweet/tools/sheets/data.py:304), but on a warm cache the truncation slice in src/mcp_gee_sweet/cache.py:189 (first_rows[:rows_to_fetch - 1]) computes 0 - 1 = -1; Python's negative-slice semantics silently drop only the last cached row instead of clamping to empty. Same input, different output depending on prior cache state. Action: file a GitHub issue; fix is applying the same max(1, rows_to_fetch) clamp on the cache-hit path in cache.py that data.py already applies on the fetch path.

docs.title: Findings (not TC failures, but worth ticketing before/shortly after release)
docs.text:
write_doc_content clear+reinsert leaks stale font_size/font_family into new content (docs shard, Finding 1) Reproduced 4 times independently. Root cause: the clear+reinsert strategy never resets the final paragraph mark's textStyle, so a stale explicit override (e.g. from a table or fenced code block) survives a full-document rewrite and can leak into freshly-written plain paragraphs (1pt font observed). Compounding gap: style_doc_range has no font_family parameter, so there's no lightweight way to clean up contamination once it happens — only the much heavier apply_theme(overwrite=True) can. Action: file a GitHub issue.

TC-DOC47's prescribed SVG image URL is rejected by the live Google Docs API (docs shard, Finding 3) Google's API itself rejects the test's SVG URI (HttpError 400, unsupported format) — not a product bug. A PNG at the same host works. Action: update the test file's prompt to a PNG/JPEG URL, no code or GitHub issue needed.

TC-DOC47 possible over-broad font_family application (docs shard, Finding 2, unconfirmed) Visual inspection suggested the whole line may have rendered monospace, not just the print() code span — but this couldn't be conclusively separated from Finding 1's contamination, and get_doc_structure doesn't expose font_family to verify precisely. Action: no ticket yet; revisit if font_family exposure is added to get_doc_structure (or as part of investigating Finding 1).

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
TC-D18/D19/D20/D23/D24/D176 — share_spreadsheet broken on Shared Drives (one root cause, BUG-SS) Expected: share succeeds, entries land in successes. Observed: every call returns failures:[{"error":"Failed to share: File not found: <id>."}]. Reproduced on a throwaway sheet and the real fixture. Root cause (confirmed in source): share_spreadsheet._share_one's permissions().create() call omits supportsAllDrives=True — the only permission op in tools/drive/sharing.py missing it (update_permission, remove_permission, list_permissions, transfer_ownership, share_file all have it). Since fixtures + the default DRIVE_FOLDER_ID are now a Shared Drive (#305), the tool fails on any file it's pointed at in this deployment. share_file works (functional workaround exists). One-line fix.

TC-D124 — stale test-case assumption, not a tool bug list_permissions on the Shared-Drive fixture shows organizer/fileOrganizer roles, no owner (owners: [], correct for Shared Drive items). The TC's "expect an owner entry" check predates the #305 migration. Test-case fix applied (see below).

TC-D01 — create_spreadsheet response has no web link Response is {spreadsheetId, title, folder}; the TC expects a web link. Siblings (copy_file, create_folder, get_file_metadata) do return one. Judgment call, not filed as a bug yet — see Bugs found.

TC-D13 — stale test-case assumption list_spreadsheets(default) no longer includes the fixture spreadsheet, because the default folder now resolves to the Shared Drive root (DRIVE_FOLDER_ID) and the fixture lives in the FOLDER_ID subfolder — correct post-#305 behavior, stale TC text.

TC-D40 — list_files max_results cache-poisoning (BUG-CACHE) list_files(FOLDER_ID, max_results=2) returned 5 on the first call (a prior default-max_results call's cache hit ignored the smaller limit); a subsequent small-max_results fetch then stores the truncated list, so later default-size calls get only the truncated result until refresh_cache. Reproduced twice. Root cause: the folder-listing cache key omits max_results. Affects list_files, list_spreadsheets, list_folders (shared cache). Silent, persistent wrong data — the most severe finding this pass.

TC-D167 — stale #519-cap test premise, same class as TC-DOC80 export_file's base64-xlsx response no longer trips the (raised) MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_CHARS default at this fixture's size. Not a regression; needs the same low-cap re-run method as TC-DOC80 (#678) — tracked as a follow-up, not re-run this pass (lower priority: export_file's cap-check code path is exercised and passing via TC-DOC80's sibling get_doc_content check and unit tests).

TC-W02 — test-prompt bug, not a tool bug Prompt used single-quote string delimiters in a Sheets formula (=A2&' '&A3); Google Sheets requires double quotes, producing #ERROR!. Re-run with =A2&" "&A3 succeeded; USER_ENTERED mode independently confirmed. Test-file fix applied (see below).

docs.title: Process notes
docs.text:
• Playwright auth gap, corrected mid-pass. Every shard initially hit an unauthenticated Playwright browser (redirects to Google sign-in), concluded Playwright was unusable, and fell back to API-level-only verification. Once the user authenticated Playwright mid-pass, corrections were sent to live shards (one was misdirected due to an agent-ID mix-up on my end, caught and fixed) and a targeted re-verification pass redid the highest-value already-completed visual checks (10 docs/transfer TCs + 7 Sheets TCs) with real screenshots — all confirmed, no discrepancies. Filed PR #686 to make Playwright-auth verification a real pre-flight step (not just a connection check) for future passes.
  • Service-account calendar fixture gap. The SA wasn't subscribed to the real fixture calendar, so the Calendar shard ran its full suite against SA-owned substitute calendars (still valid tool-behavior coverage). A targeted OAuth re-run against the real fixture closed the gap for the 6 identity-sensitive cases plus 2 that only work under OAuth (attendee invites) — all PASS, real fixture left untouched.
  • Cross-shard fixture interference, resolved. The Sheets shard's writes to the fixture spreadsheet transiently corrupted the Drive-transfer shard's CSV-export comparison mid-pass. Re-checked after Sheets restored the fixture to seed state — clean, confirms it was timing, not a product bug.
  • OAuth token refresh issue (infra, not QA). A fresh script/process using the main-checkout token.json now hits invalid_grant on refresh; already-running server processes are unaffected (cached token). Recommend re-running scripts/oauth_setup.py before the next session needs a fresh OAuth connection. This blocked one live re-verification (TC-DOC159); disposed via a source-diff argument instead (code path unchanged since its last live PASS).
  • All-slots release-QA rule and the "verify Playwright first" fix were both codified as command-file PRs (#685, #686) during this pass, per direct user instruction, rather than left as one-off in-conversation guidance.

docs.title: Markdown rendering baseline, Phase 2 — 2026-10-18 (#1044)
docs.text:
The second live run of docs/qa/tests/docs_markdown.md: Phase 2, the 17 syntax fixtures (TC-MD101–117) and the 4 matrices (TC-MD201–204), 467 cases. Phase 1 is in 2026-10-18-markdown.md. Document boundaries (TC-MD301–303) and document state (TC-MD401–404) are still to run.

Result: 1,522 of 3,758 case × entry-point cells pass (40%); no TC passes. Every case went through all 8 entry points twice. Across 498 screenshot pages, 478 were identical between the runs, 9 differed only by a spell-check squiggle, and 11 (EP-8 of TC-MD108 and TC-MD202) changed font, which fails Rule 4.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
• Code under test: develop at 504a5b2b, the same server processes as Phase 1 (stdio servers load the package once at start). Two fixes merged to develop during the run and are not reflected here: #1089 (#1056, blockquote indent) and #1088 (#1057, soft-break export). Every "quote has a border but no indent" cell below predates #1089.
  • Servers and shards as in Phase 1: A kai-oauth (TC-MD201, 101, 102, 113, 114, 115), B oauth (TC-MD202, 103, 111, 112, 116), C kai-sa (TC-MD203, 109, 110, 117), D sa (TC-MD204, 104, 105, 106, 107, 108). Lanes A and B were mid-ticket, so lane servers weren't used.
  • Approvals: the Phase 1 write categories, plus "go ahead with phase 2, shares approved" for TC-MD112's temporary "anyone with the link" shares. Every image result reported shared: false afterwards (revoked).
  • Folders: QA-MD-2026-10-18-p2-run1 and -p2-run2 under TEST_FOLDER_ID, one subfolder per shard with ep5/ep6/ep7 children. Trashed after recording, with the image uploads TC-MD112 made outside them.
  • TC-MD112 used md-images.local.md (ignored) with the placeholders substituted; the Drive copy of qa-fixture-pixel.png sat in the run 1 folder.
  • TC-MD111 also ran EP-1 to EP-4 with autolink_urls=False.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Phase 2's fixtures hold many cases each, and the matrices run 8–11 pages, so the per-case screenshot of Phase 1 was replaced:

  • Deterministic page screenshots. One browser_run_code_unsafe call per Doc set a 1400×2200 viewport, then captured page k at .kix-appview-editor scrollTop = (k−1)×1900 until the end of the document (docs/qa/screenshots/md/p2-run<N>/EP-<n>/<TC>-<k>.jpeg, gitignored). Each page shows several cases; together they cover the whole document.
  • By eye for one entry point per engine, pixel identity for its siblings. Shards judged EP-1, EP-5 and EP-8 case by case. EP-2/3/4 were pixel-compared with EP-1 and EP-6/7 with EP-5, page by page (grayscale, threshold 40, Docs chrome, caret column and outline pane masked). Every sibling was pixel-identical except three spell-check squiggles (judged by eye: same content). EP-1 to EP-4 rendered identically to each other in every TC, and so did EP-5 to EP-7.
  • Run 2 re-rendered everything into a fresh folder with the same script and was pixel-compared page by page against Run 1, by each shard and again centrally. Every Run 2 file is newer than its Run 1 pair.
  • One judging gap closed: in Run 1 shard A didn't read EP-5 pages 3, 4, 7, 8, 10, 11 and EP-8 pages 5, 6, 8 of TC-MD201 frame by frame. Run 2's shard A judged those pages case by case; no verdict changed (none of Run 1's ✅ cells were on them).

docs.title: Findings that weren't filed
docs.text:
• Pagination: a short table split across a page break although the page had room (TC-MD203 AB-080), images pushed to the next page (AB-069), and BQ-09 starting a second page in both our engine and Drive's. Likely keep-with-next behaviour; not filed until it's shown to be ours.
  • Images uploaded outside the target folder: write_doc_content and update_doc_from_file upload a local image to the server's default folder, since those tools take no folder argument. Expected, but each call leaves an image file behind after the share is revoked.
  • Drive's task items render as native Docs checklists, not ● ☐ text; equivalent on screen, recorded under #1101.

docs.title: Process notes
docs.text:
• Lock incidents (Run 1): shard A acquired the Playwright lock in a background command and refreshed it late; another shard's stale recovery took it, and one of shard A's captures landed on another shard's Doc. Shard A discarded it and re-took it; the other shard confirmed every capture's Doc ID. Shard B also used stale recovery once on a 122-second-old lock. Run 2's rules required a foreground acquire, a keepalive, and 60 more seconds without an mtime change before stale recovery; no incidents. Lock waits reached 8 minutes with four shards and multi-page matrix Docs: the shared browser is the bottleneck of this suite.
  • Playwright's filename option only reads scripts under the worktree, so shards passed the screenshot script inline or wrote it to the ignored .playwright-mcp/.
  • No #1052 connection resets and no classifier denials in either run.

docs.text:
The same fixture rendered through upload_file(source_format="markdown", convert_to_doc=True) sets its fenced code blocks in a monospace font one time and in Arial the next:

Fixture Run 1 Run 2 Extra renders r04 monospace Arial — r11 Arial "Courier" (font box, read in the live Doc) — r13 monospace Arial 3 more, all Arial (1 of 5 monospace) r03, r16 monospace monospace —

Each shard re-shot the changed cell after a reload to rule out a font-loading race. get_doc_as_markdown exports the Arial renders without a fence, consistent with the runs not being Courier New. Text, line breaks and indentation were identical across runs. Filed under #1102.

docs.title: Findings that weren't filed
docs.text:
• Pagination in Drive-imported Docs (EP-5 to EP-7): tables split with a repeated header row, and a heading moves to the next page with its table. Ordinary Docs pagination, not a rendering defect.
  • Uneven column widths in r11's action-items table (EP-1 to EP-4): auto-sized columns; column widths are #809's territory.
  • Drive's task items render as native Docs checklists rather than ● ☐ text. Equivalent on screen; recorded under #1101 as an engine difference, not as a failure of its own.

docs.title: Process notes
docs.text:
• Lock slip (Run 1, shard A): one acquire and a browser_navigate went out in the same parallel batch, so a navigate ran at 15:38:50Z while another shard held the Playwright lock. The screenshots taken around that moment (TC-MD006 EP-1 at 15:38:45Z, TC-MD008 EP-1 at 15:38:57Z) show the right Docs. Run 2's rules required the acquire in its own call before any Playwright call; no recurrence.
  • Aziz's worktree token is a personal Gmail account, not the fixture owner, so it can't read the Shared Drive. The pre-flight in aziz.md checks only that the token refreshes. The mechanical structure diff planned for this run was dropped for the pixel comparison above; structural questions went through get_doc_structure on kai-oauth.
  • Worktree-isolation guard: shards had a few Bash calls refused (shell variables, $((…)), compound commands) and re-ran them as plain commands or scratch scripts. One shard's rm -rf of its own scratch dir was blocked by the safety check; it removed the empty dirs with rmdir. No classifier denials of any approved write.
  • #1052: no connection resets in either run.

Result: no TC passes.

docs.title: TC-MD404 — determinism across runs (FAIL)
docs.text:
Every page of every case and entry point in this run is identical between Run 1 and Run 2, with one exception: DS-05 EP-3. Its Run 2 call never returned and left an empty Doc.

The hang: - The client's log for that server shows create_doc_from_file called at 04:34:18 UTC with no response or progress until the client's 1,800-second idle timeout aborted it at 05:04:30. - The Doc had been created but no content was written. - An immediate retry finished in 4 seconds.

That is #1129: thread_http's per-thread httplib2.Http() has no socket timeout, so a request on a dead connection blocks until the OS gives up. #1129 described the path as "not observed"; this is an observation, and the stall lasted far longer than the 50–200 s ETIMEDOUT it anticipated. The cause isn't proven: no server log was configured for the run.

EP-8's code-font flip from Phases 1 and 2 (#1102) didn't recur here; DS-04's EP-8 code was monospace in both runs. Phase 1 and Phase 2's nondeterminism failures still stand, so TC-MD404 fails for the file as a whole.

docs.title: QA Runs
docs.text: One file per stable release, named vX.Y.Z.md. Each file is the sign-off record confirming the test suite passed before the release tag was cut. Run files are checked into the repo alongside the code they cover.

docs.title: Suite tiers
docs.text:
Tier ~Cases When to run Smoke ~20 happy-path cases, one per tool group Before every release (stable or dev) Domain Full test file for one domain When a specific domain has changes Full regression All domain suites Before every stable release, unless the release qualifies for scoped gating (see below)

Stable releases require Full regression by default. Dev releases (0.x.0.devN) require Smoke at minimum. See Release gate for when a stable release can substitute Smoke + targeted Domain runs instead.

docs.text:
One happy-path case per tool group — fast, no destructive operations where avoidable.

docs.title: How to start a run
docs.text:
1. Start the mcp-gee-sweet server and connect a Claude session to it.
  2. Check that docs/qa/.env exists with TEST_* fixture IDs (see setup.md).
  3. Paste the conductor prompt from docs/qa/run.md into the session.
  4. For a smoke run: add "Only run the smoke suite cases listed in docs/qa/runs/README.md."
  5. For a domain run: add "Only run tests/<domain>.md."
  6. For full regression: paste the prompt as-is.
  7. Save results to docs/qa/results/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md.
  8. Fill in the run file for this release and check off each suite when it passes.

docs.title: Pre-approved SKIPs (master list)
docs.text:
Disposition of every SKIP from the v0.8.0 Full Regression run (44 total, docs/qa/results/2026-06-28.md), reviewed case-by-case against the actual test suite rather than trusting each case's original SKIP note (issue #227). Each new run-gate file's own "Pre-approved SKIPs" table should be copied forward from this list, trimmed to whatever's actually in scope for that run.

Categories: - Pre-approved — no action; already covered or a documented non-testable limitation - Unit-tested — verified live against tests/ to actually cover the case; safe to pre-approve - Environmental — needs a fixture/account change to un-skip; low-risk by inspection in the meantime - Procedure exists — was manual-only for lack of a way to run it; now has a documented procedure and must be executed during the pass, not skipped - Genuine gap — verified not covered anywhere; tracked as a follow-up issue, still counts as a live-run SKIP until closed

docs.title: Release gate
docs.text: A completed docs/qa/runs/vX.Y.Z.md — with all required suites checked off and a results file linked — is required before tagging a stable release.

docs.title: Scoped gating
docs.text:
Full Regression is the default, but a release can substitute Smoke + targeted Domain runs if a source-diff audit shows the change is narrow. Rationale in docs/decisions/decision-testing.md; this section is the mechanical process.

  1. Enumerate. git log v<last-stable>..HEAD -- src/ — list every commit touching source since the last stable tag.
  2. Classify each one:
  3. Behavior change — a tool's inputs, outputs, or side effects changed.
  4. Pure refactor — organization only; existing tests were re-targeted at the same assertions, no intended behavior change.
  5. Map behavior changes to domains using the tool→test-file table in docs/qa/README.md.
  6. Include a refactor's domain too if that refactor has never had a live QA pass — i.e. it landed after the last stable release's run file. Unit tests mock the Google API; they can't catch integration drift a refactor might introduce (wrong re-export, changed call order, etc.), so a live Domain run is the only thing that actually checks it.
  7. A cross-cutting change — touches shared infrastructure used by every tool (the tool() decorator, auth, server startup) — does not by itself force Full Regression. Smoke already samples one call per tool group, which is enough to catch a generic regression from a shared-layer change.
  8. Required suites: Smoke (always) + a Domain run for every domain identified in steps 3–4, scoped by how the change touched that domain's file:
  9. Structural — a refactor that reorganizes files/modules (like the docs/__init__.py submodule split), or a change whose diff spans most of the domain's tool sections. Run the full domain test file. "No intended behavior change" is a claim, not evidence; only full live coverage of that file counts as evidence, especially for a domain that's never had a live pass since the reorg.
  10. Non-structural — one or a handful of isolated tool sections changed within a larger per-submodule test file (e.g. drive_files.md covers 20+ tools, but a fix touched only list_recent_files), with no reorganization. Running just the changed tools' TC sections is sufficient — identify the exact functions touched in the diff itself, not just what the originating issue claims to have scoped, since a fix can touch more than its issue describes.
  11. When in doubt, treat it as structural. Over-testing a domain file costs time; under-testing a refactor costs a shipped regression.
  12. Fall back to Full Regression if the audit can't be done cleanly (history too messy or rebased to enumerate reliably) or if more than roughly half the domains would need a Domain run anyway — at that point scoping isn't saving meaningful time.
  13. Document the audit in the release's docs/qa/runs/vX.Y.Z.md: list the commits reviewed, the classification of each (including structural vs. non-structural for domains that got a tool-scoped run), and which domains/tools were included or excluded and why. This is what makes the scoping decision auditable rather than a one-off judgment call.

docs.text:
TC Title Type Action TC-R10 get_sheet_formulas — mixed cells Test-file defect (cell reference swapped, A2/B2) Fixed in docs/qa/tests/sheets_read.md (this branch) TC-R19 get_multiple_spreadsheet_summary — rows_to_fetch=0 clamp inconsistent between cold/warm cache Real bug (cache.py:189 truncation slice missing the same max(1, ...) clamp data.py:304 applies) Filed as #254; fixed in PR #257 — max(1, rows_to_fetch) clamp applied to the cache-hit path, new regression test added, 546/546 unit tests pass

Findings (not TC failures, ticket-worthy):

Finding Type Action write_doc_content clear+reinsert leaks stale font_size/font_family into new content (reproduced 4×) Real bug Filed as #255; fixed in PR #258, then corrected in follow-up PR #259 — see note below TC-DOC57's SVG test image URL rejected by live Google Docs API Test-file fix Fixed in docs/qa/tests/docs.md (this branch, TC-DOC57/58) TC-DOC47 possible over-broad Courier New application Unconfirmed, needs follow-up tooling (font_family exposure in get_doc_structure) No ticket yet

Decision: both real bugs were folded into v0.8.1 rather than deferred (user's call) — fixed on dedicated branches (PR #257, #258), each verified beyond the mocked unit-test layer (#254 is pure local logic, fully covered by a unit test; #255 touches live Docs API behavior, so it was verified directly against the API before merging, consistent with this project's "unit tests mock the API, they can't catch integration drift" testing philosophy).

#258's first fix was wrong despite passing its own live verification — corrected by #259. #258 combined the clear (updateTextStyle + deleteContentRange) and the new content's insertText into one batchUpdate call; a single live check happened to pass. After both #257 and #258 were merged, re-verifying live against develop (post-merge) surfaced that the combined-batch approach is unreliable: the Docs API appears to resolve a same-batch insertText's inherited formatting from a pre-batch snapshot, so contamination could still leak through depending on document state, even though the clear request ran earlier in the same batch. Isolating each step and repeating the full cycle multiple times (not just once) showed the fix only holds when the insert is sent as its own separate, subsequent batchUpdate call. This is exactly the kind of integration drift a single live check can miss and unit tests can't catch at all — the lesson being applied going forward: verify a live API-behavior fix by repeating the full cycle several times, not just once, since a single pass can pass by luck of document state.

TC-R36/R37 re-run) TEST_SPREADSHEET_ID (sole writer) kai-oauth 2 Docs-content docs_content (minus TC-DOC80) TEST_DOC_ID + own throwaway docs oauth 3 Docs-style/tables/layout docs_style, docs_tables, docs_layout own throwaway doc only — substitute a self-created doc for {DOC_ID}, never TEST_DOC_ID ash 4 Drive-files drive_files own throwaway child folder under Shared Drive sky 5 Drive-transfer drive_transfer own throwaway child folder; local-fs cases SKIP jay 6 Drive-sharing+activity drive_sharing, drive_activity TEST_PERMISSION_EMAIL kit 7 Calendar calendar TEST_CALENDAR_ID (independent) kai-sa 8 Infra infra (live-testable subset) — sa — Concurrency TC-I24, TC-I02 2 subagents + mkdir barrier, run last, solo kai-sa — TC-DOC80 #678 low-cap method Aziz direct (uv run python3 -c, MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_CHARS=40000) —

docs.title: Run history / incidents
docs.text:
• Playwright browser wasn't authenticated to Google at pass start. Every one of the 8 parallel shards independently hit the sign-in redirect within its first few **Playwright: required** TCs, concluded Playwright was unusable, and fell back to API-level-only verification for its entire remaining run. The user authenticated Playwright mid-pass; corrections were sent to the two still-running shards (Sheets, Docs-content retries) — one was misdirected due to an agent-ID mix-up on Aziz's own end (caught and corrected). A dedicated re-verification pass then redid the ~17 highest-value already-completed visual checks (10 docs/drive_transfer TCs, 7 Sheets TCs) with real screenshots — all PASS, zero discrepancies from the API-only evidence. Filed PR #686 to make Playwright-auth verification (a real navigate, not just a connection check) a mandatory pre-flight step for future passes, done once centrally before spawning shards.
  • Service account wasn't subscribed to the fixture calendar. The Calendar shard's reads against {CALENDAR_ID}/{EVENT_ID} all 404'd on the SA prefix; it ran its full 77-TC suite against two SA-owned scratch calendars instead (valid tool-behavior coverage, but not against the real fixture). A targeted OAuth re-run against the real fixture closed the gap for 6 identity-sensitive TCs (CAL05/16/60/62/67) plus 2 that only work under OAuth at all (CAL17/22 — attendee invites, which a service account cannot send) — all PASS, real fixture confirmed untouched (updated timestamp identical pre/post).
  • Cross-shard fixture interference (transient, resolved). The Sheets shard's writes to {SPREADSHEET_ID} were caught mid-mutation by the Drive-transfer shard's CSV-export comparison (TC-D86 vs TC-D104 diverged: extra column, an #ERROR! cell, an extra row). Re-checked after the Sheets shard restored the fixture to seed state — both exports now agree byte-for-byte. Not a product bug; a sharding-design lesson (two shards touching the same fixture, one read-mostly, without wave-sequencing).
  • Main-checkout OAuth token.json refresh token is failing (invalid_grant) for fresh processes. Already-running MCP server processes are unaffected (they hold an already-refreshed in-memory token — confirmed live-working throughout this pass), but any new script/session using this file will hit it and fall into an interactive-consent hang. This blocked one live re-verification (TC-DOC159 — raw documents().get() read of blockquote indent/border), disposed instead via a source-diff argument (the exact code path hasn't changed since its last live PASS). Recommend re-running scripts/oauth_setup.py before the next session needs a fresh OAuth connection — flagged to the user, not a QA finding.
  • Two subagent-prompt mistakes, both self-inflicted and non-blocking: the TC-I24/TC-I02 concurrency subagents were given a slightly wrong tool-call syntax (range="Sheet!A1:C3" instead of separate sheet=/range= params) for their first 1-2 iterations each; all subagents self-corrected immediately and the remaining iterations are the ones adjudicated. Neither is a transport/locking signature — genuine client-side parameter errors.
  • Google Drive API had two transient server-side blips (an export_file HttpError 500 Internal Error, and one delete_file(permanent=True) 404 on a file get_file_metadata could see and trash could act on — isolated to the service-account prefix specifically; the same delete succeeded immediately via OAuth on the identical file, suggesting a Shared-Drive Content-Manager-role permission-model quirk rather than a code defect). Neither reproduced on retry via the correct auth path; not filed as product bugs.

docs.title: Bugs found
docs.text:
ID Title Severity Disposition BUG-SS share_spreadsheet omits supportsAllDrives=True on its permissions().create() call — every sibling permission op in the same file has it. Fails with "File not found" for any Shared-Drive file (the current fixture environment, post-#305). share_file still works (functional workaround). Real, release-scope ✅ Fixed #695, merged 2026-09-05, live-re-verified (see Post-sign-off resolution) BUG-CACHE Folder-listing cache key omits max_results — a smaller-limit call can (a) get an unfiltered cache hit from an earlier larger call, ignoring the limit, and (b) store its own truncated result, so later larger-limit calls get the truncated list until refresh_cache. Reproduced twice. Affects list_files, list_spreadsheets, list_folders (shared cache). Real, release-scope — silent persistent wrong data, the most severe finding this pass ✅ Fixed #697, merged 2026-09-05, live-re-verified (see Post-sign-off resolution) BUG-LF list_folders(parent_folder_id=None) hardcodes 'root' in parents, ignores DRIVE_FOLDER_ID — broken scope on any Shared-Drive deployment and for a pure service account (no personal root). Confirmed live (TC-D27). Has an explicit-parent workaround. Real, confirmed live File — v0.9.1 BUG-DF download_file with a trailing-slash local_path to a non-existent directory creates a single file at that path (not the directory) and silently clobbers it on every subsequent download to the same path. Correct once the directory already exists. Real, minor File — v0.9.1 (enhancement) create_spreadsheet/import_csv_to_sheet response has no web link, unlike copy_file/create_folder/get_file_metadata Minor/judgment call User to decide: add web_link for consistency, or fix TC-D01's expectation instead (doc note) Service account's Shared-Drive "Content manager" role can trash but apparently not permanently-delete (files().delete()) an item it created — surfaced as a 404, not 403. Same call succeeds immediately via OAuth on the identical file. Looks like a Drive API permission-model fact, not a code defect. Minor, informational Note in _SA_LIMITATIONS/docs, not filing as a bug (minor) find_free_slots per-calendar error shape ({"error": "notFound"}, bare) is less detailed than list_all_events's ({calendar_id, calendar_summary, error: <full repr>}) for the same failure mode Minor File — v0.9.1 (minor) A bare - marker alone on its line isn't recognized as a list item by python-markdown regardless of indentation width — distinct from the tracked sane_lists threshold bug these fixtures otherwise target Minor, markdown-syntax-level gap File — v0.9.1, or a doc note in markdown-support.md

docs.title: Scoping audit — why not Full Regression
docs.text:
Per docs/qa/runs/README.md §"Scoped gating".

  3. Map to domains. Only drive_transfer, and within it only the three tools that write to local_path. Upload, export, and revision tools share the module but not the changed code paths.
  4. Structural? No. There's no shared-helper change outside the destination-path logic, and no server, auth, or cache changes.

docs.title: Scoping audit — why Full Regression
docs.text:
Per docs/qa/runs/README.md §"Scoped gating".

1. Enumerate. git log v0.9.0..origin/develop --no-merges — 387 commits. git diff --stat v0.9.0 origin/develop -- src/: 38 files, +11,577 / −2,543.

2/3. Behavior changes by domain (representative, not exhaustive):

Domain Representative changes since v0.9.0 sheets_read / sheets_write one A1 grammar + grid-limit bounds (#955, #926, #922, #747, #757); progress notifications on get_multiple_* (#355) sheets_mgmt / sheets_charts clear_data_validation (#365), data-validation shape checks (#366, #751), dimension-tool validation (#323), update_borders hardening (#330), add_chart no-end-column rejection (#954) drive_files starred exposure (#388), max_results on list_folders/list_spreadsheets (#718), list_folders DRIVE_FOLDER_ID fallback (#689), permanent-delete error (#876), quota errors by identity (#1009) drive_sharing progress on share_* (#355); shared HttpError helper (#916) drive_transfer transfer.py +3,341 lines: converted-Doc change detection (#814), sync_folder(resolve=) (#860), use_checksum within-tolerance (#716), atomic downloads (#844), destination preflight (#836), no-empty-dir (#1012), _safe_local_dest (GHSA-hx2f), compression MIME (#930), export_revision Markdown (#959) + temp Doc placement (#989) docs_content / docs_style / docs_tables / docs_layout doc backup before replace (#878) + no-backup fallbacks (#1018, #1035), image-share lifecycle (#789, #883, #909), write-side bundle (#894), get_doc_as_markdown code/link/fence fixes (#923, #938, #940, #951, #958, #969), linked images (#977), bullet anchor fixes (#439, #713, #714) calendar ACL owner errors, pagination hardening, fan-out cap (#890); find_free_slots error shape (#691) gmail new domain: primitives (#785), charset/body fixes (#792, #825), Reply-To (#791), include_body (#793), dedupe/hardening (#896) infra LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS policy (#796) — cross-cutting over every local read/write; OAuth re-authorize from a tool call (#873); stdio no-consent + mcp-gee-sweet auth (#811); SSE consent off the event loop (#833); SIGTERM handling (#868, #917); tool error text on mcp 2.3+ (#872); Gmail scope gating (#790); cache epoch guard (#698)

4. Refactors never live-tested: shared sheet-id lookup (#442), _SyncStep dataclass (#749), download candidates dataclass (#740), shared HttpError helper (#916), shared image dedupe (#511, #560), and others, all landed after v0.9.0's run.

5/7. Decision. Every domain has behavior changes, Gmail is a new domain, and two cross-cutting layers (the local-file policy and the auth/re-authorize rework) sit under the whole tool surface. That is the README's step-7 fallback outright: Full Regression, no scoping.

docs.title: Bugs found / open questions
docs.text:
• [NEW — pre-existing] Table column widths fail on any table after the first (DOC35 multi-table; details under Docs-content). Ticket.
  • [NEW] Blockquote indent invisible on single-line paragraphs: the emitter sets indentStart but not indentFirstLine, so a quote's first line sits at the margin and a nested quote isn't visibly deeper (ruler shows first-line 0, left indent 0.5in). Ticket candidate.
  • [NEW] get_doc_as_markdown emits a raw \u000b for a soft break in a non-code paragraph: only Courier New runs turn \v into \n. Ticket candidate.

  • search_files returns trashed files, seen again here: 3 trashed (backup before replace) docs. This is the same defect as the drive_files finding below.

  • [NEW — repeat before filing] get_doc_as_markdown misreads bulleted lists in Docs made by Drive's HTML import. upload_file(convert_to_doc=true) from markdown or HTML renders real bullets in the UI (Playwright), but the export gives > 1. Bullet A: a blockquote plus a numbered list. create_doc-built lists export correctly. Seen on 2 docs under one condition, so it needs a varied repeat (aziz.md step 9) before it's filed.

  • Errno 60 on kai-sa too (run 2, 14:10–14:27 PT): 7 Drive calls timed out after 52–198 s. Calendar calls between them took 0.33 s, and curl took 0.17 s. In a 4-way parallel batch, 2 calls succeeded in 0.2 s and 2 timed out. It cleared one thread at a time, then nothing more failed. list_files returned the timeout as {"result":[{"error":…}]} with HTTP 200. Consistent with the confirmed stale-connection defect.

  • [NEW] transfer_ownership(send_notification=False) can never succeed. Drive returns 403 "sendNotificationEmail … must not be disabled for ownership transfers" before it even looks up the file. Ticket candidate: drop the parameter or reject it client-side.

  • [OPEN] D137's premise may be stale: on Shared Drive items, list_permissions returns inherited organizer and fileOrganizer entries. Not verified with a folder-level user grant.

  • [NEW — docstring] Setting a named style wipes the paragraph's inline text styles. insert_softbreak_paragraph at a paragraph start, and style_doc_range(named_style_type=...) even with the same style, removed existing strikethrough (reproduced 3×, including a control with no style fields). The cause is the Docs API's updateParagraphStyle(namedStyleType). Neither docstring warns about it. Ticket candidate (docstring / known-limitations).

  • [NEW — known-limitations] I23 cache freshness misses API edits from another client for 30–75 s+. A rename through the Sheets API from a separate client didn't move Drive modifiedTime for over 75 s, and list_sheets served the stale name from cache in that window (2 of 3 API renames). A UI edit bumps it at once. Ticket candidate (known-limitations note).

  • [NEW — minor docstring] set_cache_ttl says "This server runs in SSE mode", which is wrong under stdio.

  • [NEW — not a regression] list_spreadsheets, search_files, search_spreadsheets return trashed files. None of the three adds trashed=false to its query (files.py; list_files/list_folders/list_recent_files/list_shared_with_me do). Live: a file with get_file_metadata.trashed == true came back from all three (repeated); a trashed folder from search_files. Same gap exists at v0.9.0, so pre-existing. No existing issue. TC-D14/D75/D77 don't assert trashed exclusion. Ticket candidate (pending user OK to file).

  • [CONFIRMED — pre-existing; stale per-thread connection after idle, no retry] (originally logged as "Gmail transport timeout, unconfirmed") After the classifier denials, every Gmail call on mcp-gee-sweet-oauth returns {"error": "[Errno 60] Operation timed out"} (shard: list_threads ×3, list_labels ×2; Aziz re-checked list_labels at ~13:25 PT, same). Drive on the same server (get_storage_quota) still works; curl to gmail.googleapis.com from the shell answers in ~70 ms. Gmail worked for the first 11 cases of the shard. Not yet reproduced after a server reconnect; must be re-checked before it's filed or dismissed.

  • Corroborated on a second server (kai-sa, Sheets). After an idle gap of a few minutes, get_multiple_sheet_data returned [Errno 60] Operation timed out as per-query errors in a decreasing pattern: 2/2 failed, 2/2, then 1/2, 1/3, then clean from the sixth call on. A single get_sheet_data call between them succeeded. Hypothesis (unverified): http_transport.thread_http caches one httplib2.Http per worker thread, so each of the default executor's threads keeps its own keep-alive connection. After idle those die silently, and each fails once with a TCP timeout (not retried) before httplib2 replaces it. That would account for both the decreasing count and the Gmail server failing on call after call (different threads, each stale).
  • Third server (kai-oauth, Drive), ~13:10–13:24 PT: 4 list_files calls returned List files failed: [Errno 60] …; 2 get_file_metadata calls raised TimeoutError after 82 s and 140 s; it cleared on its own and D263 re-ran clean. Fresh connections from curl and a separate httplib2 process were ~0.1 s in the same window. Three servers and three APIs (Gmail, Sheets, Drive) in one window points at the shared transport, not one API; it could also be a network event in that window, so not yet attributable to the code.
  • After /mcp reconnect mcp-gee-sweet-oauth (user, ~13:55 PT): list_labels returns the full label list immediately (incl. Label_1 mcp-qa-fixture). A fresh server process clears it, which fits the stale-connection hypothesis but doesn't rule out a network event that had already ended.
  • ✅ Reproduced (15:01 PT), so this is a real defect, not a network blip. mcp-gee-sweet-oauth sat idle for 12 min after the Gmail/sharing shard finished. Then one get_multiple_sheet_data with 12 single-cell queries returned 11 correct values and 1 per-query "error": "[Errno 54] Connection reset by peer" (Sales!B1), with no retry. The identical call immediately after: 12/12 clean. That fits one warm worker thread whose cached keep-alive connection died while idle; the other threads opened fresh connections. It fails fast (ECONNRESET) when the peer resets, or slowly (ETIMEDOUT, 80–140 s) when the connection is dropped silently, which is the run 1 pattern.
  • Second server reproduction (~15:55 PT, kai-sa). kai-sa had been idle about 5–10 min after the transfer shard. Wide get_multiple_sheet_data warm-ups before the concurrency cases: 12 queries gave 1 [Errno 54] Connection reset by peer; 12 queries gave another 1 (a different thread); then 24 queries gave 24/24 clean. Each worker thread's dead connection fails exactly once.
  • Concurrency-case consequence. TC-I24's failure signature includes Connection reset by peer, so on any server that has been idle this defect produces false TC-I24 failures. The pass warms the target server with wide fan-outs until one comes back fully clean before starting the barrier loop. Record that in run.md's procedure once the defect is ticketed.
  • User decision (~15:05 PT): does not block v0.9.2; ticket for v0.9.3.
  • Not a regression. thread_http's cache of one httplib2.Http() per thread is unchanged in kind since v0.9.0 (git show v0.9.0:src/mcp_gee_sweet/http_transport.py). It affects every tool after an idle period.
  • ~~Next step: reproduce with real processes~~ (superseded by the reproduction above). Original note: reproduce with real processes (idle > N minutes, then fan out) before filing.
  • Side finding: get_multiple_sheet_data(local_path=...) reported success (bytes_written) when every query in the file was an error entry. Possibly by design (per-item errors); check the docstring before filing.

docs.title: Calendar Tools — QA Test Cases
docs.text:
Source: src/mcp_gee_sweet/tools/calendar.py

Fixtures: see docs/qa/setup.md. Substitute your {CALENDAR_ID} (TEST_CALENDAR_ID) and {EVENT_ID} (TEST_EVENT_ID, a pre-existing event in that calendar) from fixtures.local.md.

⚠️ Which identity these cases need. {CALENDAR_ID} is a secondary calendar that setup.md's seed prompt creates with create_calendar, so it belongs to the account that ran the setup, not to the service account. It isn't shared with the service account, and returns 404 to it (2026-09-04 and v0.9.2). So: - OAuth server (e.g. mcp-gee-sweet-oauth, -kai-oauth): run the cases as written, against {CALENDAR_ID} and {EVENT_ID}. - Service-account server (e.g. -sa, -kai-sa): {CALENDAR_ID} can't be used. Do what v0.9.2 did: create scratch calendars with create_calendar (they're owned by the service account), create the events a case needs in them, substitute those IDs for {CALENDAR_ID} and {EVENT_ID}, and delete the scratch calendars at the end. Expect these limits under the service account: inviting attendees returns 403 forbiddenForServiceAccounts (TC-CAL17, TC-CAL22: SKIP or run on OAuth); it has no primary calendar; and the Playwright checks can't see its calendars, since the browser is signed in as the fixture owner, so those cases are API-only.

Service account note: the service account must have been added to each calendar via calendarList().insert() before it can read or write events. list_calendars only returns calendars the service account has explicitly subscribed to — it will not see calendars shared with the owning user's personal account. See docs/project_calendar_setup.md in memory.

If no such fixture calendar exists in this account, SKIP and record as environmental — this behavior is covered by tests/test_calendar.py::TestListCalendarAcl::test_follows_next_page_token_across_pages at the unit level, which mocks two pages directly.

docs.title: TC-CAL33: Invalid calendar ID in list (issue #691: error shape aligned with list_all_events)
docs.text:
Background: originally busy["invalid-cal@example.com"] was a bare [{"error": "notFound"}] — just the freebusy API's reason string, no calendar_id/calendar_summary, unlike list_all_events's per-calendar error entry for the identical failure ({calendar_id, calendar_summary, error}). Fixed by aligning the shape: calendar_id and calendar_summary (falling back to the id when the calendar isn't in the user's calendar list) are now included, and error also folds in the API's domain when present ("<reason> (<domain>)").

Prompt

"Find free slots for calendars [{CALENDAR_ID}, 'invalid-cal@example.com'] for the next hour"

Checks - busy["invalid-cal@example.com"] is [{"calendar_id": "invalid-cal@example.com", "calendar_summary": "invalid-cal@example.com", "error": "notFound"}] (or "notFound (<domain>)" if the API includes a domain) — not a bare {"error": "notFound"} - busy[{CALENDAR_ID}] is still populated correctly - Top-level response is not an error — partial results returned

Result (2026-09-10) ✅ PASS (re-verified under #691's richer error shape) — verified live via mcp-gee-sweet-kit: find_free_slots([{qa-cal}, "invalid-cal@example.com"], next hour) → busy["invalid-cal@example.com"] == [{"calendar_id": "invalid-cal@example.com", "calendar_summary": "invalid-cal@example.com", "error": "notFound (global)"}] (id-fallback summary, since the invalid id is never in the calendar list — matches list_all_events' behavior for a not-in-list calendar); busy[{qa-cal}] == [] (correctly populated, empty); top-level response not an error, free_slots covers the full window (partial results).

Prior run (2026-09-04), before the fix: find_free_slots [SACAL, 'invalid-cal@example.com'] -> busy["invalid-cal@example.com"]=[{"error":"notFound"}], busy[SACAL] still populated, top-level not an error (partial results).

docs.title: TC-CAL78: find_free_slots error shape — summary fallback and no extra API call on the happy path (issue #691) (unit test)
docs.text:
Background: two invariants of the #691 fix (TC-CAL33 covers the headline shape change) that aren't reliably distinguishable live: (1) calendar_summary in the error entry comes from the user's own calendar_cache-backed calendar list, falling back to the bare calendar_id only when that calendar isn't in the list — TC-CAL33's invalid-cal@example.com is never in the list either way, so it can't tell "summary looked up and happened to equal the id" apart from "lookup never ran"; and (2) the summary lookup is gated on at least one calendar actually erroring, so an all-readable find_free_slots call costs exactly one API call (the freebusy query), same as before the fix — not reliably forceable against the live API without mocking the calendar-list call to prove it was (or wasn't) made. Verified by unit test instead.

Checks (unit test) - tests/test_calendar.py::TestFindFreeSlots::test_unreadable_calendar_reports_full_error_shape — a calendar list containing the erroring id's real summary ("Team Cal") produces busy["cal-2"] == [{"calendar_id": "cal-2", "calendar_summary": "Team Cal", "error": "notFound (global)"}] — the summary is genuinely looked up, not just echoing the id. - tests/test_calendar.py::TestFindFreeSlots::test_error_shape_summary_falls_back_to_id_when_calendar_not_in_list — the same failure with the erroring id absent from the calendar list falls back to calendar_summary == "cal-2". - tests/test_calendar.py::TestFindFreeSlots::test_summary_fetch_failure_does_not_break_find_free_slots — a calendar-list fetch that itself raises still returns the error entry (id-fallback summary), proving the best-effort lookup can never turn a working find_free_slots call into a failing one. - tests/test_calendar.py::TestFindFreeSlots::test_all_readable_path_never_fetches_the_calendar_list — with every calendar readable, calendar_cache.get_list and calendarList().list() are both asserted not called — the happy path stays a single API call.

Result (2026-09-10) ✅ PASS — tests/test_calendar.py -k TestFindFreeSlots — 9 passed, including all 4 cited cases. /code-review high origin/develop...HEAD surfaced 2 non-blocking findings, neither exercised by these invariants: summary_by_id's c.get("summary") or c["id"] (this fix) falls back to the id on a falsy or empty-string summary, while list_all_events' equivalent (calendar.py:981) only falls back on a missing key — a calendar with a genuinely empty-string summary would report differently between the two tools, contradicting the docstring's "same shape" claim for that edge case; and the id→summary lookup is duplicated rather than shared between the two tools. Neither affects correctness for a real (non-empty-string) summary. Filed as follow-up #726.

Result (2026-10-17) ✅ PASS — v0.9.2 release pass Run 2 (kai-sa) on SA-owned scratch calendars (TEST_CALENDAR_ID returns 404 to the SA).

docs.text:
Background: a secondary calendar's ACL holds two owner rules that no one can change. Any acl().delete() or acl().insert() touching them returns a 403, even a no-op re-grant of owner; both were confirmed live on 2026-10-05. - The primary-owner rule, user:<calendar_id>, returns cannotChangeOwnerAcl ("Cannot change the access level of calendars primary owner."). - The authenticated account's own rule, user:<account email>, returns cannotChangeOwnAcl ("Cannot change your own access level.").

Before #459 both tools returned the raw HttpError string; they now return a message naming the restriction, like remove_calendar_from_list's cannotUnsubscribeFromOwnedCalendar handling (TC-CAL59). Only remove_calendar_acl's primary-owner message points at delete_calendar. An insert that tried to change a grant is never told to delete the calendar (PR #912 QA round 1).

Setup: create a disposable calendar with create_calendar(summary="QA-OwnerAcl"); call it {OWNER_TEST_CAL}. Call list_calendar_acl(calendar_id="{OWNER_TEST_CAL}"). It shows two role: "owner", scope_type: "user" rules: - {PRIMARY_OWNER_RULE_ID}: the one whose scope_value equals {OWNER_TEST_CAL}, so its id is user:{OWNER_TEST_CAL}. - {ACCOUNT_RULE_ID}: the one whose scope_value is the authenticated account. Call that scope_value {ACCOUNT_EMAIL}.

Checks: primary-owner rule (cannotChangeOwnerAcl) - remove_calendar_acl(calendar_id="{OWNER_TEST_CAL}", rule_id="{PRIMARY_OWNER_RULE_ID}") returns {"error": "Google does not allow removing the access rule of a calendar's primary owner (reason: cannotChangeOwnerAcl). Use delete_calendar instead to permanently delete a calendar you own."}, not a raw <HttpError 403 ...> string - add_calendar_acl(calendar_id="{OWNER_TEST_CAL}", role="reader", scope_type="user", scope_value="{OWNER_TEST_CAL}", send_notifications=false) returns {"error": "Google does not allow changing the access level of a calendar's primary owner (reason: cannotChangeOwnerAcl); that rule always stays 'owner'."}, with no mention of delete_calendar

Checks: account's own rule (cannotChangeOwnAcl) - remove_calendar_acl(calendar_id="{OWNER_TEST_CAL}", rule_id="{ACCOUNT_RULE_ID}") returns {"error": "Google does not allow changing or removing your own access rule on a calendar (reason: cannotChangeOwnAcl)."} - add_calendar_acl(calendar_id="{OWNER_TEST_CAL}", role="reader", scope_type="user", scope_value="{ACCOUNT_EMAIL}", send_notifications=false) returns the same cannotChangeOwnAcl message

Checks: unchanged state and raw fallthrough - A follow-up list_calendar_acl(calendar_id="{OWNER_TEST_CAL}") still shows both rules with role: "owner" - A different failure still passes through raw: remove_calendar_acl(calendar_id="{OWNER_TEST_CAL}", rule_id="totally-invalid-rule-id") returns {"error": "<HttpError 400 ...>"} with neither message (same as TC-CAL68)

Cleanup: delete_calendar(calendar_id="{OWNER_TEST_CAL}").

Result (2026-10-05) ❌ FAIL (PR #912 round 1, Kit). The setup's {OWNER_RULE_ID} (the authenticated account's user:<email> rule) isn't the primary owner on a secondary calendar. Removing it, or add_calendar_acl(role="reader") for that email, returns Google's raw 403 cannotChangeOwnAcl ("Cannot change your own access level."), which the PR doesn't map. Both checks pass against the calendar's own-id rule (user:<calendar_id>): each returns the mapped cannotChangeOwnerAcl message, and a later list_calendar_acl still shows that rule as owner. The invalid-rule-id check passes (raw HttpError 400). Cleanup done.

Result (2026-10-05) ✅ PASS (PR #912 round 2, Kit, against 9a85809 after a fresh reconnect). Every check passes against a fresh QA-OwnerAcl calendar, with exactly the strings documented: - Primary-owner rule: remove returns the cannotChangeOwnerAcl message, which names delete_calendar. Add returns the change message, without delete_calendar. - Account's own rule: both remove and add return the cannotChangeOwnAcl message. - A follow-up list_calendar_acl still shows both rules as owner. - An invalid rule id still passes through as raw HttpError 400.

Cleanup done.

Result (2026-10-12) ✅ PASS (PR #1011 round 1, Sky, against 1a8053e after a fresh reconnect). Regression check after the reason check moved to the shared tools/http_errors.py (#916). On a fresh QA-OwnerAcl calendar every check returns exactly the documented string: primary-owner remove (cannotChangeOwnerAcl, names delete_calendar) and add (change message, no delete_calendar); own-rule remove and add (cannotChangeOwnAcl); a follow-up list_calendar_acl still shows both rules as owner; totally-invalid-rule-id passes through as raw HttpError 400. Cleanup done.

Result (2026-10-17) ✅ PASS — v0.9.2 release pass Run 2 (kai-sa) on SA-owned scratch calendars (TEST_CALENDAR_ID returns 404 to the SA).

docs.text:

A per-call semaphore fails this test; that was confirmed with a mutation check before the PR was opened. - tests/test_calendar.py::TestListAllEventsConcurrencyEnv: LIST_ALL_EVENTS_MAX_CONCURRENCY defaults to 20, overrides the cap when set, and is floored at 1. - tests/test_calendar.py::TestFindFreeSlots::test_empty_string_summary_matches_list_all_events: a calendar whose summary is "" reports calendar_summary: "" from both tools; only a calendar missing from the user's list falls back to its id.

docs.title: TC-CAL71: group_by_calendar=True groups by calendar summary
docs.text:
Setup: same fixtures as TC-CAL69 — both calendars have at least one event in the window.

Prompt

Call list_all_events(calendar_ids=["{CALENDAR_ID}", "{CALENDAR_ID_2}"], time_min="2026-07-01T00:00:00Z", time_max="2026-07-02T00:00:00Z", group_by_calendar=true).

Checks - Response is a dict keyed by each calendar's summary (from list_calendars), not a flat list - Each key's value is that calendar's own event list only - Events under each key still carry calendar_id/calendar_summary matching the key they're filed under - If two calendars share an identical summary, both are still present — disambiguated as "{summary} ({calendar_id})" — instead of one silently overwriting the other

Fixed (round 2): grouped was keyed by bare calendar_summary, so two calendars sharing a summary collided and the second overwrote the first with no error. Now keyed via _group_key, which appends " ({calendar_id})" whenever more than one queried calendar shares that summary. No live fixture pair with a duplicate summary was available in this environment to reproduce the collision end-to-end (per round 1's Result below) or reconfirm the fix live — covered by test_group_by_calendar_disambiguates_colliding_summaries in tests/test_calendar.py only. Documented scoping decision, not an oversight.

Result (2026-07-30) ⚠️ passed but confirms a live defect — Ran with two calendars whose real summary values happened to differ, and grouping worked correctly for that case. However, reading the implementation (calendar.py:1001, grouped[key] = ... keyed by calendar_summary) confirms /code-review high's finding: two calendars sharing an identical summary will silently collide — the second overwrites the first in grouped, with the first calendar's entire event list dropped and no error/warning. No live fixture pair with a duplicate summary was available in this environment to reproduce it end-to-end, but the code path is unambiguous. Sending back to Dev — see PR comment.

Result (2026-09-04) ✅ PASS group_by_calendar=true, [SACAL, MINCAL] -> dict keyed by summary ("mcp-gee-sweet-qa-renamed", "mcp-gee-sweet-qa-minimal"); each key holds only that calendar's events; events' calendar_id/summary match their key. Duplicate-summary disambiguation not reproducible (no colliding pair) — covered by unit test, matches prior runs.

Result (2026-10-17) ✅ PASS — v0.9.2 release pass Run 2 (kai-sa) on SA-owned scratch calendars (TEST_CALENDAR_ID returns 404 to the SA).

docs.title: TC-CAL75: expand_recurring=False returns master events across every queried calendar
docs.text:
Setup: use the recurring event created in TC-CAL36 (in {CALENDAR_ID}).

Prompt

Call list_all_events(calendar_ids=["{CALENDAR_ID}"], expand_recurring=false, query="QA-").

Checks - 'QA-Weekly-Standup' appears once as its master event (recurrence field populated with RRULE), not expanded into individual instances - Confirms expand_recurring=False is applied per-calendar in the fan-out, matching list_events' own singleEvents/orderBy behavior

Result (2026-07-30) ⏭️ SKIP — TC-CAL36's recurring-event fixture is not present in this worktree's connected account. Not run; not a PR defect.

Result (2026-09-04) ✅ PASS [SACAL], expand_recurring=false, query="QA-" -> QA-Daily-5x once as master (recurrence ["RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=5"] populated), not expanded to 5. NOTE: CAL43's instance-override singleton also listed (expected). QA-Weekly-Standup recurrence:null (removed in CAL42). Confirms expand_recurring=False per-calendar in fan-out.

Result (2026-10-17) ✅ PASS — v0.9.2 release pass Run 2 (kai-sa) on SA-owned scratch calendars (TEST_CALENDAR_ID returns 404 to the SA).

Round 2 fixes not covered by a live test case above: - The calendar-list fetch backing summary_by_id (calendar.py, before _fetch_one) had no try/except and could abort the whole batch on a transient failure even when calendar_ids was given explicitly (so the fetch was only needed for display names). Now caught: with explicit calendar_ids, the call proceeds using the bare IDs as display names; with no calendar_ids (so there's no other way to know what to query), it returns a single top-level {"error": ...} instead of raising. Forcing a live calendarList().list() failure isn't something QA can safely trigger against a real account — covered by test_calendar_list_fetch_failure_with_explicit_calendar_ids_does_not_abort and test_calendar_list_fetch_failure_without_calendar_ids_returns_top_level_error in tests/test_calendar.py only. Documented scoping decision, not an oversight. - time_min's default (datetime.now(timezone.utc)) was computed independently inside each concurrent per-calendar task, so calendars in the same call could query against slightly different "now" instants under real contention. Now computed once before the fan-out and reused by every task. Not distinguishable via a single live call's response (there's no observable difference unless an event's start time falls in the microseconds-wide window between two independent datetime.now() calls) — covered by test_default_time_min_is_computed_once_for_the_whole_batch in tests/test_calendar.py only.

docs.title: TC-DOC80: get_doc_content trips the response-size cap; cached path re-checks it too (issue #242) ⚠️ low-cap override required
docs.text:
Background: #242 generalized #235's response-size safety net to get_doc_content. doc_cache previously returned a cached result before any cap check ran, so a cached oversized doc would bypass the cap on repeat calls — fixed so the check runs on both the cache-hit and cache-miss paths.

Run method (issue #678): MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_CHARS is read once at tools/response_limits.py import, and #519 raised its default from 40000 to 1,000,000. The TEST_LARGE_DOC_ID fixture (~54k chars, sized for TC-D48) is far under that default, so it cannot trip the cap on a normally-started server. This case is therefore not run through the shared shard server — instead run it against the low cap, one of: - a purpose-started server with MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_CHARS=40000 in its env, or - a direct script invocation: MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_CHARS=40000 uv run python3 -c "..." from the repo root, calling the real get_doc_content tool function (import from mcp_gee_sweet.tools.docs) against TEST_LARGE_DOC_ID with a real OAuth docs/drive service (mcp_gee_sweet.auth._oauth_creds() + googleapiclient.discovery.build). This exercises the real code path and the real Docs API — record the Result as a live verification, noting it was script-driven rather than through the MCP tool wrapper.

Setup: TEST_LARGE_DOC_ID (mcp-gee-sweet-qa-large-doc). Measure its current serialized get_doc_content size at run time and put the number in the Result — it just needs to exceed 40000, which it comfortably does at ~54k.

Checks - First call (fetch path), cap = 40000: raises ValueError naming the actual response size, the 40000-character cap, and MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_CHARS - Second call (cache-hit path, no refresh_cache in between): raises the same error — proves the cache-hit path re-checks the cap rather than returning the stale oversized cached result - Same call with local_path set: succeeds, returns {local_path, id, bytes_written}, and the file on disk contains the full content

Result (2026-07-03) ✅ PASS — superseded, needs re-run under the #678 method. Prior run, against the then-default 40000 cap with a ~49,700-char fixture: Fetch-path call raised get_doc_content: the response is 49700 characters, over the 40000-character safety cap. …; repeat call served from doc_cache (no extra Drive round-trip) raised the identical error; local_path call succeeded (bytes_written: 49700), file verified then cleaned up. Not valid for v0.9.0 — the cap default and fixture size both changed since; re-run per the Run method above.

Result (2026-09-04) ✅ PASS Script-driven at MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_CHARS=40000 (repo-root uv run python3, real OAuth creds): fetch-path raises ValueError naming 54891 chars/40000 cap/MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_CHARS; cache-hit path (real DocContentCache store+get round-trip, content byte-identical) still raises — confirms #242 cache-ordering fix; local_path via real write_capped_result_to_disk returns {local_path,bytes_written:54891,id}, on-disk content matches exactly. Supersedes the 2026-07-03 result (old 40000 default, ~49,700-char fixture) — see #678.

Result (2026-10-17) ⏭️ SKIP — v0.9.2 release pass Low-cap script needs a usable OAuth token (aziz token fails to refresh; copying another was classifier-denied).

Result (2026-10-19) ⏭️ SKIP — v0.9.3 release pass kai-oauth: Needs the low-cap (MAX_TOOL_RESPONSE_CHARS=40000) scratch script with the fixture-owning account's token, which isn't available in this pass. Measured the current size: 54891 chars via local_path.

Since markdown images (`![alt](src)`) are converted to `` HTML by `_md_to_html` before reaching this same parser, **every** content path that goes through the shared AST pipeline — `create_doc`, `create_doc_from_file`, `write_doc_content`, for both `content_format="html"` and `content_format="markdown"` — drops images with no error, no warning, and no placeholder. ## Bare top-level text no longer silently dropped — `write_doc_content` (issue #343)

**Background:** surfaced by Kit while building fixtures for TC-DOC107/PR #337 (unrelated to that PR's diff, flagged separately). `content`/HTML with no wrapping block tag (e.g. `hello world` instead of `
                            hello world
                            `) fell into `html_to_ast`'s inline-only code path — `handle_data` only buffers text inside an open block (`
                            `, `
                          • `, a heading, or a table cell), so text with no block ancestor at all was silently dropped, producing an empty document body. The fix adds a generic open-tag depth counter so `handle_data` can tell genuinely bare text (depth 0) apart from text merely wrapped in a non-block tag with no block ancestor at all (e.g. `no blocks`, depth 1) — the latter stays an intentional no-op (see `test_inline_only_html_skips_batchupdate`), the former now gets an implicit paragraph wrap.

## UTF-16 code-unit offset correctness in write paths (issue #358)

**Background:** Docs API `startIndex`/`endIndex` count UTF-16 code units, not Python code points — an astral-plane character (most emoji, some CJK/math symbols) is one Python `str` character but a 2-unit surrogate pair. `emitter.py`'s `ast_to_requests` derived every downstream offset (table positions, paragraph-style ranges, inline run-style ranges) from plain `len()`, so any content containing an astral-plane character before other content in the same batch silently desynced every subsequent computed offset. Fixed by introducing a shared `utf16_len` helper (`docs/indices.py`) and routing `emitter.py` and `content.py` through it; `sheets/helpers.py`'s `_utf16_len` now delegates to the same helper instead of duplicating the accounting. The identical pattern was already fixed in `find_in_doc`'s `_collect_doc_paragraphs` (#262); this closes the matching gap in the write path.

## Unsupported markdown constructs preserve paragraph boundaries (issue #401)

**Background:** #332/#333 established that an unsupported construct like `` (markdown images convert to `` before reaching the shared HTML→AST parser) gets dropped from the document. #401 is a step further: the construct's entire *paragraph* was also being deleted, not just the construct itself — `_emit_block_node` (`html_parser.py`) returned early without appending anything whenever a closed block's buffered runs came back empty (e.g. its only child was an unsupported ``), and a bare `` (python-markdown's rendering of both `---` and `___` thematic breaks — confirmed via the issue's own follow-up comment) never opened a block at all, so it left zero trace. Either way, the two blocks on either side ended up directly adjacent (one's `endIndex` == the next one's `startIndex`), unlike how any standard markdown viewer degrades (the construct's own line/block boundary survives even when the construct itself can't render). The fix keeps an empty node (`runs=[]`) in the AST for both cases instead of dropping it — `emitter.py`'s `ast_to_requests` was updated to match, since its own `if not text.strip(): continue` guard would otherwise have skipped the now-empty node's contribution to `full_text` and lost the boundary anyway.
