**Background:** TC-DOC135's own review round found a same-bug-class gap: `_interrupt_open_block` (`html_parser.py`) flushed the currently-open block *before* descending into a nested construct with `preserve_if_empty=False` unconditionally, so a block whose only content was an unsupported construct (e.g. an ``) vanished entirely — not just the image — whenever it was itself interrupted by a nested list/table/pre/block instead of closing directly. The fix replaces the old `not self._block_resumed` proxy (used at every `_emit_block_node` call site) with a new `self._block_had_unsupported_content` flag that tracks, per open-block segment, whether something was actually silently dropped (an unsupported void element or unrecognized tag) since the segment last began — set in `handle_starttag`'s generic inline-element fallthrough, reset on both fresh block open and on `_resume_interrupted_block`.                           • ` that wraps *only* a nested list with no text of its own (ordinary nested-list markdown) is empty on its first flush too, and must NOT gain a spurious empty bullet — a regression the naive `not self._block_resumed` fix would have introduced, caught by the then unit test `TestNestedLists::test_parent_with_no_own_text_unaffected`.

Since #1075 that last rule is reversed: a fresh `
                          • ` always emits its bullet, empty or not, so an `
                          • ` wrapping only a nested list is an empty bullet (`TestNestedLists::test_parent_with_no_own_text_is_an_empty_bullet`), and `preserve_if_empty` no longer decides anything for a fresh `
                          • `. This case's checks are unchanged: the "Bug case" bullet is an empty bullet under both rules, and the "Control case" bullet has text of its own.

**Background:** distinct from #401's `runs=[]` case (an unsupported construct like `` leaves a block with *no* buffered content at all). Here the block's buffered runs are non-empty but strip to nothing — a lone ` ` or a run of plain spaces — which markdown authors commonly write as a standalone line to force a visible blank-line spacer, since a literal blank line collapses in markdown. `_emit_block_node` (`html_parser.py`) used to drop any block whose text stripped to empty regardless of *why*, fusing the paragraphs on either side together exactly like #401 did before its fix. ## GitHub/GitLab-style heading-anchor links resolve to working Docs jump links (issue #409)

**Background:** Markdown converted from GitHub/GitLab Pages-published source keeps internal cross-reference links as literal `#slug` URL fragments — meaningless inside a Google Doc, since Docs has its own heading-jump-link addressing scheme. `get_doc_structure` now surfaces each heading paragraph's `headingId` (`paragraphStyle.headingId`, already present in the API response — no new API capability needed). `create_doc`/`create_doc_from_file`/`write_doc_content` now run an automatic second pass after any conversion that left a `#slug` link behind: it resolves the anchor against the doc's own real headings (trying GitHub's non-collapsing and GitLab's hyphen-collapsing slugification conventions, then a normalized-word-token fallback) and rewrites it to a working `https://docs.google.com/document/d//edit?tab=t.0#heading=` link — confirmed live 2026-07-24 that this ordinary-URL form works as a real in-doc jump link, no special `Link.headingId` API field needed. An anchor that matches no heading with reasonable confidence gets its link stripped (text kept, plain) rather than left dangling or guessed — a link silently pointing at the wrong section is worse than no link. The pass is skipped entirely (no extra API round trip) when the converted content has no `#`-prefixed link at all — see unit test `test_no_anchor_link_skips_resolution_pass` in `tests/test_docs_content.py`.

## Stale block-interruption frame from a mismatched list-close no longer resumed by a later, unrelated list (issue #450)

**Background:** Surfaced during PR #449's QA pass (issue #382 — mismatched `
                                                      `/`
                                                        ` close tags), confirmed as a distinct pre-existing bug rather than a regression from that PR. `_resume_interrupted_block` pushes a `_BlockFrame` onto `_block_stack` when a list interrupts an open block (e.g. an `` interrupted by `
                                                          `). If the interrupting list is later closed by a *mismatched* tag (`` instead of `
                                                        `), the old code only matched a frame by comparing its `interrupted_by` tag against the exact closing tag — a mismatch left the frame stuck on the stack. A later, unrelated, well-formed list could then close with a tag that happened to match the stale frame's `interrupted_by` value, incorrectly restoring `self._block_tag` to the original (now long-closed) outer block and mistyping subsequent bare trailing text as that stale block type. Fixed by matching list-category interruptions (`interrupted_by` in `{"ol", "ul"}`) by the list-nesting depth recorded at interrupt time instead of by tag identity — the frame is always resolved (popped) once that depth is reached, even on a mismatch, but the outer block is only actually *resumed* (`self._block_tag` restored) on an exact tag match; a mismatched close ends the interruption without guessing at reopening the outer block.

## Oversized inline-image handling — `insert_inline_image` / `insert_local_images` / markdown-image embedding (#400)

**Background:** Google Docs' `insertInlineImage` rejects any image over ~25 megapixels with a raw `HttpError 400 "...The provided image is too large."` that names neither the actual limit nor the image's own size. `tools/docs/images.py` adds pre-validation (default: a clear error naming the limit and the image's actual size, before any upload/share/embed happens) and an opt-in `auto_downscale` param that resizes the image instead of failing — for sources whose bytes this server already has direct access to (`drive_file_id`, a `"drive:"` reference, or a local file path). A bare public `http(s)` uri can't be pre-validated this way (would mean fetching arbitrary external content just to check it) — it instead gets Google's own error message rewritten with the same explanation once the embed actually fails. See `docs/decisions/decision-pillow-image-dependency.md` for the full scope-boundary rationale.

**Setup (all cases below):** generate a throwaway oversized test PNG — 6000×6000 = 36 megapixels, safely over the 25MP limit — not committed to the repo (too large):

### TC-DOC167: `insert_local_images` — an image under the megapixel pre-check but over Google's byte-size limit is now caught by pre-validation, not just the batchUpdate fallback
**Background:** `check_image_bytes`/`check_dimensions` used to only enforce Google's ~25-megapixel limit, not the ~50MB file-size limit `images.py`'s own module docstring also cites from Google's docs — so an image under 25 megapixels but with a very large byte size (e.g. low-compressibility noise data) passed pre-validation silently and reached the real `batchUpdate` call, which Google could still reject as "too large" (see the 2026-08-09 Result below, which documents that pre-#562 behavior — it predates this fix and is kept for history, not as the current expected outcome). Issue #562 added a `check_file_size` byte-size check (Google's documented ~50MB ceiling) alongside the megapixel one, so this exact case is now caught *before* any upload, the same way an over-megapixel image already was. `downscale_image_bytes` also gained a byte-size-driven shrink loop so `auto_downscale=True` has an actual effect here too, not just for the megapixel case.

**Setup:** generate a real, Pillow-decodable PNG that stays under the megapixel limit but is large in bytes — noise data compresses poorly, so this reliably produces a large file:

                                                                      uv run python3 -c "
import os
from PIL import Image
w, h = 4800, 5000  # 24.0 megapixels — under the 25MP pre-check
img = Image.frombytes('RGB', (w, h), os.urandom(w*h*3))
img.save('/tmp/qa-bigfile.png', compress_level=1)
"

                                                                      
(Produces a ~75MB file, safely over Google's documented 50MB ceiling while staying under the megapixel pre-check.)

**Prompt**
> "In doc {DOC_ID}, insert local images: marker 'IMGMARKERBIG', local_path '/tmp/qa-bigfile.png', into folder {FOLDER_ID}"

Tool call: `insert_local_images(doc_id={DOC_ID}, images=[{"marker": "IMGMARKERBIG", "local_path": "/tmp/qa-bigfile.png"}], folder_id={FOLDER_ID})`

- No new file appears in `{FOLDER_ID}` — confirm via `list_files(folder_id={FOLDER_ID})` or equivalent, since nothing should have been uploaded
- `get_doc_structure` shows the "IMGMARKERBIG" marker text still present, unchanged

### TC-DOC193: A literal leading tab in a bullet item's own source text does not nest it deeper than its sibling (#434 finding 1) ⚠️ requires-oauth

**Background:** `emitter.py`'s nested-bullet mechanism (#336) prepends `"	" * depth` synthetic tab characters to each `BulletItem` paragraph's text as the only way to signal nesting level to `createParagraphBullets`, which infers (and removes) nesting depth from however many leading tab characters it finds — it can't tell a synthesized depth marker apart from a literal tab that happens to already be the first character of the item's own source text (e.g. hand-formatted raw HTML). ### TC-DOC203: A cancelled `insert_local_images` still revokes the image's temporary share (#883) ⚠️ requires-oauth ⚠️ destructive

**Background:** `insert_local_images` uploads each image, shares it `anyone:reader`, sends the doc `batchUpdate`, then revokes the share. The revoke used to run only after the `batchUpdate` returned, so a call cancelled during the upload/share gather or the `batchUpdate` left the uploaded image publicly readable, with nothing reporting it. Now the upload/share gather is shielded from cancellation, so every granted share is recorded, and a shielded revoke runs on every exit, including a cancelled one. A cancelled call returns nothing, so every file it uploaded is logged as a WARNING, on every exit path: before the edit, with nothing left to embed, while the `batchUpdate` runs, and during the post-edit revoke (PR #903 round 2). A cancellation that arrives during the gather lands before the `batchUpdate` is sent, so the doc is left untouched. One that arrives while the `batchUpdate` runs can't stop it: the edit is atomic, so the doc is either untouched or has the image embedded, and either way no public share is left. This is the same pattern `_apply_doc_content` got in PR #877 (TC-DOC202), and both log through the same helper.

No MCP client can cancel a tool call at a chosen point, so this case uses `scripts/qa_cancel_insert_local_images.py`. The script runs the checkout's own `insert_local_images` against the real APIs inside an anyio task group and cancels it at one point: `share` (while the permission is being granted), `share-fail` (the same, but the share then fails, leaving an unshared upload), `edit` (just before the `batchUpdate`), `inflight` (while the `batchUpdate` runs), or `revoke` (during the post-edit revoke). Run it from the checkout under test with that checkout's OAuth token (`TOKEN_PATH`). It prints the tool's WARNING to stderr.

IMGMARKER883

After", content_format="markdown", folder_id={FOLDER_ID})`. Record `docId` as `{DOC_ID}`.

Step 1: every rule draws (first line, between paragraphs, two separate lines in a row, above the heading, in the list at "Item one"'s text indent with **2.** after it, above the table, after "Tail"). One defect: the quoted rule's line starts at the bar, but the bar breaks below it. "Quoted one" plus the rule carry one bar, then the rule's 6pt space below opens a gap, and "Quoted two" gets a bar of its own, so on screen it reads as two quotes while the export says one. Sent back. Cleanup: the three docs plus a probe doc trashed.

**Result (2026-11-01) ✅ PASS — PR #1326 round 2 (Sky)**
Live on `mcp-gee-sweet-sky` at 28c464a4, after `/mcp reconnect` (OAuth, Shared Drive folder), all seven steps. Step 1: every rule draws as listed. The quote bar now runs unbroken from "Quoted one" through the rule to "Quoted two", with the line closer to "Quoted two". Step 2's export is unchanged from round 1 and matches every check. Steps 3 and 4 pass as in round 1, re-run on this head. Step 5 exports both `---`. Step 6 exports `text before`, `---`, `text after`; then `> 1. item one`, `>`, `>    ---`, `>`, `> 2. item two` (the line inside "item one", one list; Drive imports the list indented, which reads as a quote); then `## heading`, `---`, `end`. Step 7 draws three bullets in one list with the line under the empty middle one at the item's text indent. The quoted list is a separate Docs list (its own `listId`), with offset bars. Its export is `- a`, `- `, `  ---` (no blank line after the empty marker), a blank line, `- b`, a blank line, then `> - qa`, `>`, `>   qb`, `>`, `> - qc`, `>`, `> after`. docs.title: Docs — Markdown Rendering — QA Test Cases
docs.text:
Source: every write path that turns a user's Markdown into a Google Doc. That's our converter (tools/docs/content.py _md_to_html → html_parser.py → emitter.py), Drive's native Markdown import (tools/drive/transfer.py _CONVERT_MIME[".md"]), and Drive's HTML import of upload_file(source_format='markdown').

Tracking: #1044. This file is the release gate for Markdown rendering in the ornithomimus release (label planned: ornithomimus; it gets a number when it goes in flight): it ships when every case below passes on screen through every entry point.

Fixtures: docs/qa/fixtures/md/. The nesting, containment, adjacency, inline-matrix, long-document and docstart/ fixtures, and the four matrix tables in this file, are generated by uv run python scripts/qa_gen_md_fixtures.py (--check reports drift); change those there, not by hand. Substitute {FOLDER_ID} (a throwaway child folder of TEST_FOLDER_ID, see "Running this suite") and {REPO} (absolute path of the checkout the server under test runs from).

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. Playwright is the oracle. Every case is Playwright: required. The verdict comes from the rendered Doc on screen, with one screenshot saved per case per entry point. get_doc_structure and get_doc_as_markdown are supporting evidence only, never the verdict: the Markdown export writes every numbered item as 1., so it can't see a numbering restart, and it may be blind to more. "Confirmed via unit tests" or "known gap, visual only" is not a result.
  2. The expected rendering is written down before a case runs (this file). It says what a reader sees: numbering, indent level, glyph, font, link target. Where the screen alone can't settle a detail, the case names the structural check that does (the Structural column or line).
  3. A known failure is a FAIL. "Matches documented failure mode," "known gap," "pre-existing," and "not a new regression" are never a PASS. A failing case stays FAIL, linked to an open issue, until the fix lands and the case passes on screen. The one exception is a decision below that changes a case's expected rendering: a cell that matches the rendering the decision sets is a PASS, as D4 does for EP-5 to EP-7.
  4. Nondeterminism is a FAIL. The whole matrix runs twice (Run 1, Run 2). A case that renders differently across the two runs fails, even if both renderings look acceptable.
  5. No sampling. Every case goes through every entry point in the table below, unless the case is marked N/A for an entry point with a reason. Shared code is how a path-specific wrapper bug hides.
  6. Anything that looks wrong is a finding, whether or not a case below covers it. Phase 1 especially: read each document top to bottom against its source.

docs.title: Entry points
docs.text:
Every case runs through every entry point. EP-1 to EP-4 and EP-8 use our converter (EP-8 through create_doc's path since #1102). EP-5 to EP-7 use Drive's native Markdown import (they upload the .md file and Drive converts it). A rendering difference between engines is itself a finding: the same Markdown should read the same way whichever tool turned it into a Doc. The exception is EP-5 to EP-7, whose expected rendering is Drive's documented one (decision D4 below).

EP Tool call (fixture F = absolute path of the .md file) Engine EP-1 create_doc(title="MD-<case>-EP1", content=<contents of F>, content_format="markdown", folder_id="{FOLDER_ID}") ours EP-2 write_doc_content(doc_id=<a blank Doc in {FOLDER_ID}>, content=<contents of F>, content_format="markdown") ours EP-3 create_doc_from_file(local_path=F, title="MD-<case>-EP3", folder_id="{FOLDER_ID}") ours EP-4 update_doc_from_file(doc_id=<a blank Doc in {FOLDER_ID}>, local_path=F) ours EP-5 upload_local_file(local_path=F, parent_folder_id=<empty child of {FOLDER_ID} for EP-5>, convert=True) Drive Markdown import EP-6 upload_local_folder(local_path=<a temp dir holding only F>, parent_folder_id=<empty child of {FOLDER_ID} for EP-6>, convert=True) Drive Markdown import EP-7 sync_folder(local_path=<a temp dir holding only F>, folder_id=<empty child of {FOLDER_ID} for EP-7>, direction="upload", convert_markdown=True) Drive Markdown import EP-8 upload_file(name="<case>.md", content=<contents of F>, source_format="markdown", folder_id="{FOLDER_ID}", convert_to_doc=True) ours, through create_doc's path (#1102)

EP-5, EP-6 and EP-7 each get their own empty child folder: these tools skip a file whose converted Doc already exists in the target folder (skip_if_exists defaults to True), so a shared folder would turn a later entry point's render into a skipped.

Not an entry point: no tool inserts Markdown at an index in an existing Doc (insert_doc_text takes plain text). The "insert at an index" state in #1044 is therefore N/A; if such a tool is added, it joins this table.

Parameter variants that only some entry points take:

  • autolink_urls=False (EP-1 to EP-4 only; the Drive engines and EP-8's upload_file have no such switch): run md-links.md a second time with it. Cases LK-05 and LK-06 then expect plain, unlinked text; every other links case is unchanged.
  • Images with a local path or drive: source (IM-04 to IM-06): EP-1 to EP-4 and EP-8 resolve and embed them; EP-5 to EP-7 don't. On EP-5 to EP-7 the image not being embedded is documented Drive behavior (D4): the case's heading is followed by an empty line, with no image, no alt text, no broken-image icon and no literal ![...](...) text (both runs of the 2026-10-18 Phase 2 baseline showed exactly that). Anything else in its place is a FAIL. On EP-8 those cells expect the embedded image, as on EP-1.

docs.title: What correct looks like in a Google Doc
docs.text:
Markdown describes HTML, and Docs has no direct equivalent for some constructs. These conventions turn "renders correctly" into something checkable. They follow the converter's documented design (docs/design/markdown-support.md, docs/design/blockquote-representation.md) where one exists.

# Construct Expected on screen Structural check when the screen is ambiguous C1 ATX/Setext heading level N Docs "Heading N" style (font size and weight of that named style) get_doc_structure: namedStyleType == HEADING_N C2 Bullet list, levels 0/1/2 Glyphs ● / ○ / ■, each level indented one step further bullet.nestingLevel = 0/1/2; contiguous same-type items of one Markdown list share one listId (a bullet run nested in a numbered list is its own Docs list) C3 Numbered list, levels 0/1/2 1. 2. … / a. b. … / i. ii. …; numbering never restarts inside one Markdown list, including after a nested block contiguous same-type items share one listId; the screen is the verdict for the number shown, since a nested block of the other type is a separate Docs list C4 Task item Bullet item whose text starts with ☐ (unchecked) or ☑ (checked); no literal [ ]/[x] — C5 Inline code Courier New on exactly the code characters textStyle.weightedFontFamily.fontFamily == "Courier New" on that run only C6 Code block (fenced or indented) One Courier New block; each source line on its own visual line; leading indentation and blank lines kept; no Markdown inside it interpreted one paragraph (lines joined by soft breaks), all runs Courier New C7 Blockquote, depth N Indented N steps with a gray left border; content inside keeps its own formatting (lists stay lists, headings stay headings) paragraphStyle.indentStart = 36pt × N and borderLeft set C8 Thematic break A visible horizontal line across the page; never an empty-looking gap — C9 Hard break (two trailing spaces, \) Line break inside the same paragraph: no extra blank line, no paragraph spacing between the two lines one paragraph containing a \v (soft line break) C10 Soft break (a plain newline inside a paragraph) The lines join into one paragraph, separated by a space one paragraph C11 Image The image itself is visible at its natural size (or scaled to page width); alt text is not shown as visible text inlineObjectElement present C12 Link Link-styled text (blue, underlined) whose target is the Markdown URL hover or textStyle.link.url C13 Table A Docs table, header row bold, cell text and inline formatting intact; column alignment from :--/:-:/--: applied to the cells of that column tableCells[].content[].paragraph.paragraphStyle.alignment C14 Block inside a list item (paragraph, code, quote, table, heading) Shown under the item, indented to the item's text, not as a new top-level block and not as literal Markdown; the list continues after it (next item keeps the list's numbering and nesting) the screen is the verdict: the next item shows the continued number or glyph; it shares the preceding items' listId when they're the same type C15 Empty paragraph spacing No visible empty paragraph that the source doesn't imply. The known collapsed blank paragraph before each table (docs/known-limitations.md, "Blank paragraph before every table") must stay invisible — C16 Image Docs can't embed (an SVG, an unreachable URL, a missing local file) Its alt text in its place, link-styled with the image's link if it had one; with an empty alt, the last segment of its source (a URL's file name, percent-decoded; a local file's name, never its path). Never an empty line (#1099). In a heading it's left out instead, so the heading's text and its slug stay as written (IM-13) the call's images entry has error and fallback_text

Decisions on the expected rendering. D1–D3, where CommonMark/GFM and what a user means disagree, were approved by the maintainer on 2026-10-17; D4 has its own date. Each is the expected behavior for this plan; changing one changes the expected rendering of the cases that cite it.

  • D1 — nesting width. A list marker indented at least 2 spaces (or one tab) further than the previous item's marker nests under that item, whatever the parent's marker width. CommonMark requires the child to reach the parent's content column, so 1. A followed by - a1 (2 spaces) doesn't nest under CommonMark, but that is how models and people write sub-bullets, and #1044's own example expects it to nest.
  • D2 — a table starts its own block. A pipe table directly under a paragraph, list item or quote line (no blank line) renders as a separate table after that block, not as text joined to it.
  • D3 — YAML front matter is not shown. A leading ----delimited YAML block is omitted from the Doc (docs/design/markdown-support.md currently calls it "acceptable" that it renders as a rule; that is a FAIL under this plan).
  • D4 — EP-5 to EP-7 render the way Drive's Markdown import does (maintainer, 2026-10-18, #1101). upload_local_file, upload_local_folder and sync_folder stay on Drive's engine. On those columns C1–C16 and D1–D3 still apply, except where the list in docs/known-limitations.md, "Converting .md on upload uses Drive's Markdown import, which renders differently", names a difference. A cell passes when every construct either meets C1–C16 and D1–D3 or differs only in a way that list names. So a 2-space sub-list under a numbered item that doesn't nest passes (the list names it, overriding D1), while D2 and D3 apply unchanged, since the list names nothing about them. Any other difference is a FAIL, and so is a rendering that changes between runs (Rule 4). Routing these paths through our converter is #1113; when that lands, these columns go back to C1–C16. EP-8 isn't covered: it uses our converter since #1102, so C1–C16 and D1–D3 apply to it in full.

Anything CommonMark/GFM permits that the converter deliberately won't support goes into docs/known-limitations.md, tied to an open issue, and its cases stay FAIL until a decision changes the expected rendering here.

docs.title: Running this suite
docs.text:
1. Server and slot. Use a server running the code under test with LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=full (EP-3 to EP-7 are local-only tools). Use an OAuth identity, or a service account with a Shared Drive {FOLDER_ID}.
  2. Throwaway folder. Create a child folder of TEST_FOLDER_ID named QA-MD-<date>-run<N> and use it as {FOLDER_ID}. Everything this suite creates goes there. Trash the folder after the results are recorded.
  3. Placeholders. md-images.md contains {QA_IMAGE_LOCAL_PATH} and {QA_IMAGE_DRIVE_ID}. Copy the fixture to docs/qa/fixtures/md/syntax/md-images.local.md (next to the original, so IM-05's relative path still resolves the same way), substitute the absolute path of docs/qa/fixtures/qa-fixture-pixel.png and the Drive ID of an uploaded copy of it, and use the copy. *.local.md under docs/qa/fixtures/ is ignored by version control, so the substituted copy (it holds a resource ID) can't be committed by accident.
  4. One render per fixture per entry point. Each syntax fixture holds many small cases, each under its own ### <ID> — <description> heading, so one render covers them all and a failure still points at one construct. Phase 1 documents and the document-boundary files (docstart/) are one case per file.
  5. Screenshots. Open the Doc at https://docs.google.com/document/d/<id>/edit and take one screenshot per case, scrolled so the case's heading and its full content are in view. Name it docs/qa/screenshots/md/<run>/<EP>/<case>.png (the screenshots/ tree is gitignored; keep the files until every issue filed from the run has them attached). Follow the Playwright mutex in run.md §"Coordinating Playwright across parallel shards", and verify the account first per §"Verifying Playwright is signed into the right account".
  6. Order. Phase 1 first, and file its failures before starting Phase 2 (#1044, "obvious problems first"). Then Phase 2, then the document-state cases.
  7. Determinism. Repeat the whole matrix as Run 2 in a fresh folder. Compare each case's Run 2 screenshot with Run 1.
  8. Recording. Write the per-case × per-entry-point grid to docs/qa/results/<date>-markdown.md (rows: case IDs; columns: EP-1 to EP-8; cells ✅, ❌ with the issue number, or N/A with the reason). Under each TC below, add one summary line: **Result (<date>) ❌ FAIL — <passed>/<total> case×EP cells pass; failures: #…**. A TC is ✅ PASS only when every cell of every case in it passes in both runs.
  9. Group. docs/qa/operations.yaml run_group with group: docs_markdown runs this file.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Realistic documents
docs.text: Documents of the kind AI clients produce, written the way a model writes them (2- and 3-space nesting, numbered steps with sub-bullets, bold lead-ins, tables, code). For each: render it, then read the Doc on screen top to bottom against the source, as a user would. Every construct follows the conventions above. The checklist names what's most likely to go wrong in that document; it doesn't limit what counts as a finding.

docs.title: TC-MD201: Containment matrix ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Prompt Playwright: required

Render docs/qa/fixtures/md/syntax/md-containment.md through EP-1 to EP-8.

Every block construct (paragraph, heading, bullet list, numbered list, task list, code block, blockquote, table, image, rule) inside every container that can hold it: a bullet item and a numbered item at levels 0, 1 and 2, a blockquote, and a nested blockquote. Contained content is indented 4 spaces per list level, so a failure here isolates containment from the indent-width cases in TC-MD106. Blank lines appear only where CommonMark needs them (around a contained paragraph, table or image), so most cases are tight lists; TC-MD107 covers loose ones.

A list contained in a list item nests one level deeper than the item and uses that level's glyph (C2/C3); every other contained block follows C14.

Not expressible, so not in the matrix: - Any block inside a table cell: GFM table cells hold inline content only. Inline content and images in cells are covered by TC-MD113 (TB-03) and TC-MD112 (IM-09). - A list item at level 3 or deeper: covered by nesting depth in TC-MD106, not containment.

docs.title: TC-MD303: A .md file with a long name through the Drive-import entry points ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Setup: copy docs/qa/fixtures/md/realistic/r01-meeting-notes.md to a temp directory as a file whose name is 110 ASCII bytes (qa-md303- padded with x, ending .md), and a second copy whose name is 45 CJK characters plus .md (over 130 UTF-8 bytes). Don't commit either name.

Prompt Playwright: required

Render each copy through EP-3, EP-5, EP-6 and EP-7.

Checks - No error and no failed entry for either file; nothing returns 403 propertyLengthLimitExceeded (#805, #806). - list_files on the target folder shows exactly one Doc per upload: no orphan left by a failed property write. - EP-7: a second sync_folder call with the same arguments reports the file skipped (in sync), not a new upload or a conflict. - Each Doc renders the meeting notes per TC-MD001.

Result (2026-10-22) ❌ FAIL — 0/8 cells pass. The long-name checks pass for both names in both runs (no error, one Doc per upload, second sync skipped); the meeting-notes render fails on #1071, #1093, #1098 (EP-3) and #1101 (EP-5–7). Grid: results/2026-10-22-markdown-boundaries-state.md.

docs.text:

docs.title: Conversion reporting
docs.text: What our converter tells the caller about the conversion, and the link targets it writes. Our converter's entry points only (EP-1 to EP-4, plus EP-8 where a case names it): the Drive-import entry points don't run our converter and report nothing about links.

docs.title: TC-MD501: Dropped links are reported in the response, host links get https ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Prompt Playwright: required

Render docs/qa/fixtures/md/state/dropped-links.md through EP-1 to EP-4. Then render a Doc through EP-1 with content="[site](https://example.com) and [mail](mailto:team@example.com)".

Checks - Each fixture call's response has dropped_links equal to, in this order: {"url": "./guide.md", "reason": "no_scheme"}, {"url": "/guide.md", "reason": "no_scheme"}, {"url": "cell.md", "reason": "no_scheme"}, {"url": "#no-such-heading", "reason": "no_matching_heading"}. ./guide.md is listed once, though DL-01 and DL-04 both link it. - On screen, every target in that list is plain text: "the guide", "the root guide", "jump nowhere", "the guide again" and "cell file" carry no link. - On screen, "the host" links to https://example.com/host and "the www site" to https://www.example.com/www: https, never http. Neither is in dropped_links. - On screen, "kept site", "kept mail" and "jump to the heading" are linked; "jump to the heading" jumps to the "Dropped links" heading. None of the three is in dropped_links. - The second call's response has no dropped_links key.

Result (2026-10-27, PR #1272 @ a423b390, Sky) ✅ PASS — 4/4 case×EP cells pass in both runs. EP-1 to EP-4 each returned exactly the four expected dropped_links entries in order, ./guide.md once; the second call had no dropped_links key. get_doc_as_markdown on every Run 1 doc and on EP-1/EP-4 in Run 2: DL-01/DL-04/DL-05 and "jump nowhere" plain text, "the host" → https://example.com/host, "the www site" → https://www.example.com/www, "jump to the heading" → the doc's own #heading= URL. Screenshot (EP-1, Run 1) matches. Edge targets this case doesn't cover failed in a separate probe (round 1 comment on PR #1272): www.example.com:8443/x was stored as http://…, and //, // x, www.foo bar, WWW.md were stored as dead https:// links that weren't reported. href=" ./guide.md" was reported separately from ./guide.md, with its leading whitespace.

Result (2026-10-28, PR #1272 @ f10ed9f7, Sky, round 2, after the develop merge brought in markdown-it) ✅ PASS — 4/4 case×EP cells pass. EP-1 to EP-4 returned the same four dropped_links entries in order; the second call had no key; get_doc_as_markdown on EP-1 and EP-3 shows the same stored links as round 1. All of round 1's edge probes are fixed live: the port target is stored as https://www.example.com:8443/x, and //, // x, www.foo bar, WWW.md are dropped and reported, with the padded ./guide.md reported once. New edge probes failed (round 2 comment): //:80 and //- were stored as dead https:// links; href=" " was reported as {"url": ""}; and a table cell's href=" #missing" was stored as a dead #missing link that wasn't reported.

Result (2026-10-28, PR #1272 @ f773c1c6, Sky, round 3) ✅ PASS — 4/4 case×EP cells pass. EP-1 to EP-4 returned the same four dropped_links entries in order, and the second call had no key. get_doc_as_markdown on EP-1 shows the same stored links as before. Every edge probe from rounds 1 and 2 passes live. //:80, //-, www.foo_bar.example_x and www.foo_bar.example_x:8443/x are dropped and reported. //example.com:8443/y is stored as https://example.com:8443/y. href=" " is no longer reported. A table cell's href=" #missing" is reported as no_matching_heading and stored as plain text, and its href=" #real-heading" resolves to the heading. Markdown autolinks are unchanged by the shared valid_gfm_domain: bare www.example.com still gets http:// (#1281), and www.foo_bar.example_x stays unlinked.

docs.title: TC-MD502: A bare www. autolink gets https, like a written www. link ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Prompt Playwright: required

Render docs/qa/fixtures/md/state/www-scheme.md through EP-1 to EP-4 and EP-8 (upload_file runs our converter too, #1102).

Checks - On screen, in WS-01, "www.example.com" (the bare autolink) and "y" (the written link) both link to https://www.example.com, and "www.example.com:8443/x" links to https://www.example.com:8443/x. No link in the Doc uses http:// (#1281: the autolink used to get http:// while the written link got https://). - get_doc_as_markdown on each Doc shows the same three targets. - No response has a dropped_links key.

Result (2026-10-30, PR #1298 @ 833b076c, Kit, round 1) ✅ PASS — 5/5 case×EP cells pass. EP-1 to EP-4 and EP-8 each stored [www.example.com](https://www.example.com), [y](https://www.example.com) and [www.example.com:8443/x](https://www.example.com:8443/x) (get_doc_as_markdown); no response had a dropped_links key. Screenshots of EP-1 and EP-8 show all three linked. Out-of-case probe: EP-5 (upload_local_file(convert=True), Drive's importer) stores all three as http://…, the written link included, so the engines differ on the scheme; LK-06 now records that.

docs.title: TC-MD503: Inline strike, sub/sup and highlight ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Prompt Playwright: required

Render docs/qa/fixtures/md/state/inline-scope.md through EP-1 to EP-4 and EP-8 (#1231). Also run TC-MD116's HT-01, HT-02 and HT-07 through EP-1 to EP-4 and EP-8: #1077's and #1119's done-when. Two runs, with an on-screen check.

Checks - IS-01: "x" (~~) and "y" (<del>) struck, " and " plain; "h", "i" and "j" struck (<del> inside <s>), "k." not. - IS-02: the "2" in "H2O" subscript, the "2" in "mc2" superscript, the rest of that text normal; in "abcd", "a" and "c" superscript, "b" subscript, "d" normal. - IS-03: "hi" highlighted yellow and bold, the text around it plain. - IS-04: in the body row, "x" superscript, "y" struck, "z" highlighted, the spaces between them plain; the second cell's "w" highlighted; the last row's cells plain. - get_doc_as_markdown on each Doc keeps the strikes as ~~…~~ (it has no syntax for sub/sup or highlight, so those read back as plain text). - Malformed input (unclosed or misnested tags) isn't in this case: the new tags behave as <s> does there, which the unit tests pin, and browser-matching recovery is #1329.

Result (2026-11-01, PR #1332 @ eb304470, Kit) ✅ PASS — 10/10 case×EP cells pass (inline-scope.md and TC-MD116's HT-01/02/07, each through EP-1 to EP-4 and EP-8), in both runs. Every check was read from the stored text styles (strikethrough, baselineOffset, backgroundColor 1/1/0) and the two runs' read-backs are identical. Seen on screen (Playwright): IS on EP-1 (Run 1) and EP-3 (Run 2), HT on EP-8 (Run 1). get_doc_as_markdown gives ~~x~~ and ~~y~~; ~~hij~~k. and plain sub/sup/highlight text, as expected.

Result (2026-11-01, PR #1332 round 2 @ 8fd9f042, after the develop merge bringing #1326, Kit) ✅ PASS — 10/10 cells, one run through EP-1 to EP-4 and EP-8. The stored-style read-back is identical to round 1's, so the round-1 on-screen checks still apply; no new screenshots.

docs.title: Known gaps and not-applicable
docs.text:
• Insert Markdown at an index: no tool does this (see "Entry points").
  • Nested tables: Markdown can't express a table inside a table cell (docs/known-limitations.md, "Nested tables not supported via Markdown input"); not a case here.
  • Comments, headers, footers: not Markdown constructs.

docs.text:
Source: src/mcp_gee_sweet/tools/docs/style.py

docs.title: TC-DOC75: get_doc_named_styles reads named style defaults set via the Docs UI
docs.text:
Note: Named styles are only populated when the user explicitly goes to Format > Paragraph styles > Update X to match. Most docs leave named styles at Google's defaults — this tool returns empty or near-empty for those docs. Use get_doc_theme to read actual paragraph appearance instead.

Prompt

"Call get_doc_named_styles on doc {DOC_ID} and show me the result."

Checks - No error key in result - For a doc where named styles were explicitly set: returns a non-empty dict with named style type keys - For a standard doc: may return {} or only Google's default entries (expected, not an error)

Result (2026-06-20) ✅ PASS Called on a doc that had apply_theme previously applied (Georgia HEADING_1/H2, Roboto NORMAL_TEXT). Returned 9 entries: NORMAL_TEXT (Roboto 11pt, line_spacing 115), HEADING_1 (Georgia 24pt bold, space_above 20), HEADING_2 (Georgia 18pt, space_above 18), HEADING_3–6 (Google defaults with font sizes and colors), TITLE, SUBTITLE. Confirms apply_theme default mode successfully writes to named styles, and get_doc_named_styles reads them back correctly. No error.

Result (2026-09-04) ✅ PASS get_doc_named_styles returned Google default entries (9 keys), no error key — expected for standard doc.

Result (2026-10-17) ✅ PASS — v0.9.2 release pass Run 2 (sa) on a throwaway doc; Playwright visual checks plus raw documents().get() reads.

docs.title: TC-DOC52: get_doc_theme scans body paragraph styles
docs.text:
Note: get_doc_theme reads explicit per-paragraph and per-run styles from the document body. It returns data for AI-generated docs (where styles are set explicitly on runs); for standard docs whose styles are fully inherited from named style defaults it returns an empty dict.

Prompt

"Call get_doc_theme on doc {DOC_ID} and show me the result."

Checks - No error key in result - For a doc with explicit paragraph styles: returns a dict with at least one named style type key; each entry has at least one of font_family, font_size, bold, italic, color, line_spacing, space_above, space_below - For a doc with purely inherited styles: result is an empty dict {} (expected, not an error)

Result (2026-06-20) ✅ PASS Called on a test doc created with create_doc (markdown content — inherited styles): returned {}. Called on the same doc after apply_theme overwrite=True (Georgia HEADING_1, Roboto NORMAL_TEXT): returned {"HEADING_1": {"font_family": "Georgia"}, "NORMAL_TEXT": {"font_family": "Roboto"}}. font_size and bold are not returned because the Docs API normalises explicit overrides that match the named style default back to inherited. No error key in either case.

Result (2026-09-04) ✅ PASS get_doc_theme on inherited-style doc returned {} — expected, no error.

Result (2026-10-17) ✅ PASS — v0.9.2 release pass Run 2 (sa) on a throwaway doc; Playwright visual checks plus raw documents().get() reads.

docs.text:
Note: Default mode (overwrite=False) emits updateNamedStyle requests — one per named style key — updating the document's style defaults. Existing paragraphs with explicit overrides are unaffected. No doc fetch is needed. Use overwrite=True to also apply directly to all existing paragraphs.

Prompt

"Apply theme {"HEADING_1": {"font_family": "Georgia", "font_size": 22}, "NORMAL_TEXT": {"font_family": "Verdana", "font_size": 11}} to doc {DOC_ID}"

Checks - Result contains docId and requests > 0 - No error key - requests equals the number of named style keys in the theme (one updateNamedStyle per key)

Result (2026-06-20) ✅ PASS Called with HEADING_1 + HEADING_2 + NORMAL_TEXT → {"docId": "...", "requests": 3}. Each emitted one updateNamedStyle request with snake_case field mask (named_style_type,text_style.weighted_font_family,text_style.font_size). No error. Live API accepted all three requests.

Result (2026-09-04) ✅ PASS apply_theme HEADING_1+NORMAL_TEXT -> {docId, requests:2} = key count; no error.

Result (2026-10-17) ✅ PASS — v0.9.2 release pass Run 2 (sa) on a throwaway doc; Playwright visual checks plus raw documents().get() reads.

docs.title: TC-DOC55: apply_theme with table styling ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Prerequisite: doc must contain at least one table (write one with write_doc_content first if needed)

Purpose: TC-DOC230 checks that the font lands. This case checks what a font_family call leaves alone: bold already on the range, the other fields in the same call, and an existing font when a later call omits font_family. get_doc_structure doesn't report a run's font, so the checks read the raw documents().get() textStyle.

  1. style_doc_range(doc_id=<it>, ranges=[{"start_index": 7, "end_index": 11, "bold": true}, {"start_index": 18, "end_index": 23, "font_family": "Courier New"}])
  2. style_doc_range(doc_id=<it>, ranges=[{"start_index": 1, "end_index": 6, "font_family": "Roboto Mono"}, {"start_index": 7, "end_index": 11, "font_family": "Georgia"}, {"start_index": 12, "end_index": 17, "font_family": "Georgia", "bold": true, "font_size": 18}, {"start_index": 18, "end_index": 23, "italic": true}])

Checks - Steps 1 and 2 return no error, with requests: 2 and requests: 4. - Raw read after step 2: "Alpha" has weightedFontFamily.fontFamily "Roboto Mono", and the spaces on either side have no weightedFontFamily. - "Beta" is Georgia and still bold: true. The font_family-only call must not clear the bold step 1 set. - "Gamma" has bold: true, fontSize 18pt and Georgia. - "Delta" is italic: true and still Courier New.

Cleanup: delete_file the doc.

Result (2026-10-27) ❌ FAIL — Beta loses its bold (#1273) Run against PR #1026's merge in an isolated service-account sandbox on a Shared Drive. Steps 1 and 2 returned requests: 2 and requests: 4, no error. Raw read: Alpha {"weightedFontFamily": {"fontFamily": "Roboto Mono", "weight": 400}}, with plain spaces around it. Gamma bold: true, fontSize 18pt, Georgia. Delta italic: true, Courier New. Beta is {"weightedFontFamily": {"fontFamily": "Georgia", "weight": 400}} with no bold. Re-bolding Beta and then sending font_family: "Courier New" alone cleared it again. The request's field mask is only weightedFontFamily, so the Docs API clears bold on its own. Docs UI rendering wasn't checked here (TC-DOC230 covers the font on screen). Doc trashed.

docs.title: style_doc_range: link_url: null now actually clears a link (issue #408)
docs.text: Background: TC-DOC30 above covers setting a link. Clearing one (link_url: null, documented in the tool's own docstring as the way to do it) always failed with HttpError 400 ... "Invalid requests[0].updateTextStyle: Links must include at least one type." instead. _text_style_and_fields (style.py, shared with insert_softbreak_paragraph in editing.py) built the clearing request as textStyle.link = {} — the Docs API rejects an empty Link object outright, confirmed live via a direct API call reproducing the exact reported error. Fixed by omitting the link key from textStyle entirely while still naming "link" in the fields mask — the correct way to reset a nested message field to its Docs API default (no link) — confirmed live this actually clears an existing link without error. Both call sites' own if text_style: requests.append(...) guard also had to change to if fields:: a link-clear-only call now legitimately produces an empty text_style dict alongside a non-empty fields list (["link"]), and the old guard would have silently dropped the request rather than sending it.

docs.title: TC-DOC156: create_paragraph_bullets repairs a flat list by promoting specific paragraphs to a deeper nesting level (#334) ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Background: issue #334: create_doc's Markdown conversion used to flatten an indented sub-list under a numbered item into the same single-level list, and there was no way to fix that after the fact short of delete-and-retype. Since #1228 (markdown-it, plan rule D1) that sub-list nests correctly, so #334's own repro no longer produces a flat list. This case builds the flat list directly instead, writing the three settings as top-level numbered items, and exercises the repair: get_doc_structure's bullet field to see the flat list, then create_paragraph_bullets to nest the settings.

Prompt Playwright: required

"Write this Markdown to doc {DOC_ID}: '1. Select the snapshot 2. Configure the instance: 3. Instance identifier 4. Instance class 5. Storage encryption 6. Click Restore ', then show me its structure."

Tool calls: write_doc_content(doc_id={DOC_ID}, content="1. Select the snapshot 2. Configure the instance: 3. Instance identifier 4. Instance class 5. Storage encryption 6. Click Restore ", content_format="markdown"), then get_doc_structure(doc_id={DOC_ID}) — note the start_index/end_index of the "Instance identifier" and "Storage encryption" paragraphs from this call's output.

Then: "Now nest the three settings paragraphs (Instance identifier through Storage encryption) one level deeper under item 2, and show me the structure again."

Tool calls: create_paragraph_bullets(doc_id={DOC_ID}, ranges=[{"start_index": <Instance identifier para start_index>, "end_index": <Storage encryption para end_index>, "nesting_level": 1}]) (one range spanning all three contiguous settings paragraphs), then get_doc_structure(doc_id={DOC_ID}) again.

Checks - First get_doc_structure call: all 6 items ("Select the snapshot" through "Click Restore") share one listId, all at nestingLevel: 0: the flat list #334 describes, with the three settings numbered 3–5 like their siblings - create_paragraph_bullets call succeeds with no API error - Second get_doc_structure call: "Select the snapshot", "Configure the instance", and "Click Restore" are still nestingLevel: 0; "Instance identifier", "Instance class", "Storage encryption" are now nestingLevel: 1, still sharing the same listId as their siblings - The three promoted paragraphs' own text is unchanged ("Instance identifier " and so on) — no tab character leaked into text (confirms the Docs API fully consumes the leading tab characters used to signal nesting depth) - 🔍 Visual check: the three settings render as a visually indented a./b./c. sub-list under "Configure the instance", and "Click Restore" now numbers as item 3 (not item 6)

Cleanup: write fixture content back

Result (2026-08-06) ❌ FAIL — run live against PR #524 (issue #334). First get_doc_structure call matches expectations (all 6 items share one listId at nestingLevel: 0, confirming the flattening). The repair step fails: after create_paragraph_bullets(ranges=[{"start_index": 45, "end_index": 114, "nesting_level": 1}]) (single range spanning all three contiguous settings paragraphs — the tool's own documented "safe" pattern), a second get_doc_structure shows all three settings paragraphs still at nestingLevel: 0 — the promotion had no effect. Worse, the leading tab character the tool inserts to signal depth was never consumed by the Docs API: "Instance identifier"'s own text field literally reads " - Instance identifier ", tab included — contradicting this test's own third check ("no visible tab character leaked into text") and the tool's docstring claim that the API "consumes (removing)" the tab once applied. This is the PR's own flagship, headline use case (#334's original repro) and it does not work at all as implemented. Sent back to Dev (PR #524 comment) rather than approved.

Result (2026-08-06, round 2) ❌ FAIL — re-verified live against fix commit a36f1c7. The nestingLevel/tab-leak failure from round 1 is fixed: the second get_doc_structure call now shows "Instance identifier"/"Instance class"/"Storage encryption" correctly at nestingLevel: 1 sharing the sibling listId, with no leaked tab in text. However, this test's own 🔍 visual check now fails for a new reason: a Playwright screenshot of the result shows the entire list rendered as unordered bullets (●/○) instead of numbers — "Click Restore" is a bullet, not "3.". Confirmed via a control doc (identical markdown, no create_paragraph_bullets call) that the pre-repair list renders correctly numbered 1–6, so the repair call itself is what strips the numbering. Root cause: the fix's fixed algorithm applies one bullet_preset to the entire merged run (the requested paragraphs plus every already-listed neighbor it sweeps in as context) — since this test's own documented tool call doesn't pass bullet_preset (defaults to BULLET_DISC_CIRCLE_SQUARE), it silently overwrites the numbering of "Select the snapshot"/"Configure the instance"/"Click Restore" even though the caller never asked to touch those paragraphs' preset. The round 1 code-review's two non-blocking findings (uncaught KeyError on a malformed range, unvalidated negative nesting_level) are both fixed and confirmed live; the original multi-range-fragmentation finding is also fixed and confirmed live (3 single-paragraph ranges at depths 0/1/0 now correctly share one listId). Sent back to Dev (PR #524 comment) rather than approved.

Result (2026-08-06, round 3) ✅ PASS — re-verified live against fix commit 9ae16ee. Re-confirmed no regression on the original multi-range-fragmentation repro (3 single-paragraph ranges at depths 0/1/0 still land in one shared listId with correct depths). qa-approved applied.

Result (2026-09-04) ✅ PASS 1./2./3. + nested a./b./c., "Click Restore" still "3." — #334 fix holds

Result (2026-10-17) ✅ PASS — v0.9.2 release pass Run 2 (sa) on a throwaway doc; Playwright visual checks plus raw documents().get() reads.

docs.title: TC-DOC191: create_paragraph_bullets — an all-nesting_level>=1 run renders the correct nested glyph, not the disc (#713) ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Background: issue #713 — create_paragraph_bullets (style.py) has the same collapse-to-nestingLevel 0 bug that emitter.py had under #439 (fixed in PR #711, covered by docs_content.md TC-DOC190). createParagraphBullets assigns each covered paragraph nestingLevel = (its leading-tab count) − (the minimum leading-tab count across the whole call's range), so a formed run in which every paragraph sits at nesting_level >= 1 — no level-0 member to anchor the inference — collapsed entirely to nestingLevel 0: the per-level indent was bumped so it looked nested, but the rendered glyph was the depth-0 disc (●) instead of the depth-1 circle (○). Reachable either by passing only nesting_level >= 1 ranges, or when the same-listId contiguous-neighbour expansion pulls in only paragraphs already at level >= 1. Fixed by wrapping such a run with a throwaway 0-tab anchor paragraph (insertText " " at run_start → createParagraphBullets over the range extended by 1 → deleteContentRange the anchor), mirroring emitter.py's #439 fix — the insert (+1) and delete (−1) cancel, so positions outside the run are unaffected.

Prompt Playwright: required

"Write this Markdown to doc {DOC_ID}: '- Alpha - Beta - Gamma ', then show me its structure."

Tool calls: write_doc_content(doc_id={DOC_ID}, content="- Alpha - Beta - Gamma ", content_format="markdown"), then get_doc_structure(doc_id={DOC_ID}) — note the start_index of "Alpha" and the end_index of "Gamma".

Then: "Now indent all three items one level deeper, and show me the structure again."

Tool calls: create_paragraph_bullets(doc_id={DOC_ID}, ranges=[{"start_index": <Alpha start_index>, "end_index": <Gamma end_index>, "nesting_level": 1}]) (one range covering all three items — the formed run has no level-0 member), then get_doc_structure(doc_id={DOC_ID}) again.

Checks - First get_doc_structure: "Alpha"/"Beta"/"Gamma" share one listId, all at nestingLevel: 0. - create_paragraph_bullets call succeeds with no API error. - Second get_doc_structure: all three paragraphs' bullet.nestingLevel is now 1 (not 0), still sharing the same listId; no leaked tab or stray anchor " " in any text field; no extra empty list paragraph left behind. - Precise structural confirmation (get_doc_structure doesn't expose the glyph): a script-driven documents().get() shows each of the three paragraphs with bullet.nestingLevel == 1, and that list's listProperties.nestingLevels[1].glyphSymbol is the circle (○), not nestingLevels[0]'s disc (●). - 🔍 Visual check: a Playwright screenshot shows all three items rendered with the depth-1 circle glyph (○) at a single indented level — not the depth-0 disc (●).

Result (2026-09-11) ✅ PASS — run live against PR #723 (commit 9bd4ca1), script-driven documents().get() + Playwright visual check. First get_doc_structure: "Alpha"(1-7)/"Beta"(7-12)/"Gamma"(12-18) share one listId, all nestingLevel: 0. create_paragraph_bullets(ranges=[{start_index:1, end_index:18, nesting_level:1}]) → no error, 7 requests (delete + 3 tab inserts + anchor insert + create + anchor delete — the isolated-run anchor-wrap shape). Second get_doc_structure: all three still share one listId (new list, as expected — delete+recreate always spawns a fresh one), now nestingLevel: 1, indices and text unchanged ("Alpha "/"Beta "/"Gamma ", no leaked tab or stray anchor ), trailing empty paragraph still bullet: null. Raw documents().get() on that listId: nestingLevels[1].glyphSymbol == '○' vs. nestingLevels[0] == '●' — the fix confirmed structurally, matching TC-DOC190's own emitter.py result. Playwright screenshot: Alpha/Beta/Gamma render the hollow-circle (○) glyph at one indented level, not the disc (●).

Note: sharing the fixture doc to the Playwright browser's own Google identity (TC-DOC190's mechanism) was blocked by the Claude Code auto-mode classifier this round; navigated directly instead once the human logged the Playwright browser into an account that already has access to the fixture — no share/revoke needed. Record which approach worked for the next run rather than assuming TC-DOC190's share-based one still does.

Result (2026-09-12) ✅ PASS (regression check, PR #735/#727) — PR #727 extracted this fix's insert/createParagraphBullets/deleteContentRange triple into a shared isolated_bullet_run_wrap_requests helper (indices.py), reused by both style.py (here) and emitter.py. Re-ran the tool-call steps above (not the full Playwright/glyph pass, since the underlying mechanism is unchanged from the 2026-09-11 PASS — only its call site moved): create_paragraph_bullets(ranges=[{start_index:1, end_index:18, nesting_level:1}]) → no error, 7 requests. Second get_doc_structure: all three share one new listId, nestingLevel: 1, text/indices unchanged, no leaked tab or anchor artifact, trailing paragraph still bullet: null — confirms the extraction is behavior-preserving. tests/test_docs_indices.py/tests/test_docs_style.py (79 tests) pass. Fixture restored to baseline.

Result (2026-09-12) ✅ PASS (re-verification, fix 31d5dd2, PR #735) — Ash's fix drops the redundant min_nesting seed, computing it once via min(u["nesting_level"] for u in run). Re-ran the tool-call steps: create_paragraph_bullets → 7 requests, no error; second get_doc_structure shows all three items sharing one new listId, nestingLevel: 1, text/indices unchanged, no leaked artifacts — identical outcome to the pre-fix run. tests/test_docs_style.py/tests/test_docs_indices.py (79 tests) pass. Fixture restored.

Cleanup: write fixture content back to the documented baseline (docs/qa/setup.md), NOT the Alpha/Beta/Gamma test content used above — an earlier version of this line told the next run to restore Alpha/Beta/Gamma itself, which would have permanently overwritten the real fixture baseline: write_doc_content(doc_id={DOC_ID}, content='<h1>Test Document</h1><p>This document is used for QA testing of mcp-gee-sweet.</p><ul><li>Item one</li><li>Item two</li></ul>').

Result (2026-10-17) ✅ PASS — v0.9.2 release pass Run 2 (sa) on a throwaway doc; Playwright visual checks plus raw documents().get() reads.

docs.title: TC-DOC234: create_paragraph_bullets sets nesting_level absolutely on already-listed paragraphs (#1069) ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Background: issue #1069. deleteParagraphBullets leaves a level-N item indented 36pt × N, and createParagraphBullets counts that leftover indent as depth on top of the tabs the tool inserts. So on a paragraph that was already a list item, the tool added the requested level to the current one: re-running the same 0/1/2 call gave 0/2/4, and a call naming one paragraph moved its untouched expanded neighbours too. Fixed by zeroing indentStart/indentFirstLine over each run after its deleteParagraphBullets and before the tab inserts, so the tabs alone set the level.

Prompt

"Write three plain paragraphs Alpha, Beta, Gamma to doc {DOC_ID}, then show me its structure."

Tool calls: write_doc_content(doc_id={DOC_ID}, content="Alpha Beta Gamma ", content_format="markdown"), then get_doc_structure(doc_id={DOC_ID}). Note each paragraph's start_index/end_index.

Then: "Make them a numbered list at levels 0, 1 and 2."

Tool calls: create_paragraph_bullets(doc_id={DOC_ID}, ranges=[{"start_index": <Alpha start>, "end_index": <Alpha end>, "nesting_level": 0, "bullet_preset": "NUMBERED_DECIMAL_ALPHA_ROMAN"}, {"start_index": <Beta start>, "end_index": <Beta end>, "nesting_level": 1, "bullet_preset": "NUMBERED_DECIMAL_ALPHA_ROMAN"}, {"start_index": <Gamma start>, "end_index": <Gamma end>, "nesting_level": 2, "bullet_preset": "NUMBERED_DECIMAL_ALPHA_ROMAN"}]), then get_doc_structure(doc_id={DOC_ID}).

Then: "Run exactly the same call again." Repeat the same create_paragraph_bullets call with the indices from the latest get_doc_structure, then get_doc_structure(doc_id={DOC_ID}).

Then: "Set only Beta to level 1." Tool calls: create_paragraph_bullets(doc_id={DOC_ID}, ranges=[{"start_index": <Beta start>, "end_index": <Beta end>, "nesting_level": 1}]), then get_doc_structure(doc_id={DOC_ID}).

Then: "Flatten Gamma to level 1, then put it back at level 2." Tool calls: create_paragraph_bullets(doc_id={DOC_ID}, ranges=[{"start_index": <Gamma start>, "end_index": <Gamma end>, "nesting_level": 1}]), get_doc_structure(doc_id={DOC_ID}), create_paragraph_bullets(doc_id={DOC_ID}, ranges=[{"start_index": <Gamma start>, "end_index": <Gamma end>, "nesting_level": 2}]), get_doc_structure(doc_id={DOC_ID}).

Checks - After the first bullet call: Alpha/Beta/Gamma share one listId at nestingLevel 0/1/2. - After the repeated call: still 0/1/2, not 0/2/4. - After the Beta-only call: still 0/1/2; Gamma, pulled in as a neighbour, keeps level 2. - After flattening Gamma: 0/1/1. After putting it back: 0/1/2, not 3. - Every create_paragraph_bullets call returns no error, and after each one all three paragraphs share one listId, with no leaked tab in any text field and no extra empty paragraph.

Cleanup: write fixture content back to the documented baseline (docs/qa/setup.md): write_doc_content(doc_id={DOC_ID}, content='<h1>Test Document</h1><p>This document is used for QA testing of mcp-gee-sweet.</p><ul><li>Item one</li><li>Item two</li></ul>').

Result (2026-10-24) ✅ PASS (PR #1216 round 1, head 5de64c4, Sky) — Run on a throwaway doc (created via create_doc, trashed afterward) instead of the shared fixture, so no fixture cleanup was needed. All steps as written: the first numbered call gave 0/1/2 on one listId; the repeated call gave 0/1/2 (not 0/2/4); the Beta-only call gave 0/1/2 with Gamma kept at 2; flattening Gamma gave 0/1/1, and putting it back gave 0/1/2 (not 3). Every call returned 5 requests and no error. No tab leaked into any text, and no paragraph was added: the trailing empty paragraph came from the markdown write and was there before the first call. Extra probes: (a) an emitter-written 0/1/2 list (- pa / 4-space - pb / 8-space - pc), re-bulleting only pb at level 1, gave 0/1/2, and a raw documents().get() showed the preset indents 36/18, 72/54, 108/90, so the explicit 0pt reset doesn't survive the bullet. (b) delete_paragraph_bullets over the three left pa with no indent and pb/pc at 36/36 and 72/72, as the new docstring says. Then create_paragraph_bullets on pb@1 + pc@2 (the #713 anchor path, starting from leftover indent) gave 1/2, with the anchor removed (7 requests), and the same result again on a repeat. (c) A quoted list item (72/54 + borderLeft) came out at 36/18 with the border kept; that's the pre-existing #1090, not this PR. get_doc_as_markdown still printed the >. Note for the next run: this markdown parser needs 4-space list nesting, and a 2-space nested item is written flat at level 0, quoted or not.

docs.title: TC-D263: A complete listing serves a later, larger max_results from cache (issue #698)
docs.text:
Background: list_files now requests Drive's nextPageToken and incompleteSearch; a response with neither means the listing is complete, and the cache records it as satisfying any later max_results. Before #698 a small-max_results fetch of a folder with fewer items than requested still recorded only the requested count, so a later larger request always re-fetched. A response with a nextPageToken (a truncated listing) must still be treated as insufficient for a larger request — that half is TC-D40's scenario 2, re-checked here. The epoch guard (a concurrent mutation's mark_dirty not being overwritten by an in-flight list_files) and the keep-larger compare-and-set are concurrency races with no deterministic live trigger; they're covered by tests/test_cache.py::TestSizedCacheRaces and tests/drive/test_files.py::TestListFiles::test_mark_dirty_during_fetch_is_not_overwritten.

Setup: DEBUG_LEVEL=DEBUG with LOG_FILE set on the server under test (same log-based check as TC-D38). Note the fixture folder's item count N from a plain list_files(folder_id={FOLDER_ID}); this test needs 2 <= N < 50.

Steps / Checks 1. refresh_cache(folder_id={FOLDER_ID}), then list_files(folder_id={FOLDER_ID}, max_results=50) → returns all N items. 2. list_files(folder_id={FOLDER_ID}, max_results=1000) → returns the same N items, byte-identical to step 1, and the log shows Drive folder cache hit: {FOLDER_ID} for this call (no fresh Drive files.list). 3. refresh_cache(folder_id={FOLDER_ID}), then list_files(folder_id={FOLDER_ID}, max_results=1) → exactly 1 item. 4. list_files(folder_id={FOLDER_ID}) (default max_results) → all N items, not 1, and the log shows no cache hit for this call (the step-3 listing had a nextPageToken, so it isn't complete).

Cleanup: none (read-only).

Result (2026-09-23, PR #788 round 1) ✅ PASS — run against a throwaway folder (N=2, a spreadsheet plus a subfolder) instead of {FOLDER_ID}, per run.md's fixture-pollution guidance. Run twice. On the second, strictly sequential run: step 1 fetched and logged Cached 2 files; step 2 returned the same 2 items with Drive folder cache hit and 0.000s; step 3 logged Cached 1 files; step 4 returned both items and logged Cached 2 files with no cache hit, so it was a fresh fetch. The first run sent some calls in parallel and they ran out of order, but it gave the same hit/miss pattern.

Result (2026-09-23, PR #788 round 2, ba3fbb9) ✅ PASS — rerun sequentially on the same throwaway folder after reconnecting to the fixed code, which now also requests incompleteSearch. The log matched round 1: step 1 Cached 2 files, step 2 Drive folder cache hit, step 3 Cached 1 files, step 4 Cached 2 files with no hit. Also re-checked the Sheets gap bug round 1 sent back. On a sheet with data in rows 1–2 and row 10 and rows 3–9 empty, refresh_cache → get_multiple_spreadsheet_summary(rows_to_fetch=5) → (rows_to_fetch=20) now fetches fresh and returns the rows through ["row10a","row10b"], where round 1 returned a cached result that hid row 10. A repeat rows_to_fetch=20 call logged Sheet data cache hit. The throwaway fixture was trashed afterwards.

Result (2026-10-17) ✅ PASS — v0.9.2 release pass Run 1 (kai-oauth).

docs.title: TC-D248: Single-quote in MIME type is escaped
docs.text:
Third sibling of TC-D155/TC-D247 (#494, PR #577 QA round) — list_files had the worst version of the same bug: mime_type was interpolated with zero escaping (not even the broken quote-doubling the other two had), and the .execute() call plus result mapping had no try/except around them at all. Live-reproduced during QA as an uncaught HttpError 400 "Invalid Value". Fixed with the same backslash-escape convention and try/except-returns-{"error": ...} wrapping used for TC-D155/TC-D247.

Prompt

"List files in {FOLDER_ID}, filtered to a MIME type containing an apostrophe like \"it's a test\""

Checks - No Drive API syntax error and no uncaught exception (previously threw HttpError 400 "Invalid Value") - Returns [] (no real MIME type will match) rather than crashing - Unit test test_mime_type_single_quote_is_escaped confirms \' appears in the constructed query string - Unit test test_api_error_returns_error_dict_not_raised confirms a genuine API failure returns [{"error": ...}] rather than propagating - Confirms the folder cache is not populated with a bad entry when the call errors (no folder_cache.store on the exception path)

Result (2026-08-12) ✅ Live list_files(folder_id=<fixture folder>, mime_type="it's a test") returned [] cleanly, no uncaught exception. 64 unit tests in tests/drive/test_files.py pass. Code-inspection confirms folder_cache.store sits after the list comprehension inside the try block, so an exception path never reaches it — no cache pollution on error.

Result (2026-09-04) ✅ PASS list_files(FOLDER_ID, mime_type="it's a test") returned [] cleanly — no HttpError 400 / uncaught exception. Backslash-escape + try/except wrapping confirmed.

Result (2026-09-21) ✅ PASS — PR #780 (issue #578, dedupe of the escaping logic into _escape_drive_query_mime_type) list_files(FOLDER_ID, mime_type="it's a test") → [] cleanly, no HttpError 400. Regression fix survives the extraction into a shared helper.

docs.title: TC-D260: get_file_metadata/list_files/search_files surface the starred field (issue #388)
docs.text:
Background: TC-D202/TC-D203 above could only verify star_file/unstar_file round-trip via the mutating tool's own response — there was no way to independently read a file's starred state. #388 adds starred to get_file_metadata's, list_files's, and search_files's response fields.

Setup Star {SPREADSHEET_ID} first (star_file), so this test starts from a known starred=true state. As of this issue's QA round 2 fix, star_file/unstar_file mark the file's parent folder(s) dirty in drive_folder_cache, so list_files({FOLDER_ID}) reflects the new state immediately with no manual cache step (confirmed live 2026-09-17, both directions). The explicit refresh_cache(folder_id={FOLDER_ID}) step below is kept anyway — harmless once the fix is in, and it's what round 1's QA pass used to catch the gap before the fix landed.

Prompt

"Get metadata for {SPREADSHEET_ID}, then refresh the folder cache for {FOLDER_ID}, then list files in {FOLDER_ID}, then search for it by name"

Checks - get_file_metadata({SPREADSHEET_ID}) response includes "starred": true - refresh_cache(folder_id={FOLDER_ID}) before the next check - list_files({FOLDER_ID}) includes an entry for {SPREADSHEET_ID} with "starred": true - search_files (matching the fixture's name) includes an entry for {SPREADSHEET_ID} with "starred": true (uncached, so no refresh needed here) - Unstar {SPREADSHEET_ID} (unstar_file), then re-run get_file_metadata — "starred": false

Teardown Ensure {SPREADSHEET_ID} ends unstarred (matches TC-D202/TC-D203's own convention of restoring fixture state).

Result: PASS (round 1, 2026-09-17, with the refresh_cache step above included). get_file_metadata → starred: true; refresh_cache(folder_id=...); list_files → starred: true for the fixture entry; search_files → starred: true for the fixture entry; unstar_file → starred: false; get_file_metadata re-check → starred: false. Round 1 separately confirmed the underlying gap this step existed for: repeating the same sequence without refresh_cache reproduced a stale list_files result (starred: false) immediately after starring, while get_file_metadata on the same file correctly showed starred: true. Sent back to the Dev as a blocking finding (PR #760 comment).

Result: PASS (round 2, 2026-09-17, commit 6bad917) — re-ran the round-1 gap repro without any manual refresh_cache call: list_files({FOLDER_ID}) warmed cold, star_file, then list_files({FOLDER_ID}) again with no cache call in between → correctly returned starred: true for the fixture entry. Repeated for unstar_file → correctly returned starred: false, no manual cache call either time. The fix (star_file/unstar_file now fetch parents and call drive_folder_cache.mark_dirty() per parent) works as intended. Fixture left unstarred.

Result (2026-10-17) ✅ PASS — v0.9.2 release pass Run on a throwaway spreadsheet; starred state visible in metadata, list_files and search_files.

docs.title: TC-D280: Permanent delete without permanent-delete permission — clear error, file kept (issue #876) ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Requires: an identity with the Content manager role (not Manager) on the mcp-gee-sweet-shared Shared Drive. The QA service account is added at exactly that role (setup.md Step 1), so run this on a service-account server (mcp-gee-sweet-sa, or the lane's own server relaunched with AUTH_METHOD=service_account). An OAuth identity that manages the Shared Drive gets canDelete: true and can't reproduce this.

Setup: upload_file(name="QA-876-Delete-Denied.txt", content="x", folder_id={FOLDER_ID}) as the Content-manager identity. Note the returned file ID.

Steps 1. delete_file(file_id=<id>, permanent=True) 2. get_file_metadata(file_id=<id>) 3. delete_file(file_id=<id>, permanent=False)

Checks - Step 1 fails with a ValueError saying the identity lacks permanent-delete permission, noting that on a Shared Drive this usually requires the Manager role, and suggesting permanent=False. It is not Drive's HttpError 404 "File not found". - Step 2 returns the file with trashed: false: nothing was deleted. - Step 3 returns {"fileId": <id>, "action": "trashed"}.

Cleanup: step 3 leaves the file in the Shared Drive's trash. Purge it with delete_file(file_id=<id>, permanent=True) from an identity with the Manager role (e.g. the lane's OAuth server), or leave it for a later empty_trash(drive_id={SHARED_DRIVE_ID}) run.

Result (2026-10-04) ✅ PASS Run as the QA service account (Content manager) from a fresh interpreter in the kit worktree driving PR #888's delete_file (kit's server is OAuth/Manager). Pre-check: capabilities={canDelete: false, canTrash: true}, file on the Shared Drive. Step 1 raised ValueError naming missing permanent-delete permission + permanent=False hint; no files().delete sent. Step 2 trashed: false. Baseline: a raw files().delete as the same SA still returns Drive's 404 "File not found", so the pre-flight check is what fixes it. Step 3 {"action": "trashed"}, then trashed: true. Cleanup: delete_file(permanent=True) via kit's OAuth (Manager) server returned {"action": "deleted"}, which also covers the canDelete: true path live.

Result (2026-10-04, round 2) ✅ PASS Re-run the same way against 255512b (Shared Drive note scoped to driveId). Step 1's ValueError now reads "...lacks permanent-delete permission on it. On a Shared Drive this usually requires the Manager role. Use permanent=False to move it to the trash instead." Steps 2–3 and the raw-delete 404 baseline as in round 1. Cleanup via kit's reconnected OAuth server: {"action": "deleted"}. The My Drive (no driveId) wording isn't live-tested: it needs a file owned by someone else, where a wrong result would be a real permanent delete. Unit test test_delete_file_permanent_without_can_delete_on_my_drive_omits_shared_drive_note covers it.

Result (2026-10-17) ⏭️ SKIP — v0.9.2 release pass Environmental: needs the SA identity plus a personal-Drive folder / a Content-manager SA.

docs.title: TC-D75: Search by name across all MIME types
docs.text:

Match by id, not by an empty result: fullText search also matches any live doc that mentions the name, such as a QA run log.

Cleanup: delete_file(file_id=<id>, permanent=True) on both, or leave them in the trash for a later empty_trash run. TC-D77 reuses them if run in the same pass, so clean up after TC-D77.

After trashing (trashed: true on both), no result of the unscoped or mime_type=folder search had either id.

Result (2026-10-19) ❌ FAIL — v0.9.3 release pass kai-sa: The #1054 checks pass: positive controls found both QA-Trashed-1054 fixtures, and after trashing neither appears in search_files("QA-Trashed-1054") (also with mime_type=folder). docs.title: TC-D299: Unscoped search under a service account finds Shared Drive files it never opened (#1127)
docs.text:
Servers: an OAuth server for setup and cleanup, and a service-account server (e.g. mcp-gee-sweet-kai-sa) for every check. Run on an OAuth server only, this case proves nothing: the bug was that Drive's default user corpus leaves out Shared Drive files the service account hasn't created or opened.

Setup: 1. On the OAuth server: create_doc(title="QA-Untouched-1127-Doc", folder_id={FOLDER_ID}) and create_spreadsheet(title="QA-Untouched-1127-Sheet", folder_id={FOLDER_ID}); note both ids. From here until cleanup, call nothing on the service-account server that reads either file by id (get_file_metadata, get_doc_content, get_sheet_data, ...). Once the service account opens a file, the file enters its user corpus and the case stops reproducing the bug. Listing and search calls don't count as opening. 2. Positive control, on the service-account server: search_files(query="QA-Untouched-1127", folder_id={FOLDER_ID}) must return both ids. Drive's search index can lag a new file, so retry until it does; an unscoped check run before this proves nothing.

Checks (all on the service-account server, none with a folder): - search_files(query="QA-Untouched-1127") returns both ids. - search_spreadsheets(query="QA-Untouched-1127") returns the spreadsheet's id. - list_recent_files(days=1, mime_type="application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet", max_results=100) includes the spreadsheet's id, and list_recent_files(days=1, mime_type="application/vnd.google-apps.document", max_results=100) includes the doc's id. - Before the fix, each of these returned neither id while the step-2 control found both.

list_spreadsheets() and list_folders() have the same fix, but no team server reaches their unscoped path: each sets DRIVE_FOLDER_ID, so a call with no folder is scoped to it. tests/drive/test_files.py::TestCorporaSelection covers that path.

Cleanup: on the OAuth server, delete_file(file_id=<id>, permanent=True) on both.

Result (2026-10-24) ✅ PASS — PR #1200 (#1127), QA round 1 (Sky) Setup on mcp-gee-sweet-sky (OAuth); every check in a fresh interpreter in the QA worktree, calling this branch's registered tool functions with a service_account.Credentials Drive client (no live server runs this branch as a service account). The fixtures were never read by id from the service account. Positive control (folder-scoped search_files) found both on the first try. Bug reproduced first: the same raw files().list query without corpora returned neither id, and with corpora="allDrives" returned both (incompleteSearch=False both ways). Checks, run twice with identical results: unscoped search_files → both ids; search_spreadsheets → the spreadsheet; list_recent_files(days=1, …spreadsheet, 100) → the spreadsheet; list_recent_files(days=1, …document, 100) → the doc. Cleanup: both permanently deleted from OAuth.

Result (2026-10-24) ✅ PASS — PR #1200 QA round 2 (Sky) @ 0073914c Rerun from scratch on the new head, because it moves the all-drives flags into _list_drive_files, which list_recent_files uses. Fresh fixtures, same method as round 1. Positive control found both. The raw query without corpora again returned neither, and with allDrives returned both. Unscoped search_files → both ids; search_spreadsheets → the spreadsheet; list_recent_files (spreadsheet / document, days=1, 100) → each id. Under OAuth, list_recent_files(max_results=100) → 41 results, no error. Cleanup: both permanently deleted.

docs.title: TC-D155: Single-quote in MIME type is escaped
docs.text:
Regression test for #494: the original implementation escaped mime_type by doubling the quote ('', SQL-style) instead of backslash-escaping it (\') like search_files/search_spreadsheets do — Drive's query grammar doesn't recognize the doubled form, so a mime_type containing an apostrophe live-crashed with an uncaught HttpError 400 "Invalid Value" rather than returning a clean result. Fixed by switching to the same backslash-escape convention as the sibling search tools, plus wrapping the call in the same try/except-returns-{"error": ...} pattern those tools already use.

Prompt

"List files shared with me, filtered to a MIME type containing an apostrophe like \"it's a test\""

Checks - No Drive API syntax error and no uncaught exception (previously threw HttpError 400 "Invalid Value") - Returns [] (no real MIME type will match) rather than crashing - Unit test test_mime_type_single_quote_is_escaped confirms \' (not '') appears in the constructed query string - Unit test test_api_error_returns_error_dict_not_raised confirms a genuine API failure still returns [{"error": ...}] rather than propagating

Result (2026-08-11) ✅ Live list_shared_with_me(mime_type="it's a test") returned [] cleanly, no uncaught exception. 62 unit tests in tests/drive/test_files.py pass. Note: list_files (a third sibling, same file) has the identical bug — reported as a blocking finding on PR #577, not covered by this test case.

Result (2026-09-04) ✅ PASS list_shared_with_me(mime_type="it's a test") → [] cleanly, no HttpError 400. Backslash-escape + try/except regression fix (#494) confirmed.

Result (2026-09-21) ✅ PASS — PR #780 (issue #578, extracted into shared _list_drive_files helper) list_shared_with_me(mime_type="it's a test") → [] cleanly, no HttpError 400. Regression fix survives the extraction.
