Cleanup: SIGTERM the server; delete the scratch token and log.

Result (2026-10-06, PR #925 round 2 @ a3af056, Sky) ✅ PASS SSE on 127.0.0.1:8937, OAUTH_CONSENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=25. A: initialize 0.2s, then the TC-I48 link with within 24s. After expiring the token: B and C each initialize in 0.1s (not 25s), and each list_files starts No usable OAuth token at '<scratch token>'. To re-authorize, open this link ... within 24s with the same link A got. The log has 0 Please visit, 0 earlier browser consent, and 2 Starting without Google access: ... a re-authorization link a tool call offered is still open lines. SIGTERM exited cleanly. B's and C's auth-status have no restart the server. A's does, from its gmail_not_authorized limitation: the team token lacks gmail.modify, and a missing scope still needs a restart by design. So I narrowed that check's wording to the oauth_not_authorized limitation.

Result (2026-10-17) ⏭️ SKIP — v0.9.2 release pass Needs OAuth token manipulation, a degraded start, SSE, or the auth consent flow.

docs.title: TC-I54: replacing a nearly expired tool-call link leaves the old link working until its stated deadline (PR #925 QA round 2) ⚠️ requires-oauth ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Background: a tool call's own consent attempt with less than min(60, timeout/2) seconds left isn't offered again; the next failing call gets a fresh link. In round 2 that replacement also stopped the old attempt, so link 1's callback port closed while its offer still promised it several more seconds, and a user on link 1's consent page landed on a dead localhost redirect. Now the old attempt keeps listening until its own deadline. The two attempts share a group: whichever completes publishes the token and sends elicitation/complete to both attempts' clients (unit-tested in tests/test_reauth.py::TestUserConsent::test_either_link_completes_and_notifies_both_clients).

Setup - The TC-I48 scratch token (dead access token, bogus refresh token).

Action Start a stdio session against uv run mcp-gee-sweet with AUTH_METHOD=oauth, TOKEN_PATH=<scratch token>, CREDENTIALS_PATH=<oauth client json>, OAUTH_CONSENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=25 (replacement threshold 12s), BROWSER=/usr/bin/false, DEBUG_LEVEL=INFO, LOG_FILE=<tmp log>, using the mcp SDK's stdio_client + ClientSession (no elicitation callback): 1. Call list_files (folder_id: "root", max_results: 1). Note the link (link 1), its within <N>s, and the time of the call; link 1's deadline is that time plus <N> 2. 16s after step 1, call list_files again. Note its link (link 2) 3. 2s after step 2, TCP-connect to link 1's and link 2's redirect_uri ports 4. 2s after link 1's deadline, TCP-connect to both ports again

Checks - 1: the TC-I48 consent-link error, within 24s or within 25s - 2: a different link, with a different redirect_uri port, and a time left of at least 23s - 3: both connects succeed (link 1 still open, with time left on its stated deadline) - 4: link 1's connect is refused (closed at its own deadline), and link 2's still succeeds - The log has 0 Please visit lines

Cleanup: end the session; delete the scratch token and log.

Result (2026-10-08, PR #925 round 3 @ e5f6fed, Sky) ✅ PASS mcp 2.3.0, stdio, fresh CACHE_DB_PATH. Step 1: Google rejected the OAuth token refresh: invalid_grant ..., link 1 within 24s, port 63319. Step 2 at +16.1s: a different link, port 63322, within 24s. Step 3 at +18.1s: both ports open (round 2 had link 1 closed by now). Step 4 at +26.0s (link 1's deadline +24s): link 1 refused, link 2 open. 0 Please visit. Extra check (the fix's "either link completes" claim, TC-I51-style): OAUTH_CONSENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=120 (threshold 60s). Link 1 within 119s. At +61.6s a second list_files gave link 2 (a different port), with both ports open. Playwright, under the mutex, after the fixture-doc sign-in check, then completed consent through link 1 (the replaced one): account chooser, the Workspace account, Allow, and the callback page on link 1's port read The authentication flow has completed. You may close this window. The scratch token's refresh_token changed and its mode is 0o600. Link 1's port then closed, and the retried list_files succeeded. Link 2's port stayed open after the consent completed, as designed: it listens until its own deadline. 0 Please visit. Scratch files deleted.

Result (2026-10-17) ⏭️ SKIP — v0.9.2 release pass Needs OAuth token manipulation, a degraded start, SSE, or the auth consent flow.

docs.title: TC-I55: SIGTERM with a streamable-http GET /mcp stream open closes the stream cleanly (issue #917) ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Background: TC-I47's sibling on the other HTTP transport. On SIGTERM, sse_starlette cancels the open GET /mcp event stream without its closing chunk, and mcp's handler then simply returns. Nothing follows the cut-off body, so uvicorn logged ASGI callable returned without completing response. and the client got a chunked body that never terminated (IncompleteRead(0 bytes read)). SingleResponseGuard (sse_shutdown.py) now sends the missing closing body when the app returns during shutdown with a started, unfinished response. Outside shutdown it leaves that alone, so uvicorn still reports a genuine incomplete response. main() serves --transport streamable-http through the guard with the same launch as --transport sse (anyio.run(uvicorn.Server(config).serve)), instead of mcp.run(transport="streamable-http"), which builds its own unguarded app.

Setup: none beyond a checkout of this branch. No Google credentials are needed: the case only needs an initialized session with its GET stream open.

Action Start uv run mcp-gee-sweet --transport streamable-http with HOST=127.0.0.1, PORT=<free port>, AUTH_METHOD=oauth, CREDENTIALS_PATH=<nonexistent>, TOKEN_PATH=<nonexistent>, DEBUG_LEVEL=DEBUG, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, stdout and stderr to one file. 1. With Python http.client: POST /mcp a JSON-RPC initialize (Content-Type: application/json, Accept: application/json, text/event-stream) and keep the returned mcp-session-id header. POST /mcp notifications/initialized with that session ID (expect 202). Then, on a separate connection, open GET /mcp with Accept: text/event-stream and the session ID, and read the response status (expect 200). Wait 2 seconds 2. Send the server process SIGTERM (not SIGKILL) and time its exit. Then read the GET response to EOF 3. Repeat steps 1–2 two more times against a fresh server, then once more with --reload added to the command line 4. Start a fresh server the same way; with the mcp SDK's streamable_http_client + ClientSession, initialize and list_tools, close the session, then SIGTERM the server 5. Run uv run mcp-gee-sweet --transport websocket

docs.title: TC-I56: over SSE with LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS unset, local-only tools aren't registered and an optional local_path is refused before any fetch (issue #796) ⚠️ requires-oauth ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Background: #796's policy defaults to off under any network transport, because a network-facing server's caller isn't necessarily its operator. In off mode the nine tools that only work on local files aren't registered. Tools with an optional local path stay registered and refuse it at entry, before any Google API call, so a refused destination costs no fetch and never reports an unrelated API error first. Design: docs/design/local-file-access-policy.md.

Setup: a checkout of this branch with working OAuth credentials in src/mcp_gee_sweet/.env (or CREDENTIALS_PATH/TOKEN_PATH). A spreadsheet ID the account can read (QA_SPREADSHEET_ID). Make sure LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS and LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS are unset in the environment and not set in .env. An empty scratch directory <scratch>.

Action Start uv run mcp-gee-sweet --transport sse with HOST=127.0.0.1, PORT=<free port>. With the mcp SDK's sse_client + ClientSession: 1. initialize, then list_tools 2. read_resource("server://auth-status") 3. call_tool("get_sheet_data", {"spreadsheet_id": QA_SPREADSHEET_ID, "sheet": "Sheet1", "local_path": "<scratch>/out.json"}) 4. call_tool("get_sheet_data", {"spreadsheet_id": "not-a-real-id", "sheet": "Sheet1", "local_path": "<scratch>/out.json"}) 5. call_tool("create_doc", {"title": "TC-I56 image probe", "content": "Text\n\n![x](<scratch>/x.png)", "content_format": "markdown"}) after writing any small PNG to <scratch>/x.png

Checks - 1: none of upload_local_file, upload_local_folder, download_file, download_folder, sync_folder, import_csv_to_sheet, create_doc_from_file, update_doc_from_file, insert_local_images is listed. get_sheet_data, send_message, create_doc are. - 2: local_file_access is {"mode": "off", "explicit": false, "roots": [], "unregistered_tools": [<the nine names above, sorted>]} - 3 and 4: both return an error whose text is exactly local file access is disabled on this server: LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS is unset, which means off for the sse transport. Step 4 does not report an HttpError 404, which proves the refusal comes before the fetch - 3, 4: <scratch> is still empty - 5: the doc is created with its text. The result's image outcome for <scratch>/x.png carries the same refusal text, and no file was uploaded to Drive for it

Cleanup: delete_file the TC-I56 doc. SIGTERM the server.

Result (2026-10-15, PR #1039 round 1 @ fb49e7d, Sky) ✅ PASS mcp 2.3.0, uvicorn 0.47.0, uv run mcp-gee-sweet --transport sse, SDK sse_client, OAuth, LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS/LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS unset in the environment and both .env files. Step 1: none of the nine local-only tools listed; get_sheet_data, send_message, create_doc listed. Step 2: {"mode": "off", "explicit": false, "roots": [], "unregistered_tools": [<the nine, sorted>]}. Steps 3 and 4: both is_error with exactly local file access is disabled on this server: LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS is unset, which means off for the sse transport; step 4 reported no 404. <scratch> held only x.png afterwards. Step 5: doc created with its text, images[0].error the same refusal text, and no PNG appeared in the target folder. Doc deleted.

Result (2026-10-15, PR #1039 round 2 @ 6ba5297, Sky) ✅ PASS Same driver as round 1, fresh subprocess on this head. Steps 1–5 matched round 1 exactly: no local-only tools listed, {"mode": "off", "explicit": false, ...} with the nine sorted, both get_sheet_data calls refused with the defaulted-off text (no 404), <scratch> held only x.png, and the doc was created with the image's per-item refusal. Doc deleted.

Result (2026-10-16, PR #1039 round 3 @ b8d0ced, Sky) ✅ PASS Same driver, fresh subprocess on this head. Steps 1–5 matched round 2: no local-only tools listed, {"mode": "off", "explicit": false, ...} with the nine sorted, both get_sheet_data calls refused with the defaulted-off text (no 404), <scratch> held only x.png, and the doc was created with the image's per-item refusal. Scratch folder trashed.

Result (2026-10-17) ⏭️ SKIP — v0.9.2 release pass Needs SSE, a LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS change, an invalid startup setting, or an HTTP transport.

docs.title: TC-I57: LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=roots allows paths inside a root and refuses the rest, symlinks included (issue #796) ⚠️ requires-oauth ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Background: In roots mode a path is resolved, symlinks included, and must land under a LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS directory. The refusal lists the allowed directories so a caller can choose a valid path. During a folder walk each entry is checked, so a symlink inside a root that points outside it is refused while the rest of the walk continues.

Setup: working OAuth credentials, a Drive scratch folder (QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID). Local directories <root> and <outside> (siblings, not nested). Files: <root>/ok.txt (fine), <outside>/secret.txt (secret), and a symlink <root>/escape.txt → <outside>/secret.txt.

Action Start uv run mcp-gee-sweet --transport sse with HOST=127.0.0.1, PORT=<free port>, LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=roots, LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS=<root>. With the SDK client: 1. list_tools, then read_resource("server://auth-status") 2. call_tool("upload_local_file", {"local_path": "<root>/ok.txt", "parent_folder_id": QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID, "skip_if_exists": false}) 3. call_tool("upload_local_file", {"local_path": "<outside>/secret.txt", "parent_folder_id": QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID}) 4. call_tool("upload_local_file", {"local_path": "<root>/escape.txt", "parent_folder_id": QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID}) 5. call_tool("upload_local_file", {"local_path": "<root>/../<outside basename>/secret.txt", "parent_folder_id": QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID}) 6. call_tool("sync_folder", {"folder_id": QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID, "local_path": "<root>", "direction": "upload", "dry_run": true}) 7. call_tool("upload_local_folder", {"local_path": "<root>", "parent_folder_id": QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID, "skip_if_exists": false})

Checks - 1: all nine local-only tools are listed. local_file_access is {"mode": "roots", "explicit": true, "roots": ["<root>"], "unregistered_tools": []} - 2: succeeds, returning a fileId - 3, 4, 5: each fails with <the path as passed> is outside this server's LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS. Allowed directories: <root>, and no file is created in QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID (check with list_files) - 6: actions has escape.txt with action: "local_read_fail" and a reason containing outside this server's LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS. ok.txt is planned normally - 7: uploaded is ["ok.txt"] and failed has one entry, escape.txt, with the same refusal text. secret never appears in Drive

Cleanup: delete_file every file the case created in QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID. SIGTERM the server. Remove <root> and <outside>.

Result (2026-10-15, PR #1039 round 1 @ fb49e7d, Sky) ✅ PASS Same driver as TC-I56, with LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=roots, LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS=<root>. Step 1: all nine local-only tools listed; {"mode": "roots", "explicit": true, "roots": ["<root>"], "unregistered_tools": []}. Step 2: fileId returned. Steps 3, 4 (symlink) and 5 (.. traversal): each <path as passed> is outside this server's LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS. Allowed directories: <root>. Step 6: escape.txt → local_read_fail with that reason plus ; not synced; ok.txt → skip / in sync. Step 7: uploaded: ["ok.txt"], failed: [{escape.txt, <same refusal>}]. list_files on the scratch folder never showed secret.txt or escape.txt. Note: a first harness run crashed after step 2 and left extra ok.txt copies, which made step 6 plan collision; the copies were deleted and the case rerun clean, as recorded here.

Result (2026-10-15, PR #1039 round 2 @ 6ba5297, Sky) ✅ PASS Fresh subprocess on this head. Step 1: nine listed, roots status as expected. Step 2: fileId. Steps 3–5: the same outside this server's LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS refusal for each. Step 6: escape.txt → local_read_fail, ok.txt → skip / in sync. Step 7: uploaded: ["ok.txt"], failed: [escape.txt]. Neither secret.txt nor escape.txt reached Drive. Scratch folder deleted.

Result (2026-10-16, PR #1039 round 3 @ b8d0ced, Sky) ✅ PASS Fresh subprocess on this head, in its own empty Drive folder. Step 1: nine listed, {"mode": "roots", "explicit": true, "roots": ["<root>"], ...}. Step 2: fileId. Steps 3–5: the outside this server's LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS refusal for each. Step 6: escape.txt → local_read_fail, ok.txt → skip. Step 7: uploaded: ["ok.txt"], failed: [escape.txt]. A first run in a folder that already held a control ok.txt planned collision at step 6 (fixture, not product); this clean rerun is the one recorded. Scratch folder trashed.

Result (2026-10-17) ⏭️ SKIP — v0.9.2 release pass Needs SSE, a LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS change, an invalid startup setting, or an HTTP transport.

docs.title: TC-I58: the server's own credential files are refused in full mode too (issue #796) ⚠️ requires-oauth ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Background: In every mode, including stdio's default full, tools can't read or write the server's own CREDENTIALS_PATH, TOKEN_PATH, SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH, .env, ADC key files, cache DB, or log files. Files are matched by identity, so a hardlink or symlink to the token is refused too, and a write target that doesn't exist yet is still refused, so a download can't plant a token.

Setup: a server whose TOKEN_PATH is a real OAuth token (a stdio server launched from this branch, e.g. via an MCP client config pointing at uv run mcp-gee-sweet). A Drive scratch folder holding a small text file named token.json (QA_TOKEN_NAMED_FILE_ID). A hardlink <scratch>/innocent.json to TOKEN_PATH (ln <TOKEN_PATH> <scratch>/innocent.json). For step 6: a subdirectory <directory containing TOKEN_PATH>/sub, a symlink <scratch>/link → that subdirectory (ln -s <directory containing TOKEN_PATH>/sub <scratch>/link), and a Drive subfolder of QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID holding one copy of QA_TOKEN_NAMED_FILE_ID named exactly TOKEN_PATH's basename (copy_file, then move_file).

Action 1. upload_local_file(local_path=<TOKEN_PATH>, parent_folder_id=QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID) 2. upload_local_file(local_path="<scratch>/innocent.json", parent_folder_id=QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID) 3. create_draft(to=<QA mailbox>, subject="TC-I58", body="x", attachments=[{"local_path": <TOKEN_PATH>}]) 4. download_file(file_id=QA_TOKEN_NAMED_FILE_ID, local_path=<directory containing TOKEN_PATH>) 5. read_resource("server://auth-status") 6. download_folder(folder_id=<the step-6 Drive subfolder>, local_path="<scratch>/link/..", skip_if_exists=false). The kernel resolves link before .., so this writes into <directory containing TOKEN_PATH>, not <scratch>

Checks - 1–4: each fails with <path> is one of this server's own credential, config, cache, or log files and can't be read by a tool (written for step 4) - 1, 2: no file is created in QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID. 3: no draft is created (check list_messages with label_ids=["DRAFT"]). 4: TOKEN_PATH's content and mtime are unchanged - 5: local_file_access is {"mode": "full", "explicit": false, "roots": [], "unregistered_tools": []} - 6: downloaded is empty and failed holds the one file, with the ... can't be written by a tool refusal naming the path as passed (<scratch>/link/../<TOKEN_PATH basename>), which the kernel resolves into <directory containing TOKEN_PATH>. TOKEN_PATH's content and mtime are unchanged (PR #1039 QA round 2)

Cleanup: rm <scratch>/innocent.json (the hardlink, not the token) and rm <scratch>/link (the symlink); rmdir <directory containing TOKEN_PATH>/sub. Trash the step-6 Drive subfolder. Leave QA_TOKEN_NAMED_FILE_ID for re-runs.

Result (2026-10-15, PR #1039 round 1 @ fb49e7d, Sky) ⚠️ PARTIAL: steps 1, 2, 4 run against a deny-listed log file, not TOKEN_PATH; step 3 pending This role's stdio mcp-gee-sweet-sky server (defaulted full). Claude Code's auto-mode classifier refused creating a hardlink to the real OAuth token, so the identity check was exercised with LOG_FILE (/tmp/mcp-gee-sweet.log), which goes through the same _is_denied path. Step 1 (upload_local_file on LOG_FILE): ... is one of this server's own credential, config, cache, or log files and can't be read by a tool. Step 2 (a hardlink to LOG_FILE in a scratch dir, same inode confirmed with ls -li): the same refusal, naming the hardlink path. Step 4 (download_file of a Drive file named mcp-gee-sweet.log to /tmp/): /tmp/mcp-gee-sweet.log is one of ... and can't be written by a tool. Steps 1–2 added nothing to the scratch folder. Step 3 pending: the classifier also refused create_draft with an attachment, and this slot's token lacks the Gmail scope anyway. Step 5: {"mode": "full", "explicit": false, "roots": [], "unregistered_tools": []}. Not yet run: steps 1, 2 and 4 against the real TOKEN_PATH.

Result (2026-10-15, PR #1039 round 2 @ 6ba5297, Sky) ⚠️ PARTIAL: steps 1, 2, 4 against LOG_FILE; step 3 pending; a regression found outside the case's steps Fresh SSE subprocess on this head with an explicit LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=full and LOG_FILE=<denied>/log.txt (round 1's substitution, for the same reason). Step 1: <denied>/log.txt ... can't be read by a tool. Step 2 (hardlink <scratch>/innocent-log.txt): the same refusal. Step 4 (as download_folder(local_path=<denied>) of a Drive folder holding log.txt): failed: [{log.txt, "... can't be written by a tool"}]. Step 5: {"mode": "full", "explicit": true, ...}, as expected for the explicit setting. Step 3 still pending. Outside the steps: download_folder(local_path="<scratch>/link/..", skip_if_exists=false), where <scratch>/link → <denied>/sub, downloaded log.txt and overwrote the deny-listed LOG_FILE with the Drive file's content. many_checks()' _realpath collapses .. with abspath before resolving the symlink, so the check sees <scratch>/log.txt, while the write's <scratch>/link/../log.txt lands in <denied>. At round 1's head the plain realpath refused it. Sent back on the PR.

Result (2026-10-16, PR #1039 round 3 @ b8d0ced, Sky) ⚠️ PARTIAL: steps 1, 2, 4, 6 against LOG_FILE; step 3 pending Fresh SSE subprocess on this head, explicit LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=full, LOG_FILE=<denied>/log.txt (the same substitution as rounds 1–2). Steps 1, 2, 4: the same refusals as round 2. Step 5: {"mode": "full", "explicit": true, ...}. Step 6, with <scratch>/link → <denied>/sub and a Drive folder holding log.txt plus the control files a.txt and ok.txt: download_folder(local_path="<scratch>/link/..", skip_if_exists=false) put log.txt in failed with <scratch>/link/../log.txt is one of this server's own credential, config, cache, or log files and can't be written by a tool. The same probe through sync_folder(direction="download") failed log.txt with the same refusal plus ; not synced. LOG_FILE's head was unchanged after both. The control files landed in <denied>, not <scratch>, so the walk really did go through the symlink. Step 3 still pending (the auto-mode classifier and the slot token's missing Gmail scope, as in round 1).

Result (2026-10-17) ⏭️ SKIP — v0.9.2 release pass requires-oauth; step 5 covered by server://auth-status local_file_access mode "full".

Result (2026-10-24, PR #1222 round 1 @ 5a30c76, Sky) ⚠️ PARTIAL: steps 1 and 5 only, step 1 against LOG_FILE mcp-gee-sweet-sky (stdio, defaulted full), run because #1212 changed LocalFileAccess from str, Enum to StrEnum. Step 1 against LOG_FILE (/tmp/mcp-gee-sweet.log, the same substitution as PR #1039's rounds): ... is one of this server's own credential, config, cache, or log files and can't be read by a tool. Step 5: local_file_access is {"mode": "full", "explicit": false, "roots": [], "unregistered_tools": []}, so .value still serializes as before. Steps 2–4 and 6 not run (unaffected by the enum change).

Result (2026-10-25, PR #1222 round 2 @ 7690b8c, Sky) ⚠️ PARTIAL: steps 1 and 5 only, step 1 against LOG_FILE After the pydantic 2.14.1 re-lock, reconnected. Step 1: the same ... can't be read by a tool refusal. Step 5: {"mode": "full", "explicit": false, "roots": [], "unregistered_tools": []}.

docs.title: TC-I59: an invalid local-file setting stops the server at startup with a one-line message (issue #796) ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Background: LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS/LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS are validated at import, but an invalid setting only resolves to off there, with its reason recorded. main() exits on it before serving, so a misconfigured server never serves, while mcp-gee-sweet auth and scripts/gen_tool_docs.py still run (PR #1039 QA round 1, finding 4). A LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS set outside roots mode only warns. With ENABLED_TOOLS naming a local-only tool that off mode drops, the server warns which ones are missing and why.

Setup: none beyond a checkout of this branch. No Google credentials are needed.

Action Run each with uv run mcp-gee-sweet --transport sse and HOST=127.0.0.1, PORT=<free port>, stderr captured. Stop a server that starts with SIGTERM after 3 seconds. 1. LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=everything 2. LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=roots with LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS unset 3. LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=roots, LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS=/no/such/dir 4. LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=full, LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS=/tmp 5. LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=off, ENABLED_TOOLS=sync_folder,get_sheet_data 6. LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=roots, LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS=/no/such/dir, running uv run mcp-gee-sweet auth --help instead of the server 7. LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=everything, running uv run python scripts/gen_tool_docs.py instead of the server

Checks - 1: exits non-zero with mcp-gee-sweet: LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS='everything' isn't valid (use full, roots, or off) and no traceback. Steps 1–3 also log one ERROR mcp_gee_sweet.local_files Local file access is off: <the same reason> line first - 2: exits non-zero with mcp-gee-sweet: LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=roots needs LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS, a ':'-separated list of directories - 3: exits non-zero with mcp-gee-sweet: LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS entry '/no/such/dir' isn't an existing directory - 4: starts; stderr has LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS is set but ignored: it applies only when LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=roots - 5: starts; stderr has LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=off: not registering local-only tools named in ENABLED_TOOLS: sync_folder, and an SDK list_tools returns only get_sheet_data - 6: exits 0 and prints usage: mcp-gee-sweet auth, so a root that isn't mounted yet doesn't block re-authorization - 7: exits 0 with gen_tool_docs: docs already up to date (on a clean checkout), and git status shows no change to docs/tools.md: the generated docs list every tool whatever the policy

Cleanup: SIGKILL any server still running.

Result (2026-10-15, PR #1039 round 1 @ fb49e7d, Sky) ✅ PASS uv run mcp-gee-sweet --transport sse, stdout and stderr captured. Steps 1–3: exit 1 with exactly the three expected one-line messages and no traceback. Step 4: started; WARNING mcp_gee_sweet.local_files LOCAL_FILE_ROOTS is set but ignored: it applies only when LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=roots. Step 5: started; WARNING mcp_gee_sweet.server LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=off: not registering local-only tools named in ENABLED_TOOLS: sync_folder, and SDK list_tools returned ["get_sheet_data"]. Exit 143 for the started servers is uv forwarding SIGTERM.

Step 6: exit 0, usage: mcp-gee-sweet auth [-h] [--no-browser] [--include-tools INCLUDE_TOOLS]. Step 7: exit 0, the ERROR ... isn't valid line, then gen_tool_docs: docs already up to date; git status clean.

Step 6: exit 0, usage: mcp-gee-sweet auth [-h] [--no-browser] [--include-tools INCLUDE_TOOLS]. Step 7: gen_tool_docs: docs already up to date, and git status showed no change outside this file.

docs.title: TC-I60: an HTTP request reaching a defaulted full policy is refused (issue #796) ⚠️ requires-oauth ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Background: The transport default is read from --transport on the command line. A server served some other way, such as uvicorn mcp_gee_sweet.server:app directly, has no --transport, so it resolves to stdio's default full while actually serving SSE. _timed marks every call that arrives over HTTP, and the policy then refuses all local access unless LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS was set explicitly, logging one warning. The local-only tools are registered in that launch, but every call they make is refused.

Setup: working OAuth credentials (a call needs Google services to reach the tool body). A scratch file <scratch>/a.txt. LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS unset in the environment and in .env.

Action 1. Start uv run uvicorn mcp_gee_sweet.server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port <free port>. With the SDK's sse_client: list_tools, then call_tool("upload_local_file", {"local_path": "<scratch>/a.txt", "parent_folder_id": QA_SCRATCH_FOLDER_ID}) twice. SIGTERM the server 2. Same with LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=full set, calling upload_local_file once

Checks - 1: upload_local_file is listed. Both calls fail with local file access is disabled for HTTP requests unless LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS is set explicitly, nothing is uploaded, and the server log has exactly one Refusing local file access for an HTTP request warning - 2: the upload succeeds (an explicit full over HTTP is the operator's choice)

Cleanup: delete_file the step-2 upload. SIGTERM the server.

Result (2026-10-15, PR #1039 round 1 @ fb49e7d, Sky) ✅ PASS uv run uvicorn mcp_gee_sweet.server:app (uvicorn 0.47.0), OAuth, SDK sse_client. Step 1: upload_local_file listed; both calls returned local file access is disabled for HTTP requests unless LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS is set explicitly; the run's stderr has exactly one Refusing local file access for an HTTP request warning; nothing uploaded. Step 2 (LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=full): upload succeeded, no warning. Upload deleted.

Step 1: upload_local_file listed, both calls refused with local file access is disabled for HTTP requests unless LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS is set explicitly, and exactly one Refusing local file access for an HTTP request warning (the same record appears once in LOG_FILE and once in stderr). Step 2: upload succeeded, no warning. Scratch folder trashed.

docs.title: TC-I61: with MCP_SERVER_TOKEN set, SSE and streamable HTTP reject every request without the bearer token (GHSA-mpw3-mr4r-6cqh) ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Background: the SSE and streamable HTTP transports used to accept any request, on every interface by default, so a network peer could call every tool as the configured Google identity. BearerAuth (http_auth.py) now sits inside SingleResponseGuard on both apps (server.app and _streamable_http_app()), and checks every HTTP request against MCP_SERVER_TOKEN. A missing and a wrong token get the same 401. The token is read per request and never logged. The same wrapping covers --reload, which serves those apps by import string.

Setup: a token T from python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))". A free port. Google access isn't needed: AUTH_METHOD=oauth with a nonexistent CREDENTIALS_PATH and TOKEN_PATH starts degraded, which still answers initialize and list_tools. Find this machine's LAN address (ipconfig getifaddr en0 on macOS). Run each server in its own process group, stdout and stderr to one log (docs/qa/run.md §"Running server-startup and CLI cases").

Action 1. Start uv run mcp-gee-sweet --transport sse with HOST=0.0.0.0, PORT=<port>, MCP_SERVER_TOKEN=T, AUTH_METHOD=oauth, CREDENTIALS_PATH=<nonexistent>, TOKEN_PATH=<nonexistent>, DEBUG_LEVEL=INFO, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1. Against http://<LAN address>:<port>, with http.client or urllib: a. GET /sse with no Authorization header b. GET /sse with Authorization: Bearer wrong c. GET /sse with Authorization: Bearer T followed by one extra character d. POST /messages/?session_id=00000000000000000000000000000000 with no header e. With the SDK's sse_client(url, headers={"Authorization": "Bearer T"}) + ClientSession: initialize, then list_tools f. Same as e with "bearer T" (lowercase scheme) SIGTERM the server. 2. Start uv run mcp-gee-sweet --transport streamable-http with the same environment. Against http://<LAN address>:<port>/mcp: a. POST /mcp with a JSON-RPC initialize request and Accept: application/json, text/event-stream, with no Authorization header b. With the SDK's streamable_http_client and the Authorization: Bearer T header: initialize, then list_tools SIGTERM the server. 3. Repeat step 1a and 1e once with --transport sse --reload. 4. grep -c the token T in every log from steps 1–3.

Checks - 1a–1d, 2a: each gets 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, and 1a, 1b, 1c and 1d have byte-identical status, headers (apart from date) and body - 1e, 1f, 2b: initialize succeeds and list_tools returns the full tool list - 1: the log has one Rejected an unauthenticated request warning per rejected request, each naming the client's address and the path (/sse, /messages/), and no Authorization header value - 3: same as 1a (401) and 1e (tools listed) under the reloader - 4: 0 in every log

Cleanup: SIGTERM any server still running (by pid, never pkill -f). Delete the logs.

Note for the probe: an in-process probe of server._streamable_http_app() (Starlette TestClient) gets 401 with or without MCP_SERVER_TOKEN: with no token the middleware serves only a loopback local address (scope["server"]) naming a loopback Host, and TestClient's default testserver is neither.

Result (2026-10-19) ✅ PASS — Kit, GHSA-mpw3 fork PR #1 @ 46ce96b1 Real servers on 0.0.0.0, driven over the LAN address, token from secrets.token_urlsafe(32). Steps 1a–1d and a non-ASCII Bearer é header all got 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, and 1a–1d were byte-identical (status, headers minus date, body Unauthorized). 1e, 1f and 2b listed 130 tools. 2a got 401. Under --reload (step 3), 401 without the header and 130 tools with it. The log had 5 Rejected an unauthenticated request warnings for 5 rejections, each naming the LAN client and /sse or /messages/, and no Authorization value. Step 4: the token appears in no log or stdout capture. Joy's in-process repro (_streamable_http_app(), LAN client and Host) got 401 on initialize and tools/list, with MCP_SERVER_TOKEN set and unset alike, 0 tools exposed.

Result (2026-10-19) ✅ PASS — Kit, GHSA-mpw3 fork PR #1 @ 15638736 (round 2) Steps 1–4 rerun on real servers after BearerAuth gained its host argument; every check matched round 1 (byte-identical 401s, 130 tools for 1e/1f/2b and under --reload, one warning per rejection, token in no log).

docs.title: TC-I62: an HTTP transport on a non-loopback address with no token refuses to start; the default address is loopback (GHSA-mpw3-mr4r-6cqh) ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Background: main() runs http_auth.check_startup() for --transport sse and --transport streamable-http, with or without --reload, before serving. A non-loopback HOST (anything but 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 or localhost) with MCP_SERVER_TOKEN unset or blank stops the server, unless ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP is 1 or true. Any other opt-out value stops it on every address. HOST now defaults to 127.0.0.1. stdio and mcp-gee-sweet auth never run the check.

Setup: a free port for each step. HOST, FASTMCP_HOST, MCP_SERVER_TOKEN and ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP unset in the environment and in src/mcp_gee_sweet/.env, except where a step sets them. AUTH_METHOD=oauth, nonexistent CREDENTIALS_PATH/TOKEN_PATH, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, stdout and stderr captured. Stop a server that starts with SIGTERM after 3 seconds.

Action 1. --transport sse with HOST=0.0.0.0 2. --transport streamable-http --reload with HOST=0.0.0.0, MCP_SERVER_TOKEN= (empty) 3. --transport sse with HOST=<LAN address>, MCP_SERVER_TOKEN=" " 4. --transport sse with HOST=127.0.0.1, ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP=yes 5. --transport sse with HOST=0.0.0.0, ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP=1. While it runs, GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/sse with no header 6. --transport sse with HOST=0.0.0.0, MCP_SERVER_TOKEN=T, ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP=true. While it runs, GET /sse with no header 7. --transport sse with no HOST. While it runs: lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN, then GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/sse with no header, then GET http://<LAN address>:<port>/sse 8. stdio (uv run mcp-gee-sweet, no --transport) with HOST=0.0.0.0 and ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP=bogus: send an initialize request on stdin. Point CREDENTIALS_PATH at a file that exists (a dummy {"installed": {...}} client JSON is enough): under stdio a missing client JSON exits at startup (#790's fail-fast), which isn't what this step checks 9. uv run mcp-gee-sweet auth --help with HOST=0.0.0.0 10. Launch without main(): uv run uvicorn mcp_gee_sweet.server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port <port> with no token and no opt-out. While it runs: GET http://<LAN address>:<port>/sse; GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/sse; the same loopback GET with Host: evil.example:<port>; the same with X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 sent to the LAN address. Then grep -c 'MCP_SERVER_TOKEN is unset' the log. Then relaunch the same command twice more: with HOST=0.0.0.0 and ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP=1, GET http://<LAN address>:<port>/sse; with ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP=yes (no HOST), the LAN GET and the plain loopback GET 11. Optional, if Docker is available: docker build -t mcp-gee-sweet-qa ., then docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:<port>:8000 mcp-gee-sweet-qa with no -e MCP_SERVER_TOKEN 12. --transport sse with HOST=127.0.0.2, no token (macOS only answers on 127.0.0.1 until sudo ifconfig lo0 alias 127.0.0.2 up; remove it after with sudo ifconfig lo0 -alias 127.0.0.2. Without that, check the same requests in-process: Starlette TestClient(server.app, base_url="http://127.0.0.2:8000") with HOST=127.0.0.2 set before import). While it runs, GET http://127.0.0.2:<port>/sse. Then relaunch with ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP=1 added, and send the same GET twice: once plain, once with Host: attacker.example:<port> 13. --transport sse with HOST=0.0.0.0 and MCP_SERVER_TOKEN= (set but empty, as docker-compose passes it when its own .env lacks it), with MCP_SERVER_TOKEN=T in src/mcp_gee_sweet/.env. While it runs, GET http://<LAN address>:<port>/sse with no header, then with Authorization: Bearer T

Checks - 1, 2, 3: exit 1 with one line, mcp-gee-sweet: refusing to serve --transport <transport> on <host> without authentication: ..., naming MCP_SERVER_TOKEN, HOST and ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP. No traceback, nothing listens on the port, and 2 never logs Started reloader process - 4: exit 1 with one line naming ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP and 1 or true, without echoing yes - 5: starts; the log has a warning that it is serving 0.0.0.0 without authentication; the GET gets 200 and event: endpoint - 6: starts; the log has ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP is ignored because MCP_SERVER_TOKEN is set; the GET gets 401 - 7: lsof shows a listener on 127.0.0.1:<port> only; the loopback GET gets 200; the LAN GET fails to connect - 8: the server answers initialize; no refusal - 9: prints the auth usage and exits 0 - 10: it starts (no main(), so no startup check). The LAN GET gets 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer; the plain loopback GET gets 200 and event: endpoint; the evil.example Host and the X-Forwarded-For request get 401. The grep counts 1: one warning however many requests were refused. With HOST=0.0.0.0 and the opt-out, the LAN GET gets 200 and event: endpoint (without HOST, the app is built for the 127.0.0.1 default, where the opt-out does nothing, so the LAN GET gets 401). With the invalid opt-out, the LAN GET gets 401, the loopback GET 200, and the server keeps running with no traceback - 11: the container exits at once with the step-1 message for 0.0.0.0 - 12: both launches start. The plain GET gets 200 and event: endpoint both times (any 127.0.0.0/8 bind that starts is reachable). The attacker.example Host gets 401: the opt-out does nothing on a loopback HOST - 13: starts (the blank variable doesn't hide the .env token); the plain GET gets 401, the bearer GET 200 and event: endpoint

Cleanup: SIGTERM any server still running (by pid). docker rmi mcp-gee-sweet-qa if step 11 ran. Remove the step-13 line from src/mcp_gee_sweet/.env.

Result (2026-10-19) ✅ PASS — Kit, GHSA-mpw3 fork PR #1 @ 46ce96b1 Steps 1–3: exit 1, one refusing to serve line naming all three settings, no traceback, nothing listening; step 2 never started the reloader. Step 4: exit 1 naming 1 or true, yes not echoed. Step 5: started, serving-without-authentication warning, loopback GET 200 + event: endpoint. Step 6: ignored-opt-out warning, GET 401. Step 7: lsof showed 127.0.0.1:<port> only; loopback GET 200, LAN GET connection refused. Step 8: initialize answered (first attempt used a nonexistent CREDENTIALS_PATH and hit #790's stdio fail-fast; the step now says to use a dummy client file). Step 9: usage, exit 0. Step 10: LAN 401, loopback 200 + event: endpoint, evil.example Host 401, X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 to the LAN address 401; one MCP_SERVER_TOKEN is unset warning over 8 rejections. Step 10's relaunches: with the opt-out and no HOST, the LAN GET got mcp's 421 (Host check built for the 127.0.0.1 default); with HOST=0.0.0.0 and the opt-out, 200; with ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP=yes, LAN 401, loopback 200, no crash or traceback. Step 11: the container exited 1 about 6 s after start with the step-1 line for 0.0.0.0.

Result (2026-10-19) ✅ PASS — Kit, GHSA-mpw3 fork PR #1 @ 15638736 (round 2) Steps 1–10 rerun on real servers, all matching round 1 except the intended change in step 10: with the opt-out and no HOST, the LAN GET now gets our 401 (the opt-out does nothing on the loopback default), and with HOST=0.0.0.0 and the opt-out it still gets 200. Step 12 ran in-process (no lo0 alias, so no sudo): with HOST=127.0.0.2, check_startup passed, the built BearerAuth layer had host 127.0.0.2, a 127.0.0.2:8000 Host passed through, and attacker.example:8000 got 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, with and without ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED_HTTP=1. Step 13: with MCP_SERVER_TOKEN= in the environment and the token in src/mcp_gee_sweet/.env, the server started on 0.0.0.0; plain GET 401, bearer GET 200 + event: endpoint; .env restored. Step 11 not rerun: the Dockerfile is unchanged since round 1 and the container sets no token.

docs.title: TC-I63: two Google identities sharing one cache DB never see each other's entries (GHSA-8jqx-w7j8-6xwm) ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Background: every cache row carries the Google identity it was fetched as (drive:<permissionId>, else sa:<service account email>), and every read filters on it. Invalidation doesn't: refresh_cache and write-side invalidation reach every identity's rows. A cached sheet list is served stale only on a 5xx, 429 or network failure, never in place of a 403/404. Run the servers from this lane's own worktree, not the shared -oauth/-sa MCP servers, which serve main-checkout code.

Setup: a fresh scratch path C=<tmp>/qa-cache/cache.db, with <tmp>/qa-cache created (empty) before each run. An explicit CACHE_DB_PATH never creates its parent directory, on develop or the fix: with it missing, both servers log falling back to :memory:, share nothing, and the case passes vacuously. Check each log has no not usable/unusable line before reading any result. Two stdio servers, each driven by an SDK stdio_client + ClientSession script per docs/qa/run.md §"Running server-startup and CLI cases in a scoped lane pass", both with CACHE_DB_PATH=$C, DEBUG_LEVEL=DEBUG and their own LOG_FILE: server A with AUTH_METHOD=oauth (the fixture OAuth account), server B with AUTH_METHOD=service_account. {SPREADSHEET_ID} below is a scratch spreadsheet that only A can open, not the fixture TEST_SPREADSHEET_ID, which the service account can read (it's on the Shared Drive). Create it in A's My Drive root with a fresh-interpreter script (drive.files().create(body={"name": ..., "mimeType": "application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet"}) on auth._oauth_creds(), per CLAUDE.md "MCP restart"), not with create_spreadsheet, which puts it in DRIVE_FOLDER_ID. B's service account must also have no access to A's calendars. Run steps 1–2 on the fork's develop first (before resetting to the fix branch), then the whole case on the fix branch.

Action 1. A: list_calendars(); record the calendar IDs. Then B: list_calendars(). 2. A: list_sheets(spreadsheet_id="{SPREADSHEET_ID}"). Then B: list_sheets(spreadsheet_id="{SPREADSHEET_ID}"). Then A: refresh_cache(spreadsheet_id="{SPREADSHEET_ID}"), and B: list_sheets(spreadsheet_id="{SPREADSHEET_ID}") again. 3. With both servers stopped: sqlite3 $C "SELECT DISTINCT principal, namespace FROM cache". 4. Restart A only. list_sheets(spreadsheet_id="{SPREADSHEET_ID}") twice; grep A's log for Cache hit. 5. With A still running, start B and call refresh_cache() (no arguments). Then A: list_sheets(spreadsheet_id="{SPREADSHEET_ID}"); grep A's log again.

Checks - On develop (the defect): B's step-1 list_calendars returns A's calendars, or B's step-2 list_sheets returns A's sheet names instead of an error. Record which. - On the fix branch: - 1: B's list contains none of A's calendar IDs (only calendars B itself is subscribed to, possibly none). - 2: both of B's list_sheets calls return an error (403/404 permission text), never A's sheet names, including after A's refresh_cache left A's row dirty (the old stale fallback). - 3: two distinct principal values, each drive:... or sa:...; no row has an empty principal. - 4: the second call logs Cache hit (A's own entry is still served to A). - 5: A's call after B's flush logs no new Cache hit for {SPREADSHEET_ID} (B's invalidation reached A's row) and still returns the sheet names.

Cleanup: stop both servers; rm -rf <tmp>/qa-cache; delete the scratch spreadsheet.

Result (2026-10-20, GHSA-8jqx fork PR #1 round 1 @ 9e6f4d06, Kit) ✅ PASS Two-server SDK driver from the Kit worktree, A-only scratch spreadsheet (2 sheets) in A's My Drive. Fork develop @ b009e72d, steps 1–2 (defect reproduced, both ways): B's list_calendars returned all 3 of A's calendar IDs (B itself has 0); B's list_sheets returned A's sheet names, and again after A's refresh_cache (stale fallback). A first develop run with <tmp>/qa-cache missing fell back to :memory: on both servers and showed no leak, hence the setup fix above. Fix branch, directory created first, no not usable lines: 1: B got 0 calendars, overlap with A 0. 2: both B calls 403 The caller does not have permission. 3: 2 distinct principals, both drive:... (the SA resolves its own permissionId), 0 empty; rows calendar ×2, sheet_structure. 4: after restart the first call re-fetched (row still dirty from step 2's refresh), the second logged Cache hit: 2 sheets. 5: after B's refresh_cache() (invalidated: all), A's call logged Cached 2 sheets and no new Cache hit, sheet names returned. DB file -rw-------. Scratch spreadsheet deleted, scratch dirs removed.

Result (2026-10-20, GHSA-8jqx fork PR #1 round 2 @ 18a0e4bc, Kit) ✅ PASS Same driver, fresh A-only scratch spreadsheet, <tmp>/qa-cache created first, no not usable lines in either log. 1: B 0 calendars, overlap with A 0. 2: both B calls 403. 3: 2 distinct drive: principals, 0 empty. 4: second call Cache hit: 2 sheets. 5: after B's refresh_cache(), A re-fetched (Cached 2 sheets), no new hit. The cache opened lines now appear only when a cache is first used, and name the real path. Scratch spreadsheet deleted, scratch dirs removed.

Result (2026-10-20, GHSA-8jqx fork PR #1 round 4 @ 295b5118, Kit) ✅ PASS Rerun after merging develop and the GHSA-mpw3 branch in. Same driver, fresh A-only scratch spreadsheet, no not usable lines. 1: B 0 calendars, overlap with A 0. 2: both B calls 403. 3: 2 distinct drive: principals, 0 empty. 4: second call Cache hit: 2 sheets. 5: after B's refresh_cache() (invalidated: all), A re-fetched (Cached 2 sheets), no new hit. DB -rw-------. Outside the case, over SSE with MCP_SERVER_TOKEN set: an unauthenticated GET /sse got 401 before any cache DB existed; two authenticated connections both bound the same drive: principal, and the second was served from the first's entry. Scratch spreadsheet deleted, scratch dirs removed.

docs.title: TC-I64: the default cache location is per-user and owner-only; a symlinked cache isn't used (GHSA-8jqx-w7j8-6xwm) ⚠️ local-filesystem
docs.text:
Background: with CACHE_DB_PATH unset, the DB is ~/Library/Caches/mcp-gee-sweet/cache.db (macOS), or $XDG_CACHE_HOME / ~/.cache plus mcp-gee-sweet/cache.db (Linux). The directory is 0700, the DB and its -wal/-shm files 0600. A directory or file owned by another user, or a symlink in place of one, makes the server warn and cache in memory. The old /tmp/mcp_gee_sweet.db is tightened to 0600 if it's ours, never deleted. Importing the package creates nothing.

Setup: a scratch HOME=<tmp>/home (created, empty), XDG_CACHE_HOME unset, CACHE_DB_PATH unset in the environment and in src/mcp_gee_sweet/.env, umask 022. A stdio server driven by an SDK client script (as in TC-I63), AUTH_METHOD=oauth with TOKEN_PATH/CREDENTIALS_PATH pointing at the fixture files, DEBUG_LEVEL=DEBUG, LOG_FILE set. D below is the platform's default cache directory under the scratch home.

Action 1. HOME=<tmp>/home uv run python -c "import mcp_gee_sweet.server", then find <tmp>/home. 2. Start the server; list_sheets(spreadsheet_id="{SPREADSHEET_ID}"); stop it. stat -f '%Sp %N' D D/cache.db* (Linux: stat -c '%A %n'). 3. chmod 755 D; start the server, make one call, stop it; stat D. 4. Unless a /tmp/mcp_gee_sweet.db already exists (then record its owner and mode, and skip the rest of this step): create it, owned by you, mode 0644. Start the server, make one call, stop it; stat it. 5. rm -rf D, then ln -s <tmp>/elsewhere D (<tmp>/elsewhere an empty directory). Start the server, list_sheets twice, stop it. 6. rm D. Set CACHE_DB_PATH=<tmp>/explicit/cache.db, after creating <tmp>/explicit with mode 0755 and an empty cache.db in it with mode 0644. Start, one call, stop; stat the directory and the file. 7. CACHE_DB_PATH=:memory:: start, one call, stop; find <tmp>/home <tmp>/explicit -newer <tmp>/explicit/cache.db. 8. CACHE_DB_PATH unset again, LOCAL_FILE_ACCESS=full: start, then upload_local_file(local_path="D/cache.db", parent_folder_id="{FOLDER_ID}") (parent_folder_id is required; without it the call fails argument validation before the policy check runs).

Checks - 1: find lists only <tmp>/home itself: nothing created at import. - 2: D is drwx------; cache.db (and any -wal/-shm) is -rw-------. - 3: D is drwx------ again. - 4: /tmp/mcp_gee_sweet.db is -rw------- and still exists. - 5: the log has Cache file not usable (... isn't a directory), falling back to :memory:; both calls succeed; <tmp>/elsewhere stays empty. - 6: the file is -rw-------; its directory is still drwxr-xr-x. - 7: find prints nothing; the call succeeds. - 8: refused with ... is one of this server's own credential, config, cache, or log files and can't be read by a tool; nothing uploaded. - Another user's directory or file needs a second uid, so it's unit-tested only (tests/test_cache_isolation.py::TestPermissions).

Cleanup: rm -rf <tmp>/home <tmp>/elsewhere <tmp>/explicit. If step 4 created /tmp/mcp_gee_sweet.db, delete it and its -wal/-shm.

Result (2026-10-20, GHSA-8jqx fork PR #1 round 1 @ 9e6f4d06, Kit) ✅ PASS (step 4 skipped) SDK driver from the Kit worktree, macOS, umask 022, scratch HOME (with UV_CACHE_DIR pointed at the real uv cache so uv itself writes nothing under it). 1: find lists only <tmp>/home. 2: D drwx------, cache.db -rw------- (no sidecars left after stop). 3: D chmod'd to drwxr-xr-x, back to drwx------ after one call. 4: skipped, /tmp/mcp_gee_sweet.db already exists, ours, already -rw-------; tightening covered by unit tests only this round. 5: log Cache file not usable (<tmp>/home/Library/Caches/mcp-gee-sweet isn't a directory), falling back to :memory:; both calls returned the sheet names; <tmp>/elsewhere empty. 6: cache.db -rw-------, <tmp>/explicit still drwxr-xr-x. 7: call succeeded, find -newer printed nothing. 8: first run without parent_folder_id failed pydantic validation (step text fixed above); rerun refused with ... is one of this server's own credential, config, cache, or log files and can't be read by a tool, nothing uploaded. Scratch dirs removed.

Result (2026-10-20, GHSA-8jqx fork PR #1 round 2 @ 18a0e4bc, Kit) ✅ PASS (step 4 skipped) Same driver, all 8 steps. 1: nothing created at import. 2: D drwx------, cache.db -rw-------. 3: drwxr-xr-x tightened back to drwx------. 4: skipped, same /tmp/mcp_gee_sweet.db (ours, -rw-------). 5: Cache file not usable (... isn't a directory), falling back to :memory:, and the only cache opened line reads sheet_structure cache opened: :memory: (round 1 logged the refused path here); both calls succeeded; <tmp>/elsewhere empty. 6: file -rw-------, directory still drwxr-xr-x. 7: find -newer empty. 8: refused by the deny-list, nothing uploaded. Outside the case: check_read now refuses /tmp/mcp_gee_sweet.db and -wal (round 1 allowed them), and in python:3.12-slim-bullseye (glibc 2.31) both an explicit and the default cache open and write, with the file -rw------- and directory drwx------ (round 1 raised NotImplementedError). Scratch dirs removed.

Result (2026-10-20, GHSA-8jqx fork PR #1 round 4 @ 295b5118, Kit) ✅ PASS (step 4 skipped) Rerun after merging develop and the GHSA-mpw3 branch in. Same driver, all 8 steps, every check matching round 2. 1: nothing created at import. 2: D drwx------, cache.db -rw-------. 3: tightened back to drwx------. 4: skipped, same /tmp/mcp_gee_sweet.db (ours, -rw-------). 5: not usable ... falling back to :memory:, cache opened: :memory:, both calls succeeded, <tmp>/elsewhere empty. 6: file -rw-------, directory still drwxr-xr-x. 7: find -newer empty. 8: refused by the deny-list. Scratch dirs removed.

docs.title: TC-I65: the first calls after a long idle don't fail on a stale connection (issue #1052)
docs.text:
Background: thread_http caches one transport per worker thread, and a thread's pooled keep-alive connection sits unused while the server is idle. Before #1052, the first request on a connection Google had since dropped failed with no retry: [Errno 54] Connection reset by peer at once, or [Errno 60] Operation timed out after 50–200 s. In a wide get_multiple_sheet_data call that showed up as one per-query error among otherwise correct results. Now a pooled connection idle longer than _IDLE_RECONNECT_SECONDS (wall-clock time, so a laptop's sleep counts) is closed before reuse, a connection that fails is closed rather than left pooled, and a read (GET, HEAD, or a method-override GET) or a token refresh that still hits a dead connection is resent once. Writes are never resent, so step 3 checks that a write after idle succeeds on its first attempt. The mocked unit tests can't show what Google's front end actually does to an idle connection, so this needs a live server and real idle time.

Setup: a server that has already made a few calls, so its worker threads hold pooled connections. Before each step, leave it idle (no tool calls at all) for at least 10 minutes, the idle time that reproduced the defect in the v0.9.2 pass.

Action 1. Run steps 1–3 on a second server prefix too (both OAuth and service account, if both are available)

docs.title: TC-I66: dev and stable releases both publish through publish.yml, with no PyPI provenance warning (issue #1124)
docs.text:
Background: PyPI flags a release whose trusted-publisher workflow differs from the previous release's with a "Change of provenance" warning on its page. Dev builds came from publish-dev.yml and stable releases from release.yml, and a dev build always precedes a stable release, so v0.9.2's page carried the warning. PyPI compares against the previous upload, not the previous stable release: v0.9.1's page carries the warning although v0.9.0 and v0.9.1 both came from release.yml, because a publish-dev.yml dev build came between them. #1124 merges both tracks into .github/workflows/publish.yml. The first upload through publish.yml follows a publish-dev.yml build, so it's expected to carry the warning once; that's the transition, not a failure. No MCP tool or unit test reaches a GitHub Actions run or PyPI's attestation record, so this is a manual check after merge and after the next stable release.

Setup - PyPI has a trusted publisher registered for publish.yml in this repo (the maintainer step on #1124). - For checks 1–2: a push to develop touching src/**, tests/**, pyproject.toml, or uv.lock has landed since #1124 merged. - For checks 3–5: a stable GitHub Release has been published since #1124 merged, and at least one dev build published through publish.yml before it (checks 1–2 passed first). Merging #1124 alone publishes nothing, since it touches no src/**. If the release's predecessor upload is still a publish-dev.yml build, check 5 fails while the workflow is behaving correctly: record SKIP for check 5, not FAIL.

Action 1. gh run list --workflow=publish.yml --event push --limit 1, then gh run view <run-id>. Note the published X.Y.Z.devN version from the build log or pip index versions mcp-gee-sweet --pre. 2. Read the dev wheel's provenance: curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/mcp-gee-sweet/<version>/json for the .whl filename in urls[], then curl -s "https://pypi.org/integrity/mcp-gee-sweet/<version>/<filename>/provenance". 3. gh run list --workflow=publish.yml --event release --limit 1, then gh run view <run-id>. 4. Repeat step 2 for the stable version's wheel. 5. Open https://pypi.org/project/mcp-gee-sweet/<stable version>/.

Checks - 1, 3: the run completed with success; its jobs are Run tests, Build distribution, and Upload to PyPI, and Upload to PyPI ran. - 2, 4: every attestation_bundles[].publisher is {"kind": "GitHub", "repository": "khuisman/mcp-gee-sweet", "workflow": "publish.yml", ...}. release.yml or publish-dev.yml there means the upload didn't go through the new file. - 5: the release page shows no "Change of provenance" warning.

Re-run cadence: once after the first qualifying develop push following #1124's merge (checks 1–2), and once at the first stable release after that (checks 3–5). After that, only if publish.yml is renamed or split.

Result (2026-10-20) ✅ PASS (checks 1–2) — v0.9.3 release pass (Aziz) @ c90b88d3 Check 1: the two publish.yml push runs after #1124's merge, 39553304435 (746136d4, the GHSA-mpw3 merge) and 39553920594 (c90b88d3, the GHSA-8jqx merge), both concluded success, with jobs Run tests, Build distribution and Upload to PyPI, all success. Check 2: the wheels for 0.9.3.dev34 and 0.9.3.dev35 each carry one attestation bundle whose publisher is {"kind": "GitHub", "repository": "khuisman/mcp-gee-sweet", "workflow": "publish.yml", "environment": null}. So PyPI's last upload before the stable 0.9.3 comes through publish.yml. Checks 3–5 run after 0.9.3 is published.

Result (2026-10-20) ✅ PASS (checks 3–5) — v0.9.3 stable release (Aziz) @ b5e2810b Check 3: publish.yml run 39557996212, event release, on b5e2810b, concluded success, with Run tests, Build distribution and Upload to PyPI all success. Check 4: the mcp_gee_sweet-0.9.3-py3-none-any.whl provenance has one attestation bundle, publisher {"kind": "GitHub", "repository": "khuisman/mcp-gee-sweet", "workflow": "publish.yml", "environment": null}; the uploads just before it were 0.9.3.dev34 and dev35, both through publish.yml. Check 5 (Playwright, since curl gets PyPI's "Client Challenge" page): the 0.9.3 page's Provenance section reads "Full provenance — All 2 files in this release have provenance metadata", with no "Change of provenance" banner. Control: the 0.9.2 page, loaded the same way, still shows the "Change of provenance" banner.

docs.title: TC-I67: uploads over 100 MB complete, and a request that gets no answer fails with a readable message (issue #1129)
docs.text:
Background: thread_http built each per-thread transport as a bare httplib2.Http(), unlike the build_http() that build() gives the services' own transports. That left out two settings. First, there was no socket timeout, so a pooled connection that died silently (no RST or FIN) blocked a request until the OS gave up: 50–200 s, or a 30-minute hang seen live in the TC-MD301 run. Now each socket operation is bounded by HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 60, googleapiclient's own default). A timed-out read is resent once on a new connection; a timed-out write isn't resent, and its error says it may have landed. Second, 308 was still treated as a redirect. Drive answers each non-final chunk of a resumable upload with "308 Resume Incomplete" and no Location, so any upload larger than googleapiclient's 100 MB chunk failed with Redirected but the response is missing a Location: header. (reproduced live before the fix). Unit tests cover both against local sockets; this case checks the real Drive upload path and the configured server. Steps 3–5 need a server started with its own env, as docs/qa/run.md §"Running server-startup and CLI cases in a scoped lane pass" describes.

Setup: a 150 MB file of random bytes, e.g. head -c 157286400 /dev/urandom > /tmp/tc-i67-150mb.bin. The steps say /tmp; a lane uses its own scratch directory instead.

Action 1. upload_local_file(local_path="/tmp/tc-i67-150mb.bin", parent_folder_id="{TEST_FOLDER_ID}", skip_if_exists=false) 2. get_file_metadata(file_id=<the id from step 1>) 3. Start a server with HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=abc and CACHE_DB_PATH=:memory: (so the call can't be answered from cache), and call list_sheets(spreadsheet_id="{SPREADSHEET_ID}") 4. Start a server with HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=0.001 and CACHE_DB_PATH=:memory:, and call list_sheets(spreadsheet_id="{SPREADSHEET_ID}") 5. On the same server as step 4, call create_folder(name="TC-I67 timeout write", parent_folder_id="{TEST_FOLDER_ID}") 6. Start a server with HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=inf and CACHE_DB_PATH=:memory:, and call list_sheets(spreadsheet_id="{SPREADSHEET_ID}")

Checks - 1: the upload succeeds, with no RedirectMissingLocation or "missing a Location" error - 2: size is 157286400 - 3: the server log has one warning, Ignoring HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS='abc': not a positive number; using 60, and list_sheets returns the sheet list - 4: the call fails within a few seconds, not minutes, and the error starts Google API request timed out:. It says the connection layer resent the read once on a new connection, and names HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS - 5: the error starts Google API request timed out: and says it was a write the connection layer didn't resend, which may still have been applied. It doesn't say it was resent - 6: the server log has one warning, HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS='inf' is over the 86400 s maximum; using 86400, and list_sheets returns the sheet list, with no OverflowError

Cleanup: delete_file the step 1 upload, and any TC-I67 timeout write folder in {TEST_FOLDER_ID} (step 5 can time out before or after Drive creates it). Delete /tmp/tc-i67-150mb.bin.

Result (2026-10-24) ✅ PASS — PR #1198 round 1 (Sky) @ e9719f2b Step 1: upload_local_file of a 157286400-byte random file into {TEST_FOLDER_ID} (Shared Drive, OAuth) succeeded, with no RedirectMissingLocation. Step 2: size 157286400, md5_checksum matches the local file. Step 3 (stdio server, HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=abc, CACHE_DB_PATH=:memory:): one warning Ignoring HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS='abc': not a positive number; using 60, and list_sheets returned Sales | Notes & Misc | Empty. Step 4 (0.001): list_sheets failed in 0.42 s with Google API request timed out: no data from Google for 0.001 s. This was a read, so it was retried once on a new connection, which also failed. If Google needs longer to answer this request, raise HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. Step 5: create_folder failed in 0.05 s with the write wording (This was a write, so it wasn't retried, and Google may still have applied it ...), and nothing about a retry. Cleanup: no TC-I67 timeout write folder in {TEST_FOLDER_ID}, since the connect timed out before the write was sent. Upload trashed. Off-case probe: HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=inf logs no warning, and every tool call then fails with a bare Error executing tool list_sheets (OverflowError: timestamp out of range for platform time_t from sock.settimeout). Sent back on the PR, not a TC-I67 check.

Result (2026-10-24) ✅ PASS — PR #1198 round 2 (Sky) @ 4324571d Step 1: a fresh 157286400-byte upload into {TEST_FOLDER_ID} succeeded (OAuth, Shared Drive, after /mcp reconnect). Step 2: size 157286400, md5 matches the local file. Step 3: warning Ignoring HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS='abc': not a positive number; using 60, and list_sheets returned Sales | Notes & Misc | Empty (the first attempt got a transient Sheets 503 The service is currently unavailable after 51 s, and the rerun passed). Step 4: failed in 0.42 s with ... This was a read, so the connection layer resent it once on a new connection, which also failed. .... Step 5: failed in 0.05 s with ... This was a write, so the connection layer didn't resend it, and Google may still have applied it .... Step 6: warning HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS='inf' is over the 86400 s maximum; using 86400, and list_sheets returned the sheet list with no OverflowError. An extra 1e10 probe behaved the same. Cleanup: no TC-I67 timeout write folder; upload trashed.

docs.title: TC-I68: the MCP Bundle installs, offers OAuth consent, and reuses its token after a restart (issue #1036)
docs.text:
Background: scripts/build_mcpb.py builds mcp-gee-sweet-<version>.mcpb from manifest.json (MCPB manifest v0.4, uv server type). The bundle ships the source and uv.lock, staged from files committed at HEAD only (an uncommitted edit is left out of the bundle, so commit before building), with the version stamped from server.json or the release tag, and the host runs uv run --frozen --no-dev python -m mcp_gee_sweet. It's OAuth only: the install dialog asks for the OAuth client file (CREDENTIALS_PATH), and the token lives at ${HOME}/.mcp-gee-sweet-token.json, outside the extension directory. With no token, the stdio server starts degraded and its first tool call offers the consent link (#873). Unit tests and the MCP Bundle workflow cover the manifest, the file allowlist, and a uv install of the built bundle. Two things only a person can check: completing consent in a browser (steps 2–4), and a real Claude Desktop install (steps 5–7). scripts/qa_launch_mcpb.py runs the bundle's mcp_config the way a host does, with ${HOME} pointed at a scratch directory, so steps 2–4 never touch a real token.

Setup - This slot's OAuth client JSON (the file its server's CREDENTIALS_PATH names). Below, <client.json>. - An empty scratch directory, <scratch>, e.g. under $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp. It must not hold .mcp-gee-sweet-token.json yet. - For steps 5–7: macOS with Claude Desktop, and no mcp-gee-sweet extension installed. Back up ~/.mcp-gee-sweet-token.json if one exists, and move it aside.

Action 1. uv run python scripts/build_mcpb.py --smoke, then unzip -l dist/mcp-gee-sweet-<version>.mcpb 2. uv run python scripts/qa_launch_mcpb.py dist/mcp-gee-sweet-<version>.mcpb --credentials <client.json> --home <scratch> --wait-for-consent. Open the printed accounts.google.com link in a browser and approve it before the deadline in the message. 3. ls -l <scratch>/.mcp-gee-sweet-token.json 4. Repeat step 2's command with the same --home, without --wait-for-consent. 5. Open dist/mcp-gee-sweet-<version>.mcpb in Claude Desktop (double-click, or drag it onto Settings → Extensions). Pick <client.json> for OAuth client file and leave Enabled tools empty. 6. In a new chat, ask Claude to call list_spreadsheets. Open the consent link from the result, approve it, and ask again. 7. Quit and reopen Claude Desktop, then ask Claude to call list_spreadsheets once more.

Checks - 1: mcpb pack reports Manifest schema validation passes!, and the build ends with smoke: bundle installs and imports as mcp-gee-sweet <version> and the bundle's path. unzip -l lists manifest.json, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, README.md, LICENSE, icon.png and src/mcp_gee_sweet/... only: no credentials.json, token.json, service_account.json, .env, .venv/ or tests/ - 2: env shows AUTH_METHOD oauth, TOKEN_PATH <scratch>/.mcp-gee-sweet-token.json and ENABLED_TOOLS empty; server: and the full tool count print; token file before the call: False; the first call's error contains the consent link; after approval, token file written, mode 0o600, and a retry N line (at most 3) has is_error=False with the spreadsheet list - 3: the file exists, mode -rw------- - 4: token file before the call: True, and the first call has is_error=False, with no consent link - 5: Claude Desktop installs the extension, shows its name, version and icon, asks for the OAuth client file before enabling it, and lists the server's tools - 6: the first result carries a Google consent link; after approval the second call returns the spreadsheet list, and ~/.mcp-gee-sweet-token.json exists with mode -rw------- - 7: the call returns the spreadsheet list with no consent link

Cleanup: delete <scratch>. After steps 5–7, uninstall the extension in Claude Desktop, delete ~/.mcp-gee-sweet-token.json, and restore the backup from Setup. Revoke the test grants at https://myaccount.google.com/permissions if you don't keep them.

Re-run cadence: steps 1–4 whenever manifest.json, scripts/build_mcpb.py or the server's OAuth startup changes. Steps 5–7 once before the first release that attaches the bundle, and again when manifest.json's server or user_config changes.

Result (2026-10-25) ⚠️ PARTIAL — PR #1255 round 1 (Kit) @ 2454722f Steps 1–4 PASS; steps 5–7 SKIP (need a person with Claude Desktop on macOS; owed before the first release that attaches the bundle). Step 1: Manifest schema validation passes!, smoke: bundle installs and imports as mcp-gee-sweet 0.9.5; unzip -l lists 53 files: LICENSE, README.md, icon.png, manifest.json, pyproject.toml, uv.lock and src/mcp_gee_sweet/*.py only (.mcpbignore dropped .mcpbignore itself and src/mcp_gee_sweet/.env.template). Step 2: env shows AUTH_METHOD oauth, TOKEN_PATH under the scratch home, ENABLED_TOOLS empty; uv built the bundle on CPython 3.15.1; server: Google Spreadsheet (empty server_info.version: server.py never passes one, pre-existing), tools: 143, token file before the call: False, consent link in the first error; approved in this slot's browser, then token file written, mode 0o600 and the retried list_spreadsheets returned the fixture spreadsheet with is_error=False. Step 3: -rw-------. Step 4: token file before the call: True, is_error=False, no consent link. Run under an agent, step 2 printed nothing past the uv install with stdout redirected to a file (block-buffered), so the link never appeared; python -u worked around it (sent back). Cleanup: scratch home deleted; the grant is this slot's own OAuth client, so it was kept.

Result (2026-10-25) ⚠️ PARTIAL — PR #1255 round 2 (Kit) @ c16fcacd Steps 1–4 PASS; steps 5–7 SKIP (need a person with Claude Desktop on macOS; owed before the first release that attaches the bundle). Step 1: Manifest schema validation passes!, smoke: bundle installs and imports as mcp-gee-sweet 0.9.5 (stamped from server.json), 53 files, same list as round 1. Extra: --version v9.8.7 with an uncommitted README.md edit warned building from HEAD; these uncommitted changes aren't in the bundle: M README.md, stamped version and UV_DYNAMIC_VERSIONING_BYPASS 9.8.7, smoke reported 9.8.7, and the bundled README.md had no trace of the edit. Step 2, run with stdout redirected to a file and no python -u: the env: block and consent link appeared in the file as printed; tools: 143, token file before the call: False; after approval token file written, mode 0o600 and retry 1 of list_spreadsheets: is_error=False with the fixture spreadsheet. Step 3: -rw-------. Step 4: token file before the call: True, is_error=False, no consent link. Cleanup: scratch home deleted; the grant is this slot's own OAuth client, so it was kept.

Same call, same result: duplicate_sheet(spreadsheet_id, sheet="Sales") → index 1, list_sheets → ["Sales","Copy of Sales","Notes & Misc","BrandNew","Empty"] — copy still lands immediately after Sales, confirming the success path (loop finds the match and returns its index) is unchanged by the removed catch-all. docs.title: TC-S131: format_cells — unbounded or trailing-newline range is rejected without formatting anything (PR #922) ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Background: _parse_a1_notation used to accept a bare : (every group optional, so the regex matched with no bounds) and any range with a trailing newline ($ matches before a final ). For format_cells, range=":" produced a GridRange with only a sheetId, so repeatCell formatted the entire sheet. PR #922 switched to re.fullmatch and requires at least one row or column bound. Partial-bound forms (A1:, A:, :B5, 1:B) are tracked separately in #926.

Destructive because a regressed build formats the whole sheet. Never run it against a shared fixture; use the scratch spreadsheet from Setup.

Setup: create_spreadsheet(title="qa-tc-s131-scratch"), then update_cells(spreadsheet_id=<new id>, sheet="Sheet1", range="A1:E5", data=<5×5 of any text values>). Keep the ID; TC-S132 reuses this spreadsheet.

Prompt

"Read get_sheet_data(spreadsheet_id=<scratch id>, sheet="Sheet1", range="A1:F8", include_grid_data=True). Then call format_cells(spreadsheet_id=<scratch id>, sheet="Sheet1", range=":", bold=True), then format_cells(..., range="A1\n", bold=True) (a real trailing newline). Then read A1:F8 the same way again."

Checks - range=":" → {"error": "Invalid A1 notation: ':'"} - range="A1 " → {"error": "Invalid A1 notation: 'A1\n'"} (the range is quoted with Python repr, so the newline shows as a literal inside the quotes) - The before and after A1:F8 reads are identical, with no bold cell (no batchUpdate reached the API)

Teardown: none if TC-S132 runs next (it deletes the spreadsheet); otherwise delete_file(file_id=<scratch id>).

Result (2026-10-06) ✅ PASS Scratch spreadsheet with values in A1:E5, no formatting. Both calls returned the expected error. A grid-data read of A1:E5 (include_grid_data=True) taken before and after the two calls was byte-identical, with no bold cells. format_cells resolves the sheet ID before it parses the range, so a nonexistent spreadsheet ID would 404 at the sheet lookup for valid and invalid ranges alike; the unchanged grid is the live evidence that no write was sent. Tested in an isolated service-account sandbox on a Shared Drive.

Result (2026-10-08, PR #929 QA re-run) ✅ PASS Fresh scratch spreadsheet (create_spreadsheet, then update_cells A1:E5 with a1…e5), via mcp-gee-sweet-kit running code that includes #922 (6dd5e6a). range=":" → {"error":"Invalid A1 notation: :"}; range="A1 " → {"error":"Invalid A1 notation: A1 "}. No format_cells call preceded these two, and update_cells writes values only, so the new sheet started with no bold; a grid-data read of A1:F8 (include_grid_data=True) afterward showed no bold cells. No separate "before" read was taken, so this rests on the fresh sheet's default formatting rather than a byte-identical before/after comparison.

Result (2026-10-17) ✅ PASS — v0.9.2 release pass Run 2 (kai-oauth): every check matched; visual cases checked under the Playwright mutex.

Prompt

"For each of A1, A1:B2, A:A, 1:2, B2:D in turn: call format_cells(spreadsheet_id=<scratch id>, sheet=\"Sheet1\", range=<range>, bold=True), read get_sheet_data(..., range=\"A1:F8\", include_grid_data=True) and list the bold cells, then reset with format_cells(..., range=\"A:Z\", bold=False) (all 26 columns of a new sheet, so 1:2's bold past column F is cleared too)."

Checks - A1 → only A1 is bold - A1:B2 → A1, B1, A2, B2 only - A:A → all of column A, including rows past the data - 1:2 → all of rows 1–2, including columns past the data - B2:D → columns B–D from row 2 down, including rows past the data - No cell outside the target is bold, and every call returns replies: [{}] with no error

Teardown: delete_file(file_id=<scratch id>).

Bold cells after each call: A1 → [A1]; A1:B2 → [A1, B1, A2, B2]; A:A → [A1–A8]; 1:2 → [A1–F1, A2–F2]; B2:D → [B2–D8]. All calls returned replies: [{}]. Result (2026-10-08, PR #929 QA re-run) ✅ PASS Same scratch spreadsheet as TC-S131's re-run (values in A1:E5), read A1:F8 after every call, reset with format_cells(range="A:F", bold=False) between ranges. Bold cells: A1 → [A1]; A1:B2 → [A1, B1, A2, B2]; A:A → [A1–A8]; 1:2 → [A1–F1, A2–F2]; B2:D → [B2–D8]. Every call returned replies: [{}]. The A:F reset doesn't clear the bold 1:2 applied from column G onward, and the A1:F8 window can't see past column F, so "no cell outside the target is bold" was confirmed only within A1:F8 (the 2026-10-06 run used the same window). docs.title: TC-S122: add_data_validation — values count/shape mismatch per condition_type returns a local error (unit test)
docs.text:
Background: Issue #366 — before this, a mismatched values count reached the real Sheets API and got a clean 400 back (e.g. NUMBER_BETWEEN with 1 value: "requires exactly two ConditionValues, but 1 value was supplied"), which was already safe, just a round-trip later than necessary. Now caught locally via _condition_value_count_error before any API call, covering all five value-count shapes: zero-only (DATE_IS_VALID, TEXT_IS_EMAIL, TEXT_IS_URL; BLANK/NOT_BLANK were removed in PR #986 as unsupported by data validation, see TC-S134), zero-or-two (BOOLEAN), exactly-one (NUMBER_GREATER, CUSTOM_FORMULA, ONE_OF_RANGE, and the other single-value TEXT_/DATE_/NUMBER_* types), exactly-two (NUMBER_BETWEEN, NUMBER_NOT_BETWEEN, DATE_BETWEEN, DATE_NOT_BETWEEN), and at-least-one (ONE_OF_LIST).

Checks (unit test) - NUMBER_BETWEEN with 1 value → {"error": ...}, before any API call (the issue's own example) - BOOLEAN accepts 0 or 2 values (a plain checkbox or custom checked/unchecked labels), rejects exactly 1 - A zero-value type (DATE_IS_VALID) rejects any supplied value - ONE_OF_LIST rejects an empty/omitted values - Exactly-one types (NUMBER_GREATER, CUSTOM_FORMULA, ONE_OF_RANGE) reject 0 or 2 values - Exactly-two types (NUMBER_BETWEEN, DATE_BETWEEN) reject 1 or 3 values - Covered by TestAddDataValidation::test_value_count_mismatch_returns_error_without_api_call, test_boolean_accepts_two_custom_label_values, test_boolean_rejects_exactly_one_value, test_zero_value_condition_type_rejects_a_value, test_one_of_list_requires_at_least_one_value, test_exactly_one_value_types_reject_zero_or_two, test_exactly_two_value_types_reject_one_or_three

Result (2026-09-13) ✅ PASS (live spot-check) — ran add_data_validation(Empty!H1:H5, NUMBER_BETWEEN, ["5"]) (the issue's own example) against the fixture spreadsheet on the running server (not just the mocked unit tests): returned {"error": "condition_type 'NUMBER_BETWEEN' requires exactly 2 value(s), got 1"} with no sheet mutation, confirming the local check is wired up end-to-end.

Background: Every other sheet-taking tool in structure.py (~22 of them, including add_data_validation) checks sheet existence first and returns {"error": "Sheet 'X' not found"}. get_data_validation skips this check entirely.

docs.title: TC-S119: clear_data_validation removes an existing rule ⚠️ destructive
docs.text:
Background: Issue #365 — before this tool, the only way to remove a data validation rule was delete_sheet + create_sheet on the whole sheet. clear_data_validation calls setDataValidation with no rule, which the Sheets API documents as clearing any existing rule on the range.

Prompt (direct tool call)

  1. add_data_validation(spreadsheet_id=<fixture>, sheet="Empty", range="E1:E5", condition_type="ONE_OF_LIST", values=["Yes","No","Maybe"])
  2. clear_data_validation(spreadsheet_id=<fixture>, sheet="Empty", range="E1:E5")
  3. get_data_validation(spreadsheet_id=<fixture>, sheet="Empty", range="E1:E5")

Checks - Step 1 succeeds (sets up the rule to clear) - Step 2 returns no error - Step 3 (get_data_validation) returns [] — the rule set in step 1 is gone

Result (2026-09-13) ✅ PASS Ran live against the fixture spreadsheet. add_data_validation set the ONE_OF_LIST rule on E1:E5 with no error; clear_data_validation returned no error; get_data_validation on E1:E5 returned [] afterward — confirms the tool's core premise (setDataValidation with rule omitted actually clears an existing rule against the real Sheets API, not just in the mocked unit tests).

Re-verified (2026-09-13) ✅ PASS — after PR #745's _apply_data_validation dedup refactor (commit 931363a): re-ran the same set/clear/confirm sequence on G1:G5 directly against the reconnected server. add_data_validation still sets the rule correctly, clear_data_validation still clears it (get_data_validation → [] afterward) — no behavior change from the extraction.

Result (2026-10-17) ✅ PASS — v0.9.2 release pass Run 2 (kai-oauth): every check matched; visual cases checked under the Playwright mutex.
